Grand Theft Contract: 5 Worst Cardinals Free-Agent Signings Under Monti Ossenfort
full_text:
Grand Theft Auto VI has taken world by storm, delivering on the hype of making it one of the most popular video games of all time.
That got us thinking about some of the worst contracts under current Arizona Cardinals general manager, who has been with the team since 2023. We omitted his 2026 class since they've barely played half of a season.
The five worst deals Ossenfort's made:
Year : 2024 Contract : 2-YR, $30M
This probably takes the cake for the worst contract Ossenfort has ever awarded. Williams was awarded $15 million annually to anchor the team's right tackle spot but was placed on injured reserve after just one game in 2024 and also landed on the list in Week 10 of 2025 – playing just 17 games across two seasons.
Year : 2024 Contract : 3-YR, $30.1M
Jones was awarded $10 million annually to help bolster the Cardinals' defensive line. The results? He tore his triceps in Week 3 of his first season before a knee injury in 2025's training camp placed him on IR again. He was paid $19.75M guaranteed for just three games across two years.
Year : 2024 Contract : 3-YR, $25.5M
There was plenty of hype around Murphy-Bunting and his prior Super Bowl experience. However, he did miss two games with a neck injury and graded poorly for his first year in Arizona. Next offseason, he landed on the reserve/NFI list with a torn ACL/MCL, which kept him out for all of 2025. He didn't make it past final roster cuts this past season.
Year : 2024 Contract : 3-YR, $21M
Nichols, a prior teammate of Jones in Chicago, also struggled in the health department once he landed in Arizona. He played in six games his first season before suffering a neck injury (which landed him on injured reserve) before he also landed on injured reserve after four games due to a knee injury.
Year : 2025 Contract : 2-YR, $29M
Tomlinson signed with Arizona last offseason in hopes of making a bigger impact than he did. While he did play all 17 games in 2025, he statistically had the worst year of his career with just 26 tackles and one sack — which was a massive letdown considering his price tag, and the Cardinals agreed when they cut him last offseason.

title: Cardinals-Chiefs Injury Report Keeps Door Open For Carson Beck
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are holding on to hope.
Carson Beck is not expected to be the team's starting quarterback when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11 thanks to a back injury that popped up this week.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said the team isn't closing the door on Beck playing Sunday, though they're preparing for their fourth starting quarterback in as many weeks with Josh Johnson now expected to be under center.
"Carson will be DNP today. Not going to shut the door on him, but we're going to proceed as if Josh [Johnson] is going to be starting on Sunday," LaFleur told reporters on Friday.
The Cardinals stuck true to their word, as Beck was listed as questionable on the team's official Friday injury report.
The picture for both sides entering Week 11:
OUT - Zach Carter (knee), Jon Gaines (ankle) QUESTIONABLE - Carson Beck (back)
Carter remains out while working through his 21-day practice window in his return from injured reserve while Gaines practiced Wednesday but not Thursday/Friday before being ruled out.
Beck carried no injury designation after his rookie debut, practiced fine on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday, which raised some concerns.
Now, barring an eye-opening turnaround, Beck is set to be sidelined.
OUT - Jaylon Moore (ankle), Trey Smith (concussion), Kenneth Walker (groin) QUESTIONABLE - Omarr Norman-Lott (knee), Peter Woods (neck)
None of Kansas City's three players marked out practiced in any capacity this week while both Norman-Lott and Woods hit the field for all three days in some capacity.
This is the second time Beck suffered a back injury, as earlier in the regular season the rookie quarterback was listed on Arizona's injury report with the same issue that's now flaring up once again.
"I can't answer that because you just treat it," LaFleur told reporters when asked if there's anything that the Cardinals can do for Beck's back injury.
"You go with the people that know what they're doing to treat it, and it's not like it's the first time he's dealt with it. So he's going about his business. He's going to handle it just like he does preparing for a football game, just like he does playing a football game. So we'll see. We'll see more tomorrow."
Official game inactives are due 90 minutes before kickoff in Arrowhead, and it seems like the Cardinals are wanting to keep the door open down to the wire.

title: Daniel Jones Could Give Cardinals GM One Last Chance
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' quarterback situation feels beyond saving.
Third-round rookie Carson Beck isn't expected to play this week due to back spasms, elevating the recently signed 40-year-old Josh Johnson to starting duties.
Johnson is set to be the fourth starting quarterback for Arizona this season, who sits with a 3-7 record entering Week 11's road test against the Kansas City Chiefs — who were 16.5-point favorites before Beck's injury.
Things look bleak right now, though Friday morning's chaotic news cycle for quarterbacks across the league does open the door for the Cardinals to welcome an experienced and ready quarterback... that could potentially save their general manager's job as well:
Daniel Jones was just released by the Indianapolis Colts after their blowout loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football. Jones, a veteran who had a short-lived resurgence in Indianapolis, now hits waivers.
The Cardinals are seventh in the NFL's waiver priority system, using the league's inverse order of standings. This, if they so choose, could be a reality — though he's largely expected to clear waivers, as teams would take on $2.3 million for the rest of the year and $38 million (non-guaranteed) for next season.
Money, for this year or next, isn't an issue for Arizona. 2027 projects the Cardinals to have the second-most cap space in the league.
Monti Ossenfort is wrapping up his fourth season running the Cardinals, one that could very much be his last depending on these final seven games. Arizona's already surpassed expectations this season with three wins in the first half of the schedule, though as injuries mount and losses accrue, more pressure will land on Ossenfort to finish the season strong.
There's a possibility a few wins at the end of the year could very well save Ossenfort's job for 2027, and with Beck's back injury unknown for the remaining slate of the schedule, Arizona's general manager may be looking for a Hail Mary to prevent the 2026 season from getting truly ugly all while keeping his seat secured.
Enter Jones — a former first-round pick with plenty of experience and the ability to be plugged and played immediately if needed. The Cardinals were reportedly interested in Jones after he was released by the New York Giants a few seasons ago before he opted to join the Colts.
That interest could again rise if/when Jones clears waivers. There's not many opportunities that make sense for Jones in terms of immediately emerging as a starter, but that could very well be the case in Arizona if Beck's injury persists.
While it wouldn't be a play for the long-term, Ossenfort demonstrated at the trade deadline (by not offloading Josh Sweat and Budda Baker) that he clearly was trying to squeeze wins in the second half of the schedule.
The long term doesn't matter for a guy who might not make it through the short term.
The Cardinals are beaten, and depleted. Arizona's not making the playoffs, and with such a cloudy future ahead in the desert, Ossenfort may be looking for any last lever to pull to ensure he's still running the show at the end of the season.
That final move could come in the form of Jones.

title: Carson Beck's Latest Injury Raises Big-Picture Questions for Cardinals
full_text:
TEMPE — The last 48 hours in the desert could have a much longer-lasting impact on the Arizona Cardinals and the future of football's most important position.
The Cardinals approach their Week 11 road trip to Kansas City with Carson Beck's health taking a massive turn in the last 48 hours.
The rookie quarterback practiced with no issues on Wednesday before back spasms made him a surprise on Thursday's injury report. He practiced — but in limited fashion.
Friday's announcement from head coach Mike LaFleur revealed Beck's back injury would prevent him from taking the field today, while also placing the recently signed veteran Josh Johnson in position to start.
"Carson will be DNP today. Not going to shut the door on him, but we're going to proceed as if Josh [Johnson] is going to be starting on Sunday," LaFleur told reporters on Friday.
The Cardinals' season at 3-7 is already lost, though Beck's recent injury only throws a wrench into Arizona's plans for the rest of the year while raising questions around Beck's future with the organization.
Beck, a third-round pick, finds himself in odd territory. He's not quite in pole position to be the team's franchise quarterback, but the Day 2 capital invested in him suggests the Cardinals desperately want him to work out.
However, a holdout from prior starter Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew's arrival via free agency planted Beck as an afterthought in the desert for the first half of the season. Beck wasn't even the team's No. 2 quarterback as an inactive/emergency-only quarterback on gamedays.
After Brissett was traded and Minshew was injured, the door opened for Beck's long-awaited arrival to starting duties. It was inevitable due to Arizona's poor record and the need to evaluate Beck with actual game film.
It's been an odd rookie season for Beck, who isn't exactly afforded the luxury of time to grow and develop thanks to an impending 2027 offseason where the Cardinals could very much look to add another quarterback.
Beck has an injury history that isn't exactly crystal clear.
Prior to emerging out of the draft, the former Miami/Georgia product had UCL surgery on his throwing arm, which brought some questions on his ability to fully recover from the injury while also bringing on questions surrounding his arm strength.
Beck suffered a rib injury in preseason play, which ultimately kept him out of the team's final three exhibition games. Early in the regular season, Beck dealt with similar back spasms — though circumstances and stakes were much different.
The Cardinals needed every possible bit of information available to form an opinion/evaluation on Beck prior to 2027, where they're loaded with the second-most projected cap space and six picks in the first four rounds of the draft.
Beck would have to play considerably well down the stretch of this season to convince the Cardinals to not pursue another serious option at the position, especially with the possibility of a new general manager arriving next offseason.
However, Beck simply needs to be healthy and available to play during these final few games for that possibility to even be on the table — and an injury-filled rookie season puts a massive damper on the short evaluation of Beck that we do have in this moment.
There's a small chance Beck can feel much better waking up on Saturday or Sunday and manage to play. There's an even bigger chance Beck returns sooner as opposed to later and finishes out the season.
The Cardinals are hoping Beck pans out to be a franchise guy, but the early returns bring more questions than answers at this point in time.

title: Cardinals QB Carson Beck Suffers Alarming Injury Setback
full_text:
TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals' whirlwind of a season continues.
The Cardinals are preparing for rookie quarterback Carson Beck to miss Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs due to back spasms picked up this week in practice.
"Carson will be DNP today. Not going to shut the door on him, but we're going to proceed as if Josh [Johnson] is going to be starting on Sunday," Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Friday.
40-year-old Josh Johnson is currently in line to start, which will mark the fourth starting quarterback Arizona's had this season. The Cardinals are massive underdogs to the Chiefs entering Week 11.
Beck previously dealt with back spasms earlier in the year, though that was when he was Arizona's third-string quarterback. A preseason ribs injury and a college UCL surgery gives plenty of concern for Beck's overall health as an NFL player.
The Cardinals are taking things, as LaFleur says, one minute at a time with Beck right now.
"Just taking it one minute at a time right now, not even one day at a time," LaFleur said of Beck, who is still holding out hope to play. "Taking one minute. It's basically just kind of responding to the treatment, you know, see how he feels when he wakes up tomorrow."
Beck practiced with no issues Wednesday before practicing in limited fashion on Thursday. He won't practice Friday, and it sounds like it's a longshot for him to be healthy enough to go at Arrowhead.
Johnson, signed less than two weeks ago, has prior experience with LaFleur and just NFL experience in general. He's played 15 years in the league with over a dozen teams, last appearing on Cincinnati's practice squad.
"I'd be lying to you if I said that I'd be okay not seeing him [Beck] go on Sunday. But it is what it is. Show goes on in this league," LaFleur continued.
"I mean, this ball's getting put down at noon on Sunday, and we're gonna go. The cool part is, if it is Josh, I've called plays for him before and had a really great experience calling plays for him. So we'll go shoot our shot, and I expect nothing less from our guys."
The Cardinals will reveal official game statuses later today, and while Arizona sounds like they're going to label Beck as questionable, it's quite clear there's serious doubt around the rookie third-round pick making his second start in the league.
It's a brutal blow for both Beck, fans and the Cardinals organization itself — who is trying to get every possible evaluation of Beck before the 2027 NFL Draft.

title: Carson Beck Added to Cardinals-Chiefs Injury Report
full_text:
Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck popped on Thursday's injury report with a familiar injury.
Beck, after practicing with no injury designation on Wednesday, was added to today's report with a back injury — something that hindered the rookie quarterback weeks earlier in the regular season.
He was marked as limited, which means he practiced but didn't handle his typical workload. Arizona has 40-year-old Josh Johnson listed as their backup in case Beck, for whatever reason, won't go this week.
The Cardinals prepare for the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11. They're one of the largest underdogs of the season with a 16.5-point spread at Arrowhead on Sunday — and that was with Beck.
Beck previously dealt with a back flare-up that materialized out of nowhere, according to head coach Mike LaFleur earlier in the year. However, circumstances are now very different for the Cardinals and Beck.
Preseason play also saw Beck miss three games due to a ribs injury suffered in the Hall of Fame Game.
No longer the team's third-string/emergency quarterback, Beck is now the full-time starter after Arizona traded Jacoby Brissett and lost Gardner Minshew for the season with a UCL injury — the same elbow injury Beck suffered in college before being drafted as third-round pick this past spring.
Friday morning will see LaFleur speak to reporters, and the coach is expected to give an update on the rookie passer plenty of fans were waiting to see. Arizona lost 34-6 in Beck's debut last Sunday, though the rookie himself looked solid.
After practice, the Cardinals will officially place designations such as out, questionable or doubtful ahead of the weekend.
There was hope Beck would be able to continue adding to his rookie resume this week in what would be his second start.
"I think you guys saw; there was no flinch in him," LaFleur said of Beck on Wednesday. "There wasn't a look in his eye, whether it was going decent in those first two drives, even though we stalled out to then what happened in the rest of the game, (he) never changed. I just think that's his DNA. We're short-term into this thing, but excited to continue to work and watch him grow."

title: Carson Beck Sends Clear Message After Cardinals Debut
full_text:
ARIZONA — Carson Beck officially has an NFL game under his belt.
The Arizona Cardinals ' rookie suffered a 34-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams last week — not ideal by any means — though the general consensus is Beck was let down by the various factors around him.
Beck now moves forward against a highly touted Kansas City Chiefs team, and even in light of what was considered a strong individual debut , he knows he can be even better.
The Cardinals' offense looked functional in their first two drives, walking away with back to back field goals before stalling out the rest of the game.
“I thought we started out hot to be able to go down our first two drives and score, obviously not punch it into the end zone, but (in the) first quarter and even (the) first half, we were right there," said Beck, who had a ball slip through a receiver's hands for an interception near the end of the half.
"We got the ball with a minute and 20 seconds left, I think, somewhere around there with a chance to go down and maybe score a field goal at the end of the half, and we don't do that. We don't execute situational football, and they do a better job in the middle eight than we do. Then at that point, it's six offensive snaps and they've [Rams] scored 21 points. We have to be better. We have to execute better and when we do have opportunities to make plays, especially against really good defenses, you have to make them. You're not going to make them every time, but you want to make them more than you don't.
"We just weren't able to execute in those situations. Looking back at it, I think we did a lot of good and there's a lot to build off, especially as a new group playing together for the first time (with) a lot of the wide receivers, me (and the) running backs, (so) just getting the chemistry with everybody. (I'm) definitely looking forward to these next couple of weeks and seeing how we continue to build chemistry with each other and continue to go out and execute.”
Head coach Mike LaFleur was a big fan of Beck's first game, even in spite of the low box score numbers.
Beck was calm and composed in his first taste of NFL action, which isn't always the case for rookie quarterbacks.
When asked what he thought he did well, Beck answered:
“I think the overall operation of our offense was really good. That's something that (Head) Coach (Mike) LaFleur talks about a lot is the operation (and) getting in and out of the huddle. There were a couple (of) communication things that (for) the first time being out there — calling plays again in a live game and live action and just getting better, being more clear and concise with the huddle, being able to get in and out quickly and get on the ball and snap it right.
"Everything that you can control before the ball is actually snapped and there are live bullets flying, but I think that was good. Just going where the defense told me to go, reading the defense, reading out our plays and trying to give guys opportunities to make plays. For me as a quarterback, that's what I'm here to do. Run the offense, have great operation, get in and out of the huddle and then ultimately play clean football. I think that's something that this offense can do.”
That's also what Beck believes he can improve moving forward.
“Just going back to being clear and concise in the huddle, having elite communication and knowing the play like the back of my hand where I hear the first couple of words come out of Coach LaFleur's mouth or on the wristband and I already know what the play is. I could spit it out without even looking at it," said Beck.
"Being that level of prepared and having elite communication and then ultimately just going out and letting it rip. I think that's something that I did decent in the last game, but that's something that I want to build up to my standard where I see the defense, I see the play and you already know the ball's coming out. Just let it rip. Don't even think once it goes. Once the ball's out of my hand, it's out of my control and just continue to go through my reads and my process and trust guys to go make plays because they're going to.”

title: Every Cardinals Player Drafted in the UFL
full_text:
The NFL regular season is in full swing, and while the Arizona Cardinals are just hoping to finish 2026 on a high note, a few of their former players are set for a change of scenery.
The UFL held their 2026 draft ahead of their spring football season. Through 15 rounds, a few familiar faces here in the desert were selected — including the second overall pick and a Cardinals fan favorite.
Every former Cardinals player taken in the UFL Draft:
Background : Thomas was a former fifth-round pick by Arizona in 2024 and spent two seasons with the organization. He had plenty of hype after a nice showing in preseason during his rookie year but failed to deliver. He also played for the Texans and 49ers.
Background : Martin didn't join the Cardinals until Aug. 1 of this year and was waived as part of final roster cuts. He was a former third-round pick by Detroit who also played for the Chiefs, Steelers and Raiders.
Background : Spears went undrafted this spring and signed with the Cardinals as a free agent in August. Two weeks later he was released as part of final roster cuts.
Background : After spending his rookie season with the Vikings, Lee was cut on Aug. 30 of this year and was signed to Arizona's practice squad shortly after. The Cardinals released him on Oct. 6.
Background : Weaver, a former fan-favorite in the desert, signed with Arizona as an undrafted free agent in 2024 and was a surprise addition to their final 53-man roster that season. Weaver suffered a hamstring injury in August that eventually led to an injury settlement. In 12 games for the Cardinals, he registered seven receptions for 67 yards.
E.J. Warner, the son of Cardinals quarterback Kurt Warner, was drafted in the 13th round (101 overall) by the St. Louis Battlehawks — the same city his father won a Super Bowl in.
While Warner wasn't quite able to accomplish the same in Arizona, he's obviously a franchise legend for the Cardinals, and it should be cool to see how his son performs in the UFL.

title: Cardinals' Trey McBride Problem is Impossible to Ignore
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have a Trey McBride problem.
McBride, the last standing weapon for Arizona's offense entering Week 11's road trip to face the Kansas City Chiefs , is set to finish the 2026 regular season with more attention than he's ever seen in his short but accomplished NFL career.
And the Cardinals might not have a counter-punch to what defenses are doing.
McBride is being doubled (or bracketed) at high rates by opposing defenses — such was the case last Sunday, where he was held to a five-reception, 37-yard performance.
That will continue to be the case for the Cardinals until they and their crew of overlooked receivers can prove otherwise.
Arizona may revert to cloning McBride, according to a (joking) Mike LaFleur:
"We looked into getting a second Trey — like a DNA copycat so you can't (cover both) (laughs). That's part of our deal. If you're going to play man coverage and you're going to bracket, you can scheme whatever you want on that wall — they're going to bracket the guy like I was telling you. They don't care where they're at in those situations. It's just deciding how often they're going to do that," LaFleur told reporters.
"The defensive coordinator in Kansas City (is) deciding how often they're going to do that situationally (and) when they want to do that. When you do that, as you know, you're technically thin a little bit somewhere else. They'll pick and choose their spots like most people do and we have to counter it. What a great opportunity for other guys because if one guy's getting bracketed, guess what? The other guys aren't."
McBride, arguably the best tight end in football, has seen names such as Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne among others evaporate from the lineup due to season-ending injuries. Arizona's top receivers last Sunday included Simi Fehoko, Zay Jones and Devin Duvernay.
Those wideouts (mostly) weren't able to take advantage of those looks in Week 10, as numerous passes slipped through hands, stalling drives in Carson Beck's NFL debut and leading the Cardinals to just 34 offensive plays ran.
Opponents are likely to neutralize McBride with extra attention and bank on Arizona's other weapons to make plays throughout the game in order for a Cardinals win to come to fruition.
McBride is a player that demands respect from defenses, but also targets, regardless of the coverage he's facing. The balance of relying on others to step up while still keeping McBride at the top of priorities in the passing game is one fight — but overcoming the clear advantage opposing defenses will have moving forward is a different beast in itself.
Is there even a way for the Cardinals to get McBride open on those bracket looks?
"Well, again, it doesn't matter. Once there are two guys because unless the safety's blind, they're going to find where he's at," LaFleur said.
"I'm not trying to be (funny) but once it's called — the combination, the bracket, the double stars, whatever it is — they don't care where he's at, they're going to work off of that. Unless they have a tell on us in terms of, 'Hey, when he's in this spot, they're not targeting him.' I don't think that's probably the case with a guy like Trey McBride."
It feels like the impossible is on the horizon for Arizona in the coming weeks.

title: Cardinals-Chiefs Reveal Star-Studded Week 11 Injury Report
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Kansas City Chiefs have revealed their first injury reports of Week 11 ahead of their clash at Arrowhead.
It's a fairly lengthy report with 25 total names between the two sides, with stars such as Patrick Mahomes and Budda Baker headlining their respective squads.
Wednesday's practice report:
With new rookie quarterback Carson Beck in the mix, the Cardinals' offense is hoping to take the next step — and a big part of that could be with starting center Hjalte Froholdt progressing through concussion protocol.
Froholdt wasn't spotted wearing a yellow non-contact jersey during practice — a good sign for his availability moving forward.
"I texted 'Fro' (Hjalte Froholdt) Sunday night after the game because he wasn't there just being in the protocol and all that. I said, 'You're going to have a lot of fun playing with this guy.' So that'll be good," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters.
"This was basically the first walkthrough that they've had where Carson's running the huddle so I'm curious to see what he felt like in that 35, 40 minutes. What he'll provide with practice if he's able to go tomorrow and then into Sunday if he's able to go, is just a guy that's done it for a really long time. He's played in hostile environments. Up until the injury, I thought he was just getting better and better each week handling his job. I'm excited if he's able to clear this thing and be out there."
Top NFL MVP candidate Kenneth Walker III is likely to miss another week, reading between the words of Chiefs head coach Andy Reid today.
"He had a sore groin (last week). It's getting better. We just don't want to do something stupid. ... He's feeling better," he said today ( h/t Nate Taylor ).
It sounds like the Chiefs are being cautious with a game next Thursday (Thanksgiving) around the corner.
Though Kelce and Mahomes are listed on the report, it'd be a surprise if either missed Sunday's game against Arizona.

title: Falcons Fans Aren't Going to Like NFL Network's Re-Ranking of 2024 QBs
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons surprised the NFL landscape when they called Michael Penix Jr.'s name at No. 8 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft.
He was the fourth quarterback taken, with Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, and Drake Maye going with the first three picks. J.J. McCarthy and Bo Nix would both go in the next four picks, giving the Class of 2024 six quarterbacks in the first 12 picks.
Two and a half seasons have gone by, and each of the quarterbacks has seen their share of ups and downs. Penix's journey in Atlanta is well documented, so we won't rehash the Kirk Cousins debacle and subsequent knee injury in 2025 that helped limit Penix to just 20 starts thus far.
NFL Network's Bucky Brooks recently took a look back at the Class of 2024 and ranked the quarterbacks and rendered a verdict on whether or not each quarterback should have his fifth-year option picked up this spring. The decision on the fifth year of first-round picks must be made before they begin their fourth season.
Brooks kept the first three in draft order before shaking up the next three.
Brooks points to Penix's injury history and lack of development because of missed time as reasons he would not exercise his fifth-year option. Though, he has massive praise for Penix's overall ability.
"In an offense that allows him to throw to multiple blue-chip playmakers, Penix could post ridiculous numbers while operating like a point guard leading a fast break. Although he is still finding his way in navigating Kevin Stefanski's system, the impressive flashes from the left-handed gunslinger could still allow one to envision him as a long-term solution in Atlanta," Brooks wrote on NFL.com.
What he liked didn't overcome what he didn't like about Penix, though. Penix is one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL when pressured, and Brooks acknowledges a new system and missed time as possible causes. However, he worries about Penix's ability to be on the field enough to gain the needed experience.
That said, it still feels like a bit of recency bias to put Penix behind McCarthy. They entered the league under similar circumstances, with a veteran taking the snaps during the first season. They both had season-ending injuries. The Vikings dumped McCarthy for a lowly fifth-round pick from the Giants.
McCarthy is 2-1 for the 5-3-1 Giants, but his numbers are nothing to write home about. He's thrown for 915 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions.
We can give Brooks the benefit of the doubt that he gave the nod to McCarthy based on recurring injury history and age. Yes, McCarthy (23) missed last season with an injury as well, but Penix (26) has had five season-ending injuries in seven seasons as a starter, dating back to college.
Still, this feels like a typical "Falcons Tax": When players are pushed down in individual rankings based on the collective failure of the team and franchise. Penix hasn't played better than McCarthy in the last two weeks, and he's playing for a worse team. But, he's been objectively better in nearly every meaningful quarterback category.
Heck, Spencer Rattler has played more games, has a better TD-to-INT ratio and passer rating than McCarthy to date.
At the end of the day though, Penix's competition isn't McCarthy; it's himself. He has seven games to prove to the general manager Ian Cunningham and the Falcons that he can take the reins of the team in 2027 to push them towards a playoff push.
If he doesn't, the Falcons will be investing in the quarterback position this offseason .

title: Falcons’ Young Defensive Core Gives Atlanta Reason for Hope
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have fallen short of expectations during the 2026 season, but the development of several young defensive players has provided reasons for optimism about the future.
Atlanta is in the middle of its bye week at 3-7, sitting at the bottom of the NFC South.
While the team’s postseason hopes have taken a significant hit, the final games present an opportunity to evaluate the young talent that could become the foundation of the defense moving forward.
Daniels has arguably been one of Atlanta’s biggest surprises this season.
Selected 134th overall out of Oklahoma, Daniels entered the season expected to provide linebacker depth. Instead, he has worked his way into a significant defensive role.
Through 10 games, Daniels leads the Falcons with 69 total tackles, including 43 solo stops. He has also recorded one sack, one interception and a fumble recovery.
His performance against the San Francisco 49ers was a defining moment in his rookie campaign. Daniels finished with 11 tackles, nine solo stops, an interception, and a fumble recovery.
His versatility has become increasingly valuable, particularly with Divine Deablo dealing with injuries. Daniels has also taken on additional leadership responsibilities, including wearing the green dot and communicating defensive adjustments.
Perkins has also emerged as an important piece of Atlanta’s defense.
The sixth-round selection out of LSU has recorded 49 tackles, four tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks through 10 games.
His ability to contribute in coverage has been particularly encouraging. According to Pro Football Focus, Perkins owns a 79.6 coverage grade, ranking third among 82 qualifying linebackers.
His athleticism and versatility give Atlanta another option against both the run and pass. With Deablo’s injury history and the emergence of two young linebackers, Perkins could have an opportunity to establish himself as a long-term starter.
Atlanta’s defensive future is not limited to Daniels and Perkins.
Second-round rookie Avieon Terrell has recorded 12 tackles through eight games while adjusting to the speed of the NFL. The Clemson product finished his final college season with 48 tackles, three sacks, and nine pass breakups. He's battled a hamstring injury most of the season; the same injury that contributed to him falling out of the first round in the first place.
Meanwhile, second-year safety Xavier Watts continues to develop into an important contributor. Through 10 games, Watts has recorded 62 tackles, one interception, and two forced fumbles.
The Falcons also have young defensive linemen Maason Smith and Brandon Dorlus contributing. Smith has recorded 17 tackles and one sack, while Dorlus has produced 17 tackles, 1.5 sacks and six quarterback hits.
Anchoring the defensive line is Gervon Dexter Sr. General manager Ian Cunningham acquired him in a trade just before roster cutdowns, and he has arguably been the Falcons' best defensive player this season.
Dexter is the highest-graded defensive player on the team at 79.4, placing him No. 9 in the NFL, according to PFF. He leads the team with 23 quarterback hurries. The Falcons locked him down to a four-year, $78 million extension in September, a week before his 25th birthday
There are also reasons to monitor James Pearce Jr. and Jalon Walker. Pearce missed the first eight games due to suspension, while Walker suffered a season-ending ACL injury during training camp. Both are expected to contribute heavily in 2027.
Atlanta’s 3-7 record tells one story about its season. The development of its young defenders tells another.
The remaining seven games should provide valuable opportunities for Daniels, Perkins and Terrell to establish themselves while the coaching staff evaluates its long-term defensive personnel.
The Falcons still need improvements in their pass rush and overall consistency, but the emergence of two late-round linebackers is an encouraging development.
If Atlanta can continue developing its young talent, the organization could enter the 2027 offseason with a stronger defensive foundation than its record suggests.

title: 5 Falcons Veterans Who Need a Strong Finish to the 2026 Season
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have seven games remaining in the 2026 season, and the bye week provides an opportunity for several players to reset before the final stretch.
At 3-7, Atlanta has fallen well short of its preseason expectations . With the team’s playoff hopes fading, the remaining schedule is about more than wins and losses. It is also an opportunity for important pieces of the roster to prove they belong in the franchise’s long-term plans.
Here are five Falcons players who need a strong finish to the 2026 season.
Few players have more riding on the final seven games than Michael Penix Jr.
The young quarterback entered the season with expectations of taking another step forward and establishing himself as Atlanta’s franchise quarterback. Instead, his development has become one of the biggest concerns surrounding the team’s disappointing season.
Through eight games, Penix has completed 147 of 242 passes for 1,730 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has completed 60.7% of his attempts while posting an 84.2 passer rating (23rd in the NFL among 31 qualifying QBs). He has also taken 12 sacks and lost one of his five fumbles.
His recent performances have been particularly concerning. Against Kansas City, Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards, zero touchdowns, and one interception in a 35-13 loss. He has thrown six interceptions over his last three games.
The Falcons need to see improved decision-making, better accuracy, and more consistency in the passing game. Atlanta cannot afford continued offensive struggles, especially with the quarterback position being one of the most important pieces of its long-term future.
Is Penix still the unquestioned starting quarterback heading into 2027, or will Atlanta need to consider bringing in legitimate competition ? The final seven games could go a long way toward answering that question.
A.J. Terrell is another player who needs a strong finish after a disappointing 2026 campaign.
The veteran cornerback has been an important part of Atlanta’s secondary for years, but his performance this season has raised concerns about whether he can return to his previous level of play.
Through six games, Terrell has recorded 21 combined tackles and three passes defended without an interception. According to Pro Football Focus, his 37.4 overall defensive grade ranks 99th among 103 qualified cornerbacks. His coverage grade of 38.5 ranks 97th.
He has also allowed a 148.5 passer rating when targeted, according to PFF.
Those numbers are concerning for a player expected to be a difference-maker in the secondary. Atlanta needs Terrell to become more consistent in coverage, limit explosive plays, and provide the type of veteran leadership that can help stabilize the defense.
Can Terrell return to being a top-level cornerback, or is Atlanta approaching a point where it needs to reconsider his role as a foundational piece of the defense? His remaining performances will be important in determining how the organization evaluates its secondary heading into the offseason.
Kyle Pitts might have one of the most interesting situations of any Falcons player entering the final seven games.
Atlanta made a significant commitment to Pitts this offseason, signing him to a three-year, $54 million contract extension that includes $36 million in guaranteed money. The agreement keeps him under contract through the 2028 season.
However, his production has not consistently matched the expectations that come with that investment.
Through 10 games, Pitts has recorded 29 receptions for 270 yards and four touchdowns on 42 targets. He is averaging just 9.3 yards per reception.
Although his four receiving touchdowns are a positive, his overall production has been underwhelming. His 270 receiving yards rank 22nd among 38 qualified tight ends, while his 60.2 PFF grade ranks 33rd.
The former first-round selection has the physical tools to become one of the NFL’s most dangerous tight ends. However, Atlanta needs more consistent production from him, particularly as the offense continues searching for answers.
With seven games remaining, Pitts needs to establish himself as a dependable part of the passing game. Creating mismatches, making contested catches and becoming a bigger factor in the red zone should all be priorities.
Can Pitts become the consistent offensive weapon Atlanta envisioned when it invested $54 million in him? His contract suggests the organization believes in his future, but the Falcons need to see that investment translate into production.
Veteran offensive tackle Jake Matthews also has something to prove during the final stretch of the season.
Matthews has been one of Atlanta’s most experienced offensive linemen, providing stability at left tackle since being selected in the first round of the 2014 NFL Draft.
However, his performance this season has not been without concerns.
According to Pro Football Focus, Matthews has allowed 14 pressures, including three sacks and two quarterback hits through 10 games. His overall PFF grade of 62.2 ranks 49th among 71 qualified offensive tackles.
His pass-blocking grade of 72.5 has been more encouraging, but his run-blocking grade of 51.7 ranks 65th at the position.
Protecting Penix has to remain a priority. Atlanta’s offense cannot find consistency if its quarterback is constantly dealing with pressure and struggling to establish himself in the pocket.
At 34 years old, Matthews is also approaching the latter stages of his NFL career. The Falcons must begin evaluating their long-term plans at offensive tackle, especially as they consider how to build a more consistent offensive line.
How much longer can Matthews remain Atlanta’s starting left tackle, and should the organization begin preparing for his eventual replacement? A strong finish would provide some reassurance that he can continue serving as a reliable starter.
Divine Deablo could be facing an important stretch of games as the Falcons evaluate the future of their linebacker room.
Atlanta brought Deablo in to provide experience and stability at linebacker, but injuries have made it difficult for him to consistently remain on the field. His 2026 season has already included a forearm injury suffered against the Chicago Bears in Week 6, forcing him to miss two consecutive games. Although he returned against Cincinnati in Week 9, the injury continued to be an issue heading into the Kansas City matchup, where he was listed as doubtful.
Deablo’s availability has become an important storyline, especially with two rookies taking advantage of their opportunities in his absence.
Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr. have emerged as two of Atlanta’s most promising young defensive players. Daniels has taken over the defensive play-calling responsibilities and has shown impressive instincts, athleticism, and playmaking ability.
Against San Francisco, Daniels recorded 11 tackles, nine solo tackles, an interception, and a fumble recovery. His emergence has been particularly impressive, considering he entered the season expected to develop behind Atlanta’s veteran linebackers.
Perkins has also made a strong impression. The sixth-round selection has recorded 30 solo tackles, two sacks, and a 79.6 PFF coverage grade through the bye week. His ability to contribute against the run, rush the passer, and defend in coverage has given Atlanta another intriguing young option.
With both rookies continuing to develop, Deablo’s place in the linebacker rotation is becoming an increasingly interesting question. With his contract set to expire at the end of the year, he’s not doing himself any favors with free agency approaching.
The Falcons need dependable production and availability from their linebackers. While Deablo brings valuable NFL experience, the organization must consider whether his injury concerns and the emergence of its young talent could change how the position is handled moving forward.

title: ESPN Analyst Delivers Blunt Verdict on Falcons' Quarterback Future
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are into the bye week at 3-7, but still have plenty of questions to answer over the final seven games of the season. The playoffs are still (theoretically) in play for this team , so they still have plenty to play for. However, finding these solutions should be top of mind , with none bigger than who plays quarterback in 2027.
The conversation over whether Michael Penix Jr. can be the long-term answer has dominated the conversation all season. But with seven games remaining, the Falcons appear no closer to finding a definitive answer. At this point, that uncertainty is becoming a problem in itself.
ESPN ’s Ben Solak attempted to tackle this question in his weekly evaluations of the league. His take aligns with what many now believe as we hit the second half of the NFL season: “I think ... the Falcons need a new starting QB in 2027,” Solak wrote.
Solak pointed to injury concerns surrounding Penix, who has only 20 starts. He has delivered impressive performances this season, including against the Packers, Saints, and 49ers, but has struggled to maintain that level consistently.
His arm strength is undeniable, but that alone is not enough to justify a fourth year to see if he can figure it out.
Solak correctly points out the timeline the Falcons have set for themselves after paying Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts Sr. This talented offensive core is entering its prime, but those investments mean little if the team cannot find a quarterback who can consistently get them the football.
The Falcons don't necessarily need to have their long-term answer figured out this season, but they cannot afford to let too many more pass without meaningful progress at the position.
Penix has started eight games this season, and the Falcons are 3-5. He has an NFC Offensive Player of the Week to his credit, but the recent struggles have been central to the team's three-game losing streak . Overthrows, interceptions, slow starts, and struggles against pressure have hurt his consistency and cost the Falcons games.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski made it clear that the organization evaluates its players weekly.
“Big picture, just our evaluations of our players are weekly and season-long, of course. But in terms of anything past that, I'm not really thinking about that,” Kevin Stefanski said. “But anytime you're evaluating any player, you're taking everything into consideration, circumstances and whatnot.”
But the numbers have not been in Penix’s favor. Down-to-down accuracy was a top priority coming into the year, and it hasn't improved as much as many hoped. He has an 18.4% off-target rate on quick passes this season, the second-worst mark in the NFL. His QBR (63.6) is also well below the league average (76.0) on those throws.
Solak called Penix “a bit robotic mechanically” and lacking a “particularly fluid build.” As a result, he telegraphs those quick throws, giving defenders time to respond. Solak also sees a quarterback who struggles to throw to the right side of the field, citing an off-target rate of 25.3% when throwing to the right compared to 18.8% to the left.
“So quick-game throws are tough, and half the field is cut off,” he wrote.
More concerning, his biggest strength has recently exposed another weakness.
Penix’s big arm helps mitigate those issues, but those routes take time and require a quarterback who can hold onto the ball a bit longer. With his issues standing tall in the pocket against looming pressure (he is 22nd out of 37 QBs in the league in EPA per unpressured dropback compared to 36th in EPA per pressured dropback), these plays are almost impossible to call consistently.
Teams have recognized this and have dialed up blitzes. Even though they aren’t hitting him (his 4.7 contacts per game is the league low and his QB pressure rate is second-lowest), Penix rushes through his progressions because of the looming defenders and misses his targets.
When defenders do get to him, Penix has a 39.1 passer rating and 35% completion percentage (63 attempts), both NFL-worst.
His teammates backed him up on Sunday after the loss, but that doesn't mean the front office will this spring. Penix has seven games to change that perception, but barring a turnaround after the bye week, the Falcons could start over at quarterback in 2027.
Garrett Chapman is a sports broadcaster, writer, and content creator based in Atlanta. He has several years of experience covering the Atlanta sports scene, college football, Georgia high school football, recruiting for 24/7 Sports, and the NFL. You can also hear him on Sports Radio 92.9 The Game.

title: Atlanta Falcons Face Defining Moment Entering Bye Week at 3-7
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons enter their bye week at 3-7 following three consecutive losses, including a disappointing 35-13 defeat against the Kansas City Chiefs . With seven games remaining, Atlanta is running out of time to turn its season around.
After entering the year with expectations of competing for the NFC South title, the Falcons have struggled to find consistency on both sides of the football. Their 201 points scored rank 24th in the NFL, while their 258 points allowed rank 23rd. Head coach Kevin Stefanski and his coaching staff have an important opportunity to evaluate the team’s shortcomings and find solutions.
Atlanta’s biggest issue has been establishing an offensive identity . The Falcons have scored just 20.1 points per game and converted 34.4% of their third downs, ranking 27th in the league.
Michael Penix Jr. has completed 60.7% of his passes for 1,730 yards, 10 touchdowns, and seven interceptions through eight games. His inconsistency has contributed to Atlanta’s offensive struggles , particularly against defenses that force the Falcons to rely on the passing game.
Bijan Robinson remains one of Atlanta’s biggest strengths, totaling 951 rushing yards and six touchdowns on 185 carries. He is averaging 5.1 yards per carry, but the team’s rushing production has declined significantly. Atlanta averaged 181 rushing yards per game through its first four games but has averaged just 101.8 over its last six.
Drake London has also been productive, recording 50 receptions for 801 yards and one touchdown. Jahan Dotson has added 416 receiving yards, while Kyle Pitts leads the team with four receiving touchdowns. Finding ways to maximize those weapons needs to be a priority coming out of the bye.
The defense has struggled to provide consistent support, allowing 25.8 points and 358.2 total yards per game. Opponents have also scored touchdowns on 67.6% of their red zone trips against Atlanta.
There have been individual bright spots. Za’Darius Smith leads the Falcons with 4.5 sacks, while Kendal Daniels leads the team with 43 tackles. Harold Perkins Jr. has contributed 31 tackles, giving Atlanta another young defender to develop during the second half of the season.
Stefanski accepted responsibility following the loss to Kansas City, saying, “The responsibility falls on me.” However, accountability must eventually translate into better results.
The bye week gives Atlanta time to evaluate its personnel, playcalling and overall approach before returning to action.
Despite its 3-7 record, Atlanta still has an opportunity to compete in the NFC South. The Falcons face Minnesota, Detroit, Cleveland, and Washington before closing the season with three consecutive divisional matchups against Tampa Bay, New Orleans, and Carolina.
Those final games could determine whether Atlanta has a chance to salvage its season.
The talent is there, but the numbers show how much improvement is needed. The bye week provides an opportunity to reset, get healthy, and establish a new direction. With seven games remaining, Atlanta has one final opportunity to show that its season is not over.

title: What's Gone Right and Wrong for Tommy Rees, Atlanta Falcons Offense
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons entered 2026 as a transition year. The team had a new general manager, new head coach, and new offensive coordinator. But with limited draft picks and very little salary cap room, the personnel, especially on offense, looked pretty much the same.
Tommy Rees took over as offensive coordinator and play caller for the Falcons and Jahan Dotson came in as a starting wide receiver. But those were the only real changes made on that side of the ball.
The big question coming into the year was whether the Atlanta Falcons could find their franchise quarterback in Michael Penix Jr. or not.
Penix has had his ups and downs this season, not totally surprising for a player coming into the season on a repaired ACL and 12 starts to his name. But with seven games left in the season, the jury is still out on him.
ESPN asked its legion of beat writers what has gone right and what has gone wrong for each team, and Marc Ramondi epitomized the Jekyll and Hyde nature of this team by naming running back Bijan Robinson and Penix in both categories. He points out that Robinson is third in the NFL in rushing yards and has the most runs of 20 or more yards of anyone in the NFL.
"The Falcons staff has also successfully made Michael Penix Jr. into an under-center quarterback after he spent almost all of the past two seasons and college working mostly out of the pistol," Ramondi wrote on ESPN .
Penix has thrown for 1,730 yards and 10 touchdowns, while throwing seven interceptions in eight starts (4 of which came in the Tampa monsoon). However, teams have figured out that if they blitz Penix, crash the pocket, they can not only limit Robinson by stopping him before he gets started, but Penix isn't going to make them pay for bringing extra defenders.
"Penix has been poor under pressure, and Rees and company have not yet figured out a way to mitigate the problem. Penix has the worst completion percentage in the league while under pressure (34.9%) and the second-worst success rate (21.5%)," Ramondi continued.
Kill two birds (no pun intended) with one stone. Defenses have one target. If they aim about five yards behind center, they'll either find Penix trying to pass or Penix handing off to Robinson. The pre-snap and post-snap reads aren't punishing defensive coordinators for taking a risk sending six defenders into the offensive backfield.
The Falcons have a bye week to try and figure it out. The Chiefs blitzed the Falcons on nearly every play, and their bllitz percentage on the season is just 28.7%.
Atlanta faces the Minnesota Vikings next week, who blitz on 67.3% of defensive plays, nearly double the New York Giants, who come in second at 37.5% (the Falcons are 28th at 19.8%).
Questions about Penix's ability to handle pressure have already led some national pundits to predict the Falcons will be in the quarterback market in April's NFL Draft . If he's going to stop that from happening, he and Rees need to figure out how to have some success against pressure.
The Vikings present the ultimate test on Sunday, November 29th.

title: Atlanta Falcons Move On from Michael Penix Jr. in ESPN's Latest Mock Draft
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons came into the season with their biggest question being at quarterback. Could Michael Penix Jr. or Tua Tagovailoa show enough this season to solidify himself as the quarterback of the future for this team?
We have a definitive answer on the Tagovailoa part of that question, but after 10 weeks of the 2026 season and a 3-7 record, the jury is still out on Penix. Maybe it shouldn't be all that surprising that a quarterback with 12 career starts, coming off a season-ending knee injury, would have ups and downs this season.
But three years is a lifetime in the NFL, and Penix is running out of time to lock down the Falcons starting quarterback job in 2027.
ESPN's Jordan Reid has already seen enough, and has the Falcons taking Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr with the No. 8 overall pick, a spot in the draft order made popular by former head coach Arthur Smith.
Reid's reasoning for selecting Carr almost sounds like he's course-correcting for the Falcons and choosing the anti-Penix option.
"Carr is an instinctive passer who consistently has answers and has already been given considerable autonomy in Notre Dame's offense," Reid wrote on ESPN . "He doesn't have the high-end traits of some passers in the class (picture a more mobile Kirk Cousins), but he is polished in many of the skills that are essential to playing the position."
Reid may have hurt his case with Falcons fans by mentioning Cousins, but I've also heard Carr described as a more toolsy Brock Purdy. Purdy didn't have the traits to get drafted in the first round (or almost drafted at all), but he's loaded with all of the "skills essential to playing the position."
At 3-7 with the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions on deck, the Falcons are facing 3-9 in the face and could end up with a higher selection than No. 8. Drew Mestemaker is the only quarterback Reid has taken higher than Carr, going to the Jets at No. 2 overall after a trade with the Chargers.
The Dolphins (No. 3), Eagles (No. 5), and Cardinals (No. 7) will also be threats to take a quarterback, and the Chargers (No. 4) could be a trade-down candidate for a team behind the Falcons looking for a quarterback.
If the Falcons stay put, but don't like the quarterback options available when they're on the clock, offensive tackle, wide receiver, and cornerback are glaring needs. Indiana wide receiver Charlie Becker goes No. 4 to the Chargers. Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore is selected by the Jets (ironically, with a pick they got from the Colts for Sauce Gardner) at No. 6. Offensive tackle Jordan Seaton of LSU is taken by the Cardinals at No. 7.
Utah offensive tackle Zereoue Williams is an intriguing prospect still on the board when the Falcons pick and goes to the Texans at No. 9.
General manager Ian Cunningham took the job in January when the Falcons were light on draft picks and low on available salary cap. That won't be a problem this offseason.
However, he's got a lot of holes to fill on a team that is headed towards its ninth consecutive losing season.

title: Falcons Have a ‘Streetball’ Solution to Their Offensive Struggles
full_text:
Jahan Dotson had a simple solution for the Atlanta Falcons (3-7) to overcome their recent offensive slump.
“We need to get an edge as an offense,” the wide receiver told reporters Monday. “And come out with a demeanor like we can’t be stopped and get things going.”
Atlanta has been mercurial with the football this season.
It’s experienced the highest of the highs with quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and the Bijan Robinson-led run game complementing each other. And it’s been at rock bottom, such as when the now-division rival Cooper Rush started the first two games while Penix recovered from a torn ACL.
But the offensive struggles continue despite Atlanta having a relatively healthy unit, with Brian Robinson Jr. among its notable absences .
“I told some of the guys it’s like streetball out there,” Robinson said last Sunday, Nov. 15, after the Falcons turned in a poor output in a 35-13 Week 10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs .
“Free-flowing, you know your assignment, and just make it happen. That needs to be our mentality.”
Atlanta ranks 17th in total offense, 22nd in passing offense, and third in rushing offense, though not as explosive early in the season.
It also had a midseason surge, scoring a league-leading combined 80 points in Week 3 and Week 4 wins. In their active three-game losing streak, Atlanta averages 10 points.
As offensive coordinator Tommy Rees faces scrutiny over predictable play-calling, slow starts and low-scoring performances, the Falcons are searching for their own version of the NFL Street video game.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski reaffirmed Monday that Rees would retain play-calling duties. But if the offensive struggles persist, that decision could face renewed questions.
“Just trying to dominate,” Dotson said. “That’s really what you do in streetball – to get what we want to do on offense.”
For Atlanta, establishing an edge goes beyond simply playing with more aggression. It’s about developing habits that allow the offense to execute consistently, regardless of the opponent or situation.
The Falcons have proved they can put points on the scoreboard in bunches. The challenge is sustaining that production week to week, especially during a losing streak when scoring opportunities have become increasingly difficult to capitalize on.
Building the right mentality during the week and carrying those habits into games could help Atlanta recapture some of the offensive confidence from earlier in the season.
“It’s definitely a mentality; it’s habits,” Dotson said. “It’s what you do every day in practice. It doesn’t just happen on game day. If you’re going to say you want to be that, you’ve got to be about it every day.”

title: 3 Reasons Why Bijan Robinson Is Underused by Atlanta Falcons
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have come under heavy criticism for their use, or lack thereof, of All-Pro running back Bijan Robinson. Much was made of Sunday's anemic effort against the Kansas City Chiefs when the Falcons went three-and-out on their first possession without Robinson touching the ball.
There are several reasons contributing to the perceived misuse of their star player, but let's dig into three big ones.
Defenses have figured out that the way to stop the Falcons' offense is to stop  Robinson and put pressure on Michael Penix Jr. Unfortunately for the Falcons, this can be accomplished by the same method: stack the box and blitz the gaps.
On the Falcons' first play from scrimmage, the Chiefs had seven players on the line of scrimmage, and they had nine in the box. They sent six on a blitz. That's an awfully tough front to run against.
They sent six on the snap; Penix made the right read, throwing the ball to Drake London, whose cornerback came on a blitz, but he airmailed the throw. Now it's second and 10, and you're behind the sticks. The Chiefs blitzed on second down, and the Chiefs blitzed on third down.
Whether you blame offensive coordinator Tommy Rees, the offensive line, Penix, or some combination of all three, Penix's passing numbers against the blitz and against pressure are atrocious.
Of 34 quarterbacks who have faced at least 35 blitzes, Penix ranks 27th in EPA per play, according to Sumer Sports .  His EPA when pressured is 31st of 33 quarterbacks who have faced at least 50 pressures, and his 36.5% completion percentage is dead last.
Robinson leads the NFL in yards after contact, and that's not necessarily a stat I'd be bragging about as an offensive coordinator. The better metric? Yards before contact. Robinson is 12th in the NFL at 2.7 yards per rush, according to Pro Football Reference . It was 1.5 yards before contact against the Buccaneers.
If I'm a defensive coordinator, I know I can flood the Falcons' offensive backfield and stop Robinson, and Penix isn't going to beat me by throwing the ball. That makes playing defense awfully easy.
Robinson had nine touches in the first half. That's not an eye-popping low number of touches, but the Falcons only ran 24 plays, nine of them coming on the only drive on which they converted a first down. They had six drives, and five of them were three-and-out.
No one is getting a lot of touches when you have five three-and-outs and are 5-of-16 on third down in the game. The Falcons have fallen to 27th in the NFL in third-down conversions at 32.4%.
The inability to convert on third down and turn drives into points helps contribute to the team falling behind early. Call this reason 2b, but the Falcons have played more snaps down two scores than any team in the NFL.
Rate of offensive snaps trailing by double-digits... Falcons 35.9% Cardinals 33.5% Titans 31.9% Dolphins 31.6% Chargers 29.1% Steelers 27.5% Raiders 27.3% Patriots 26.9% Panthers 25.3% Browns 24.6% Cowboys 21.9% Commanders 21.9% Jets 19.9% Bucs 18.2% Packers 17.6% Giants 15.9%…
It's hard to establish a running game when you can't extend drives and you're behind in games.
How many people critical of Robinson's lack of use would be surprised to learn he has the second most touches (220) in the NFL behind Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (240)?
The Falcons haven't had a bye yet, but his touches per game are still No. 4 in the NFL at 22.0, trailing only James Cook of the Bills, Kenneth Walker III of the Lions, and Gibbs.
Robinson is getting the ball. Other than the blowout loss to the Bears, he has had at least 19 touches in every game this season.
Maybe. But I don't know that I want Bijan Robinson slamming his head into nine-man fronts, down two scores, on a 3-6 (now 3-7) team who were sellers at the trade deadline.
Until the Falcons figure out how to back defenders off the line of scrimmage, Robinson is going to continue to be limited in his effectiveness, or as some might call it: Misused.

title: Falcons DT Gervon Dexter: 'We’re Not Worried About What’s Going On Offense'
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons ’ defensive struggles have become increasingly difficult to overcome as the team’s offense continues to search for consistency.
Atlanta suffered its fourth consecutive loss on Sunday, falling 35-13 to the Kansas City Chiefs and dropping to 3-7 on the season. While the defense managed to produce several important stops early in the game, the Falcons ultimately struggled to contain Patrick Mahomes, who finished with 348 passing yards and five touchdown passes.
Following the loss, Falcons defensive lineman Gervon Dexter discussed the importance of complementary football and explained why the defense cannot afford to focus on the struggles happening on the other side of the ball.
“I don’t think none of the guys on defense is worried about what’s going on offense,” Dexter said. “I think we’re more so focused on if we do have to go back out there, get another stop, taking the ball away, getting turnovers and putting points on the board ourselves.”
The numbers illustrate the challenges Atlanta faced against Kansas City. The Chiefs finished with 461 total yards of offense, compared to 370 for the Falcons. Kansas City also scored five touchdowns through the air, consistently finding ways to capitalize on opportunities.
Still, it was a 7-3 game with 3:49 left in the first half when the Falcons had 1st and 10 at their own 19. Three plays later, the Falcons punted, their fifth three-and-out on six possessions in the first half. Kansas City got a quick score before half and took control of the game 14-3.
Dexter acknowledged that Atlanta’s defense had opportunities to keep Kansas City from taking control but emphasized that containing a quarterback like Mahomes requires consistent execution throughout all four quarters.
“Obviously he’s a good quarterback, so you can’t just do it for 30 minutes. You got to do it for the whole game,” Dexter explained.
The defensive lineman pointed to keeping Mahomes off the field and forcing longer down-and-distance situations as areas where Atlanta could have performed better.
Kansas City converted four of its 13 third down attempts, while the Falcons’ defense recorded seven punts. However, the Chiefs were particularly effective when reaching scoring territory, converting all three of their red zone opportunities into touchdowns.
That challenge becomes even more difficult when an offense struggles to sustain drives.
Atlanta converted just five of 16 third-down opportunities and finished with nine penalties for 65 yards. The Falcons also committed two turnovers, including an interception and a lost fumble, further limiting their opportunities to establish offensive momentum.
Another Falcons defender, Cameron Thomas, echoed Dexter’s comments about maintaining accountability rather than pointing fingers at another unit.
“If the offense is going three-and-out, then we got to make them go three-and-out,” Thomas said. “It just comes down to everybody staying together, and let’s keep fighting.”
Thomas’ comments reflect the mentality coming from Atlanta’s locker room entering the bye week. Players understand that neither side of the football can consistently carry the team without receiving support from the other.
The Falcons have seven games remaining to turn their season around, but their margin for error continues to shrink.
With the bye week providing an opportunity to evaluate their performance, Atlanta must find a way to establish more consistency offensively while allowing its defense to play with the support it needs.
The defense cannot control what happens on the offensive side of the ball. However, as Dexter made clear, Atlanta’s defenders must continue to find ways to make plays regardless of the circumstances.
For the Falcons to have any chance of salvaging their season, complementary football must become more than just a talking point.

title: What To Expect From Jacoby Brissett In His Second Ravens Start Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens nearly got Jacoby Brissett knocked from the football game in his second series playing quarterback for them last week.
The journeyman starter, who will finish the season at QB if able to stay healthy with Lamar Jackson essentially done for the season , quickly showed he can provide a modicum of hope in the passing game but it also comes with serious limitations. And without time to throw, any chance rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has of salvaging this campaign is down the drain .
There are also things Doyle can do to make life easier for him, and after getting blown up with multiple offensive linemen spun around and beat and pushed back into him , Brissett will surely lean into those options now having grasped from field level (and not just film) how desperate of a situation this is. Brissett will hang in there and try to create plays for others downfield, but Doyle must recalibrate himself and if they drop Brissett back 50 times again this game is not going to go well on the scoreboard or on next week’s injury report.
Here’s what to expect from Brissett in his second game with the Ravens:
We chronicled from the moment it was clear Baltimore was interested in Brissett who stood to gain the most from his arrival. He throws to TEs more than anyone else and has far and away his best success with those big targets … yet Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas, rookie TEs, combined for just 33 offensive snaps in his debut with all that passing.
That was silly, since Brissett was 11/11 on passes to TEs and he raised Mark Andrews’s career from the dead with his best game in over season-and-a-half. Rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane has size too, but he is raw and missed a ton of time and I would recommend getting into 12 and 13 personnel HYPER and letting Hibner and Cuevas run those seam routes from the slot.
Teams haven’t really tried to push the ball downfield with TEs against the Panthers. Brissett should. Getting an explosive play out of Hibner and Cuevas absolutely needs to be an objective in Week 11.
Running back Justice Hill carved out an immediate role in the pass game, and when he is your third-down back and best pass protector and your line stinks this bad, he’d better be on the field and available a bunch . Screens for Derrick Henry – not as adroit in space – went nowhere but Hill and rookie Adam Randall need to show up with targets.
If they don’t trust Randall is pass pro, get him in pony packages with Hill but use him more as a pass catcher while manning an internal stance in the offense. The screens to Zay Flowers behind the line of scrimmage can be pretty devastating too. Doyle was yammering about “five-man routes” this week; that’s silly. Make the most of 3-4 potential targets with misdirection and multiplicity in the pass game and help the OL while you are at it.
If Joe Fagnano (in the preseason, but still) can run to a spot and throw a screen back across his body to the far side, Brissett can do it better. Those concepts better get some run on Sunday.
The Ravens don’t have the weapons or the offensive line to sustain that much volume in the pass game. They need to stick with the run to keep the game close given their failing defense . Brissett needs to check into runs, they need to commit to heavy personnel to help the run and be willing to take play-action shots out of that.
If there is not a completion to a tight end for 25+ yards – or a few – out of heavy personnel looks in play action, something ain’t right. Sadly, lately, a lot ain’t been right about this crew, but Brissett is a gamer and he more than did his part on Monday. What he was asked to do was, in so many ways, misguided.
The overarching emphasis from this staff must be on finding ways to fight for 30 rushes in this game as a team, if not more, against a Panthers defense that is in the bottom six in the NFL in run defense Expected Points Added.

title: It's Time For These 5 Young Ravens Players To Get A More Meaningful Look
full_text:
The Ravens insisted on keeping 10 of the 11 players they drafted around into Thanksgiving.
It’s time to start playing them. Some, just getting active on game day and into some semblance of a rotation, and others need to be given a wide ramp to more meaningful playing time. Frankly, in a lost season amid a five-game losing streak with rampant issues on all sides of the ball, it’s time for a bunch of players on rookie contracts to be more empowered.
Rookie head coach Jesse Minter has been tasked with pretending this was a Super Bowl contender, and, if weighed against those expectations, is being questioned around the league as a potential one-and-done . His defense stinks and the offense, without Lamar Jackson, can’t run or throw the ball, and the bloated and overpaid roster is loaded with veterans who Minter cannot reach or get to perform anything close to the level at which they are being compensated .
Enough of all the BS about “accountability” and “telling the truth.” With $19M corner Marlon Humphrey embarrassing the franchise this week, getting called out by Mayor Brandon Scott , and then finally benched, it’s the perfect time for Minter to lean into youth. It better be about building a future and finding pieces for the future, because the present is as bad as it can get losing on Monday night at home to a winless team. A lot needs to change in Owings Mills and the obvious rebuild should be getting a jumpstart Sunday in Carolina with Jackson out for the season (trust me) and Humphrey suspended by the team and top defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike already ruled out with a hamstring injury.
These kids need to start getting a look, or a longer look:
Yeah, the Chargers were the rare team this season that invested any volume in their run game at all. I get that. But getting him on the field for just four snaps and not seeing him as someone with the potential to play regularly in this defense seems silly. Roquan Smith shouldn’t be playing every snap, maybe more Kyle Hamilton in coverage – with safety Jaylinn Hawkins still hurt – helps create a spot, too.
It’s not impossible for Buchanan and Trenton Simpson – who has made the case for a new contract with a breakout season – to be on the field more together. Slashing this kid’s role as he works back from ACL surgery, unless mandated by physical condition, would be foolish. Was one of very few youngsters to standout in 2025 and did so as a rookie.
Fellow-rookie Josh Cuevas has passed him by and is getting a chance to do more in the slot and run seam routes. Hibner should be faster and more explosive and play faster and more explosive and this offense should be living in 12 and 13 personnel. The fact that overpaid veteran Mark Andrews had his best game in two years shouldn’t deter from an effort to get the kid TEs on the field more with a quarterback in Jacoby Brissett who loves throwing to that position group.
The fact Hibner and Cuevas combined for 33 snaps on offense is fairly ridiculous and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is struggling mightily right now with concepts and formations .
We’ve been calling for him to start phasing Humphrey out on the boundary all year. Humphrey should have never been on this team in the first place. The Ravens love to create whisper campaigns about how great their mid-round picks are going to be, but then when they have to play, if general manager Eric DeCosta picked them, it’s usually bleak.
He should be a fit with Minter’s scheme but whatever he was showing in practice had to be ugly since it took Humphrey getting international scorn for his juvenile podcast in order to finally get Tampa on the field more.
Could be an interesting jack-of-all-trades piece at a time when the offensive roster is flat. Can he create for himself in space? Let’s find out, because this broken offensive line can’t do anything for anyone in the run game or the pass game. Catch balls out of the backfield, get him involved in pony packages . Let’s go.
Remember him? Took him near the end of the draft. Been on the practice squad. With Madubuike out, let’s start taking a look. Madubuike is only signed for one more year, anyway, and that neck injury was a big deal. Travis Jones is a guy who can help out, but he’s not special and playing 40-year-old Calais Campbell in a lost season ahead of this kid is silly.
Evaluators I trust thought he was a potential steal and this franchise is brutal evaluating tackles and abstained from leaning into loaded recent drafts at the DT spot. He might surprise them if they let him play.
