title: How The Bengals Cooled Down a Hot Pittsburgh Defense in Week 10
full_text:
The offseason discussion on the Bengals' run game wasn't a waste of time.
Well, it was, but it was an understandable conversation! Teams that are too spread out and can't present a credible threat on the ground are getting beaten over the head by the flexibility that allows defenses. The Bengals have, from time to time, had issues with it, and it stood in the way of maximizing their output and efficiency.
There was another part of that.
The pass protection was egregiously bad. Yes, it was more exposed to difficult rush conditions, a big part of that flexibility I just mentioned, but they were bad. That is emphatically no longer the case.
Now, Burrow, Chase, and Higgins, who have always been good enough to do this, are able to attack any defense and any coverage. They're fine with light boxes, shifting/disguised coverages, and teams putting a lid over the top. Almost no other team has a QB that can live this way, but now that he has enough time to do so, the Bengals can throw options out there and allow Burrow to point out the coverage, get through his read, and find an answer.
Nowhere is safe from a QB who can truly survey and get the ball accurately to every inch of grass. Teams know this. Now that their four-man rushes aren't working, they are beginning to get desperate and make bigger and bigger mistakes. On Sunday night, the Bengals torched Pittsburgh's pressure packages, specifically targeting the structures of their pressure coverages.
So what did exactly did they attack? And how?
Fire Zones are five-man pressures where you don't want to push all your chips in and play man. Also known as "zone pressures" or "zone blitzes". Fire zone is a specific set of coverages. It's constructed as a balance between aggression and coverage. You're only sending five instead of six like a true blitz, and you're playing softer zone coverage but matching guys that enter your zone.
Between aggression and coverage, man and zone coverage, it's almost the ultimate balance of everything.
pic.twitter.com/4Kjyamb4gd
Your typical fire zone configuration is an even 3-deep, 3-under coverage like the above.
Michigan is running a traditional Fire Zone path with a Trap 2 behind it. On the bottom, the CB plays a Squat technique to support the Deep 1/2 player coming from low to high. Plays out similar to Quarters & how the Chiefs play their 'Tango' coverage. #ArtofX pic.twitter.com/fJQTI458NN
You can also play what's called a "two-trap fire zone" where the corners can help out underneath. Standard 3d3u fire zone is very exposed in the flat with the SCF (seam-curl-flat) defenders working inside out and the CBs playing a loose third. This is meant to give some support into the flat.
These are the main way zone pressure coverages are played. When teams play the Bengals, this is how they tend to do it when they send extra pressure because they don't want to give up an automatic 50 yards down the sideline to Chase.  Understandable, but it also happens to be a terrible idea. There is no safe way to send extra bodies at the Bengals passing offense.
When blitzed in the last three games, #Bengals QB Joe Burrow is: 30 of 33 for 391 yards -- 11.8 yards per attempt!! -- with 5 TDs, 1 INT and a passer rating of 143.0. Next week's opponent, Washington, has the fourth highest blitz rate in the league.
Elite processing QBs are unblitzeable because they are comfortable speeding up their operation and finding the weakness. Even more, Burrow's pre-snap command and unlimited protection-adjusting autonomy allows them to customize based on look and optimize their pickup.
The Bengals are so effective against fire-zones for a few reasons. Against the standard 3u-3d structure, DCs tend to give the CBs big cushions, as again fire zone is designed to prevent the all or nothing nature of standard man pressures. With two of the best go-ball threats in the league, that is even more pronounced against the Bengals' offense
Primary issue with running fire zones against the Bengals is that you have to give them huge cushions on the outside to stay out of go ball territory and they're very aware of it pic.twitter.com/AsDau20fTe
The Bengals absolutely love to take these freebies whenever they're given them, and they get them a lot.
2-Trap fire zones are not much better https://t.co/oVK9ePVjCl pic.twitter.com/EMIjOJwvcS
Because 2-trap fire zones are so focused deep and outside, they leave a lot of space in the middle. This happens to be the area the Bengals are most above the rest of the league as a passing attack.
Al Golden has found a pressure that works in this 3 deep 2 underneath hot coverage pic.twitter.com/fauU7Fjq4u
The idea of HOT blitzes, which are blitzes with the unique "HOT" pressure coverage is simple. They're basically fire zone with one less guy, 3 deep, 2 under instead of 3 deep, 3 under. This is because when you send a true blitz of six guys instead of a standard pressure with five, you obviously lose that one guy in coverage. The Steelers played it a little differently than normal, with the deep middle S playing more of a "lurk" technique instead of a deep post, but the structure is the same.
This coverage exists for the same reason fire zones do though. The idea is to prevent those easy 1v1 bombs into huge deep voids. The outside CBs and deep S will play it similarly to fire zone, but the seam defenders inside will park themselves on the seams and read the eyes of the QB. They almost freeze, don't overcommit anywhere, and react as best they can. It's the best they can do given the space they have to cover.
The issue is that it's extremely vulnerable in the intermediate middle. Because a lot of college QBs struggle to process here, as it's an unclear and shifting picture with all the bodies that populate the MOF, and effectively maximize this area, HOT has become very popular in the college game.
What about "HOT" pressures? https://t.co/oVK9ePVjCl pic.twitter.com/kZecfLBHV3
Joe Burrow is not a college QB. Essentially, hot coverages need the blitz to get someone to the QB and disrupt the play. If protection is good, it is not designed to hold up at all. The Bengals pass protection has been fantastic this year, especially relative to its exposure.
Post-wheel is a concept that is death to "HOT" coverages like this with the SEAM (eyes technique) defenders having so much space to account for. It's very hard to protect for long enough against 6 rushers for it to work so it's not normally exploited pic.twitter.com/sdUCXGb1Su
Because the CB can be run off taking the outside WR deep, the seam defender is sometimes asked to carry anything vertically from the slot.
The Bengals exploited this here by putting Chase at two on a post-wheel concept. This takes a minute to develop so it's not a common answer vs this coverage, but if you can protect it and give your QB the time, it's lethal. This is where Burrow becomes a force multiplier too. In addition to the protection command and pre-snap sense we discussed above, his ability to negotiate space and get up in the pocket consistently meets the OL halfway and, in this case, unlocked a filthy coverage beater with some high barriers to entry.
The Bengals are rolling out the Greatest show on Turf 2.0.
That said, Joe Burrow isn't any different than he was last year or especially in 2024. The only difference between this offense and year's past is that, as Bengals fans have been arguing on social media for years, the pass protection wasn't there. The one answer teams had in the past was to play MacDonald-ball.
They could rush four and still create havoc while shifting on the back end to make Burrow dig through his reads and find an answer without the time. He has the time now, and he's going to find it. Sending extra guys is only going to make the beatings worse.

title: Bengals' WR Ja'Marr Chase Says He and Tee Higgins Are Embracing Historic Pursuit
full_text:
The night the Cincinnati Bengals drafted Ja’Marr Chase back in 2021, the wide receiver said he was coming to break all of the team’s records.
He’s already crossed off several, and Chad Johnson’s career mark of 66 is within reach before the end of the season with Chase sitting on 60.
But Thursday afternoon, while wearing Joe Burrow’s orange No. 9 jersey after swapping news conference dates due to his quarterback being under the weather, Chase said he has his eyes on a specific NFL record.
And it’s one he would share with teammate Tee Higgins.
No team in NFL history has ever had two wide receivers top 1,500 yards in a season, but both Chase and Higgins are on pace to accomplish it.
Asked if that would be meaningful, Chase said “100 percent.”
And Chase made it clear he was already aware of the possibility before being asked about it in the news conference.
And he made sure Higgins was as well.
“I’m definitely speaking it into existence with me and Tee, just letting him know how close we are,” Chase said.
“Close” might not be the right word. They’re each barely halfway there. But the season is barely halfway old.
Chase currently has 878 yards, which are fourth most in the league. That puts him on pace for 1,658.
Higgins has 824, sixth most in the league. He’s on pace for 1,556, which would blow away his career high of 1,091, set during the Super Bowl season in 2021.
“I’m just trying to put it out there and let him know how great we’ve been going,” Chase added.
The closest any teammates have come to accomplishing the double 1,500 feat was in 1995 when the Detroit Lions, with Scott Mitchell at quarterback, had Herman Moore register 1,686 yards while Brett Perriman logged 1,488.
In 2000, the St. Louis Rams saw Torry Holt get 1,635 while Isaac Bruce posted 1,471 with Kurt Warner starting 11 games and Trent Green five.
The last time a team had two receivers finish in the top six of receiving yards was 2011, when Patriots wide receiver Wes Welker was second (1,569) and tight end Rob Gronkowski was sixth (1,327).
Chase’s 231 yards in Sunday night’s 38-18 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers marked the fourth 200-yard game of his career.
The NFL record is five, shared by Lance Alworth, Calvin Johnson, Don Hutson, Charley Hennigan and Jerry Rice.
Only Johnson and Rice did it in the Super Bowl era.
“I got a couple more years in me,” Chase said. “I ain’t rushing it.”
As for how close he is to Johnson’s franchise record, Chase shut down the conversation.
“I don’t wanna know that,” he said. “I don’t wanna hear that.”
“I just don’t want to think about it. I just want to ball out.”
Jay Morrison covers the Cincinnati Bengals for Bengals On SI. He has been writing about the NFL for nearly three decades. Combining a passion for stats and storytelling, Jay takes readers beyond the field for a unique look at the game and the people who play it. Prior to joining Bengals on SI, Jay covered the Cincinnati Bengals beat for The Athletic, the Dayton Daily News and Pro Football Network.

title: Browns Have an Under-the-Radar Contract Extension Candidate Emerging
full_text:
When the Cleveland Browns used a second-round pick back in 2025 on a linebacker from UCLA, it was hard to understand just how impactful that player could be in the Orange and Brown.
But just north of 25 games in his professional career, former Bruin Carson Schwesinger has been unstoppable.
He has recorded a whopping 258 tackles, 17 tackles for a loss, 5.5 sacks and 13 quarterback hits , all while playing an active role in defending the passing game with four pass deflections and two interceptions. He plays hard, fights through injuries and leads one of the league's best defenses game in and game out.
Carson's been an absolute demon out there 😈 pic.twitter.com/oT4IcVP3k8
Earlier in the year, it looked like Schwesinger was going to miss a game due to injury, but as always, he fought to play on Sunday. Head coach Todd Monken, who is in his first season with the team, recognized immediately that he's the type of player who will do anything he can to play.
"And Carson, what's interesting, early in the week the trainers were semi-optimistic," Monken said back in mid-October. "But they said, Well, it's Carson.' And every time I'd see Carson and I'd ask him, he'd get this silly smirk on his face like, 'Do you know who you're talking to?'"
Earning AP Defensive Rookie of the Year honors in 2025, Schwesinger looks on his way to potential All-Pro status, or even the Defensive Player of the Year award race , as the 2026 season approaches the back half.
#Browns Carson Schwesinger is the only LB currently in the NFL with -100+ tackles -3 sacks -3 Forced Fumbles Doesn’t matter where on the field you are. If you have the ball Carson will find you pic.twitter.com/kzGabdYeUI
While it is great to see a player succeeding at the level Schwesinger has, especially considering he wasn't even a Top 15 pick, let alone a first-rounder, his quick rise to stardom puts the Browns' front office in a peculiar situation.
Do you lock down the 23-year-old on a long-term deal as soon as he is willing to talk about it? Or wait till the final year of his deal to begin talks?
It feels like in today's era of the game, some players aren't rewarded as often as they should be, at least on the money side.
Someone like Schwesinger, who has such a vital role in the day-to-day operations of the Browns' defense, shouldn't fall into such a framework. Instead, the Browns should do everything they can to give him an extension this offseason, locking him down as the long-term staple of the unit.
Back in 2020 , the Browns showed that type of loyalty to defensive end Myles Garrett, who still had two years left on his rookie deal. They signed him to one of the sport's biggest deals, with the contract containing $100 million in total guarantees, the most ever paid to a defensive player.
While Schwesinger may or may not get that type of deal, one that breaks open the league's linebacker market, he should still be treated like a top player on the defensive side of the ball.
Oftentimes, deals like this will come for those at the quarterback position, such as Josh Allen, Joe Burrow, Patrick Mahomes and Justin Herbert, among others.
But that shouldn't hurt the 23-year-old's chances of getting paid the big bucks.
If the front office was willing to do it on Garrett, there is no reason not to have a similar stance with Schwesinger.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: 4 Browns Players Rank Top 10 in Highest-Graded Rookies This Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns exited the 2026 NFL Draft, and almost immediately, the praise started to come in.
Not only did the Browns' front office attack every offseason need the organization was facing, but it also seemingly grabbed the best player off the board at the same time. Not having to balance one or the other, but instead ending up in the right spot at the right time, gave the team arguably the best draft of anyone.
And through the first 10 games of the 2026 season, many of the players selected have shone brightly.
On Thursday, Nov. 19, the Pro Football Network announced its current highest-graded NFL offensive rookies this season, with four Browns first-years making the list.
Ranking third, offensive guard Austin Barber (77.5), who wasn't even a starter until injuries thrust him into the spotlight, took the top spot for the Browns. Following him at the No. 6 spot in the rankings, wideout Denzel Boston (75.0) was slotted in, with offensive tackle Spencer Fano (74.9) just a spot behind at No. 7. The final spot on the list, the No. 10 ranking, was given to wideout KC Concepcion (73.8).
📊 The highest-graded NFL offensive rookies this season, per PFN’s Impact metrics: 1. OG Vega Ioane, BAL (79.2) 2. RB Emmett Johnson, KC (77.6) 3. OG Austin Barber, CLE (77.5) 4. WR Caleb Douglas, MIA (76.4) 5. OT Kahlil Benson, KC (76.3) 6. WR Denzel Boston, CLE (75.0) 7. OT… pic.twitter.com/9dbDmZEumR
Such praise for Cleveland's rookies should come as no surprise, especially as both the stats and film show just how impactful they have been every game day.
Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson wouldn't have likely had the comeback season he has had so far without Boston and Concepcion.
The two have combined for a whopping 981 yards across 10 games, with Boston leading the way with 523 yards. Concepcion isn't too far behind, though, recording 458 yards.
Their two totals are ahead of every other wideout selected in the 2026 draft. The next closest to both Boston and Concepción is the Tennessee Titans' Carnell Tate with 413, while Caleb Douglas of the Miami Dolphins and Malachi Fields of the New York Giants sit below 400.
Rookie receiving leaders heading into Week 11: 1. Denzel Boston, Browns - 523 2. KC Concepcion, Browns - 458 3. Carnell Tate, Titans - 413 4. Caleb Douglas, Dolphins - 367 5. Malachi Fields, Giants - 350 Can one or both of the Browns rookies eclipse 1,000 yards in their rookie… pic.twitter.com/JdILfr26aX
Both Concepcion and Boston will likely be in the running for the Offensive Rookie of the Year award as the race heats up in the coming weeks. However, unless someone else really starts to stand out and puts together one of the best rookie stretches in recent memory, it seems like the two will just be competing against each other.
While Cleveland's flashy wideouts continue to steal the spotlight, the big men up front, Barber and Fano, continue to protect Watson so that he can find them down the field.
The two get a good bit of praise within Cleveland, but certainly deserve more on the national end.
Barber jumped headfirst into the starting spot at right guard with a back injury sustained by Teven Jenkins early in the year. He has impressed , even though he wasn't expected to have such a role in his first year with the team.
Fano, on the other hand, had high expectations after being drafted in the top 10. Fortunately, while he has had to go through plenty of growing pains after shifting positions, he has been consistent enough to maintain the starting spot and still be looked at as a long-term piece of Cleveland's future.
Heading out of the first 10 games of their careers, Barber ranks as the 28th best guard in the league out of 77 eligible, while Fano is a bit further ahead on the offensive tackle side, ranking 16th out of 72. Both rankings are according to Pro Football Focus.
Back in action in two weeks, the rookies will have a chance to catch their breath during the bye week, with hopes of putting together a strong push down the back half of the season. Sitting 6-4, the Browns have plenty of room to chase the No. 1 spot in the AFC North and make the playoffs.
The Browns next hit the field on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 8:20 p.m. EST against the Fernando Mendoza-led Las Vegas Raiders . The two sides will clash in Cleveland at Huntington Bank Field.

title: The Highest-Graded Rookie on the Browns May Not Be Who You Think
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have had rookies succeed everywhere on the field this season .
Denzel Boston may have saved their season by breaking tackles on his way to a touchdown in Tampa Bay. Todd Monken has schemed up plays for KC Concepcion to showcase his speed and playmaking ability. The offensive line has been anchored by Spencer Fano, and he has allowed them to operate smoothly late in games.
However, it seems that no rookie has been more impactful than Emmanuel McNeil-Warren.
The University of Toledo alum has been flying all over the field on defense this season. He has improved every game, highlighted by his play in the win against the Houston Texans. Pro Football Focus (PFF) ranked McNeil-Warren second in the entire 2026 rookie class.
Which rookies have caught your eye? pic.twitter.com/NVGvtDfEFh
He has 50 tackles so far this season, with 23 of those being solo tackles. He has made impactful plays at every level for the defense while playing safety.
In the Browns’ first matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, he met the big and strong DK Metcalf in the middle of the field with physicality right as the ball arrived to get an important incomplete pass. Against the Tennessee Titans, he snuffed out a fourth-and-goal play and made a tackle for a loss, causing a turnover on downs.
His best play was nullified by an iffy pass-interference call, but it should not be ignored. He was playing center field at safety, and there was a one-on-one matchup on the outside. McNeil-Warren reacted and closed the gap quickly. He made a diving interception that will rival any in the league this season.
His flashy plays are more than just surface-level. PFF is a sports analytics company that focuses on the NFL. They use advanced statistics to grade every player in the league, and McNeil-Warren has passed their test.
The emergence of McNeil-Warren can lift the ceiling of this defense for years to come. The Browns have staples at every level of the defense for the foreseeable future. Mason Graham will be the central focus on the interior of the line, and behind him is former Defensive Rookie of the Year, Carson Schwesinger. McNeil-Warren caps off the back end of the defense .
Free safety Ronnie Hickman is an unrestricted free agent at the end of the year. They extended Grant Delpit’s contract in the offseason, so they are set at the position.
For a rookie, McNeil-Warren exudes confidence and instincts. He has the speed, intelligence, and physicality to become one of the best safeties in the NFL.
McNeil-Warren was graded 86.7 by PFF. Fano was also in the top-ten list at number seven with a 75.5 grade. They have Boston at 69.4, followed by Concepcion at 67.2. The rookie class has been as good as advertised so far this season, but McNeil-Warren is in a class of his own .

title: Analyzing What Deshaun Watson's 2027 Offseason Contract Extension Could Look Like
full_text:
Anyone who followed the Cleveland Browns closely knew that the 2026 season was going to be an interesting one.
Not just because it felt like nearly everyone had counted the Browns out, even after they put together a strong offseason, but because the quarterback situation was a big talking point. Would the team go with second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders or turn the keys of the offense back over to controversial Deshaun Watson?
Well, not only did they give Watson a chance to be the starter in the season opener, but he has done his job well enough to lock down the job for the entire year.
And now, one major question has started to arise: will the Browns' front office extend him this offseason?
The 31-year-old is in the final year of a five-year, $230 million contract . With how he is playing right now, leading the Browns to a 6-3 record while under center and keeping up the hunt for a playoff spot, it seems likely that the front office would at least consider it.
Here is what the contractual situation could look like in just a few short months:
This past offseason, t here were actually quite a few quarterbacks who hit free agency and commanded quite a bit of attention. Funny enough, a couple were even tied back to the Browns.
But weeks came and went and the Browns stood still, opting to stick with the quarterback room they already had.
Now, though, the front office might actually be able to use some of the discussions they saw behind-the-scenes to work through Watson's upcoming contract situation.
The Browns were never really in the running for Pittsburgh Steelers veteran Aaron Rodgers, but being over 40 years old and still playing at a high level, he somewhat sets a line for what Watson's value could be at. He commanded a one-year, $22.5 million deal.
Following Rodgers, 27-year-old Malik Willis, who is still relatively unproven, grabbed a whopping $22.5 million a year deal across three seasons with the Miami Dolphins.
Being almost four years younger than Watson and entering what is expected to be his prime, the contract makes sense, especially with where the quarterback market is at right now.
The final two deals that align somewhat with where the Browns should be at with Watson are Kirk Cousins, who signed a one-year, $11.3 million deal with the Las Vegas Raiders, and Marcus Mariota, who signed a one-year, $7 million deal with the Washington Commanders.
Both of those contracts make sense for where they were at in their careers; however, Cousins has quickly re-emerged as one of the league's most consistent quarterbacks. He's a good example of taking a low-to-mid-level financial risk on an aging quarterback, something Cleveland could end up taking into account.
When looking at the current quarterback market and comparing some of the deals that were signed last offseason, it is quite likely that Watson ends up inking a two- to three-year deal worth anywhere from $15-22 million a season.
The $15 million mark puts him just ahead of Cousins, while the $22 million high point puts him on pace for Rodgers- or Willis-type money.
That would make his total value worth anywhere from just $30 million across two seasons, all the way up to $66 million across three seasons.
If he can continue playing at the high level he has been this season, that type of contract would be worthwhile for a young team still finding its groove in a loaded AFC North. The bigger storyline, though, is whether this season has been a fluke for Watson or not.
The Browns' front office could end up deciding to lean towards a short-term contract, just to protect themselves and the amount of money they already invested in the controversial quarterback, or if wins really do matter, they could give him another nice deal to stay in Cleveland.
Watson's future in The Land rides heavily on how he finishes the 2026 season.
The Browns return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 29, for a date with the 2026 No. 1 pick, Fernando Mendoza, and the Raiders . The two sides will clash at 8:20 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field.

title: Full Cleveland Browns 2027 Mock Draft: All Seven Rounds
full_text:
As the Browns sit at 6-4 in the playoff chase, draft discussions haven’t quite taken center stage in Northeast Ohio as we approach Thanksgiving.
But it’s never too early to start considering potential draft picks. With that in mind, let’s explore some names and ideas Cleveland might consider in the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft.
For this mock draft, we'll use the Week 11 draft order from Tankathon.com :
No. 18 (via Los Angeles Rams)- Arch Manning, QB, Texas
The Browns will be looking to draft their franchise quarterback in the first round after not being able to take one in the last two drafts. Cleveland might have to trade up to draft its quarterback. But for this exercise, we will not make any trades.
Cleveland has the benefit of having two first-round picks and will grab Manning here from the selection the Browns received in the Myles Garrett trade.
Manning may not declare for the draft, as he still has eligibility remaining. Many people believe he should return to school for another season. However, he has already been in college for four years and has been a full-time starter for the last two seasons.
Another season of college football might not be beneficial, and joining the NFL, even if it means sitting on the bench for a while, could provide him with a better opportunity to learn from an NFL coaching staff.
The Browns will be linked to Manning during the draft, as owner Jimmy Haslam knows Arch's uncle, Peyton, from his time as a quarterback at the University of Tennessee, where Haslam is a native and booster.
It doesn’t matter what head coach Todd Monken and general manager Andrew Berry want. If Haslam has his heart set on a Manning, he usually gets what he wants since he is the one writing the checks. Owners often draft quarterbacks in the first round, and Haslam is exactly the type who doesn’t stay out of the way too often and let the football people make the big-time decisions.
No. 20- Greg Johnson, Interior OL, Minnesota
The Browns had to rebuild their offensive line last offseason, bringing in five new starters. It looks like they have two rookies, left tackle Spencer Fano and right guard Austin Barber, who will be in Cleveland for a while. The Browns still need to add to the offensive line, and Johnson would be a nice fit. He can play both center and guard. Most likely, the Browns would use him at center.
Currently, starting center Elgton Jenkins is on a two-year, $24 million deal with a potential out after this season for $7.7 million in dead cap, according to Spotrac.
No. 53,- Matayo Uiagalelei, EDGE, Oregon
Since Cleveland doesn't select a pass rusher in the first round, it will choose one with its second-round pick. Uiagalelei was among a handful of Oregon players who returned to school instead of entering the 2026 NFL Draft.
In 10 games this season, Uiagalelei has recorded 10 tackles for loss, 9.5 sacks and 40 combined tackles.
No. 84- Melvin Siani, OT, Texas
The Browns will still be looking for a need at tackle, and Siani appears to fit their style. Siani is listed at 6-foot-6 and weighs 302 pounds. The 22-year-old tackle may not match the weight of current Browns tackle Dawand Jones, who came in at 6-foot-8 and 374 pounds at the 2023 combine. However, Siani possesses a large frame that could help him develop into a solid professional player.
No. 119 (via Seattle Seahawks)- Nate Frazier, RB, Georgia
No. 122- Owen Chambliss, LB, Nebraska
No. 123 (via New York Giants)- Lawson Luckie, TE, Georgia
The Browns focus on Georgia players in the fourth round, as Monken was the Bulldogs' offensive coordinator from 2020 to 2022 and helped them win two national championships. Monken still has connections inside the Georgia football program, and it is one of the best schools for producing tight ends and running backs.
Frazier could step in to help carry the running game alongside Quinshon Judkins, allowing Dylan Sampson to focus more on third-down work. Additionally, Luckie could help free up tight end Harold Fannin Jr. in the passing game. Fannin and Luckie could be used in multiple two-tight-end sets, creating mismatches for opposing defenses.
Cleveland has to get more depth at linebacker, and adding Chambliss, who has 55 tackles, five tackles for loss and a half-sack in eight games this season.
No. 148 (via Houston Texans)-Zeke Berry, CB, Michigan
No. 157- Jordan Faison WR, Notre Dam e
Cleveland uses its fifth-round pick to select two players from significant programs: Berry from Michigan and Faison from Notre Dame. The Browns don't necessarily need a starter at cornerback, with Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell already in place, but they do need depth.
Adding Berry could be a valuable addition. The same goes for wide receiver, as the Browns have Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion starting.
But Cleveland is likely to part ways with Jerry Jeudy this offseason, creating opportunities to add a few receivers, both in the draft and through free agency.
No. 230- (via Texans)- Peter Clarke, TE, Temple
No. 241- Knijeah Harris, Guard, Florida
The Browns add another tight end since they have a deep need at that position. And they add Harris as a depth piece on the offensive line.
Often, seventh-round picks don't make the 53-man roster, and since Cleveland won't have many roster spots to spare with all its draft picks and possible free-agent additions, both players might be camp bodies.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Five 2027 NFL Draft Targets for the Cleveland Browns to Watch
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are in the thick of the race for a postseason berth , so unlike a few recent seasons, upcoming draft chatter hasn’t really churned up this early in the season.
Nonetheless, it’s never too early to look at potential draft targets. That’s especially true for a team with two first-round picks in its pocket that has found ways to win despite so many obvious roster holes.
Here are five 2027 NFL Draft prospects that could land firmly on the Browns’ radar over the next few weeks:
If the Browns are looking at passers in Round 1, then all signs are starting to point towards forgetting about Drew Mestemaker, who looks like QB1 for the 2027 NFL Draft.
After that, things aren’t so clear. Notre Dame’s C.J. Carr has a chance to solidify himself as the second quarterback selected, but he lacks ideal size and arm strength, much like the two passers selected by Cleveland in the 2025 Draft, so the team might want to look at a different type of passer.
That brings us to LaNorris Sellers, who’s had an up-and-down season like most of next year’s prospects. Sellers is a bigger passer with a stronger arm, but he’s had to deal with accuracy questions in the past. He faces a monumental challenge this week against top-ranked Georgia.
Word on the street before the season began was that Jimmy Haslam was totally enamoured with Manning and wanted to have him as his franchise quarterback by the time the team moved into the new Brook Park Stadium sometime in 2029.
Good news for the Browns. Manning doesn’t look like the surefire No. 1 overall pick many were talking about before Texas’ season began, and there’ve even been rumors that he could stay for another college season, either with the Longhorns or by transferring to another program.
Manning might not be having the stellar season so many observers predicted this year, but he’s displayed great leadership and resiliency, regardless. Should he make the jump to the NFL Draft, he might even become available to the Browns after Round 1, if Haslam’s heart is truly set on a Manning.
Leaving quarterbacks aside, Cleveland should take a long, hard look at offensive tackles in Round 1, even after selecting Spencer Fano in the Top-10 and Austin Barber in the third back in April .
If Fano stays permanently on the left side, Lauck could come in on the right side and help stabilize a unit that has struggled throughout the season. Plus, the Browns could certainly use Lauck’s nasty demeanor in the run game. Along with Fano, Austin Barber, and potentially Parker Brailsford down the line, the Browns could put together a solid unit that could end up playing together for years.
If Cleveland wants to wait until the second round for some O-Line talent, Johnson could make sense as a versatile piece with experience playing multiple positions.
Whether it’s taking the center spot and kicking Elgton Jenkins out, or taking a guard spot, Johnson looks like a Day 1 starter on most offensive lines, including the Browns’.
Finding a young edge rusher in one of the top rounds seems like a must for Cleveland at this point. With South Carolina’s Dylan Stewart and Texas’ Colin Simmons likely out of range for the Browns, Traore looks like the next man up.
The Irish star has prototypical size for the position and a non-stop motor that will instantly win fans over when he reaches the pro ranks.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: How Todd Monken Played a Role in This Pivotal Stage of Deshaun Watson's Career
full_text:
Many Browns fans were not in favor of seeing Deshaun Watson ever start a game for Cleveland heading into the season.
But one man didn't care what the public thought.
Head coach Todd Monken entered the season ready to choose the best quarterback. That turned out to be Watson, who has guided the Browns to a 6-4 record, including 6-3 as a starter, despite missing the Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints.
It felt like Watson's career was over after he missed all of the 2025 season with a torn Achilles. However, Monken has found something in Watson, and the 31-year-old quarterback has given a lot of credit to his new head coach for helping him prepare during this stage of his career.
"I think the biggest thing is he took time to really get to know me," Watson said on Wednesday. He took time to understand the situation instead of just writing stories and taking what the media says about me, which they really don't know. I think just being able to sit down and talk and see the larger picture. He understood, of course; I'm not broken. I had a lot of personal things going on, and I had a lot of injuries going on in my career.
"And I think anyone who had to deal with what I had to deal with will have ups and downs too; that's part of life. You learn from it. You grow from it. He believed in me, so it's always good to have a coach and a friend, a person in the building that can sit there and talk to you and make sure that you're straight mentally."
During camp and the preseason it didn’t look good for Deshaun Watson, but he credits head coach Todd Monken’s people skills for helping him get on track #Browns pic.twitter.com/CBnBR1E02o
Watson has had his fair share of injuries ever since he came to Cleveland in 2022. He underwent surgery for a displaced fracture of the glenoid of his right shoulder in November 2023. Then, in the middle of the 2024 season, he tore his Achilles and re-tore it again in the winter of 2025.
Perhaps Watson just needed time to get back into the swing of football, and with Monken's belief in him, he helped Watson get back on track.
Watson hasn't put up great stats this season, throwing for 2,118 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions in nine games.
But what has he done? Win six games, all coming on game-winning drives.
The Browns and Watson may not have many more games together, as Cleveland may not re-sign him after the season. However, Monken might have helped Watson keep his career going a bit longer than expected if another team signs him.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Former Browns Preseason Star Luke Floriea Drafted by Columbus UFL Team
full_text:
Luke Floriea shined for the Cleveland Browns this past preseason. The Mentor High School and Kent State product was a feel-good story, but ultimately didn't make the final roster or even the practice squad .
Yet he did make a name for himself, and the former undrafted NFL free agent just got drafted, albeit by a different professional football league. The good news for him is that he will once again suit up and play football in his home state of Ohio.
The United Football League draft began Wednesday with former Vanderbilt star Diego Pavia going No. 1 overall to the Columbus Aviators. He will now have Floriea as a top target after the former Browns receiver was taken by the Aviators in the ninth round at pick. No. 65 overall.
Luke Floriea has been selected with our 9th round pick ✈️ pic.twitter.com/gnzwH7F9wz
The Aviators began play as a new UFL franchise in 2026 with Ted Ginn Jr. as the head coach. The team finished 3-7 and just made a big splash by taking Pavia with the No. 1 overall pick. That should certainly get some eyes on the team when the UFL season begins in March.
This is also a great opportunity for Floriea to put great play on tape and potentially parlay that into a full-time NFL opportunity. He did have a tryout with the Seattle Seahawks after getting cut by the Browns, but he did not show enough to earn a spot.
Floriea seemed to be right on the cusp of making the Browns roster before the season. The final receiver spot was ultimately won by Tylan Wallace, who had already spent time with Todd Monken in Baltimore.
The local receiver's breakout performance came in the final preseason game when he caught two touchdown passes from Dillon Gabriel. It was a dream come true for the Mentor native, just not enough to convince the front office to roster him.
Playing with Pavia as his quarterback should mean Floriea has a chance to shine in the national spotlight when the UFL season begins in a few months. The outspoken quarterback was the Heisman runner-up in 2025 and spent the summer with the Baltimore Ravens. He, too, will try to show off his abilities and aim to get back into the NFL.
That path is possible and was proven by current Browns kicker Andre Szmyt , who spent the 2024 season with the St. Louis Battlehawks.
Steve is a lifelong Cleveland sports fan who proudly wears his Guardians, Browns, and Cavs gear in his current home of Santa Barbara. He has covered Cleveland sports online for the past decade and is still waiting for the Browns to draft a QB who signs a second contract in town.

title: How the Browns Can Flip the Script and Run the Ball for a Playoff Push
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ bye week comes at the perfect time for a playoff push. They are 6-4 and are in the last wild-card position. The other AFC teams behind them have issues at quarterback, with more difficult schedules remaining.
The Browns will need to use the bye week to improve a major area of their offense.
The rushing offense ranks 24th in the NFL with 97.5 yards per game. That number plummets to just 63.6 yards per game from all running backs. Deshaun Watson is second on the team in rushing with 266 yards, which includes broken plays that result in him improvising a run.
There is not just one problem with the run game, as both the line and running backs have been ineffective between the tackles.
In their win against the Houston Texans, the Browns used more read options. When Watson handed the ball off to Quinshon Judkins in the shotgun position, he would read the defensive end. When the ultra-aggressive defensive end crashed down the line to meet the running back, Watson would pull the ball back from the handoff and run through the exposed end of the line.
This play led to the Browns first touchdown on their way to come back from 17-0. Todd Monken called that play throughout the first half, and it continually worked as Watson led the team in rushing yards and averaged 6.1 yards per rush.
However, in the second half, the Texans adjusted. When Watson would hand the ball off to Judkins, the defensive end made his way to the quarterback no matter who had the ball. The interior offensive line was not effective enough to move their own defenders, so the defensive line did not need the defensive end. Monken and the offense can use the bye week to put in a wrinkle or two in the read option to get the ground game going.
Watson can be called a design run in the shotgun position. He can appear to do a read option by the elongated handoff, and the opposite-side guard can pull to block the defensive end going after Watson. This would open up the end, similar to the defensive crashing down, leaving his side open.
This could work against the Las Vegas Raiders, as Maxx Crosby is focused on getting to the quarterback. He could think that he has a free pass to Watson, but then the pulling guard would pick him up, and Watson would have an open field.
Monken can also mix old school with new school. He can align both Judkins and Dylan Sampson in the backfield alongside Watson. The read option would go to Judkins, but if Watson takes the ball back due to reading the defensive end, then he and Sampson would run the option. This would work if the defensive end stays home and Watson could pitch the ball to Sampson after occupying the defender.
Watson opened up the field against the Texans by airing the ball out deep. He has been more of a check-down quarterback at the beginning of the season. He heads into the bye with three straight 300-yard games. Defenses will have to start respecting the pass, which could help the run game by reducing the number of run stoppers on the field. The Browns scored the game-winning touchdown on the ground as it looked like the defense was playing the pass.
The Browns should use their bye week to focus on getting more production on the ground, which they will need as the weather gets colder. Monken has shown that he will keep trying new ways to get that production, and he now has two weeks to figure it out.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: 2 Browns Players Who Need To Be Better Coming Out of Bye Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are heading into their bye week with a 6-4 overall record.
Over the past few weeks, the talk of the town is whether or not the Browns can win the division, along with making the playoffs.
If Cleveland wants the chance to do either, here are two guys who need to step up their play after the week off.
Jared Verse Was Really Talking To The Texans Offensive Lineman Who Just Jumped Offsides. Letting Him Hear It After The Flag. By The Way, He Hasn't Sniffed A Quarterback Yet This Year. pic.twitter.com/qkQRW8unJO
This one pretty much goes without saying.
So far this season, Jared Verse has yet to record a sack. On top of that lack of production, the 2024 defensive rookie of the year has a combined total of 20 tackles.
For reference, Verse had a total of 58 tackles and 7.5 sacks a year ago.
Obviously, when you get traded for the best player in football along with multiple high draft picks, the expectation will be higher. However, having zero sacks and really being outplayed by backups is unacceptable.
Some may blame it on the schemes or defensive formations, but at a certain point, you have to go out and perform no matter what cards you're dealt. Especially if you are going to trash-talk at any given moment.
While Tytus Howard is coming off of his best game with the Browns, he needs to perform at that level in every game from here on out.
This past offseason, the Browns went out and traded for Howard before signing him to a new three-year deal. In return, they have gotten a mid-tier starting tackle. According to PFF, Howard ranks 42nd out of all 72 tackles in the league.
While we are on the topic of statistics, Howard has done a good job in the pass-blocking game as he ranks 16th in that category.
On the other hand, Howard has been one of the reasons why the run game hasn't been working this year, as he ranks near the bottom of the league at 52nd in run blocking.
To sum it all up, the Browns need to see more from the guys they traded for this offseason.
If Verse can produce on the field half as much as he talks about it, he will be a great player for this Browns defense. As for Howard, if he can work on blocking for the run game, the Browns offense can gain another dimension and become even more consistent.
There's still work to be done, but this is the bye week after all.
After the time off, these guys will have the biggest stage in football to prove it.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Unreal Stat Shows Cowboys Fleeced Steelers in Joey Porter Jr. Trade
full_text:
Several things have gone wrong for the Dallas Cowboys this season as they enter Week 11 with a record of 4-6. They spent the entire offseason rebuilding their defense to fit new defensive coordinator Christian Parker's scheme, but have not found any success.
That's led to a big change this week as the Cowboys took play-calling duties away from Parker and will give senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine the job. There's hope in Big D that this will provide a spark for their struggling defense.
While we don't know how much the move to Pettine will help, there's one true certainty when it comes to the Dallas defense, and that would be that Joey Porter Jr. is going to lock down whoever he matches up against.
Porter, who was traded following their Week 3 loss to the Baltimore Ravens, has been an absolute stud since arriving in Dallas. According to Next Gen Stats, he has allowed the fewest yards per target in coverage, and it's not close. Porter is giving up just 1.5 yards per target, which is 1.6 yards better than Emmanuel Forbes, who is second in the league.
Fewest yards per target allowed in coverage this season, per @NextGenStats : 1. Joey Porter Jr. – 1.5 2. Emmanuel Forbes – 3.1 3. Trent McDuffie – 3.5 4. Isaiah Rodgers – 3.6 5. Denzel Ward – 3.8 > Minimum 100 coverage snaps
Dallas sent a conditional 2027 sixth-round pick as well as a 2028 second-round pick to Pittsburgh in exchange for Porter, and with these numbers, it's clear that they won the trade.
While giving up a second-round pick is a steep price, it's hard to see the Cowboys adding anyone with their 2028 second-round selection who can impact the game the way Porter can. Of course, the key will be agreeing to a new contract with Porter, who is scheduled for free agency in 2027.
We should also be fair to the Steelers. They didn't trade Porter because they felt he wasn't good enough. They also didn't likely think they could easily replace him with a future second-round pick. Instead, they moved on because Porter forced their hands. He wanted a new deal and was not playing, citing a back problem.
Since arriving in Dallas, he hasn't had the same issue , although he has missed multiple games due to a foot and ankle injury . When he has been on the field, however, he has been their best defender and one of the league's true shutdown cornerbacks. That's why it would make plenty of sense for the Cowboys to lock him up in 2027 and beyond.

title: Jerry Jones Comments On Dallas Cowboys Fan's Death After AT&T Stadium Fight
full_text:
Days after last weekend's loss to the San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium , a Dallas Cowboys fan passed away. The fan reportedly died from injuries suffered in a fight at the game , where his family claims he was pushed down a flight of stairs.
The fan, 36-year-old Mario Narro, stayed to watch the game after the alleged altercation before complaining of pain, and his condition worsened as the game went on. After he lifted his shirt to show his friends the injuries to his abdomen, they alerted medical personnel in the stadium , and he was transported to the hospital.
Sadly, Narro passed away days later. Police are investigating his death, and Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was recently asked about the incident.
During his appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Jones said he was unaware of any incident until right before his appearance and said the stadium has plenty of cameras that he is willing to turn over to investigators.
“I just got that information, and so we had no record of an incident , and we’ll be obviously looking into that,” Jones said. “My understanding is that the individual went to the game and didn’t feel good at the game, and then left, and [had] been hospitalized. But we weren’t aware of any incident that involved a fan at the game.”
“We really do have quite a — eons above what it was 10, 15 years ago. We have quite a surveillance of what’s going on at every aspect of our game. And so it is really rare if we didn’t know of any incident. We’ve got too many people out there. We have 6,000 workers on game day.”
The incident could create a situation for Jones as well, with a full investigation creating potential liability issues for the venue. As Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk writes, authorities can "use the subpoena power to go get anything and everything that will allow the complicated puzzle to be put together as to what happened to Marco Narro, whether it could have or should been prevented, and whether the aftermath could have or should have been handled differently."
Our deepest condolences go out to Narro's family and friends during this incredibly difficult and tragic time.

title: Dallas Cowboys' Biggest Unanswered Question For Second Half of Season Is Obvious Issue
full_text:
Believe it or not, the Dallas Cowboys are very much alive in the NFL Playoff race , thanks to the wide-open NFC East opening the door for the team to win the division. But if Dallas is going to sneak into the postseason, the defense needs to step up.
That's exactly why the Cowboys pulled the plug on the Christian Parker experiment and stripped the defensive coordinator of play-calling duties. Now, it's up to veteran NFL coach Mike Pettine to save the day .
Ahead of Sunday's Week 11 showdown against the Tennessee Titans , Brad Gagnon of Bleacher Report shared his thoughts on every team's biggest question entering the second half of the season , and of course, for Dallas it is defense.
Dallas has the league's worst overall defense, allowing nearly 400 yards per game (393.8) and allowing 33 touchdowns. Is there actually any hope for the defense entering a crucial stretch? That's what we're all holding our breath to find out.
"A unit that ranks 31st in EPA allowed per play, 30th in points allowed per game and 32nd in total defense must turn it around soon, or the Cowboys will be done by January no matter how productive the offense continues to be," Gagnon wrote. "Is it possible?
"They aren't trending in the right direction following an embarrassing performance against San Francisco, but they have a soft homestand the next two weeks before road games against the Seahawks and Rams on either side of their Week 14 bye."
Dallas is throwing a Hail Mary by hoping that Pettine can save the day, but is that actually possible? The team is heading in the wrong direction, but the good news is that the team's next two games before the bye week are very winnable.
Sure, Dallas lost at home on a short week to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers earlier in the year, but right now, the pressure is on and Dallas can't afford to lose to the Titans or Eagles over the next week. The season is on the line, so we'll really learn what this team is made of.
Kickoff between the Cowboys and Titans on Sunday afternoon is set for 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX, so let's see if the Cowboys are up for the task.

title: Mike Pettine Discusses Uncertain Cowboys Future, Assigns Blame for Defense's Woes
full_text:
When senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine calls the plays for the Dallas Cowboys in Week 11 against the Tennessee Titans, he will become the team's sixth defensive play-caller since 2020.
Pettine is taking over for defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who was stripped of his play-calling duties this week after what has been a putrid season for the Cowboys' defense.
While Pettine will be in the role the rest of this season, it remains to be seen if he'll stay with the team and become Dallas' official defensive coordinator in 2027.
“I haven’t even thought that far yet," head coach Brian Schottenheimer said when asked about the topic.
When asked on Friday about what the future holds for him in Dallas in terms of possibly becoming the defensive coordinator after this season, Pettine expressed how much he loves football and coaching but wouldn't commit to anything.
“I’ll have to check with my wife on that one. We’re just going to take it week to week and see what plays out," Pettine stated, according to Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com .
"But I love this. This is what I’ve done for a long time, and when you’re back immersed in it – it’s been a passion for a long time. Now that I’m back in it, like I said, I’m full speed ahead.”
Pettine admitted that taking over play-calling duties was never in the plans when he was hired in October.
“It certainly wasn’t the intention,” he said, per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “There was no seed of this planted at any point. As we know in this business, we’re week-to-week, and sometimes circumstances happen. Things build up and changes have to be made."
The overwhelming belief is that while Parker is certainly to blame for a lot of the defensive woes the Cowboys have experienced in 2026, he isn't the only culprit.
The pathetic showing from the defense is on the players, also, and Pettine echoed that. He also noted the changes on defense will be "subtle" but "nothing major."
“There will be subtle changes, but nothing major,” he said. "The guys knew that it was a shared responsibility, myself, the rest of the staff, the players... It’s on all of us.”
We would also assign blame on Jerry Jones and Schottenheimer , who hired a first-time play-caller knowing there could be growing pains that the Cowboys would not be willing to have the patience to see through given the increased sense of urgency in 2026.
As is the case for Parker, this is a tough spot for Pettine to be in, and for several reasons, the first of which has to do with him having the daunting task of trying to fix a broken defense .
The veteran coach is not only taking over play-calling duties from a fellow coach who has worked under him in the past, Pettine is also being asked about taking the job title Parker still holds.
It's hard to envision Pettine being around beyond this season, though.
For starters, we're not even sure Schottenheimer is going to be around.
We all know he shouldn't be , but never say never when it comes to Jones, who could opt to keep Schotty against all logic. But if Jerry does what he should, Schottenheimer will be gone and so will Dallas' staff, Pettine included.
But let's say for a second that Schottenheimer stays and Pettine does enough to warrant Dallas keeping him, Pettine is 60 years old and was just enjoying retirement before the Cowboys pried him off the couch.
If Mrs. Pettine has anything to say about it, the newest Cowboys play-caller may not be back in 2027, no matter what.

title: 6 Dallas Cowboys Earning Contract Extensions for 2027 & Beyond
full_text:
There is no doubt that the Dallas Cowboys have been incredibly disappointing through the first 10 games of the 2026 season.
But while that's the case with the team as a whole, there are a slew of players who are having strong individual seasons, and some of them are either slated to be free agents in 2027 or will enter a contract year next season.
Here's a look at six players who fall into either one of those categories and have played well enough to earn a contract extension from the Cowboys next year.
Pickens' numbers are down from last season but that was to be expected with CeeDee Lamb healthy and playing every game.
Even still, Pickens is on pace to break 1,000 yards again and hasn't reverted to the problem child he used to be with the Pittsburgh Steelers, which no doubt helps his stock further.
But just because Pickens is playing well enough to earn a contract extension doesn't mean the Cowboys are going to give it to him.
In fact, the Cowboys shouldn't because Dallas should be focusing its resources elsewhere (like on the defense, for example) instead of paying big money to two wideouts.
Bass has been thrust into a starting role in four games this season due to the injury to Tyler Smith , and he is set to start multiple more games now that Tyler Booker is injured .
According to Pro Football Focus , Bass' 73.5 run-blocking grade ranks 18th among guards, and he has yet to give up a sack while permitting just 13 pressures.
The Cowboys are going to have a tough time keeping Bass since they can't offer him a starting role and some teams out there will almost certainly be willing to do so. But if they can find a way to keep him around, they should.
Durant missed four games earlier in the season due to a hamstring injury, but when he has been on the field over six games, the veteran has been solid.
Durant is giving up a completion rate of 55.6% and a passer rating of 73.4 when targeted in coverage this season.
The Cowboys have an out in DaRon Bland's contract in 2027 with a post-June 1 release and they should absolutely take it. From there, the Cowboys can re-sign Durant to take Bland's spot.
Acquired in a trade with the Steelers during the season, Porter has lived up to the hype over five games. The only blemish has been an ankle injury that has limited him.
The veteran cornerback has been lights out in coverage, giving up a completion rate of just 25% and a passer rating of 39.6. His 74.6 coverage grade ranks 13th among qualified cornerbacks.
The franchise tag is a possibility for Porter, but we suspect Dallas will ultimately get a lucrative long-term deal done with him.
Signed to a one-year deal in free agency, Ogbonnia has no doubt exceeded expectations and is the team's best nose tackle.
Ogbonnia has a respectable PFF grade of 63.8 in run defense and ranks top 10 at his position in run stops (eighth) and solo tackles (eighth).
For $2.75 million, Ogbonnia has been a total bargain. If Dallas can keep him for close to that price, it's a no-brainer.
Cooper hasn't just been a good center in 2026, he has been one of the best in the NFL.
PFF has Beebe with grades of 73.4 overall, 69.3 in run-blocking and 75.6 in pass-blocking, which rank sixth, 11th and fourth among centers. Beebee has yet to allow a sack and has surrendered just 12 pressures in 461 pass-block snaps.
Beebe still has one more year left on his deal after 2026, but the Cowboys would be wise to lock him up sooner rather than later before he becomes more expensive.

title: Cowboys Legend Michael Irvin Rips D For Being Worse Than Expected, Calls Out Offense
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have been making headlines throughout the week after stripping Christian Parker of his defensive play-calling duties and turning them over to veteran NFL coach Mike Pettine.
While the move essentially makes Christian Parker a lame-duck defensive coordinator and uses the first-time DC as a scapegoat for the team's struggles , everyone knows that a change had to be made. Not only was the defense brutal throughout the first 10 weeks of the season, but they were even worse than imagined.
Everyone expected some type of improvement from the unit after revamping the roster in the offseason and hiring Parker. Sure, injuries have held the unit back, but nothing has worked out.
Cowboys legend Michael Irvin is the latest to sound off on Dallas' struggles, appeari ng on The Pat McAfee Show to share his disbelief at just how bad things have gotten.
"I can't believe that a defense in the NFL can play as bad as the Dallas Cowboys.. I was expecting them to have problems on defense this season but not like this" ~ @michaelirvin88 #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/8KTfROCPkw
"You know, that's part of this whole craziness. The division is still sitting right there, even though you've gone through all of these changes and all of these situations on that defense. Oh, my God, man. I just cannot believe that a defense in the National Football League can really play as bad as the Dallas Cowboys defense has played some this year," Irvin said.
"But on the other end of that, you know what else I say? I can't believe. The Dallas Cowboys offense can go and put up 40 points on the third-ranked defense, and then on some defenses, I can't even find them. Why can't we find consistency at least on that side of the ball? Because I came into the league season saying, okay, you're going to give me 30 every game. Then I can work a defense sooner or later. I knew I was expecting to have problems on defense, but I wanted 30 a game from that offense, and that vacillates up and down."
It's refreshing to see that Irvin is taking a more nuanced approach to the Cowboys' struggles. Yes, the defense is terrible, but the Cowboys' offense has been getting away with its inconsistency without being called out.
Until now, people were hesitant to call out the offense because of how bad the defense has been, but on the games that the defense did step up, the offense hasn't always delivered. If the team can put together a balanced effort, there is no reason they can't make a postseason run in the wide open NFC East.
It all starts during the final stretch of November, where the team welcomes the 1-8 Tennessee Titans and 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. If that doesn't get Dallas back on track, then nothing will.

title: Cowboys' Dak Prescott Hit With Ridiculous Criticism From LeSean McCoy
full_text:
Former NFL running back LeSean McCoy has been the king of bad takes when it comes to the Dallas Cowboys. For whatever reason, he seems to have a vendetta against Dak Prescott, something that was on full display when he said Prescott needed to get a realtor because Joe Milton was going to take his job.
For those who are unaware, Milton lasted just one season as Prescott's backup and is now with the Philadelphia Eagles . Despite being wrong with that take , McCoy refuses to stop bashing Prescott.
While appearing on Up & Adams with Kay Adams, McCoy was asked about the recent discussion about Prescott being the most "betrayed" quarterback in the NFL. This topic gained steam when The Athletic's Mike Sando pointed out how well Dak is playing compared to how poorly the defense is playing.
Adams asked McCoy for his take on this and he seemed to lose his mind. McCoy was visibly annoyed by the thought of Prescott not getting enough credit, instead saying that Prescott gets a million excuses.
"Dak Prescott will have, he gets a million excuses, right? And if I die, I hope to come back like him. Like, I just, he's like a cat got nine lives. We're going to find a way to make sure that Dak doesn't get blamed for anything," McCoy said.
"There was a point in time where the window was open and he didn't deliver when they needed him to" LeSean McCoy isn't giving Dak Prescott a pass on this season because of the defense @heykayadams | @CutonDime25 pic.twitter.com/srwhY0dgQ6
Adams then pointed to the Week 10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers , saying Prescott played well. McCoy attributed that to the defense playing soft coverage with a huge lead before reminding everyone that Prescott and the Cowboys lost to the 49ers in the playoffs in 2022 and 2023.
"But I'll say this, this is how football works. You say that now, right? But I remember two years back-to-back years where they played the Niners in the playoffs, and the defense was excellent. Everything was excellent. And the only guy that wasn't excellent was Dak," Mccoy Said. "
So how football works when it's time to strike, because the window goes up and down. And right now it's closed. It's like completely closed, right? No robber can get in the house. But there was a point in time where the window was open, and he didn't deliver when they needed him to. But we never talk about that."
McCoy also ripped Prescott for their last playoff appearance when he had multiple turnovers against the Green Bay Packers leading to a blowout loss before saying "we don't talk about them things."
McCoy has to be living under a rock if he thinks Prescott didn't get criticized for those performances. Following those losses, every talk show was ripping Prescott for the losses. The criticism grew loud again when Prescott signed his extension ahead of the 2024 season.
So while he's right that Prescott dropped the ball big time during that time, that's not the talking point. The discussion now is centered on how well Prescott is playing in 2026. And in all honesty, he's been a solid quarterback who is leading a high-powered offense. Is he perfect? Absolutely not, but no NFL quarterback is.
That said, he's playing well enough to win, but the defense is letting him and the rest of the offense down. That's not an excuse, but a fact. Just like it's a fact that Prescott received a ton of justified criticism for the failures that McCoy says were ignored.

title: Dallas Cowboys Injury Report: Jaishawn Barham Shock Addition, 5 Out For Week 11
full_text:
We are getting closer to game day for the Dallas Cowboys, with the Tennessee Titans set to visit AT&T Stadium for a Week 11 showdown on Sunday afternoon.
On Friday, the team dropped its final injury report of the week after wrapping up practice, and there was a major surprise. Standout rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham , who had been practicing all week, is suddenly listed as questionable.
Barham popped up on the injury report with a hip/groin history and sat out of Friday afternoon's practice. On the positive side, pass rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku is officially back after battling an ankle issue all week.
A total of five players were ruled out, while Barham and three others are listed as questionable. A full look at the Cowboys' Week 11 injury report can be seen below.
Hopefully Barham will be good to go in time for Sunday afternoon's kickoff, along with starting safety Jalen Thompson, who has not played in a game since Week 3. Even if Thompson returns to the field, he will likely be limited, but his return will still be a positive influence for the struggling Cowboys' defense.
It would also help the Cowboys if Schoonmaker could recover from the illness that has knocked him out of practice the past two days, especially with starting Pro Bowl tight end Jake Ferguson already officially being ruled out.
Kickoff between the Cowboys and Colts is set for 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX, with Adam Amin and Drew Brees in the booth, while Kristina Pink will provide updates from the sideline throughout the afternoon.
Sunday's game can make or break the season for the Cowboys, who will then have a quick turnaround to host the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. With a mini winning streak to end the month, the Cowboys may be able to find a way to salvage their season.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Offers No Certainty For Mike Pettine's Future With Cowboys
full_text:
Since 2020, the Dallas Cowboys have seen a ridiculous amount of turnover at the defensive coordinator spot.
In that span, the Cowboys have seen six different coaches take on play-caller duties, with Christian Parker being No. 5 and senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine being No. 6 after Parker was stripped of play-calling duties this week.
Now, the Cowboys will hope Pettine can offer some much-needed stability and get the defense on track, but his tenure might only last the rest of the season.
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer was a guest on 105.3 The Fan on Friday and was asked if Pettine would be open to taking on the defensive coordinator role after this season.
Schottenheimer made it clear he hasn't even thought about that yet, which leaves Pettine's future uncertain.
“I haven’t even thought that far yet," Schottenheimer said .
Truth be told, Schottenheimer shouldn't be thinking about that right now. After all, he isn't even guaranteed to be kept after this season.
One thing we wondered is if the Cowboys would have moved off of Parker if Pettine wasn't in the building.
Well, Schottenheimer confirmed that with or without Pettine, the Cowboys would have made a change anyway .
“Yeah, I think at the end of the day, the results are the results," he said. "At the end of the day, I felt the change in perspective was important.”
There are multiple reasons why we expect Pettine won't be here for longer than the rest of this season, with the first being he's unlikely to turn things around with the same cast of characters.
While coaching has been an issue, the players are definitely not blameless in the defense's struggles, so expecting drastically different results with Pettine is expecting too much.
Another reason comes from our belief that this entire coaching staff isn't going to be around next season, barring a miracle.
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer has done an abysmal job in the role since last season and he has done nothing to warrant a third try, so he should be fired once 2026 ends .
Even if Schottenheimer stays on for another season, and even if Pettine does a great job and is offered the role, he may opt to go back into retirement.
That's where Pettine was before he was offered the job , and he even turned the Cowboys down initially because he was retired. Pettine said he decided to take the job in Dallas because he wanted to help out his former assistant.
Any way you slice it, Dallas will probably be on its seventh defensive play-caller since 2020 when next year rolls around.

title: Mike Pettine Is Cowboys' Savior & Will Lead Team To NFC East Crown, Skip Bayless Predicts
full_text:
We are days away from finding out just how much of an impact Mike Pettine will make on the Dallas Cowboys' defense . The veteran NFL coach is set to take over play-calling duties on Sunday afternoon against the Tennessee Titans at AT&T Stadium , after the team decided to pull the plug on the Christian Parker experiment .
The Cowboys are insisting that Parker is not a lame-duck defensive coordinator because he is still leading team meetings and helping with the game plan, but this is Pettine's show now.
When discussing Dallas' recent change, a predictable debate broke out between notorious Cowboys hater Stephen A. Smith and Skip Bayless on ESPN's First Take , with Skip claiming Pettine will save the day in Dallas with his influence.
Bayless did not only say that he believes Pettine will be a game-changer for the Cowboys, but that he could help lead them to the NFC East crown.
"[The Dallas Cowboys] are about to take off and win this bad division." @RealSkipBayless believes moving Mike Pettine to playcaller is the answer for Dallas 🙌 pic.twitter.com/GW4Vxt9nVT
"You are about to have to eat a heaping helping of chicken fried crow, courtesy of Jerry Jones. Jerry Jones just finally made a painfully obvious move that is going to jump-start this Cowboys season," Bayless said. "We are about to take off and win this bad division, this 'NFC Least.' Jerry tried to sell us Christian Parker as a savior and a savant of our defense, and it was clear from the start, from game one at the Giants, that Christian Parker was in over his 34-year-old head. He was overmatched. He was, frankly, overrated.
"Mike Pettine, Jerry went out and got him to oversee all the way back on October 12 because Jerry knew it wasn't working. We had just lost at home to winless Tampa Bay on Thursday Night Football, and an undrafted rookie quarterback. And Jerry finally said, 'That's enough.' And he's elevated Mike Pettine, a real defensive coordinator, to take this team over."
While the first part of Bayless' comments were a little over the top, which is his shtick, he did make some realistic points and speak common sense in the second-half of his rant, pointing out how the Cowboys can actually put themselves in position to win the division.
"We have two very winnable home games this Sunday, then right around the corner on Thanksgiving. We will get in rhythm with Mike Patton's defense in those two games," Bayless added.
"Then we get 11 days off for a Monday night game at Seattle. Then we get two weeks off for a game out here in L.A. against the Rams that I think we will win or at least steal. And we finish with the Giants at home and at the Commanders, and we will win those two games. And at 9-8, we will win the NFC East."
If the Cowboys can't put two wins together at home against the 1-8 Titans and the 2-7 Eagles, they don't deserve to be taken serious for the rest of the year. So over the next week, the Cowboys' season will be on the line.
We'll have to see if the Pettine effect helps the defense and if the team can string together some wins to make Bayless' prediction even more realistic.

title: Bo Nix Unleashed: 5 Bold Predictions for Broncos vs. Raiders
full_text:
In their last 12 meetings with the Las Vegas Raiders, the Denver Broncos are 4-8, with all four wins coming in their last four games.
Of the 12 games, six have been one-score games: two went Denver's way, while four went the Raiders' way. Some might think that Sunday's latest Broncos-Raiders matchup is destined to follow the one-score suit.
But if my bold predictions come true, it's going to be an explosive Broncos victory, and far from the one-score variety.
First, remember that Nix has never lost to the Raiders.
Ever since the mini-bye after beating the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6, Nix has taken steps forward. Since coming into the NFL, he's also made a jump coming out of the traditional bye, and this bold prediction encapsulates that.
The Raiders' defense isn't great , and the Broncos have put in the work to solve their problems on offense. Sean Payton knows how to attack the Raiders, and Nix goes off in a big way.
During the bye, Payton sent a message that the blocking wasn't good enough against the Carolina Panthers and that jobs could be on the line. The Broncos have had issues with run blocking for weeks.
The O-line and tight ends heard Payton loud and clear, and the blocking opens up a rushing touchdown of 40-plus yards by a Broncos running back. On top of that, this game ends up being one of the Broncos' better blocking games of the season.
The Raiders decided to march their rookie franchise quarterback out against the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos in his first two career stars. Much like against Seattle, i it doesn't go well in Denver.
Fernando Mendoza showed a lot of issues in his first start last week, and the Broncos have the pieces to exploit them and the Raiders' offensive inefficiencies. Due to the Raiders' lackluster offensive line, Denver turns up the pressure on Mendoza, leading to a rough day for the No. 1 overall pick in the draft.
Broncos pick up six sacks, a strip-sack, two interceptions, and a defensive touchdown.
I told you it was going to be a long day for the rookie. Denver puts Mendoza on the ground a lot and capitalizes on the pressure by forcing three takeaways and returning one of them for a touchdown.
The Broncos' defense should dominate in the trenches, leading to a massive game and a big divisional win.
All four of my previous bold predictions lead to this one. Nix goes off; the blocking not only improves, but it actually does a great job, and the defense dominates as the Broncos win by a wide margin.
Coming off the bye, Payton-coached teams come out swinging. The Broncos have to be aware of the disrespect they're getting from the media as a 7-2 team and will be looking to send a clear message.
