title: Marvin Mims Jr. Makes Revealing Admission About Broncos Extension Talks
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' bye came and went without them extending a player, as they'd done at the bye in each of the previous two seasons.
The NFL trade deadline landing in the middle of the Broncos' bye this year may have had a little something to do with that, especially given the Daiyan Henley trade that fell through with the Los Angeles Chargers and the fallout that followed .
As the Broncos began preparing to host the Las Vegas Raiders this week, they reached out to cornerback Riley Moss and agreed to a four-year, $67 million extension on Thursday. There are other extension candidates Broncos GM George Paton could still be considering, including wide receiver/returner Marvin Mims Jr.
However, Mims told The Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson that he told his agent he didn't want to hear from him during the bye unless it was a serious offer from the Broncos.
“I told my agent I didn’t want to talk about it unless it was serious,’’ Mims told Tomasson .
Mims didn't hear from his agent, so if the Broncos reached out to his representative, we can only assume it wasn't serious. Moss revealed at the podium on Thursday, after the news of his extension broke, that his agent's conversations with the Broncos began on Tuesday of this week. So it can happen fast, if the team makes contact.
In his conversation with Tomasson, Mims also expressed his desire to stay in Denver beyond 2026 to continue contributing to the winning culture he's helped establish since arriving as a second-round draft pick four years ago.
“I like it here.  It feels like home," Mims told Tomasson. "I feel like we’ve been able to build a culture with the guys here. … Not everyone’s going to be able to stay. It’s really on (the Broncos) who they want to keep on. … It’d be nice to continue to keep growing with this group but you never know what the future has in store.”
Unlike Moss, Mims has been twice decorated with accolades as a punt returner, earning All-Pro and Pro Bowl honors in each of his first two seasons. Von Miller has been the only other Bronco to pull that off in his first two years in team history.
However, when a team extends a player, it's not about rewarding them for past production; it's about paying them for what is expected in the future. And Moss has been significantly more productive at his post as a cornerback this season than Mims has as a receiver or as a returner.
Mims has just 10 receptions for 92 yards thus far and has yet to score. As a returner, his 10.7 yards-per-attempt as a punt returner is a career-low. His previous low as a punt returner was 15.6 yards per return in 2025.
The year prior, Mims averaged 15.7 yards per punt return and 27.7 yards per kick return, earning first-team All-Pro honors and a Pro Bowl selection. He's only returned eight kick-offs this season so far, and his 25.8 yards-per-return average is also a career low.
All the markers for Mims are pointing in the opposite direction, which is no doubt a big reason why he remains un-extended. It didn't help that a training camp injury cost him weeks of availability, and just when he was healthy, he suffered a foot injury in his return to the field in the Broncos' preseason finale.
That foot injury affected Mims initially, when the regular-season got underway, and then a concussion also cost him two games. No injury can ever be considered timely, but it was certainly inconvenient for Mims in his bid to earn an extension in a contract year.
In Mims's defense, the Broncos' offense hasn't exactly been lighting it up. The Broncos gave up a first- and third-round draft pick to acquire wideout Jaylen Waddle in the offense, and while he leads the team in receiving, he only has 337 yards and two touchdowns on 30 receptions.
Even Courtland Sutton is having a career-worst season, with just 25 receptions for 266 yards and two touchdowns. No receiver in Denver is really eating well, mainly due to Bo Nix's slow start this season in his return from a broken ankle and the toughest schedule in the NFL when it comes to opposing defenses.
Per Tomasson, Mims said his low receiving production isn't "just a me thing," pointing to how disappointing the season has been for Waddle and everyone else. Mims called it a "letdown," and he's not wrong.
But factoring in just how tough the Broncos' level of competition was through the first half of the season, as disappointing as the offense has been, the struggles are at least understandable.
The key has been Denver's ability to win so many games against these quality opponents, even if it hasn't often looked all that impressive offensively. The Broncos are 7-2, and while that's the most important thing, I'm not sure that it really serves Mims in his quest for a second contract.
The Broncos know that it's been rough for all of their receivers this season. That's why, even if the team is open to extending Mims, it might wait a while yet to see if the offense can come alive down the stretch, now that the Broncos' schedule is finally opening up. But Mims could help accelerate that possibility by at least improving his return numbers.
Nix seems to have climbed out of his early-season slump, beginning in Week 7. His last three games have been good, and he's looked more like the quarterback he was down the stretch and in the playoffs last season, but the Broncos' offense is still yet to really take off.
With the benefit of the bye, perhaps we start to see signs of that this week against the Raiders. And with Moss getting paid, maybe it reenergizes Mims to go out there and show the Broncos that he's capable of producing at a much higher level on offense and special teams.
Other extension candidates the Broncos could consider this season are nickel cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian and safety Brandon Jones. Getting Moss inked during a game week is more evidence that Paton is willing to do business whenever, so long as he's ready to talk.
Time will tell whether the 24-year-old Mims ends up hearing from the Broncos. As the first draft pick of the Sean Payton era, Mims has been a big part of the Broncos' turnaround, and he's been decorated as a pro.
Because of that, I'd be shocked if the Broncos aren't keeping Mims in mind for a possible extension, but he's going to have to give them more than he has through the first half of the season.

title: Why Broncos Hit Pause on Caleb Lohner's Return Ahead of Raiders Clash
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are rested, coming off the bye, and they're about as healthy as they could expect to be at the midway point of the season. There are a couple of key players on injured reserve, but the Broncos will get them back soon, like running backs RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie.
Tight end Caleb Lohner could be back soon, too, as the Broncos started his 21-day clock earlier this week to return from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, but after practicing all three days since then, he's been ruled out of Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders .
The Broncos will see how Lohner looks next week, though it'll be a short week ahead of their Black Friday road tilt vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers.
With both the Broncos and Raiders dropping their final injury reports on Friday, let's take a look at how things are shaping up ahead of this AFC West throwdown, starting with the home team.
One thing to remember about Lohner is that Denver would have to make room for him on the 53-man roster if he's activated off the PUP list. So, as much as I know Sean Payton has a hankering to get Lohner on the field for his red-zone offense, the first-year tight end will have to give the coaches some confidence that he can contribute because another valued player would have to be cut.
The Broncos get 21 days to make that decision on Lohner, and during that time, he can practice with the team in full, as he did this whole week. If the Broncos don't activate him with that 21-day window, he'd revert back and be unavailable for the rest of the season.
Hufanga is back after missing the past four games. His experience and physical presence will be a welcome sight on the back end of Denver's defense.
The newly paid Moss has cleared concussion protocol, as have Waddle and Prentice. And even Abrams-Draine progressed from limited on Wednesday to full participation the past two days.
Allen and Sutton were only listed because the Broncos gave them a rest day of sorts on Wednesday, easing the veterans back into action after the long lay-off of the bye. They're healthy and good to go.
Bowers went from having a very doubtful outlook on Wednesday to practicing on each of the past two days. He's questionable, but trending toward playing.
I've been told that Bowers is the type of player who, if he makes the trip with the team, is absolutely going to play. He'll do everything within his power to force the issue.
It appears Fernando Mendoza may have his security blanket against the Broncos. Bowers is not only a star tight end for the Raiders, but he's also their No. 1 receiver, as Patrick Surtian II talked about earlier this week.
"I mean, some people think that he's a tight end. I think he's a receiver, the way they utilize him in the route tree," Surtian said of Bowers on Wednesday. "I feel like his route tree and his yards per target is very telling."
Surtain and company will be dialed in on Bowers, if he plays, but they can't lose track of fellow tight end Michael Mayer or wide receiver Tre Tucker either.
"They utilize him [Bowers] in a multitude of ways that you've got to be keyed in on," Surtain said. "So it's all about honing in on the details and understanding how they're trying to use him."
Beyond Bowers, the Raiders have ruled out Hemingway, giving them one less body up front on defense. We'll keep an eye on Fatukasi as well, but the Raiders already rank 31st against the run, and if Hemingway and Fatukasi miss this game, the Broncos will look to capitalize on their absence with their ground attack.

title: Mile High Roundtable: Broncos vs. Raiders Predictions After the Bye
full_text:
The 7-2 Denver Broncos aren't taking the 4-6 Las Vegas Raiders lightly entering their first divisional clash of the season.
There may be a different coaching regime and quarterback in Vegas now, but the Raiders took the Broncos to the limit last year at Mile High. Denver held on for a narrow 10-7 win, but it came at the cost of losing starting running back J.K. Dobbins for the season.
Yeah, Broncos-Raiders tends to get chippy.
When it comes to divisional rivalries and the matchups that come with them, all bets are off. The Broncos are emerging from their bye and are about as healthy as they could hope to be, while the Raiders are settling into life with rookie Fernando Mendoza under center after trading away Kirk Cousins early last week.
Sean Payton has an excellent record coming off the bye — 17-6 (.739) — but Klint Kubiak's Raiders are hungry. It could be a rock-fight on Sunday.
How will the first 2026 iteration of Broncos-Raiders shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 7-2 : Raider Week is an opportunity for the Broncos to stack another divisional win in the standings. Of course, there's the Kubiak family sub-plot and a rookie starting quarterback to throw into the mix, but the Broncos' roster is simply better. Bo Nix throws for three scores as the Broncos pull away from the nomadic Raiders.
Pick : Broncos 31, Raiders 14
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 7-2 : The Raiders' defense is ripe for the picking, ranking 31st against the run and 23rd against the pass. Nix and the Broncos' offense have a prime opportunity to continue on the upward trend they've established since Week 7. Look for Jonah Coleman to have a big day on the ground — notching his first-career 100-yard rushing performance — while Nix passes for 250 yards and two touchdowns. Fernando Mendoza gets acquainted with the Mile High turf, as the Broncos sack the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft five times. Mendoza gets a few garbage-time licks in to pad his stats and make this game look closer than it was.
Pick : Broncos 27, Raiders 20
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 7-2 : Coming out of their bye, the Broncos are rested and nearing full strength with players like Talanoa Hufanga returning to the starting lineup. No game can be overlooked — especially a divisional game — but it’s nonetheless a contest that Denver should win. And remember, no matter if it’s by one point or 100, a win is a win is a win. 8-2.
Pick : Broncos 23, Raiders 17
Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 7-2 : The Broncos are a horse at home, quite literally. With or without Brock Bowers , the Broncos should have Mendoza in a tough position at Mile High. The Raiders are feisty, but are they actually “good?" One thing about this team in the Payton era: the Broncos will play up or down to their competition at times, but they beat the opponents they should. The Broncos should win.
Pick : Broncos 30, Raiders 16
Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 6-3 : The Broncos are rested, healthy, and ready for a second-half-of-the-season push. The Broncos come out motivated, especially on the defensive side of the ball, wanting to give Mendoza a true welcome to the NFL. Fans will be fired up, leading to a couple of big turnovers, making this a game no one has to sweat all the way down to the last whistle.
Pick : Broncos 28, Raiders 10
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 7-2 : The Raiders' defense has a good pass rush, but it's bad against the run, so it's time for the Broncos to get it rolling on the ground . As for the Raiders' offense, the key will be for the Broncos to get the pressure on Mendoza. This is a game where the Broncos need to show they can put a team away in the second half. Here's hoping they do just that.
Pick : Broncos 27, Raiders 13
Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 6-3 : I want to predict a blowout at Mile High, but that's not who this Broncos team is. They're going to lean into conservative play, make the plays they need to have on offense, and beat the heck out of a rookie quarterback making his second career start. Denver is going to win, but I don't think it covers a double-digit spread.
Pick : Broncos 16, Raiders 10
Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 5-4 : After an eight-game losing streak, the Broncos have now won four straight against the Raiders. The Raiders have thrown Mendoza to the wolves, and the Broncos are salivating for this matchup. Meanwhile, the Broncos' offense is facing the easiest defensive schedule, and the Raiders have been among the NFL's worst . While I could see this being a big win for the home team, the Broncos have a bad habit of playing down to the Raiders' level, and that leads to another one-score game.
Pick : Broncos 28, Raiders 20
Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 5-4 : The Broncos should have an easy outing against the Raiders, with Mendoza only two games into his career. The Raiders' defense has been abysmal over the last several weeks and coming off a bye, Nix will carve them up, dropping four total touchdowns. The Broncos win in a balanced offensive and defensive effort, looking the most convincing they have all season.
Pick : Broncos 31, Raiders 10
James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 4-5 : Division games can be tricky, but Denver should win. In this one, the Broncos rattle Mendoza, and the newly paid Riley Moss gets a timely interception that leads to points. On offense, a running game keyed by Coleman gets rolling, and a mistake-free Nix leads to a 20-point margin of victory for Denver.
Pick : Broncos 37, Raiders 17

title: 3 Keys to a Broncos Victory Over Raiders in Week 11
full_text:
The Denver Broncos return from the bye and, in the second half of the season, face what is considered the easier part of their schedule, with just two plus-.500 teams remaining.
Of course, what's easier on paper doesn't always translate to the field. And while the Las Vegas Raiders are 4-6, with all their wins coming against teams with a losing record, that doesn't mean the Broncos can take Sunday's game for granted.
New Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak — the son of former Denver Broncos backup quarterback and Super Bowl-winning head coach Gary Kubiak — has shown he can do some good things. And while the Raiders may be without tight end Brock Bowers , they still have some talented players on the roster.
The Broncos cannot afford to look past the Raiders, particularly with the AFC West crown still at stake. Let's look at the three keys to the Broncos beating the Raiders in Week 11.
While the Broncos are doing a better job on offense in more recent games, they have yet to be consistently good for four quarters. If there ever were a week for the Broncos to show they can string together four quality quarters of offense, this is it.
The Raiders have given up 3,851 yards of total offense to opponents this season. While their defense has some quality pass rushers — namely Maxx Crosby, who leads his team with 35 pressures and five sacks — the Raiders have struggled in other areas.
In particular, the Raiders have been bad against the run. They've given up 1,511 rushing yards to opponents thus far at 4.9 yards per carry. The only opponent to get fewer than 100 yards rushing against Las Vegas was Miami in Week 1.
There's no excuse for the Broncos not getting it done in the run game this week. If Jonah Coleman doesn't have his best game of the season and J.K. Dobbins doesn't show consistency, then something is wrong here.
Head coach Sean Payton is aware of the issues with the running game and has hinted at what must be done to fix it. We'll see what Payton has in mind on Sunday, but between run blocking and the performance of the backs themselves, it's time for the Broncos to get it together there.
If Denver can do that, it will help mitigate the Raiders' pass rush and take some pressure off Bo Nix. That should allow Nix to settle down and press his advantage in the passing game, where the Raiders have some issues in the secondary.
We've heard the talk from Payton about the need to fix the running game issues. Now it's time to deliver with a quality run game.
Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, had a solid debut against the Seattle Seahawks this past week. He completed 62.2% of his passes, with seven of his 37 attempts considered bad throws. He had no turnovers, and two of his receivers dropped passes.
Where the Seahawks were able to get to Mendoza was through the pass rush. They pressured Mendoza on 42.9% of his dropbacks, blitzed him nine times, and got seven QB hits and five sacks.
If Bowers doesn't play, that means the Raiders are without their top playmaker. They can still get production out of fellow tight end Michael Mayer and wide receiver Tre Tucker, but they aren't the caliber of player Bowers is.
Additionally, the Raiders haven't been good at running the football. Ashton Jeanty has struggled, averaging just 3.1 yards per carry this season. Rookie Mike Washington has had more success with 3.8 yards per carry, but he's not a game-changer.
The Broncos, of course, can't take anything for granted when it comes to the Raiders' skill positions. But the Seahawks showed that the best way to neutralize Mendoza is to pressure him.
We'll see whether Vance Joseph decides to dial up more pressure and not be content to drop too many players into coverage. And while the Broncos might not force many turnovers against Mendoza, if they get pass rushers to him as often as the Seahawks did, it should limit the rookie's impact.
The one area where the Raiders have excelled is on special teams, so this is where the Broncos need to be at their best. The Raiders have a couple of third-phase players who have done their part to keep them in games.
Dylan Laube has 822 yards on 26 kickoff returns, including a 95-yarder for a touchdown against the New York Jets. The Broncos' kickoff return team will need to keep a close eye on him, as he can be dangerous.
Punter AJ Cole currently leads the NFL in punting, with 52.1 yards per punt. His net average is 44.6. He has pinned opponents inside the 20-yard line on 41.2% of his punts.
The Raiders aren't as threatening in the punt return game, though Malik Benson does have a 23-yard return to his credit. The Broncos will have to be as disciplined in punt coverage as they are in kickoff coverage.
The good news is that the Broncos' special teams is one of the better units in the NFL and has mostly done well with coverage. But this week, the Broncos' coverage units will likely get their biggest test yet.
As for the Broncos' own punt return game, Marvin Mims Jr. hasn't been as explosive in that department this season. Given how well Cole has played, Mims might not get as many opportunities.
But this is a game where special teams could be a big factor, as it's the one area in which the Raiders rank among the top teams in the NFL.
One should not assume that the Broncos' easier schedule ahead means that a win against the Raiders is all but in the bag. That's particularly true when it's an AFC West rival that would love nothing more than to surprise everyone with a win.
The Broncos have to approach the Raiders as though they're facing a top team. If the Broncos manage to build an early lead, they need to keep playing well and keep the Raiders from getting back into the game.
There are still those who have doubts as to whether the Broncos are capable of a deep playoff run. A decisive win over the Raiders would be another step toward showing that the Broncos belong in the Super Bowl conversation.

title: Two Key Matchups That Give Broncos a Decisive Edge vs. Raiders
full_text:
Coming off a bye, the Denver Broncos have to be licking their chops with the Las Vegas Raiders next up on the schedule.
The Broncos will face a Raiders team with serious, exploitable issues on both sides of the ball. The door is wide open for Denver to have a big game.
Of course, the Broncos have to go out there and exploit those issues without shooting themselves in the foot. If the Broncos can win these two key matchups, they'll be in a prime spot to walk out with their eighth win of the season, which would give them the AFC West-leading tiebreaker and vault them back to the No. 2 playoff seed.
The Raiders have been one of the worst passing defenses in the NFL, and when narrowing it down to position groups, they're terrible against tight ends. Opponents haven't really attacked them with running backs in the passing game, mainly because they don't have to, due to the Raiders' tight end issues.
Opponents remain highly efficient when using their running backs in the passing game against the Raiders.
Dean has played well, but Walker has been a liability in coverage for the Raiders' defense. Engram and Coleman are the two prime weapons the Broncos can use to exploit Walker.
The Broncos can mix it up between Coleman and Engram on Walker, but whoever Walker ends up covering should be a quick and easy read for Bo Nix to keep the Broncos ahead of the sticks.
Over the years, Joseph has done well against rookie quarterbacks, and Mendoza will be starting his second game . It will be interesting to see what Joseph pulls out to deal with Mendoza, not only in the coverage looks but also in the pressure looks up front.
It won't be surprising to see Joseph unveil some new tricks and looks to heap more onto Mendoza's plate and add to the difficulty of playing the Broncos' defense at Mile High.
The Raiders' offensive line is terrible, so Joseph should be able to create looks to exploit the unit's awareness and chemistry issues. Combine that with some new and creative coverage looks, and Mendoza will have a tough go of it.
He's a rookie quarterback getting his second start and it's on Joseph to expose him.

title: Brock Bowers' Injury Situation Just Took an Unwelcome Turn for Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are getting healthier as the practice week progresses.
Coming off their bye, the Broncos are close to full strength, not counting the handful of players on injured reserve, some of whom they'll be getting back in the next few weeks.
Things are looking good on the health front for the Broncos, and they're still buzzing over the Riley Moss extension , but things are also improving for the Las Vegas Raiders. Let's take a look at how Thursday's practice report shook out for both teams.
Everyone but Jones was a full participant on Thursday, including Abrams-Draine, who was limited on Wednesday. Jones remains limited, but given that he's had nearly three weeks to bounce back from his hamstring injury, there's a good chance he'll play on Sunday, even if he ends up listed as questionable on the final injury report.
But that's me putting an optimistic spin on things. The Broncos have been without Hufanga for the past four games, so just getting him back will be great for the defense, but having him and Jones patrolling the back end will be just what the doctor ordered.
Lohner continues to practice in full after the Broncos started his clock to return from the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list on Wednesday. It's unclear when the Broncos plan to make a decision on Lohner, but it could come before Sunday's game.
If Lohner gets activated, though, the Broncos will need to make room on the 53-man roster, and they already have four tight ends. With each practice Lohner has, there are a handful of guys at the bottom of the roster who get a little more uncomfortable.
Allen and Sutton returned to full participation, too, though they're limited designation on Wednesday was for rest only, as the Broncos ease them back into the swing of things after the bye. If Jones can progress on Friday, all the health stars will be aligned for Denver.
The Raiders have been trying out kickers this week with Gay's injury, but the real story on Thursday was Bowers's return to practice. The star tight end suffered a " significant " injury on Sunday against Seattle, and did not return in the second half.
Bowers didn't participate on Wednesday, but he was back out there on Thursday, albeit in limited form. Sources close to the Raiders indicate he's very focused on trying to play this game against the Broncos, so despite the early signs this week being unfavorable, it's too soon to count him out.
The Raiders are dealing with some injuries on their defensive line, as you can see, so it'll be interesting to see how Fatukasi and Hemingway progress on Friday.

title: Gut Reaction: 3 Big Takeaways From Riley Moss' $67M Broncos Extension
full_text:
At one point, I didn't think it was likely that the Denver Broncos would extend cornerback Riley Moss. The 2023 third-round pick would have drawn interest — and a significant payday — if he had made it to the open market.
But the Broncos got a deal done on Thursday, keeping Moss in the fold for the next few seasons as he agreed to terms on a four-year, $67 million extension that runs through 2030.
It may take some time before we know more about the finer points, such as fully guaranteed money, injury-only guarantees, contract structure, and whether or not option bonuses or void years were utilized.
But let's consider a few things about what this contract extension means.
First, while the Broncos didn't get the deal done during the bye week, they actually got it done earlier in the season than the multiple extensions they finalized during last year's bye.
Last year, the Broncos' bye was in Week 12, while this season's was Week 10. Thus, general manager George Paton got a deal done with Moss a week earlier than the three extensions he inked last year.
It's another example of Paton's willingness to get deals done with players during the regular season, and he was right on schedule when it came to this extension for Moss.
Time will tell whether Paton gets any other players extended in the coming weeks, but if there are others the Broncos see as a priority to keep, they could still strike in the next few weeks.
It's important to note that the fourth-year cornerback could have made more money if he had hit the open market in 2027 free agency. Instead, Moss took a deal that, while still a considerable sum at $16.75 million per year, was less than he might have found elsewhere.
It shows that Moss wants to be with the Broncos. He likes the organization, the coaching staff, and his teammates. While he certainly wanted to be well-compensated, he showed that it wasn't just about the money.
Moss's deal pays him less in terms of average per-year salary than the Los Angeles Rams gave Jaylen Watson during the 2026 offseason. The flipside, though, is that Watson signed for three years while Moss signed for four.
Again, we should know more about Moss's contract details in the days to come, but it will be interesting to see how much he got in full and total guarantees. Watson got $26.5 million fully guaranteed and an additional $7.5 million in injury-only guarantees.
A four-year deal would allow the Broncos to put more fully guaranteed money into the deal. Thus, it wouldn't be a surprise if Moss got more guaranteed money than Watson and stood to earn more over the long term.
Finally, the Broncos showed that they want to keep their homegrown players in the fold if they have proven themselves worthy of an extension. That means we can't rule out an extension for Ja'Quan MacMillian at some point.
Other teams might not have tried to keep a player like Moss around if they expected his free-agent market to be so strong. But the Broncos saw things differently and kept a player whom many people (myself included) expected to move on after 2026.
I'm happy to eat crow on this one. It's good to see the Broncos get a deal done with Moss and secure an important part of the defense for a few more seasons.

title: Broncos' Riley Moss Extension Raises New Questions About Ja'Quan McMillian
full_text:
Just when Denver Broncos fans had written off the possibility of GM George Paton getting any in-season extensions done, the Riley Moss news hit the wire on Thursday morning.
It wasn't technically done over the bye week — as Paton has done with four different players over the past two years — but the Broncos extended Moss to a four-year, $67 million deal that'll keep him in the fold through 2030.
Moss gets $16.75 million per year as one of the NFL's best No. 2 cornerbacks, which is a pretty nice bargain, given the projections this past offseason that he could command $20-plus million on the open market.
It's great news for Moss and the Broncos' defense. But what does it mean for nickel cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian?
Many Broncos fans fear that since the Broncos obviously prioritized Moss first, perhaps McMillian doesn't fit into the team's post-2026 plans. That trepidation was only intensified by The Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson , who reported on Thursday afternoon that there "haven't been serious discussions" yet between McMillian and the Broncos.
Tempering Tomasson's report, though, was 9NEWS ' Mike Klis, who said in an appearance on 104.3 The FAN's Dover and Cecil show on Thursday that the Moss deal "doesn't affect Ja'Quan."
"Ja'Quan's going to get his deal, too. I think they're going to work on securing him also," Klis said on The FAN.
So, if you're pining for a McMillian extension , let not your heart be troubled. The NFL trade deadline, coming a few days into the Broncos' bye, likely pushed some of Paton's plans back.
The drama of the failed Daiyan Henley trade and its subsequent fallout only further delayed any extension actions Paton could take. McMillian will get his — of this, I have no doubt.
McMillian is one of the NFL's best nickel cornerbacks. And he's the Broncos' best ballhawk, which is important for a defense that has struggled, at times, to take the ball away over the past few years.
The Broncos' have improved their takeaway numbers this season, even though McMillian only has one interception. But it was a doozy, picking off Sam Darnold in overtime to help seal a big win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6.
In the four years McMillian has been the Broncos' nickel, his fingerprints have been on seven interceptions, five forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, and 10 sacks. He's also broken up 31 passes, and this doesn't count playoffs.
McMillian has the clutch gene. It was his amazing overtime interception in the divisional round of the playoffs that helped the Broncos clinch a 33-30 win over the Buffalo Bills to advance to the AFC championship game.
JA'QUAN MCMILLIAN INTERCEPTION BUFvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/S3yuoRu30c
The only knock on McMillian is his 5-foot-10, 183-pound size, though he plays much bigger. He's an extremely physical player, as evidenced by his sack totals and tackle numbers (221 over his four-year run as a starter).
However, the NFL has transitioned to bigger nickels over the past two years as offenses have prioritized two- and three-tight-end personnel sets. We're seeing more 'big nickel' types, meaning guys like, say, a Devon Key, who may otherwise be a safety, but is just a little bit bigger and well-equipped to handle the physical assignment of running with tight ends in coverage and shedding their blocks to make tackles in the run game.
For the most part, though, McMillian has gotten around this obstacle against opponents, like the Los Angeles Rams, who've deployed heavy tight-end sets. And while it's a factor that defensive coordinator Vance Joseph has to take into consideration as a schemer and play-caller, it's the last thing on Denver's mind when it comes to McMillian.
Undrafted out of Eastern Carolina in 2022, McMillian appeared in one game as a rookie, before beating out experienced nickel K'Waun Williams for the starting job in 2023. McMillian has never looked back.
As a restricted free agent this past offseason, the Broncos tendered McMillian at the second-round level, which guaranteed him $5.8 million in 2026. He's been worth every penny.
McMillian's time will come. And it wouldn't surprise me if an extension gets done before the 2026 season ends.
Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron have played a lot this season, thanks to a three-game absence of Patrick Surtain II and a couple of Moss injuries. While the young tandem turned in some admirable play, especially in Week 6's win over the Seahawks, it wasn't enough to persuade the Broncos to kick the Moss can down the road.
The same will hold true for McMillian. Abrams-Draine, a 2024 fifth-round pick, has another year left on his rookie deal, while Barron is in just his second year as a 2025 first-rounder. Abrams-Draine is clearly a boundary corner, while Barron has proven that he's not reliable outside the numbers, and belongs inside.
When it comes to their top three cornerbacks — Surtain, Moss, and McMillian — there's a comfort and a confidence there for the Broncos. The Broncos want to keep that trio intact, and will find a way to get McMillian re-signed; it's just a matter of when.

title: Broncos Lock Down CB Riley Moss with Massive Contract Extension
full_text:
It was Garett Bolles in 2024 . Then Luke Wattenberg in 2025. Now it's Riley Moss' turn to cash out with the Denver Broncos coming out of a bye week.
And cash out he did, agreeing to a four-year, $67 million contract extension on Thursday, ahead of the team's Week 11 home matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders. The deal was reported by multiple media outlets and confirmed by 9NEWS insider Mike Klis.
Moss is now the NFL's 23rd-highest-paid cornerback at $16.75 million per year — a substantial leap from the $1.36 million he's earning in 2026 as part of his initial rookie deal.
A former third-round draft pick, Moss has appeared in eight games this season (missing one due to a rib injury), notching 17 solo tackles, eight pass breakups, and one interception across 434 defensive snaps.
Moss ranks as the league's 28th-best CB among 105 qualifiers, according to Pro Football Focus , which also assigned him the 21st-highest coverage mark (71.6).
“The one thing about him is his grit and his competes, and those guys [are] out there on an island a lot of times, so there’s going to be times where it’s not always what you want and yet, and he’s onto the next play. I think that’s a great skill set he has," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Moss in September.
Especially after the Daiyan Henley ordeal , this was an especially pragmatic move by Broncos general manager George Paton, who continues his longstanding habit of locking down players during the regular season.
Denver secured Moss on an extremely team-friendly pact, certainly less than he would've gotten by testing the unrestricted free-agent waters this coming offseason. It ensures both starting CBs — Moss and Patrick Surtain II — are manning the defensive backfield for the long term.
Some fans will express disappointment that Moss was signed over several other extension candidates, including CB Ja'Quan McMillian, wide receiver/returner Marvin Mims, and safety Brandon Jones. McMillian now seems destined to shop his wares on the open market.
But young, capable boundary cornerbacks don't exactly grow on trees, and Moss has shown more good than bad during his starting tenure in the Mile High City, which makes his new contract palatable — if not preferable.

title: Detroit Lions Week 11 Rooting Guide for Best Possible Playoff Outcome
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are firmly in the thick of the NFC playoff race.
Entering Week 11, there appears to be a collection of teams separating themselves from the pack in the postseason push. Detroit will enter the week in first-place in the NFC North thanks to a tiebreaker over the Chicago Bears and Minnesota Vikings, with all three teams entering the week at 7-2.
According to the New York Times' Playoff Simulator, the Lions currently hold a 74 percent chance to make the playoffs, an 18 percent chance to win the NFC North and a 6 percent chance to earn the No. 1 seed and a first-round bye.
Here's a rooting guide for the Lions' best possible playoff outcome across the NFL Week 11 slate.
Saints at Bears: Saints 1 p.m., FOX
Detroit could use some insurance ahead of their massive Thanksgiving game against the Bears on Thursday. Both teams are 7-2, but they haven't played each other yet which means the head-to-head tiebreaker will be on the line when they play in front of a national audience.
Ultimately, next week is bigger for the Lions as a win over Chicago would give them the head-to-head tiebreaker for the time being. Still, a loss from Ben Johnson's team could be big moving forward as it will give the Lions a game of separation should they defeat the Buccaneers.
Ravens at Panthers: Ravens 1 p.m., FOX
The Lions lost earlier in the season to the Panthers, and as a result the Panthers have the head-to-head tiebreaker. The NFC South doesn't appear to have a team in the Wild Card race, and a loss from Carolina would continue to trend toward eliminating them from challenging the Lions in the Wild Card and making that head-to-head loss make an impact later in the year.
Titans at Cowboys: Titans 1 p.m., FOX
Another AFC vs. NFC matchup should see Lions fans rooting for the AFC option. The Cowboys' offense is as explosive as any, as they showed against the 49ers last week. While their defense could ultimately keep them from making any run in the postseason, they're still in the hunt at 4-6.
With the New York Giants showing some flaws, the Cowboys could get back into the NFC East race if they get on a roll. However, if the Titans win they could push Dallas toward the brink heading into December.
Cardinals at Chiefs: Chiefs 1 p.m., CBS
This is a case of rooting for the AFC over the NFC. The Cardinals are struggling, and could be in line to start veteran Josh Johnson at quarterback after rookie Carson Beck has been dealing with back spasms.
Steelers at Eagles: Steelers 1 p.m., CBS
The Eagles have had a turbulent season this year, with quarterback Jalen Hurts being sidelined due to blood clots. They're currently in last-place in the NFC East, and another loss could be too much for them to overcome even if they were to go on a late-season run.
Jaguars at Giants: Jaguars 4:25 p.m., CBS
New York is currently in first-place in the NFC East, but is coming off a tough loss to the Washington Commanders at home. The Jaguars were active at the trade deadline and look like a potential juggernaut.
Vikings vs 49ers (NFL Mexico City Game): Vikings 8:20 p.m., NBC
This game is a tricky evaluation, as the two teams are both directly competing with the Lions for different things. On one hand, a Vikings win would give the Lions a better chance of earning the No. 1 seed because it would drop the 49ers to even with Detroit at 7-2.
The 49ers winning would drop Minnesota to a game below the Lions should Detroit win, so there are advantages to both results. However, the best possible playoff outcome for Detroit would be the No. 1 seed, and with a Vikings win the Lions' chance of obtaining that would jump from 6 to 12 percent.
Bengals at Commanders: Bengals 8:15 p.m., Monday, ESPN/ABC
This is another case of rooting for AFC over NFC. Washington gained some momentum with a win over the Giants last week, but may not be able to keep the mojo going as they run into the buzzsaw that has been the Bengals' offense as of late.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: 5 Players Detroit Lions Must Scout in College Football Week 12
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions face a test in the form of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, now without star EDGE Aidan Hutchinson. The Buccaneers face their own adversity, with starting quarterback Baker Mayfield questionable for Sunday’s contest.
Meanwhile, college football has reached the final push towards conference titles and the playoffs. As the season wraps up, the margin of error is zero and players push for the final footage on their draft tape. It has already been confirmed by Lions On SI that both the Lions and Buccaneers were in attendance to Friday’s contest between Michigan State football hosting Oregon.
Two of the players who the Lions could have scouted from that contest include Oregon LB/EDGE Matayo Uiagalelei, who had 0.5 sacks, a blocked field goal, and an interception, and MSU EDGE Kenny Soares Jr., who contributed 7 tackles, 4 pressures, and a sack against the Ducks.
Here are five players the Lions must scout in college football, week eleven.
Swain has been a weapon on both the defensive and special teams side of the ball during his time with the Gamecocks. The 6-foot defensive back was the opposite corner of second-round pick Brandon Cisse last season, shutting down the other half the field.
Swain is touted as potentially having more upside with his 5 career punt return touchdowns. Additionally, he has three career interceptions, three career sacks, and three career forced fumbles. In the last two seasons combined, he has surrendered less than 500 yards in pass coverage in nearly 550 snaps in coverage.
The Gamecocks take on No. 1 Georgia at 7:30 p.m. EST.
The Bruins are one of the few remaining undefeated teams in college football, and Omosigho is a big reason why. The Oklahoma transfer has exploded onto the scene in his first year in Los Angeles, leading the NCAA with five forced fumbles and contributing 5.5 sacks and 10.5 tackles for loss alongside 4 pass breakups.
The linebacker is rated no. 3 among all linebackers in the NCAA on PFF and is a finalist for the Dick Butkus Award, handed out to the top linebacker in the nation. In only 102 pass rush snaps, Omosigho has an absurd 31 pressures.
The productive linebacker is graded out third against the rush among linebackers and 20th against the pass. He is a do-it-all linebacker that would be an instant contributor to the front seven for the Lions considering the unknown long-term status for Jack Campbell.
Omosigho briefly exited the Bruins November 14 contest against Illinois, but returned to the game and has been given the “all clear” for Saturday’s game against Michigan. The Wolverines host the Bruins at 3:30 p.m. EST, giving plenty of Lions fans a chance to watch the linebacker first-hand when cheering on their college team.
Heard has had one of the most unique journeys in college football, touring through three SEC schools with LSU, Tennessee, and now the Wildcats. The 6-foot-6, 325-pound tackle has over 2,100 snaps in his career and saved his best for last.
This year, Heard has yet to allow a sack and is rated in the top 25 for wins above average in tackles. He has experience at both tackle slots, giving him versatility that teams want. As it stands, the Kentucky tackle is in the early day two conversation, which can change during the postseason bowl process.
He overcame a drastically bad 2024, where the tackle was rated in the bottom 50 for all players at his position, to become a top player in his craft. It speaks of his dedication while also providing a warning to give the tackle an adjustment period in his next jump in competition.
The Wildcats travel to Missouri to take on the Tigers at 7:30 p.m. EST.
It is hard to argue with production and statistics, and Brown provides plenty of that. The three-year starter for the Cardinals has been a focal point of their offense since 2024, with over 3,000 total yards in his career.
The 5-foot-9 speedster born in Miami has averaged over 7.2 yards per rush for all three seasons with the Cardinals and found the endzone 29 times in total. His gap rush scheme grade and elusiveness grades are in the 90s for percentile among all qualifying backs.
The drawbacks on Brown are that he did suffer an injury, missing four games in 2025, and that he is another “Sonic” type player in the mold of Jahmyr Gibbs. Additionally, Brown is relatively unproven out of the backfield, with only 60 catches over his three-year career, averaging six yards per catch as opposed to his 7.6 yards per carry on average.
The No. 23 Cardinals host Pitt at 7:30 p.m. EST.
Crews does not have an impressive sack count that stands off the sheet, but the Bobcat is putting together a very strong senior season. Crews has 62 total pressures on the season, with five ending in sacks. The 6-foot-4 EDGE has also batted down a pass as the Bobcats sit at 10-1 on the season.
The team captain is rating among the very top of all EDGEs with an astounding 18.2 percentage in pass rush win rate. Additionally, his true pass set pass rush grade and pass rush grade are among the top.
As is the case with previously highlighted FCS prospects, strength of competition becomes a concerns, especially as Crews did not nail down a non-rotational role until this season. He does not have a versatile role with Montana State, either, as he seldomly rotated inside, with less than 20 career snaps in the B gap.
His run defense is also not in the top 50 percentile, which is a concern looking at the Lions scheme.
Crews and the Bobcats host in-state bitter rival Montana at 2 p.m. EST.
Sports writer since 2022. Emmett Matasovsky started covering the Detroit Lions in 2025. He has extensive experience covering Michigan State Spartans athletics, including MSU basketball and football. Has demonstrated passionate, in-depth coverage of college athletics.

title: Kerby Joseph Disagrees With Dan Campbell: This S**t Ain't Rusty
full_text:
Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph is ready to make his 2026 season debut. It will have been over 400 days since he last played a game in the NFL, when the former third-round pick steps foot on the field against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Naturally, many supporters and head coach Dan Campbell expect there to be a little bit of rust, as Joseph has not played at the highest level in over a calander year.
“Yeah look, he's back out there. He's back out there. I mean I think you take it as it comes," said Campell. "Thank goodness he's got an opportunity to step back on that field. And then remember, it's been a minute, so there's going to be a little rust. Now practice, there was rust when he started three weeks ago and he's kicked some of that off as we've gone here. So, this will be his first game in a minute.
"Don't expect it to be perfect, but he's a football player and I think he'll do some things, play within the system and good. But no, I don't think he's going to have eight interceptions in this game. So, I mean, if that's what you're expecting, you're probably going to be disappointed," Campbell added. "But, I think it'll be good to get him back in there. He's got instincts and he can move and he can hit and there's a role for him and let's see. Let's see where he goes.”
The 26-year-old had an opportunity to speak to local reporters about his return, but did not agree with the sentiment that he was rusty.
“This shit ain’t rusty, dog. Nah, this shit ain’t rusty, dog. I’ve always had it," said Joseph. "I keep telling y’all I’m him. Like I keep telling y’all, I’m him. Like I’m him, and I’m gonna keep saying it. I’m him.”
Joseph does not lack confidence and indicated his faith allowed him to continue believing in himself, even during the tougher moments of his rehabilitation.
"I feel like that's just always me. I'm not gonna say I'm cocky, but I'm confident in myself. I was always confident in myself, and that's what got me here. I've been believing in my myself, trusting in my instincts and trusting what God has in store for me, so I ain't never been worried . I always kept my faith and I knew I was going to be back here because I've got more to do."

title: Detroit Lions OL Ruled Out Against Buccaneers, 6 Questionable
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have released their official injury designation report, ahead of their Week 11 home contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
This week, center Cade Mays has been ruled out.
Cornerback D.J. Reed, along with Joe Bachie, Khalil Dorsey, Tyler Lacy, Ennis Rakestraw and Sione Vaki have been ruled questionable.
The veteran defensive back expressed this week he does not want to rush his return from a hip injury, citing he felt he rushed his return last season from a significant hamstring injury.
A player that has taken advantage of increased opportunities has been cornerback Roger McCreary.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard expressed McCreary did not want to be pigeon-holed, since he has bounced around the league early in his NFL career.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: 2026 Defensive Midseason Grades
“I think players that don't feel like they've had many people believe in them, I attach to those guys really fast because I know that feeling," said Sheppard. "So, we had two talks in the offseason when we were trying to acquire him as a free agent. And I'll just disclose, I won't disclose everything , but some of those talks were centered around, you know, he was a second-round pick.
"When you're a second-round pick in this League, you're expected to come to the League and start and definitely contribute and play. Whereas in his case, he's on his third team in what, five years, four or five years. So just asking him whys, the whys behind it, talking to guys that's coached him, getting their feedback."
McCreary has steadily improved in his first season in Motown, earning the trust of his teammates and the coaching staff.
"It came down to the point that he wanted people to know that he was a legit corner in this league," said Sheppard. "He could play outside and inside. 'Coach Shepp, please don't pigeonhole me and just say I'm this and that. Give me the opportunity.' And when a player asks for that, you give it to him and it's up to them what they do with it. And I tip my hat to that kid. He's worked his tail off schematically, physically to do the things that we want done here the way that we do them.
"And he's doing it at a high level," Sheppard continued further. "This past month, he's been one of our best secondary players. He's been one of our best corners, honestly. And I lean on him now. The same way he leaned on me with that trust factor of, 'Where should I sign?' I'm leaning on him now, now that things are hitting the road and that's a player that I count on come Sunday. He's earned that trust.”

title: Lions OL Tate Ratledge Has Impressive Protection Streak
full_text:
Detroit Lions right guard Tate Ratledge has put together an impressive pass-protection streak.
The second-year guard has not allowed a sack in his last 845 snaps, which is the longest active streak in the National Football League.
Broncos guard Ben Powers has not given up a sack in 808 snaps and Chicago Bears guard Jonah Jackson has a streak going of 592 snaps.
Against New England, the former second-round pick earned a 91.3 run-blocking grade, which was first among players at his positions.
As PFF explained, "Ratledge's improvement in pass protection was just as notable. After allowing two pressures and earning a 34.4 pass-blocking grade against Miami in Week 9, Ratledge surrendered just one quarterback hit across 34 pass-blocking snaps against New England. Against the Patriots, he earned an 87.1 pass-blocking grade, tied for third among guards, while recording a 100.0% pass-block win rate, tied for first at the position."
Detroit's offensive line has drastic splits in pass protection, with the majority of sacks being given up in the first half.
Of the 21 total sacks given up this season, 18 of them have occurred in the first half.
“Again, I'd have to look at all the numbers there. I mean, a lot of it is we've really ended the last five or six games running the ball probably 70 to 75 percent of the game, which probably has a little bit of hand in that," said offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. "I think settling in is a part of that. I like to think that we wear on people and bring fatigue in the way that we play and the way that we go through a game. So, some of those things could certainly play into it. And then part of it's probably just chance, a little bit of both.”
With the defense dealing with significant injuries, quarterback Jared Goff was asked earlier this week if the offense felt the responsibility to play better with what has occurred on the opposite side of the ball.
“Yeah, but I think it's kind of regardless. I think you always want to raise it," said Goff. "I think everyone knows there's slack to pick up when you lose a player of his caliber, but offensively and even in some parts defensively, they just want to keep getting better and keep improving and keep showing who they are.
"They've been outstanding the last, I don't know, four or five weeks and I expect them to continue to go, and I know they do too.”

title: Detroit Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs Is 'Gaining Strength' Each Week
full_text:
Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is not showing any signs of slowing down anytime soon.
According to head coach Dan Campbell and running backs coach Tashard Choice, the film showcases a player that Gibbs is only getting stronger as the 2026 NFL season progresses.
“I feel like he's gaining strength," said Campbell. "I feel like he's gaining strength as we go here through the season and we go through these games. We come out of New England game and as everybody does, you break down these games as a staff and you go through the players, the scheme, what did we do well, what did we not? Who are the players playing at a top level? Who are the guys that we can help here a little bit, need a little bit of help in some areas.
"And (Tashard) Choice made that comment, and he's 100 percent right, that it just feels like he's gaining strength. He came in, I mentioned this before, he came in phenomenal shape in training camp, prepared to take the load. And as this season's gone on, he's getting stronger. And so yeah, I think the best way to say it, I love where he's at right now.”
Quarterback Jared Goff mentioned the former first-round pick has not elevated himself to be talked about in the same sentence as some of the all-time great NFL running backs.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: 2026 Midseason Offensive Grades
“You look at the numbers he's doing, it's like you hear his name mentioned with LaDainian Tomlinson it seems like every week. Obviously, we know about that guy, and yeah, he's unbelievable," said Goff. "He really is. He's a special player. He's a special guy, special teammate. The work he puts in I think gets unnoticed sometimes. He's a worker and has elevated his game from last year to this year in a lot of ways that you guys have obviously seen and it's paid off. The veteran signal-caller also pointed out that many do see just how competitive the former Alabama Crimson Tide running back is during each practice.

title: Spot the Ball: 10 Thoughts Ahead of Lions Matchup With Buccaneers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are looking at the second game of a crucial three-game stretch midway through the NFL season.
After dispatching of the Patriots in Munich on Sunday, the Lions are returning home to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11 at Ford Field. Detroit has a chance to remain in first-place in the NFC North heading into a Thanksgiving clash with the Chicago Bears next week.
Here are 10 thoughts surrounding the Lions’ matchup with the Buccaneers.
Barring any changes or last-second set-backs, Sunday is expected to mark the season debut for safety Kerby Joseph . The Illinois product hasn’t appeared in a game in over a calendar year with what is being reported as a degenerative knee issue, but has looked good in practice and will get an opportunity to return to action on Sunday.
It will be interesting to see exactly how the Lions utilize Joseph, as they’ve spent the last three weeks ramping him up to his return. If he can contribute in a fairly significant way in his first game back, it will be a huge boost to the confidence of the defense.
The Lions will be facing a Buccaneers team littered with former Lions, with linebacker Alex Anzalone headlining the group. Anzalone departed Detroit after five years this past offseason, and was a huge part of the team’s resurgence throughout his time in Motown.
Joining Anzalone on the Buccaneers’ defense are players like Al-Quadin Muhammad, Ifeatu Melifonwu, A’Shawn Robinson and Miles Killebrew. All had different tenures in Detroit, but it will be an opportunity for all to make a statement against their former team.
Lions quarterback Jared Goff had been playing at an MVP-caliber level with zero interceptions through the first six games of the year. However, those fortunes have changed over the past three weeks.
Goff has thrown a total of four picks in that stretch, including two last week against the Patriots. One of those picks was an especially devastating mistake, as he was picked off in the end-zone late in the first half. The Buccaneers rank first in the league with 16 interceptions, and as a result Goff will have to be careful against the opportunistic defense.
The Buccaneers have two players that have four interceptions each, those being Anzalone and cornerback Zyon McCollum. Interestingly enough, Robinson has two interceptions from the defensive line as well.
The Buccaneers enter Sunday’s game in a dubious situation, in part due to an injury that kept Baker Mayfield out of three games. Tampa Bay currently ranks first in rushing offense led by Bucky Irving’s 825 yards, but ranks last in passing offense.
As a result, the Lions will likely enter Sunday’s game in need of a plan for stifling the run game and forcing Tampa Bay to throw. They have talent on the perimeter, with Irving serving as a receiving threat in addition to Emeka Egbuka, Tez Johnson and Chris Godwin, but Mayfield’s injuries have prevented them from getting going consistently.
The Lions will be without defensive end Aidan Hutchinson for the remainder of the season, which is a devastating blow to a defense that is already without another one of its leaders in linebacker Jack Campbell.
Hutchinson's injury will likely create opportunities for rookie Derrick Moore, who is on a hot streak with four sacks in his last two games. Additionally, it appears that this is paving the way for Ahmed Hassanein to make his debut.
Detroit has gotten plenty of pass-rush production from its other options, including Alim McNeill and DJ Wonnum. Hutchinson will by no means be easy to replace, but the team has options available to help them produce and pressure opposing passers.
The Lions will wear their black alternate uniforms for the second time this season, and the seventh time in total since they re-entered the rotation prior to the 2024 season. Detroit is 5-1 all-time wearing these uniforms, with the lone loss coming to Buffalo late in the 2024 campaign.
Detroit wore these in their most recent matchup with the Buccaneers, that being on Monday Night Football in Week 7 of last year. That was the ‘Legion of Whom?’ game, where Detroit’s secondary stifled Tampa Bay despite being without multiple starters.
Now, as Detroit looks to extend its winning streak to six games this year, they’ll be hoping to get more magic from their ‘Motor City Muscle’ uniforms.
All indications point to defensive end Ahmed Hassanein making his NFL debut on Sunday. It has been a bit of a tumultuous road to get there for the Boise State product, but it appears as though he’ll get his chance after being inactive for the team’s first nine games.
Hassanein was set to make the team as a rookie last year, but suffered an injury late in the preseason and was waived with an injury designation. At the conclusion of his injury settlement, he returned to Detroit on the practice squad but did not appear in a game.
After signing a futures contract to return, Hassanein made the team out of camp but has yet to appear in a game. Now, the motivated defender will get his chance to make an impact for the first time in his career against the Buccaneers.
The Lions remain focused on the task at hand with a big game looming on a short week and handle business. They batter Tampa Bay’s top-tier run defense, as the offensive line shines with the play of interior linemen Tate Ratledge and Christian Mahogany setting the tone.
Jared Goff doesn’t fall victim to Tampa’s opportunistic secondary, as he delivers a pair of touchdown strikes in the first half. The Buccaneers threaten with late momentum, but the Lions never lose control and win comfortably.
With that Bears game on the horizon and coming off an international trip, the Lions could fall victim to a trap game. This Buccaneers team is better than their record indicates, and can challenge Detroit’s secondary with their array of weapons.
In a worst-case scenario, former Lion Alex Anzalone picks off Jared Goff and returns it for an early score. Al-Quadin Muhammad gets a sack, and Ifeatu Melifonwu makes a big play as well. On defense, the absence of Aidan Hutchinson is felt immensely as the Lions can't corral the quarterback.
Detroit is dominated by its former players, and their hopes of earning the No. 1 seed take a big hit ahead of the crucial matchup with Chicago.
If the Lions are going to win this game, they’re going to have to do it with Jared Goff making big plays through the air. Tampa Bay’s run defense is right up there with the best in the league, and defensive-minded head coach Todd Bowles will have a good plan for Jahmyr Gibbs. My bold prediction is Gibbs is held under 100 all-purpose yards, which forces Goff to have to make big plays with his arm to help the offense be successful.

title: Aidan Hutchinson Makes Clear Decision Regarding Future Celebrations
full_text:
Detroit Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson took to social media to react to his season-ending ACL injury.
Unfortunately for the former first-round pick, the injury suffered was self-induced, jumping in celebration early in the game against the New England Patriots.
Hutchinson expressed he has celebrated in that fashion many times, but now that he is facing months of grueling rehabilitation for another significant injury, he has made the decision to stop celebrating by leaping in the air.
Here is what Hutchinson shared on social media:
"I honestly can’t believe it. I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me.
But even something like this won’t hold me back.
I can ask why over and over again, but it’ll never make sense. All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why and I trust in Him.
Very grateful for all of your prayers and well wishes.
Two things I know for sure: 1. I always come back stronger. 2. That’s the last time I go airborne
Hold down the fort til I’m back, boys."
Kelvin Sheppard, Detroit's second-year defensive coordinator, is now tasked again with figuring out how to navigate the remainder of the season after losing a star defender.
Just recently, lineabcker Jack Campbell was placed on the injured reserve after suffering a neck injury at Ford Field.
"Kind of the elephant in the room is, we lost another one of our captains on Sunday due to a very unfortunate incident," said Sheppard. "So, I'll just put it out there right now, the same thing I told the unit when we met yesterday, that there's no replacing Aidan Hutchinson. And that's not just in this building, that's in this league. I think he's the best defensive end and edge player in this league. He's the best I've ever played with. He's the best I've ever coached. He's the best I've ever seen with my two eyes. That's just my small, humble opinion.
"That's what I've always thought of Hutch and he knows that. The person that he is, the player that is, he's everything that you want in a man," Sheppard continued. "The way he goes about his day, the way he goes about life, it's a lot more than just football that we'll miss with losing his presence, but now there's weight. And what we can't do is think one person is going to carry that weight or think who's going to be the guy. It's going to take all 11 to pick up a little piece of that weight and then I believe we all can be able to carry it."

title: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions could be facing a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team devoid of two of its top players: QB Baker Mayfield (foot injury) and S Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle).
Mayfield has had a rough start to the 2026 campaign with more interceptions (four) than passing touchdowns (three). However, he's still a better option under center than undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who took first-team reps in practice Wednesday for the Buccaneers.
Daniels, who has already started three games this season due to injury issues for Mayfield, has also thrown for more interceptions (five) than touchdowns (three).
Tampa Bay subsequently has not been very proficient through the air this season. In fact, Todd Bowles’ squad ranks league worst in several passing categories: attempts (240), yards (1,277) and touchdowns (six).
Meanwhile, on defense, Winfield is one of the Buccaneers’ very best players.
A two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro, the longtime Tampa Bay defender has been especially stout against the run in 2026. The 2020 second-round pick has earned an 85.5 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the run, the 13th-best run-defense mark among 100 qualified safeties.
Additionally, he hasn't been too shabby against the pass, and has allowed just five receptions all season. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties.
Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday.
As for the Lions, they will be down two of their defensive captains and very best players in Week 11: LB Jack Campbell (neck) and EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (ACL). Hutchinson has already been ruled out for the rest of the season, while Campbell is highly unlikely to suit up again in 2026.
Detroit, however, is getting back its All-Pro safety for its tilt with Tampa Bay: Kerby Joseph. Joseph – who was activated off the physically unable to perform list Wednesday – hasn't played a single snap since Week 6 of the 2025 season due to a lingering knee issue.
Per Lions head man Dan Campbell, Joseph will be on a “pitch count” Sunday, but is still expected to log more snaps than fellow safety Brian Branch did when he returned from his Achilles’ tear earlier this season. Branch played 45 total defensive snaps in his season debut in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers.
Prior to Joseph's chronic knee ailment , he was a ball-hawk safety. In 55 career games, he's secured 20 interceptions, including a league-high nine during his All-Pro campaign in 2024. If he can come even remotely close to replicating that level of production, he'll provide a big boost to the back-end of the Lions’ defense.
At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 76 percent chance to capture the Week 11 victory.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 Midseason Grades: Defense
full_text:
Early in the season, many were concerned about the longevity of the Detroit Lions ' defense.
Through four games, the defense had been one of the league's worst. They ranked near the bottom of the league in many major categories, and had been exposed in the team's two losses.
However, things have changed for the better in part thanks to improved play in the secondary, as well as a pass-rush that ranks third in the league in sacks. There are a pair of major injuries that they will need to overcome moving forward, but the group has changed the outside tune with its performance as of late.
Here are grades for each position group based on performance through the Lion
The defensive line has been a pleasant surprise throughout the first nine games of the year. Aidan Hutchinson was every bit the dominant force he was expected to be, but unfortunately suffered a season-ending knee injury last week that the unit will have to overcome.
Fortunately, the Lions appear to be better suited to handle his absence than they were when he suffered a season-ending injury two seasons ago. Alim McNeill is playing at a potential All-Pro level, as he leads the team with 6.5 sacks rushing from the interior.
McNeill, an explosive and athletic force, has the rare ability to blend both run defense and pass-rush within his snaps, and as a result has become an every down player for the defense. DJ Wonnum has also been a nice complementary piece to Hutchinson, as he's notched six sacks playing on the opposite side.
It's also been noteworthy to see the performance of rookie Skyler Gill-Howard, who was initially viewed as an afterthought when the Lions drafted him in the sixth-round. However, he has proven to have the necessary chops as a pass-rusher and has owned his opportunities.
2025 first-round pick Tyleik Williams has taken on a bigger role this year, as he has essentially replaced DJ Reader and Roy Lopez as the team's nose tackle.
With Hutchinson out, the Lions will likely be giving Ahmed Hassanein an opportunity this week which will be intriguing. Hassanein showed plenty of flashes in the preseason, and could give the defense a huge spark if that performance carries into the regular season.
Detroit also brought back Tyrus Wheat via a waiver claim, who appeared in 15 games for the team a season ago.
The linebacking corps has been on a bit of an adventure through the first nine games. There's plenty of talent in the room, even with Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder out for the remainder of the year. Still, there have been some struggles particularly in pass coverage.
When healthy, Campbell started the year struggling but had been playing well as of late when he suffered the scary neck injury. Rolder, meanwhile, was just coming into his own after starting the year as a healthy scratch when he went down.
Devin White, who the team signed during training camp, is also sidelined currently with a forearm injury. That injury, however, is not expected to sideline him for the remainder of the season.
Derrick Barnes has anchored the group, and is having one of his best seasons as a pro. He has had some struggles in coverage, but has contributed as a pass-rusher and handled his assignments well in the run game.
With Campbell out, the Lions have relied more on Malcolm Rodriguez. The veteran has been reliable as a spot starter in the past and has lived up to that billing this year. Trevor Nowaske has served as the third linebacker, with Joe Bachie, Amen Ogbongbemiga and newly acquired K.J. Britt also contributing snaps.
After four games, the secondary did not earn high marks. However, they seem to have found a bit of a groove that could be attributed to the return of Brian Branch. The Alabama product came back after the bye, and has been a stabilizing force for a group that dealt with a number of injuries early in the year.
D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin began the year as the starting corners, but Roger McCreary soon earned more snaps after outplaying Ya-Sin. McCreary has been one of the team's best free agent adds, and notched his first pick of the season last week against New England.
With Reed out the last two weeks, Ya-Sin has re-entered the starting lineup. Detroit relied on a rotation of cornerbacks that also featured Khalil Dorsey and Ennis Rakestraw when all were healthy, but the snap counts from last week could suggest that the rotation is thinning out.
At safety, the Lions had to overcome being without Branch and Kerby Joseph at the beginning of the year. Chuck Clark has been solid, and the team leaned on rookie Keith Abney II after losing both Avonte Maddox and Thomas Harper to injured reserve early in the year.
With Branch and Joseph both back , it will be interesting to see where Abney and newly acquired safety Andre Cisco fit within the defensive scheme. Regardless, the safety room is healthy for the first time all year, and it could give the defense a big boost moving forward.
