title: Texans Have Two Offensive Injuries to Monitor After TNF Win
full_text:
The Houston Texans put together a commanding win over the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night en route to a 26-3 victory that might just be the spark needed to help this team rattle off a few wins in a row through the second half of their season.
However, in the midst of the Texans winning effort over the Colts, the team also saw their offense suffer a pair of injuries that will be worth keeping an eye on as they approach their next matchup.
According to an update from the Texans during Thursday night's game, wide receiver Kayshon Boutte (hip) and offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge (stinger) would be deemed questionable for a return in the fourth quarter.
. @ShariffLawFirm Texans Injury Update: #14 WR Kayshon Boutte is questionable with a hip injury. #66 C/G Keylan Rutledge is questionable with a stinger.
We ultimately wound up seeing neither return to the action. But given that the Texans were so close to ending the game, it's unclear as to whether or not either player was dealing with a serious injury issue, or were simply being held out for precautionary reasons as the result of the game had already been decided.
However, seeing both Boutte and Rutledge go down with an injury––each of whom has their respective key roles on the Texans' offense––is less than an ideal end to an overall successful night for Houston altogether.
One of these injuries has been an issue the Texans have already seen surface earlier in the month, and that's the stinger that Rutledge suffered that makes for his second stinger in the past two weeks.
The first stinger for Rutledge was bad enough that it led to him being sidelined for an entire week of the Texans' team practice , along with missing Week 10's game against the Cleveland Browns, forcing fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu into his first-ever start.
Rutledge was cleared to return on a short week against the Colts, but now after the same injury has surfaced once again, there might be a slim chance that Houston's first-round rookie is set to miss a little more time moving forward.
As for Boutte, his hip injury seems to be a new issue to surface throughout Thursday night, which turned out to be a pretty successful night on his behalf.
Boutte converted on both of his targets against the Colts for two catches, 40 yards, and an aggressive touchdown reception in the second quarter for C.J. Stroud's second of three touchdown passes on the night––making for his second game on the season where he's seen over 40 yards in a single game.
If Boutte is forced to miss any time, it'd mark yet another injury to the Texans’ wide receiver room following up on Jaylin Noel's injured reserve designation before Week 8 , along with the recent absence of Marvin Harrison Jr., which has led to him missing the last two games against the Browns and the Colts.
The good news surrounding both of these injuries is that the Texans are able to get a mini-bye at their disposal before they're tasked with taking on their Week 13 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
That means, for both Boutte and Rutledge, they'll have a little over a week to rest and prepare for their next game on the schedule, which could be just what each needs to get back on the field in time for this coming Sunday.
But for now, Houston's stuck in a bit of wait-and-see mode on the status of both until they're back in the building later next week.

title: What C.J. Stroud's Recent Hot Streak Means for His Contract Extension
full_text:
The Houston Texans have been witnessing some stellar play from C.J. Stroud over the first half of the regular season.
Really, it's been the best we've seen from the Texans' signal-caller since he broke out onto the scene during his rookie season .
Through the first 10 games of the year, Stroud has been averaging over 265 yards per game, completing 64% of his passes, and perhaps most impressively, is on pace to shatter his career-best touchdown-to-interception ratio as he's recorded 22 touchdowns to just four total picks.
Coming off of his last two up-and-down seasons of production, it's certainly a breath of fresh air for both the Texans and Stroud to be taking in––and especially so for Stroud himself, who's all but certain to cash in on a lucrative contract extension after holding off on a new deal this past offseason.
When Stroud was in talks of getting a big-time contract extension earlier this offseason , the general consensus remained that the Texans quarterback was due to get a noteworthy bump in pay if he decided to sign a deal before the season started.
That expected bump in pay seemed pretty certain even after Stroud's abysmal playoff exit against the New England Patriots , in which he recorded a haunting four interceptions in the first half en route to a haunting 16-28 loss in the divisional round.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and D.J. Bien-Aime , the Texans offered Stroud a deal "well within the $50 million-per-year club" when negotiations were ongoing; an offer that was considered to be a pretty strong effort, but still left Houston's signal-caller holding off on signing, and betting on himself to boost that value even further.
Fast forward to Week 11 of the season, and it seems as if Stroud's managed to do just that, plus more––to the point where it's not hard to imagine the Texans quarterback's value shooting up past those prior projections in the range of $60 million annually.
Stroud's going to find himself as one of the NFL's highest paid players if he keeps up this level of production. When combining the nature of quarterback contracts, along with the ever-appreciating value of those deals, the stage is set for Stroud to cash in.
Right now, eight quarterbacks in the NFL have an average contract value of $55 million or higher. Only two have values that reach $60 million or higher: that's Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, and Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott.
If Stroud keeps up the same momentum he's on right now by performing as one of the best quarterbacks in the league, there's little reason to believe that he can't join that exclusive club of netting $60-plus million annually on his next deal.
And that's especially so when factoring in that Stroud won't be the only big-time quarterback negotiating for a new deal this summer. Many high-end starting signal-callers are up for a fresh context as well.
Caleb Williams, Drake Maye, Jayden Daniels, and Bo Nix will all be eligible for some pretty sizable deals themselves. And the larger their respective contracts get, the same will likely happen for the Texans' quarterback as well.
Now, the landscape of Stroud's value could certainly shift significantly from where things currently stand. There's still seven weeks to go before the regular season wraps up, and that doesn't even include the postseason.
It was less than 12 months ago when everybody witnessed Stroud implode in his and the Texans' infamous postseason collapse that made many question whether or not he was the long-term answer at quarterback for the Texans, let alone a massive contract extension like he's expected to see now.
Another similar collapse from Stroud this year–– if Houston makes a late run for the playoffs –– would only spark those conversations around his future and contract value once again, and make those discussions on a new deal even more complicated than they once were.
But as Stroud currently sits, thanks to some MVP-level production through 10 games of this season, all signs are pointing towards him seeing a nice raise come his way at some point over the course of next offseason.
And based on how the Texans have leaned on him and their offense through their turbulent first half of the season, there's little reason to think that Houston will have no choice but to open the checkbook and pay their quarterback what we want to keep him around for the long haul.

title: Everything Texans QB C.J. Stroud Said After 3-TD Performance vs. Colts
full_text:
The Houston Texans took care of business in their Thursday Night Football showing over the Indianapolis Colts in a dominant 26-3 victory.
And in the process of the Texans' primetime win, we saw C.J. Stroud have a pretty impressive performance from start to finish: completing 21 of his 27 passes, throwing for 194 yards, three touchdowns, and one pick to make for only his fourth interception on the year thus far.
Let's take a look at six of the most notable quotes from Stroud's post-game presser after the win that now takes Houston to a 4-6 record with just seven games to go on the season:
While Stroud had an impressive game individually, he made sure to not go without highlighting how their Will Anderson performed in one of his best games of the season : coming away with a sack, a safety, and a season-high 37.5% pressure rate with seven pressures and four quick pressures.
"Will is a dog, man. He's the definition of what you want for a Texan. I know DeMeco loves him. I know the ownership loves him. He just works super hard. He doesn't complain. He gets put in tough spots," Stroud said of Anderson.
"Just his tenacity. I think he just brings a swag to this team that I'm just proud to call him my brother. A lot of time spent together, so just really proud of him and what he's been able to do, and his faith. And also his family, being able to be an anchor there. So, big fan of Will for life."
Texans' C.J. Stroud after Will Anderson's performance against the Colts: 🗣️ "Will is a dog, man. He's the definition of what you want for a Texan." "I know DeMeco loves him. I know the ownership loves him. He just works super hard... Big fan of Will for life." pic.twitter.com/8lUGJ9REFJ
During the first half, Stroud's most glaring error from the night would be inevitably followed by one of his best plays–– as the Texans quarterback would come off of his only interception on the night to send a bomb of a touchdown pass to Nico Collins in the first two drives of the game.
Stroud said after that interception on the first drive, he went to the sidelines, worked on his footwork, then came out a bit more recalibrated to go and allow Collins to make a big play.
"I think because on the last drive, I kind of had something similar. I didn't get touched, but I just didn't put enough on it, and then it ended up being an interception," Stroud said. "I know I can make that throw, but I think being Thursday night, I needed to get my juices going a little more. I think that was a perfect example of that."
"I went back to the sideline and started doing a little bit of footwork that I knew I needed to get more oomph on the ball, more power... That play was great. I thought Nico did a good job attacking the high point. He's a heck of a football player. So if you give him a shot, he's going to make a play."
C.J. Stroud breaking down his TD throw to Nico Collins last night vs. the Colts: 🗣️ "That play was great. I thought Nico did a good job attacking the high point." "He's a heck of a football player. So if you give him a shot, he's going to make a play." https://t.co/ffWIT8Njbn pic.twitter.com/aDLvKAS7gE
Stroud is now putting together one of the best stretches of games we've seen from him dating back to his rookie year. On his current pace, he's set to total over 4,500 passing yards on the season, with 37 passing touchdowns.
Especially after the ups and downs he's faced over the past two years, Stroud is grateful to be in the spot that he is now, not only performing as well as he has been, but also playing alongside this Texans team.
"Ever since I've been a rookie, honestly, when I started playing, I knew what type of player I could be in this league. Just to get on that groove and have a rhythm has been amazing. Honestly, I would be lying to you if I said it didn't feel good," Stroud said.
"I'm very grateful for this opportunity to even play in the NFL. People probably think I'm crazy for always saying that, but I really did not expect my life to be like this. It's nothing but the grace of God that I'm sitting up here and playing the way that I am."
"It's nothing but credit to the team. The way the defense prepared us in training camp, the way the O-linemen are blocking their tails off and giving me a shot, and the way the receivers have been running their routes and getting open. I'm just super grateful to play on a team like this. I don't take it for granted at all."
Along with a strong night from Stroud, the Texans' offense was also able to witness an impressive stat line from David Montgomery, who saw his first 100-yard game on the ground in over a year, which also came in his first appearance on the field for Houston since Week 5 because of a groin injury.
Stroud says he was talking to Montgomery all week, trying to get him fired up for a good showing on Thursday. Clearly, that strategy proved to be an effective one.
"He's a baller, bro," Stroud said of Montgomery. "I've been motivating him all week, just talking mess to him and trying to get him going. He responds in the best ways. He's been making plays since I've been in the league and even before that. I'm super proud of that guy, and I think he'll continue to do great things for us."
"We were definitely missing him, and hopefully we get Woody [Marks] back next week. That'll be great."
C.J. Stroud on David Montgomery's 100-plus rushing yards against the Colts: 🗣️ "I've been motivating him all week, just talking mess to him, just trying to get him going. He responds in the best ways." "Just to give him an opp tonight, man, I'm super proud of that guy." pic.twitter.com/YcSSO3cOBl
The Texans' defense turned things around in a big way against the Colts compared to their lowly performance from last weekend against the Cleveland Browns . Houston allowed just three points and less than 200 yards to Indianapolis on the night; their second time doing so this season.
Stroud––who faces off against the Texans' defense more than anyone in weekly practices––knew that Houston was more than capable of turning things around on that side of the ball. He also emphasized that this roster should carry themselves "as one" rather than dividing the credit or blame to one side of the football.
"If anybody has respect, hope and faith in our defense, it's me. I get to play against them on a day-to-day basis," Stroud said.
"I don't rock with the whole winning-waves thing and how people change their opinions because you can flip it on its head, have a great game and everybody flips their mindset. I'm all about the process. What is your process? I think their process has been great. I think it's getting better. I honestly think they're great, and I'm just super happy to have them."
"It's not always perfect. Last year, they held us down as an offense a lot. When it flip-flops, we're not complaining. We're a team. We're one. That's something I've been trying to preach. We're not defense and offense. I don't think that talk is good for our team. We're one."

Stroud also didn't leave his post-game presser without showing some support for the Texans' fanbase, who have stuck by him and the team throughout the ups and downs of the season, and finally saw that rewarded on Thursday in the form of their first home win since Week 18 of last season.
And while Stroud loves the support from the Texans' fans, he certainly believes that he and the rest of the team have more to show them over the course of their second-half stretch of the season:
"One thing I love about our fans, even though it might not be all of them, is that there are a select few people who are always encouraging me and telling me how much they have my back, no matter what I go through. I'm really appreciative of that."

title: Texans' Will Anderson Builds DPOY Momentum With Huge TNF Showing
full_text:
Heading into the Houston Texans' Thursday Night Football matchup vs. the Indianapolis Colts, All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. was already putting together what's been unquestionably his best season since entering the league in 2023.
He was leading the league in quarterback pressures, had claimed the lead as the NFL sack leader with 10.5 takedowns through nine games, and had already been gaining some steam as the potential frontrunner to watch for this year's Defensive Player of the Year award.
But after Anderson's dominant performance over the Colts en route to a 26-3 win, it's now become pretty tough to argue against anyone but the Texans' star edge rusher to be worthy of the award––at least at this point in the season.
Anderson–– in a game he was forced to take on without his star counterpart on the defensive line in Danielle Hunter due to a hamstring injury –– he took it upon himself to claim total control of the Colts' offensive line for one of his best performances of the season so far.
On just 36 total defensive snaps, his lowest of the season, Anderson put together some insane stats.
He tied his season-high in pressures with nine (and quick pressures with four), had his third straight game with at least one sack, paired with five tackles and four stops, and a season-high 37.5% pressure rate.
On top of those eye-catching numbers, Anderson also found his way to his first career safety on his one sack of the night against Daniel Jones in the second half.
Essentially, Anderson's night can be summed up like this: he was a problem for the Colts' backup tackles, got to the quarterback an excessive amount, and he even accounted for a couple of points in a game where he saw his lowest snap count of the season.
That's Defensive Player of the Year stuff right there. And now, Anderson is able to walk away from this week having only extended his lead as the NFL's leader in total pressures and sacks from where it was before Thursday night.
Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans praised Anderson's performance after the win , highlighting not just this particular game, but also how he's taken on this season as a whole.
“Will has a significant impact on our team, not only by the way he plays, but also by the way he leads," Ryans said. "He's one of the best players I've been around, both as a player and as a person. You couldn't find a better guy."
"I'm happy for the season he's having and proud of the way he continues to work, remain relentless and represent the way we need him to. He's having an outstanding year, and good things are coming his way.”
Could those "good things" Ryan’s mentions consist of some end-of-season hardware coming his way? If the season were to end today, it's hard to make the claim that he wouldn't be the guy to circle as most deserving.
The proof for Anderson's strengthened Defensive Player of the Year case doesn't come by just looking at the stats. Betting odds have clearly shifted in one clear direction as well.
According to odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , Anderson is squarely in front to win the award, with -160 odds of doing so, while no other defender is within reach of +500 odds or less.
The closest name within reach of Anderson is Minnesota Vikings edge rusher Dallas Turner, who currently sits with +550 odds. Fred Warner sits at +700, while Jeffery Simmons is just narrowly in the hunt at +900.
However, if the Texans continue to win some games as they look capable of doing, while Anderson keeps playing at this type of rate, it'll be pretty tough for anyone to uproot him from the status as the odds-on favorite over the next seven weeks.
For now, Anderson gets the benefit of resting on a mini-bye after a much-needed Thursday night victory , while also sitting atop the sack and pressures leaderboards among the rest of the league's pass-rushers.
It's a pretty good spot for Anderson to be, all things considered, even as the Texans sit at a 4-6 record with much more work to do.

title: Texans' Biggest Winners and Losers From One-Sided Win vs. Colts
full_text:
The Houston Texans put together a nice win over their division rival Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night for a pretty one-sided affair, 26-3, that now leaves Houston with a 4-6 record with just seven weeks to go in the season.
And in the midst of the Texans' dominant win in Reliant Stadium, there were several players from Houston's side who stuck out with a big individual performance for one reason or another.
There were also a handful of names from the Texans who didn't quite see the amount of opportunities they would've liked. And even in a winning effort, they might've been a part of a game scripy that didn't exactly pan out in a way that helps their stock much moving forward.
With that in mind, let's take a look at some of the Texans' biggest winners and losers from their Thursday Night Football win over the Colts, allowing them to split their season series with Indianapolis 1-1.
After missing the last three weeks due to a groin injury , Montgomery burst onto the scene against the Colts to put together what could be his best game in a Texans uniform, if not, second to his three-touchdown debut against the Buffalo Bills.
Montgomery had a season-high 26 carries, his first game with 100-plus rushing yards in over a year, and he averaged a little over four yards per carry. It was a much-needed strong day for the Texans' rushing offense that came even without Woody Marks being part of the equation.
The Texans' second-round tight end had been mostly a non-factor in the weekly game plan leading up to this matchup , but Klein turned in his best performance as a pro by far as Houston finally made it a priority to get him on the field.
He saw four receptions for 24 yards, and turned in one of those looks for a 13-yard touchdown reception from C.J. Stroud. It's hard to imagine the Texans don't continue to get Klein involved after a display like this one.
It was yet another game from Anderson Jr. in which he looked like a real frontrunner to come away with this season's Defensive Player of the Year award . Not only did he claim a season-high 37.5% pressure rate against the Colts and their offensive line, but he also took home his first career safety stemming from a second half sack on Daniel Jones.
Despite not having his veteran counterpart, Danielle Hunter, lining up on the other side of the line, Anderson made sure to make his impact felt as the All-Pro he was selected to be last season, and one of the league's best pass-rushers out there.
In a year that the Texans' secondary as a whole hasn't quite been as active when it comes to hauling in interceptions like they were last season, Kamari Lassiter finally got on the board with his first pick of the season thanks to an errant throw from Daniel Jones coming towards the end of the first half.
Lassiter hasn't had a perfect 2026 campaign, but he's finally begun to turn the ship around over the past few weeks. Against the Colts, he allowed zero catches on his six total targets; the second time this season where he's allowed zero yards in coverage.
As Marlin Klein finally came alive in this game, while Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau retained their respective roles, it's left Cade Stover appearing to be the odd man out in the Texans' tight end room when it comes to getting snaps and opportunities.
Stover saw zero snaps on the offensive side of the ball, only seeing 14 looks his way on special teams. And based on the game that Klein put together, Stover might be facing an uphill climb to get those looks to come back his way––especially once Brevin Jordan is back healthy from his foot injury.
Now, Brown did seem to suffer a back injury early in this game that limited him from start to finish, and ultimately led to the Texans rolling out Braden Smith as their primary right tackle. However, DeMeco Ryans also made it clear during his postgame presser that the plan was to rotate both Brown and Smith when both were healthy.
That means, for as rock-solid as Brown's starting spot on the right side of the line has been this season, there's a good chance that Smith will overtake his duties once hitting Week 12, regardless of whether or not Brown is at 100% from his back issue.
Another name in the Texans' lineup who was seemingly benched in this game was veteran safety M.J. Stewart. News surfaced before the game that Reed Blankenship would be expected to take Houston's starting safety role next to Calen Bullock, and that's exactly what we saw happen.
And Blankenship played relatively well, only allowing two receptions for 27 yards on his four total targets. There's a good chance his status as a starter carries over moving forward, while leaving Stewart in the backup role he once had earlier this year.

title: 5 Key Quotes From Texans' DeMeco Ryans After 26-3 Win Over Colts
full_text:
The Houston Texans claimed a much-needed win over the Indianapolis Colts under the lights of Thursday Night Football, leading to a dominant 26-3 victory that takes them to 4-6 on the year.
And after the game, we were able to hear a bit from Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans and his thoughts for how his team performed in a game that felt pretty one-sided once escaping the first quarter.
LetLet's take a look at five key quotes from Ryans' postgame presser that stuck out more than the rest:
It was an impressive night for the Texans' defense as a whole. But All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson certainly had a strong performance individually , where he saw a 37.5% pressure rate, a sack, and his first-career safety from that second half sack on Daniel Jones.
SAFETY. WILL ANDERSON JR. IS A MONSTER. INDvsHOU on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/E7sYceCOiZ
After the game, Ryans praised Anderson's intensity and leadership––going as far as to call him one of the best players he's ever been around.
“Will has a significant impact on our team, not only by the way he plays, but also by the way he leads," Ryans said. "What you see on game day is what you see every day. The intensity he represents, he shows in practice and in the meeting room. He's one of the best players I've been around, both as a player and as a person. You couldn't find a better guy."
"I'm happy for the season he's having and proud of the way he continues to work, remain relentless and represent the way we need him to. He's having an outstanding year, and good things are coming his way.”
Kamari Lassiter claimed his first interception of the season in the first half from an errant Daniel Jones pass; a nice moment for the Texans corner who's seen his share of ups and downs through the first half of the season.
Lassiter picks off Jones. Texans ball. INDvsHOU on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QNivTHRyr9
Ryans highlighted Lassiter's performance from the last three weeks, which resulted in a big play coming to fruition on Thursday night.
“Over the past three weeks, Kamari has played really great football. He's been locked in, being where he's supposed to be, playing with the right technique and proper leverage. He makes the plays he's supposed to make, and he just has to continue doing that," Ryans said.
"Don't put too much pressure on himself. Just go out and execute how he knows how to execute, play his style, which we all love, and he'll make the plays. I'm happy for him to finally get that interception today.”
Despite the Texans noting earlier in the week that they had not planned to make an offensive line change , Houston's front did look different on Thursday night as Braden Smith would be elevated to their starting right tackle in place of Trent Brown.
Ryans said postgame that the plan was to rotate Smith and Brown, but Brown suffered a back injury that limited his night.
“We'll look at the film and see how it went, but I thought we were moving the line of scrimmage really well," Ryans said of the offensive line performance. "Braden got in there. We planned to rotate Braden and Trent, but Trent ended up leaving the game for a little while with back spasms. We'll see how he does throughout next week.”
With three touchdowns and just six incompletions throughout the night, it was another game where C.J. Stroud really shined in what's looked to be his best individual season since his rookie campaign back in 2023.
Ryans says that such production is a product of the work that he put in this past offseason .
“C.J. is producing the way he is because of the work he put in throughout the offseason. All of that is paying dividends now," Ryans said of Stroud. "He's been ready for these moments, and he's executing at a high level, scoring the points we need to score and making the plays we need to make."
"He's keeping the offense on the field and making great decisions with the football, which is probably what I'm most proud of. It was also good to see him bounce back after throwing an interception and making a bad play. Seeing him respond positively and continue to lead the offense down the field to score was great to see.”
In a long-awaited moment for Texans fans, second round rookie Marlin Klein finally saw his first career touchdown reception come to form in the third quarter thanks to a 13-yard red zone completion from Stroud.
Stroud finds German TE Marlin Klein for six! @nfldeutschland INDvsHOU on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fS7L7wS8O3
Ryans said after the game that Klein was headed in the right direction, and praised the multiple good catches he made en route to his best game of the season with four receptions and 24 yards.
“It's good to get Marlin in there. He's a young player, and we're getting him reps and allowing him to get better," Ryans said. "He needed to get out there and play to continue improving. He made a lot of good catches for us, including a third-down conversion, and it was great for everybody to see him get his first touchdown."
"He's headed in the right direction. We'll continue working with him and allowing him to get better. He's showing up big time for us and putting points on the board.”

title: 3 Biggest Takeaways From Texans' Dominating TNF Win Over Colts
full_text:
The Houston Texans managed to claim a much-needed win over the Indianapolis Colts during their primetime matchup on Thursday night, as they rallied to a 26-3 victory on their home field in Reliant Stadium.
And really, things were clicking for the Texans in several ways in this one.
The offense was flowing smoothly for all four quarters and only incurred one turnover. The defense stepped up, allowing just three points and 167 total yards. And even special teams had a couple of highlights of note, thanks to a 56-yard punt from Kai Kroeger and a blocked field goal by Dominique Robinson.
However, when sorting through the events of the Texans' Week 11 win over Indianapolis that now takes them to 4-6 on the season, the following three takeaways tend to stick out a bit more than the rest:
The Texans defense certainly looked a lot better in this game compared to some of their previous showings this season–– and a huge part of that success was thanks to Will Anderson Jr.'s impressive performance upfront on Houston's defensive line.
Anderson didn't just claim the first safety of his NFL career thanks to a sack on Daniel Jones in the second half, but he also found his way to a resoundingly seven pressures and four quarterback hits against the Colts' beaten-up offensive line.
SAFETY. WILL ANDERSON JR. IS A MONSTER. INDvsHOU on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/E7sYceCOiZ
Anderson has now only extended his lead as the NFL's sack leader on the year with 11.5 takedowns, and he now looks to be a pretty clear favorite to come away from this season with a Defensive Player of the Year award, if he keeps up this type of production.
C.J. Stroud did have a blip on the radar in the form of a first-half interception from a questionable throw turned to a deflection into Colts safety A.J. Haulcy's hands. But outside of that one throw, it's really had to knock Stroud for the performance he had leading the way for this Texans offense.
Stroud completed 21 of his 27 throws for 194 yards and three touchdowns, spreading the ball around to nine different pass-catchers, led by Nico Collins' three receptions for 58 yards, along with yet another stellar downfield touchdown reception for his seventh score on the season.
This is an objectively insane throw from Stroud pic.twitter.com/ldHehDa2Qg
It's yet another performance from Stroud that cements him as the Texans' long-term guy under center, and continues to boost his value heading into his contract negotiations later this summer . And with more games like these, Houston putting together a few wins in a row during the second half of the season becomes a bit more possible to believe in.
In a game where the Texans were forced to move forward without their starting running back, Woody Marks, due to a concussion, David Montgomery returned to the lineup, where he put together his best performance since his Week 1 hat trick against the Buffalo Bills .
Montgomery came away with a season-high 26 carries for 107 yards on the ground (4.1 yards per carry), while also chipping in for three receptions and 17 yards–– making for just his third game since 2024 where he's recorded over 120 yards from scrimmage.
Texans were happy to see David Montgomery get 107 rushing yards in his first game back from a groin injury in week 5 ❤️ #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/desO0N6bk8
Really, he looked much more explosive and efficient compared to what's been seen over the course of his first year in Houston. The Texans dominated this game in several areas, but Montgomery's ability to be a consistent force on the ground certainly allowed them to maintain the lead and overall control down the stretch.

title: Texans Announce 7 Inactives Ahead of TNF vs. Colts
full_text:
The Houston Texans' Week 11 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts sits right around the corner, as these two teams will be facing off for the second time this season under the primetime lights of Thursday Night Football .
And leading up to the Texans' Thursday night action, they, along with the Colts, have released their official list of inactives just ahead of kickoff. For Houston, they'll be without ––––– players as they try and claim their fourth victory of the year, while splitting their season series against Indianapolis at an even 1-1.
Let's take a look at who's set to be out for the Texans and Colts for this matchup, and what those absences could mean for the night ahead:
RB Woody Marks WR Marvin Harrison Jr. OL Nate Thomas OL Jake Andrews OL Wyatt Teller DE Danielle Hunter TE Brevin Jordan
The Texans will be without a handful of impactful pieces within their lineup against Indianapolis, but most of those absences are for names that had already been ruled out on Houston's injury report following their final walkthrough on Wednesday.
Woody Marks will miss out on the action due to a concussion he sustained last weekend against the Cleveland Browns, and will thus leave David Montgomery to take the lead in the Texans' backfield for his first game back from injury since Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans . Emari Demercado will operate as Houston's primary backup.
Marvin Harrison Jr. will miss his second straight game due to a hamstring injury, as will star defensive end Danielle Hunter. As for who will step up to replace Hunter, expect Jadeveon Clowney to take a vast share of his snaps as the Texans' starting edge next to Will Anderson Jr., just as he was against the Browns.
The Texans will also be without backup tight end Brevin Jordan for a second week, who is still dealing with a lingering foot injury. That means Houston's tight end room will be slimmed down to just four names against the Colts: Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau, Marlin Klein and Cade Stover.
And since the Texans' last injury report, it appears that Wyatt Teller has been downgraded for the night due to a back injury. He had been listed as a full practice participant throughout the entire week heading into Thursday, but regardless, it seems that he won't be suiting up to play.
As for the healthy scratches, both of them reside on the offensive line. Nate Thomas remains off to the side as he still awaits his season debut, while Jake Andrews sticks out as a new addition for this week’s inactives list as well.
CB Sauce Gardner QB Riley Leonard TE Will Mallory OL Bernhard Raimann DT Jerry Tillery OL Jalen Travis CB Charvarius Ward
The Colts will be down a few key names on their side just as the Texans are. A couple of them reside on the offensive line, while two more of them are on the defense.
For one, the Colts will be without both of their usual starting tackles, Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis, opening up a potentially significant opportunity for the Texans' defensive line to expose that mismatch , even without the services of Danielle Hunter.
On the defense, the Colts will be without both of their boundary corners in Sauce Gardner, as he deals with a calf injury, and Charvarius Ward, who was carted off in last weekend's game against the Miami Dolphins due to a knee injury.
Justin Walley will operate as Indianapolis's No. 1 corner, who surprisingly came away with the AFC's Defensive Player of the Week award for last weekend's performance, as he came away with five tackles, two tackles for loss, a couple of passes defended, and a strip-sack fumble for a touchdown.
Kickoff between the Texans and Colts will land at 7:15 p.m. CT, as Houston will be hungry for a bounce-back win on their home field after the events of their Week 10 loss to the Browns.
