title: Jaguars Mailbag: Travis Hunter's Award Race, The Next Moves to Make, and More
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are not just one of the best teams in football in 2026, they are also one of the most interesting. This is not always the case in the NFL, but it certainly is in Duval this season.
Interesting times have the Jaguars sitting at 7-2 before a big road matchup with the Giants, which is when we are set to see the debut of new Jaguars Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates. Add in Trevor Lawrence hitting his peak, Parker Washington's continued big plays, and Travis Hunter's rare feats, and there is a lot to like about the Jaguars right now.
We break all of this down and more in this week's Jaguars mailbag, taking questions on Hunter's award chances , Washington, and much more.
Could Travis Hunter win DPOY?
A: I like where your head is at, even if I think it would still take quite a bit. Cornerbacks do not normally win this award since it is typically reserved for edge defenders and game-wrecking interior defensive linemen. Patrick Surtain II won the award in 2024, Stephon Gilmore won it in 2019, and Charles Woodson won it in 2009. That is just three cornerbacks among the last 17 winners, which means it is a long-shot based on his position alone.
With that said, Hunter has a few things going for him. The fact he plays some offense will likely earn him some added consideration since he is the only defender elibile for the award who is also contributing on offense. Surtain had four interceptions and 11 pass breakups in his award-winning year, and Hunter is on pace to at least match that with three interceptions and seven pass deflections in nine games, so the counting stats could be there. Advanced metrics are also high on Hunter. It also helps he is one of the most popular players in the sport.
Right now, front-runners for Defensive Player of the Year include Will Anderson Jr., Fred Warner, and Jeffery Simmons. There will be a lot of great candidates, Hunter included. If he goes on a complete tear over the second-half, never say never ...
If the Jaguars need outside edge help, who would be the first FA they should look at?
A: If we are talking current free agents as of today off the street, I guess I would say Tyquan Lewis? At least in terms of who would fit the Jaguars. I do not see Leonard Floyd or Haason Reddick as good fits for what the Jaguars like to do on defense. It is slim pickings right now. If we are talking the 2027 free agents, maybe a guy like Myles Murphy?
Why do Parker Washington and BTJ play like they got freaky fridayed at some point?
A: The cool thing about Parker Washington is he has always shown flashes of being able to be this guy. He made some big catches when he was given the chance to as a rookie, then he stepped up the next year when the Jaguars faced injuries. He was also always one of the best players on the practice field. We said during the 2025 training camp that Parker Washington had the best camp of any of the receivers, and eventually the cream rose to the top.
Thomas has never really been a big contested catch guy, even if he has the frame for it. A lot of his big plays have come on vertical routes where he can run by the defense, on hole shots down the sideline, or on drag routes that allow him to get yards after the catch. This was the case for him as a prospect, too. Both are really talented players who just have really different skill-sets.
Who do you expect the Jags to let walk this offseason. Seems like one of our premier players will be gone (i predict ventrell miller will walk)
A: I think Arik Armstead and Ezra Cleveland are set to walk. I also think they will keep both Jessie Bates and Parker Washington for sure. This would leave guys like Antonio Johnson, Ventrell Miller, Davon Hamilton, and then some role player guys like Davon Godchaux, Quintin Morris, Matt Dickerson, and Jahlani Tavai. I think the Jaguars keep most of the role players and 1-2 of the big-named trio after Washington and Bates.
Do you think Jonah Monheim could supplant Robert Hainsey if he plays well? Or would that be something explored in the off-season?
A: I do not think it would be anything that would happen in 2026. Robert Hainsey is a two-time captain for the Jaguars for a reason and if he is healthy, he is going to be in the lineup. With that said, the Jaguars will need to clear cap space ahead of the 2027 offseason and it would make sense to see them use Hainsey's deal to do so entering the final year of his contract. I could very much so see this week, and perhaps the next few, be a bit of an audition for Jonah Monheim. The Jaguars' staff really does like him, and he keeps playing well when called upon.
How good has the defense looked this week and what do you expect from them Sunday?
A: We do not get to see all that much at practices during the regular season. We are out there between 10-20 minutes to see them stretch and do special teams and the start of individual drills, and then that is it. It is not like training camp or the offseason, where we see the entire practice. With that said, I expect a few takeaways against J.J. McCarthy and an improved effort against the run compared to the last two weeks.
Who would you rather potentially face in the playoffs, Denver or Houston?
A: I think Houston is the easier matchup, even with C.J. Stroud playing like a top-10 quarterback and Bo Nix playing like, well, Bo Nix. Denver's defense is the only one that has come close to stopping the Jaguars' offense all season long. I like the Jaguars' defense's chances with a second-shot against the Houston passing offense.
The jags are moving into a weaker part of the schedule moving forward. What are some signs we can look for that this is the Super Bowl caliber team we think it is, rather than a schedule merchant?
A: My question whenever resume questions come up is usually this: which teams are people saying have a strong resume? It is the NFL. All teams play some tough squads and some not-so-tough squads. The balance is rarely 50/50, but simply winning games at any rate in the NFL is important. I think seeing the Jaguars continue to play mostly mistake-free football, regardless of who the foe is, is critical. Keep the turnovers low, work on penalties, and score in the red-zone.
What's going on with Tuten ?
A: I fully expect Bhayshul Tuten to play , even with his injuries. Liam Coen has said that he feels like running backs do not need to practice as much during the week to prepare for a game, and he has been fine with Tuten getting mostly mental reps.
Hunter buzzed the Titans sideline after his INT last week, would that have been flagged by a better crew or in a bigger game? Did the Jags coaches talk to him after?
A: I do not think it had anything to do with the crew or the game. Most penalties only happen if the players involved in these scenarios carry on with the celebration longer than they should. Hunter did it just for a moment, and I doubt anyone spoke to him. The Jaguars love Travis Hunter and the juice he brings to the field.
Do the Jaguars sign Antonio Johnson or Ventrell Miller or both this offseason? Bonus question, do they try and keep D-Ham?
A: I could see it, but I could also see them having to see what the market looks like for each player. Both have been important pieces of the Jaguars' defense all season long, and the Jaguars could stand to keep two young and ascending defenders at important spots in the defense . With that said, the Jaguars have not thrown much money at linebacker, and they have spent a ton of resources on safety already. I think everything is possible.
As for Davon Hamilton, I think that is a down the road decision. I think a short deal would make sense for both sides, though I am not sure how quickly either party would really have to move on that front after his injury.
With the holiday season coming up, what are your top 3-5 holidays of the year?
A: Thanksgiving and Christmas are in their own tier at the top. Family is what makes life, and these are the two best holidays for…

title: Jaguars' Latest Salary Cap Move Could Hint at Post-Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- November has been ... a busy month for the Jacksonville Jaguars, to say the least.
The Jaguars are in the middle of a three-game winning streak since returning from the bye week, putting them at 7-2 and in firm lead of the AFC South. Then there was the trade deadline, with the Jaguars making blockbuster trades for defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III, as well as adding defensive tackle Davon Godchaux.
The Jaguars' big moves saw them send over five draft picks (one first, two seconds, a fifth, and a sixth) over the next three drafts , and it also created some clear long-term implications. In the midst of all this, the Jaguars also reportedly created over $3 million in cap space by converting some of linebacker Foyesade Oluojun's salary into signing bonus.
The #Jaguars converted $3.85M of LB Foyesade Oluokun's 2026 salary into signing bonus last week, adding an additional void year, creating $3.08M of cap space. Cap Hit (Dead Cap) 2026: $14M ($27.6M) 2027: $16.6M ($10.5M) 2028: $2.86M (void)
Why would the Jaguars create cap space after the trades, and what could it mean about potential long-term plans for the Jaguars' front office? We take a few guesses below.
The Jaguars will have quite a few big decisions to make for 2027 and beyond once the 2026 season is over, though it is clear where the Jaguars' focus is right now. With that in mind, this offseason could see potentially even more movement for the Jaguars than last offseason, when they had starters leave in free agency like Travis Etienne, Devin Lloyd, and Greg Newsome.
The Jaguars again have several big names in contract years, including Bates, star wide receiver Parker Washington, and other starters like Antonio Johnson, Ventrell Miller, Arik Armstead, Ezra Cleveland, and more. With the way the Jaguars' cap situation looks for next year as of today, the Jaguars are going to likely have a similar offseason in 2027 that they did in 2026, which means limited to no activity in free agency and having to see a few players leave.
Due to the Jaguars being unlikely to be players in free agency, the only real reasons for the Jaguars to create cap space up until March is to provide flexibility for future moves, such as trades, or for extensions. With the trade deadline now over, the Jaguars' only real focus cap wise should be working on any potential deals.
The most obvious one would be for Parker Washington, who had contract talks with the Jaguars over the course of the 2025 offseason. It is clear both sides are interested in making a deal happen, and Washington could also be a strong candidate to be franchise tagged in the event that he does not get a new contract. It would make more sense for the Jaguars to sign a deal with him, of course, and the Jaguars have signed players to deals late in the season before under this regime.
Then there is Bates. It makes little sense for the Jaguars to make movement on a Bates deal now, even if the most likely scenario in trading for him was always for him to end up like Jakobi Meyers a year ago. The Jaguars traded for Meyers on Nov. 4 last season before signing him to a contract extension on Dec.18, six games into his tenure with the Jaguars. This timeline would make a lot of sense for Bates and the Jaguars a year later.
The Jaguars opening up cap space after the trades is likely to give themselves some breathing room more than anything else; according to OverTheCap, they now have over $6.33 million in cap for this season and are just under $21M in the red for 2027. Moves will have to be made, players will have to be signed, and the next few months should be just as busy off the field as it is on it.

title: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box.
The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected.
But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon.
Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday.
Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus.
“Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways."
The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room.
This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game.

title: Grand Theft Contract: 6 Worst Jaguars Free-Agent Signings of GTA Era
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The wait is over, and the release date for Grand Theft Auto VI is here.
The long wait for the latest release of one of the most popular video game franchises got us thinking: who has committed grand theft on the Jaguars when it comes to free agency busts over the years? We break it down from generation to generation of the game, and of the Jaguars.
The first era of GTA began with the first game in 1997, but this was far before the Jaguars became big-money spenders in free agency like we will see down the road. As a result, we went with a unique choice for this selection: wide receiver Desmond Howaard, the former Heisman Trophy winner and No. 4 overall pick who the Jaguars landed in the 1995 expansion draft. Howard did not land any kind of big contract with the Jaguars of course, but for all of the hype he had at Michigan, he did little in his one year with the Jaguars, catching 26 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown, while not making a big impact on the return teams.
It is unfair to place Zach Wiegert here, since he did not sign a major deal with the Jaguars at the time. But, like 1995, this was not a time where the Jaguars were really throwing money around at free agents. Wiegert played for the Jaguars for four seasons and started games at both guard and tackle, but injuries kept him from being an every-week player. He was a solid piece, but the Jaguars got more out of other signings at this time.
Looking for a big-game defensive end to make plays across from Tony Brackens, the Jaguars signed Hugh Douglas to a $27 million dollar deal that he never came close to justifying. In 16 games with the Jaguars, Douglas had 3.5 sacks despite recording 37 combined sacks in the three seasons before. Douglas was a complete zero for the Jaguars, and he will long be remembered as one of the worst free agency additions in franchise history.
Jerry Porter signed a six-year, $30 million deal with the Jaguars in 2008, and then only caught 11 more passes than whoever is reading this. Porter spent one year with the Jaguars and played in 10 games, catching 11 passes for 181 yards and a touchdown. The Jaguars took a lot of swings at wide receivers in free agency over the years, but Porter might have been the worst one. He was cut by the Jaguars the next year and never played another regular-season snap in the NFL.
The Nick Foles deal ... never looked like a good idea. Like, ever. Even with the benefit of hindsight, it is a bit amazing to consider that the Jaguars watched his career and opted to pay him a four0year, $88 million dollar deal with over $50 million in gurantees. One can not fault Foles for taking the Jaguars' money after he won a Super Bowl in a few flukey starts the year before, but we can blame the Jaguars for making the most misguided quarterback decision in franchise history since, well, one year before when they extended Blake Bortles. Foles spent just one year in Jacksonville before being traded to the Chicago Bears in 2020.
Before the Jaguars knew about the value of Parker Washington , they were throwing everything against the wall to find receivers. It started with DJ Chark and Laviska Shenault before turning to Christian Kirk, Zay Jones and Calvin Ridley. Then in 2024, the Jaguars took two big swings on new faces in the receiver room with drafting Brian Thomas Jr. in the first-round and signing Buffalo Bills wide receiver Gabe Davis to a three-year, $39 million deal in March. Thomas has had so-so results, while Davis, uh, did not have as much luck.
Davis had 20 catches for 239 yards and two touchdowns in his lone season with the Jaguars, and the new regime released him the next season despite carrying a big dead money hit that the Jaguars are still paying for this season. Davis battled injuries in Jacksonville, but he is the biggest Jaguars free agency bust in some time.

title: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Giants: Bhayshul Tuten's Field Day
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to take on the New York Giants in one of Week 11's most interesting matchups, and there is plenty at stake for both teams.
For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best.
So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions.
No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues.
According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)."
Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks.
The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game.
With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut.
No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab.
According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.."
The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver.
J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that.
The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week.
Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson.
The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for.

title: Chiefs vs. Cardinals Matchups: An Experiment Up Front and a Singular Problem for KC’s Defense
full_text:
After losing to the Denver Broncos in Week 8, the Chiefs were slated for three games everyone had circled since the schedule came out in May. They faced the New York Jets, then the Atlanta Falcons, and now the Arizona Cardinals, before meeting their arch-rival Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving evening.
The potential ease of that stretch has lived up to its billing, with those three opponents holding a combined record of 8-22. After the Denver loss, they were labeled as three must-win games, given how tight the divisional race had become.
The Chiefs won the first two by at least three touchdowns, and in Week 11 they face perhaps the easiest challenge of the bunch. The Cardinals are in disarray and already down to their fourth quarterback of the season . Kansas City expected Arizona to start rookie Carson Beck, who led Miami to a national championship last season after a successful collegiate career at Georgia, until back spasms ruled him out earlier this week. Instead, 19-year veteran journeyman Josh Johnson will take the reins at Arrowhead.
That makes for an extremely favorable matchup as the Chiefs try to move to 8-2. Arizona has a guy or two that Kansas City needs to key in on, so here are the two biggest matchups on each side of the ball.
Offense: Chiefs pass protection vs. Cardinals pass rush
Let's be clear: the Cardinals' pass rush is not good, so this matchup is more about Kansas City than Arizona. The Chiefs allowed single-digit pressures in Weeks 2 through 6 but have not done so since.
Patrick Mahomes has been elite at avoiding sacks. Among qualified quarterbacks, his pressure-to-sack ratio of 9.7 percent tops the league, according to PFF. That is a Mahomes stat, not one that speaks glowingly of the offensive line.
Who starts up front is a giant question mark this week. Right guard Trey Smith and right tackle Jaylon Moore have been ruled out, Mike Caliendo has struggled mightily filling in, and the Chiefs signed veteran lineman Fred Johnson this week, who has plenty of starts under his belt. Andy Reid said, "They're all going to have a shot to get in there and go," so Sunday may be a bit of an experiment.
The Chiefs will more than likely win this game regardless of their offensive line play, but you would love to see them keep Mahomes clean four days before one of the biggest games of the season. As for who they are facing, defensive end Josh Sweat and defensive tackle Walter Nolen are the two above-average talents.
Eight-time pro bowler and four-time All-Pro safety Budda Baker actually leads Arizona in sacks, with 3.5. Allowing him to affect the game as little as possible, whether it be throwing away from him or linemen and running backs picking up his blitzes, will be key to taking away their opponents' best player.
That said, four of the Cardinals' five leading pressure-getters are interior defensive linemen, and Kansas City's interior offensive line is its weakest link right now. Left guard Kingsley Suamataia struggled mightily in pass protection last week, as did Caliendo, and even all-pro center Creed Humphrey allowed two pressures. Whoever is in the lineup will have to perform well if the Chiefs want to see the second-team offense in the back half of this game.
To be clear, running back Emmett Johnson is likely the game's top performer, with Arizona allowing the 28th-most rushing yards per game. But nothing would be more encouraging than an offensive line that protects Mahomes while he builds chemistry with a revamped receiving corps. They will not have a better matchup to prove themselves all season.
Defense: Chiefs back seven vs. tight end Trey McBride
To say tight end Trey McBride is Arizona's only receiving weapon would be putting it lightly. After trading Marvin Harrison Jr. and placing Michael Wilson on injured reserve, their wide receiver depth chart reads Devin Duvernay, Simi Fehoko, and Reggie Virgil, none of whom has 100 yards on the season. Backup tight end Elijah Higgins, fresh off a multi-year extension, is currently their second-best weapon.
McBride already has 78 receptions, second in the NFL among all receivers, and 635 yards, which trails only Brock Bowers among tight ends. Higgins is not as good as Michael Mayer, but the Chiefs struggled against two-tight-end sets in Week 4 against Las Vegas, when Bowers and Mayer combined for 14 catches, and each topped 80 yards.
The Cardinals do not have quite that good a duo, nor do they have Kirk Cousins throwing the ball, but Johnson will lean on the two of them, mainly McBride. That likely means the Chiefs put their cornerbacks on an island, given how big an advantage they have on the outside, and dedicate resources to the middle of the field.
Unlike Bowers, McBride lines up in the slot or in-line 88 percent of the time, so he mostly draws linebackers and safeties, creating mismatches. With Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill not the most talented coverage linebackers, safeties Chamarri Conner, Alohi Gilman, and Jaden Hicks, along with slot corner Chris Roland-Wallace, will need to draw assignments or at least provide help over the top.
With top pick Jeremiyah Love sidelined, Kansas City will also need to contain running back Tyler Allgeier, a competent runner, but limiting McBride is Steve Spagnuolo's key to the game.

title: Injuries to Drake Maye and Puka Nacua Lighten the Challenge of the Chiefs' Upcoming Gauntlet
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs' late-season schedule is a gauntlet. After three consecutive noon games against the struggling New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals, the Chiefs will hit the road for three away games starting next week, visiting the Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams and Cincinnati Bengals before returning home to host the New England Patriots and San Francisco 49ers.
That's a stunning five-game gauntlet, but two of the NFL's most influential injuries will make the challenge slightly less steep against two of KC's upcoming opponents.
On Friday, the NFL world officially learned that Patriots quarterback Drake Maye fractured his right fibula , which will sideline him for the foreseeable future. While ESPN 's reporting notes that "Maye could return toward the end of the season," it seems unlikely that he would be back in time for a trip to Arrowhead Stadium for Monday Night Football on December 21.
Without Maye, New England's offense is led by backup quarterback Tommy DeVito—an obvious downgrade for the 5-5 Patriots.
Meanwhile, Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua certainly won't be on the field against the Chiefs in Los Angeles one week after Thanksgiving due to an injury and suspension . Without getting into the details of the (injury/suspension) designation, the already-injury-riddled Rams will be missing at least one key weapon when they host KC.
Veteran receiver Davante Adams could potentially return in time to face the Chiefs , but that's far from a certainty. On the defensive side of the ball, former Chiefs cornerback Jaylen Watson has been ruled out for the rest of the year due to a shoulder injury.
Even beyond the quarterback carousel that the Cardinals will be riding on Sunday in Kansas City , the Patriots' and Rams' injury reports are enough to recalibrate expectations for both of those December tests.
Of course, the Chiefs' trip to Buffalo to face the Bills on Thanksgiving looks just as challenging as it did when the schedule was released, the Bengals are healthier than they typically seem to be by this point in the season, and the 49ers' laundry list of injuries hasn't slowed them down yet, so most of that month-long stretch remains daunting.
Especially as the Chiefs manage injuries of their own , it's worth remembering that the NFL is a battle of attrition more often than a meeting of two perfectly healthy teams playing their best football.
The Chiefs thumped the Atlanta Falcons without Kenneth Walker. The passing game has gotten back on track after losing Tyquan Thornton (and Rashee Rice for a shorter period of time). Kansas City's preseason first-team offensive line hasn't played a single snap together, as four of the five starting positions have had injury or availability questions this season.
Still, the Chiefs and other injury-impacted squads remain among the best teams in the league, and Kansas City will need to hold their spot in the standings as their Thanksgiving-through-December gauntlet ramps up.
Tied at the top of the AFC West with the Denver Broncos, the 7-2 Chiefs could pull even with the 8-1 Bills if both teams win this week and the Chiefs pull off the Thanksgiving road win on Thursday. That would leave the Christmas Day showdown between Denver and Buffalo as the next domino that may need to fall in the Chiefs' favor if they hope to nab the AFC's No. 1 seed and corresponding first-round bye. Even then, is it fair to expect a nearly perfect stretch of football from KC as they face off with a series of the NFL's best teams? Probably not.
But if there's anything the NFL teaches us every season: there's no guarantee as to what any of these teams will actually look like until the games begin.

title: Chiefs Suddenly Face a Cardinals Team in Complete Quarterback Disarray
full_text:
In a matchup the Chiefs were already heavily favored in , they received another huge break on Thursday with the Arizona Cardinals' latest injury development.
Mike LaFleur's squad was down to its third quarterback in as many weeks after the franchise traded away Jacoby Brissett at the deadline and lost Gardner Minshew II for the season with a torn UCL in his throwing arm. They turned to third-round rookie Carson Beck last week in a loss to the Rams, an outing in which he only threw for 108 passing yards without a touchdown. However, Arizona's precarious quarterback situation worsened today. The Cardinals injury report from Friday revealed that Beck did not practice due to back spasms, putting his status up in the air for Week 11. That puts 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson in line to make the start against Kansas City this weekend (yes, that Josh Johnson).
The #Cardinals are planning to start veteran QB Josh Johnson on Sunday vs. the #Chiefs , as Carson Beck deals with a back injury. The 40-year-old Johnson arrived in Arizona on November 11th. pic.twitter.com/TC2SHuc0vl
Johnson, who has been a member of 15 NFL teams throughout his 19-year career, has only made three NFL starts in the current decade. He filled in a pair of games for the Commanders last year after Marcus Mariota got hurt and led the Ravens once in 2021.
Not only has Johnson become the Edwin Jackson of the NFL, but he's even played in three different professional leagues (UFL, AAF, and XFL). The veteran is about as well-traveled as any player in the league's history. The bigger story here is that the Chiefs hold yet another advantage over Arizona in a showdown in which they opened as double-digit point favorites. The Cardinals are merely playing for draft position right now and were hoping to develop Beck over the final handful of games, but even that plan is in jeopardy should his injury linger long-term.
For a Cardinals offense that had only mustered nine points across its past two contests and recently placed star skill-position players Michael Wilson and Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve, they couldn't afford any more bad news on the injury front. Now, they'll likely have to roll out a new signal-caller who is on the back end of his playing career and hasn't even spent two weeks with this current group since being signed off the Bengals' practice squad.
As fun as a story like Johnson's is, the Chiefs are going to do everything in their power to make his life miserable on Sunday. Steve Spagnuolo's pass rush has finally come alive in recent weeks, totaling eight combined sacks against the Jets and Falcons.
There's still a possibility that Beck suits up if he overcomes his 'questionable' designation before kickoff. Either way, Arizona is staring at another potential blowout loss, regardless of who gets the ball under center.

title: ESPN Matchup Predictor Analyzes Chiefs vs. Cardinals Showdown in Week 11
full_text:
Before entering a short week in a marquee showdown against Buffalo on Thanksgiving, the Chiefs have to get through one more contest first. They will look to remain undefeated at Arrowhead Stadium with the Arizona Cardinals coming to town for Kansas City's final home game in a month.
These two teams are in completely different positions, as the Cardinals are already playing for draft position after turning to rookie quarterback Carson Beck. The Chiefs are battling for the top overall seed in the AFC and trying to overtake the Broncos in the AFC West . Kansas City unsurprisingly enters this showdown as a massive favorite over the three-win Cardinals. However, what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor think? Here's what its computer model forecasts prior to kickoff.
ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 88.0%, Cardinals 11.9%.
With a win probability of nearly 90%, this figure marks the largest advantage the Chiefs have held in the matchup predictor all season, even more than when they played the Dolphins or Jets.
The Cardinals are in the midst of a putrid offensive stretch in which they've mustered a mere nine points over the last two weeks. They sent Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore at the trade deadline and lost Gardner Minshew II to a torn UCL, forcing them to rely on their third-round rookie to orchestrate the offense.
While the Chiefs recently endured a mini-slump that featured losses to the Seahawks and Broncos, they have bounced back by scoring 35 points in consecutive wins. Patrick Mahomes has finally shaken off the early rust coming off his torn ACL and LCL, and this squad is now playing some of its best football all year. Due to the lopsided nature of this particular game, the medical staff is in no rush to get Kenneth Walker III (groin) back on the field. Rookie tailback Emmett Johnson should continue to handle a large offensive workload, which he has undoubtedly earned with 171 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns last week.
The Chiefs will face every team from the NFC West this season and have already played Seattle. They still have the Rams and 49ers after this weekend, which will serve as the final interconference matchups on the schedule.
All three of Arizona's victories have actually come on the road, so perhaps it will give KC a run for its money. However, the computer model indicates that this one will get out of hand fairly quickly Sunday afternoon.

title: Chiefs Fans May Want to Pump the Brakes on Hype for Omarr Norman-Lott’s Return
full_text:
The Chiefs didn't make a defensive line swap at the annual NFL trade deadline , but you already know the logic is outlined for their de facto trade being the pickup of tackle Omarr Norman-Lott.
Considering that the 2025 second-round pick has yet to make his season debut, it's only natural to take anything he contributes down the stretch as a bonus. With Norman-Lott rejoining the active 53-man roster from the physically unable to perform list , he's finally closer to getting back in the lineup.
With that said, any hype surrounding Norman-Lott's return may be misplaced. Judging by defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's comments this week, getting the former Tennessee standout up to speed will be more of a slow-burning process than a rapid reintroduction.
"Yeah, I mean, good to always get those big guys back," Spagnuolo said. "We'll see where he is. He's kind of working through the injury. I think the training staff has done a great job with him. Now, it's getting him acclimated back. The hard thing when you come off this in the middle of the season [is] you don't have the luxury of training camp. We'll have to see where we're at."
What's a realistic workload for Norman-Lott in his first stint of game action this year? Looking at his past and Kansas City's present could provide a potential answer.
Casting his Week 7 showing against the Las Vegas Raiders aside due to his ACL tear, Norman-Lott got mixed involvement on defense as a rookie.
Outside of not appearing in Week 1 or Week 5, he managed to combine for 66 defensive snaps in four contests — good for 28.1% of those available. Given that he's endured a grueling rehab path that lasted longer than most expected , it's foolish to assume he'll sniff that percentage soon.
There's also the matter of how the Chiefs are divvying up their defensive tackle snaps right now. Leading the way is All-Pro Chris Jones with 438 reps; he's logged a 76% share in back-to-back weeks. Behind him, veteran nose tackle Khyiris Tonga was at 55% in Weeks 7 and 8 but has slipped to 44% and 22%, respectively, in his last two showings.
That's coincided with the likes of Bryson Eason and Marcus Harris getting a bit more work. The two have combined for 41 snaps in the last two games, largely due to the continued absence of first-round pick Peter Woods . With that said, Woods was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, a positive indicator for his Week 11 status.
Additionally, the versatility of defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah must be accounted for. The Kansas State product, according to Pro Football Focus , has actually lined up in the A-gap or B-gap on 105 snaps this year. He has 182 on the outside and 15 directly over the opposing offensive tackle. Sophomore man Ashton Gillotte, too, has experience moving inside.
Whether that's because of a perceived lack of depth at tackle or merely out of creativity by Spagnuolo is unclear. This writer leans the latter.
If one of Harris or Eason is released, that'd pave the way for a handful of Norman-Lott snaps. Said player could always return to Kansas City on the practice squad after clearing waivers — Eason was an August waiver pickup , and Harris is no stranger to being elevated to the 53. That still doesn't mean Norman-Lott would be in line for double-digit snaps, nor should he necessarily be at this juncture.
Don't get it twisted: Kansas City could benefit from another intriguing interior rusher. The club is right down the middle (16th) in pressures (128) and pressure rate (36.5%) as a defense, via TruMedia , and opts to send max pressure at the fourth-highest rate in the sport (2.8%). In college, Norman-Lott showcased the ability to win quickly and profile as a three-technique at the professional level.
After a whirlwind of a rookie training camp that saw him look closer to a nose guard and a serious knee injury, however, placing any legitimate level of expectation on him isn't wise. Fortunately for Norman-Lott, he's entering a low-pressure environment on a team that seems perfectly fine allowing him to reacclimate at his own pace.
That's best for everyone involved.

title: Chiefs Injury Report: Latest Updates on Kenneth Walker, Trey Smith
full_text:
Coming off a 35-13 victory over the Falcons , the Chiefs are hoping to heal up quickly heading into their Week 11 matchup against the Cardinals. Several Kansas City starters have been banged up over the past few weeks and the team is hoping to get healthy before Sunday.
While the franchise added former Colts wideout Josh Downs before the trade deadline, his first game in the red and gold was overshadowed by the absence of Kenneth Walker. The superstar running back was a late addition to the injury report last Friday after pulling his groin, forcing him to miss the win against Atlanta. In addition to Walker, multiple starters on the offensive line remain sidelined. Here are the latest updates head coach Andy Reid provided during Wednesday's press conference .
Wednesday marked the Chiefs' first practice session of the week, and Walker was not on the field with the rest of the squad. Reid indicated that the medical staff would take a cautious approach as the Super Bowl LX MVP works his way back.
"He had a sore groin. It's getting better," Reid said. "With those, we just don't want to do something stupid. It's still bugging him a little bit. He's feeling a lot better than he was." Yesterday, ESPN insider Ian Rapoport reported a similar sentiment , suggesting Kansas City could rest Walker for the Cardinals showdown to prepare for the short week ahead when the Chiefs face the Bills on Thanksgiving Day. The emergence of fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson , who tallied 171 yards from scrimmage and two receiving touchdowns last week, allows the team to prioritize Walker's long-term health.
Unless Walker appears on the injury report as a limited practice participant on Thursday or Friday, it can be safely assumed that Johnson will earn his second consecutive start in the backfield.
In addition to the ongoing situation with second-year tackle Josh Simmons , the Chiefs are facing additional uncertainty on the offensive line. By the second half of last week's victory, KC had to turn to a pair of backups on the right side.
Right guard Trey Smith (concussion) and right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) did not practice today either as they nurse their respective injuries. Both of their statuses for Week 11 remain up in the air.
Reid told the media that Moore was "making progress" with the ankle he injured in Week 9 against the Jets, while Smith has yet to clear concussion protocol. He didn't offer a firm timeline for either lineman's return. Mike Caliendo filled in at right guard for Smith after previously starting two games at left guard during Kingsley Suamataia's mysterious benching . Joshua Ezeudu has been filling in at right tackle for Moore. Should neither starter be ready to return, those two would be the next men up along the offensive line.
Kansas City doesn't have much reason to rush Walker or either of its offensive linemen back into action this week. The Cardinals enter Sunday's contest with a 3-7 record and are merely playing for draft position after scoring nine points over the past two games.

title: Grand Theft Contract: Which Chiefs Salary Cap Hits Are Holding KC Back in 2026?
full_text:
For those who may not be familiar with the cultural behemoth that is Grand Theft Auto VI , let's put it into context. The game, set to release on Thursday, is rumored to have cost more than $1 billion to develop . It has reportedly made more than $1.5 billion before being officially released .
For comparison, the NFL's salary cap in 2026 is set at just over $301 million per team.
So, with a new GTA just around the corner, let's take this tenuous link as an opportunity to review the Chiefs' 2026 salary cap and decide which players are underperforming on their substantial deals and which ones might be justifying their large cap hit.
While a $7 million cap hit isn't an outrageous number in a vaccuum, it is enough to make Harrison Butker the league's most expensive kicker in 2026. His $7.3 million cap hit narrowly outpaces Seattle's Jayson Myers ($7.2 million), but Butker and Myers have a $1.5 million lead on third place and beyond.
Of course, if you're reading Chiefs On SI , you don't need me to over-explain Butker's disastrous 2026 season so far. The team signed Justin Tucker to their practice squad and just worked out veteran kicker Matt Prater this week .
Still, the Chiefs are publicly holding out hope that Butker can stabilize this year. Could he return to something resembling his previous form by playoff time? It's possible! Will he have provided the kind of confidence and consistency that $7 million typically buys? Definitely not.
If there's any player who I expect an argument about, it's star defensive tackle Chris Jones. Through half the season, has he been worth nearly $45 million? No, that's an enormous number and makes him the priciest defender in the NFL this year.
The second-highest interior defensive lineman cap hit in the league belongs to Alim McNeill at $29 million, while the highest cap number for an edge rusher is T.J. Watt's $42 million . According to Spotrac , Jones has the third-highest cap hit in the entire NFL this season, behind only Matthew Stafford and Justin Herbert.
Has Jones been the best defender in football this season? No. So you'd assume his cap hit is borderline criminal, right? It's still not that simple for me.
If the 32-year-old Jones was having a better season and showing fewer signs of slowing down, I think the Chiefs would have restructured his contract by now. On his current deal , this '26 cap hit is his highest number, taking up nearly 15% of the Chiefs' cap. But any effort to restructure Jones' deal would move money into future seasons, making it harder to part with Jones in years to come. If the Chiefs wanted to cut Jones before the 2027 season, they'd free up $18.6 million in cap space but hold $19.5 in dead cap. If KC keeps Jones at his $38 million hit in '27, they could clear up $35 million in 2028 with "only" $9.75 in dead money.
Despite only having three sacks this season (with two coming against the New York Jets two weeks ago), I'm not sure that Jones' future has been decided. If he can regain his game-wrecking gear down the stretch while commanding attention from opposing offenses, he's still an extremely valuable player. Plus, I still just can't fault the Chiefs for being willing to overpay a franchise cornerstone in order to keep the defense's most important player under contract through the back end of his career while they continue to chase Super Bowls.
Is it a great contract for the Chiefs? No. Do I still understand why and how Kansas City agreed to a deal that would pay a 32-year-old $45 million this season? I do.
Jaylon Moore's time with the Chiefs has never really gone according to plan. He was expected to be the team's starting left tackle until they drafted Josh Simmons shortly after signing Moore in free agency, leaving Moore to move into a swing-tackle role behind Simmons and Jawaan Taylor in 2025. After starting six games in '25, Moore appeared to be in some level of competition with undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson for the right tackle position in training camp this summer. Moore looked to win the job before Simmons suffered a back injury, leaving Benson to take over on the left side.
This year, Moore has not performed particularly well on the right side while carrying the team's third-highest cap hit.
Free agent tackles are expensive because it's a tough position to confidently fill out and great players rarely hit the open market, but there's no real argument that Moore has met his contract numbers across his two-year, $30 million deal. I never cared which side of the line Moore played on, as long as he was a positive force. Unfortunately, it's hard to say that he's been much more than passable.
Kristian Fulton's two-year, $20 million contract looked like a borderline disaster last season, when Fulton never seemed to get fully into the mix at corner until he got more opportunity (and played well) at the very end of the year.
The Chiefs could have cut Fulton this offseason to free up $5 million with an $8 million cap hit, but through '26, Fulton has made an argument to justify his salary, even as the team's third corner.
Second-year third-round pick Nohl Williams has been the team's most consistent cornerback, playing 94% of the Chiefs' defensive snaps, while No. 6 overall pick Mansoor Delane (54%) has been excellent when he hasn't been sidelined due to a recurring shoulder injury. Meanwhile, Fulton (47%) has been very good in his part-time role. Is $13 million an expensive No. 3 corner? Sure, but with Delane's injury and so much youth in the room, Fulton's cap hit is large, not egregious.

title: Chiefs Reportedly Adding Tackle Depth: What Does It Mean for Battered O-Line?
full_text:
It's been a trying season for the Kansas City Chiefs' offensive line, as a combination of fluctuating performance and lackluster durability has created some obstacles despite a 7-2 start for the team.
Week 10's win over the Atlanta Falcons may have summed that up to perfection, as Kansas City dominated the opponent but also showed plenty of cracks in the foundation along the way. Ahead of Sunday's contest against the Arizona Cardinals, general manager Brett Veach is doing something to potentially improve the situation.
Per a Wednesday morning report from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN , the Chiefs are signing former Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Fred Johnson to the practice squad.
The #Chiefs are signing former #Eagles OT Fred Johnson to their practice squad and he’ll likely be elevated to the 53-man roster. pic.twitter.com/zV3ITTxp48
Johnson, who entered the league as an undrafted free agent in 2019, has spent time with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Cincinnati Bengals, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Jacksonville Jaguars as well. He's appeared in 86 regular-season games to date, making 22 starts and logging just under 1,900 offensive snaps in total.
Rapoport adds that Johnson is "likely" to be activated to the 53-man roster at some point, whether it be via standard elevation (he's allotted three during the regular season) for game day or a straight-up signing down the road.
Johnson brings a defined set of skills to the table, yet it's ironic that one of his core traits is versatility. According to Pro Football Focus , the 29-year-old has played most of his snaps at either right tackle (893) or left tackle (833), with a decent chunk still residing at the right guard spot (158).
He split time between tackle alignments during his fill-in duties with Philly in 2024 and 2025. His most extensive experience came during that window — he combined for 626 pass blocking opportunities and surrendered 57 total pressures.
The eighth-year man boasts intriguing physical tools, too. Per MockDraftable , Johnson is in the 94th percentile in height (6-foot-7), the 91st percentile in wingspan (84.5 inches) and the 88th percentile in hand size (10 5/8 inches). It's easy to see why the Chiefs were interested in him, especially given the state of affairs with the offensive line.
Neither tackle position is in a good place. On the left side, Kahlil Benson turned in one of his worst games as a professional down in Atlanta and looks like less of a true answer with each passing week. Projected starter Josh Simmons remains on the injured reserve list and, via head coach Andy Reid, wasn't expected to return to practice this week.
On the opposite side, veteran Jaylon Moore is dealing with a lingering ankle injury and hasn't fared particularly well when available. The jury is still out on backups Joshua Ezeudu and Diego Pounds , both trade acquisitions from August. The former is coming off a solid outing that saw him get credited with a pair of pressures ceded but appear much more competent in the lineup.
There are multiple paths the Johnson add can take. At the extreme end, he could be signed to an active roster contract and finish out the season in place of someone like Pounds if the club felt its depth needed to be improved. Thinking more conservatively, it's also possible that Kansas City simply desires someone with the ability to pinch hit at multiple spots.
Being able to count on another battle-tested chess piece is nice this time of year. That's without even factoring in right guard Trey Smith also getting banged up in Week 10. A player like Johnson entering the fold makes plenty of sense.
It's as low-risk as it gets for a franchise that's battered and bruised along the offensive line.

title: Chiefs On SI Mailbag: Which Receivers Should Get the Largest Workload in the Second Half of the Season?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 7-2 after their comfortable victory over the Atlanta Falcons , and with an impressive Chiefs debut for wide receiver Josh Downs , the Chiefs' passing game looks to be the healthiest it's been in quite some time.
Where does that leave the wide receiver rotation just after the midway point of the year? That's where we'll begin in today's Chiefs On SI mailbag.
What is the ideal, gotta-have-it, three-receiver set for this team with the players currently available on the roster today? (And if Worthy isn't on your list, do you think the coaching staff will reach the same conclusion?) - @oscarbobo.bsky.social
Downs and Rashee Rice are the obvious No. 1 and 2, regardless of which order you'd rank them in. The third spot is the tricky one.
In his third season, Xavier Worthy leads Chiefs wide receivers in snaps taken by a healthy margin, having taken 478 snaps to Rice's second-place 273. Worthy has been on the field more than Travis Kelce and Kingsley Suamataia this year; he's fifth in snaps on the Chiefs' offense. That doesn't look like a player who's about to see his role decrease significantly.
However, we've seen the same issues in recent weeks. Despite his experience and health, he hasn't been making a significant impact in the box score or on film. With a few sideline-related miscues gaining traction amongst some Chiefs fans on social media, I understand why Worthy's stock appears to be in decline.
Worthy's 33 catches on 50 targets for 278 yards adds up to more than double rookie Cyrus Allen's early-season production (seven catches on 14 targets for 109), but Worthy has quadrupled Allen's offensive snaps (108).
I've seen enough flashes from Allen and enough miscues from Worthy to at least be willing to hear out an argument on behalf of the rookie being a more useful weapon in this "gotta-have-it" scenario. For now, I do think Worthy retains that spot for the KC coaching staff. Still, Worthy's role seems destined to decrease with the addition of Downs and the return of the now-healthy Rice; if Worthy doesn't start making plays again soon, Allen will continue to close that gap.
Cyrus Allen is two months older than Xavier Worthy. They're both 23.
What playoff team in the AFC would be toughest to beat at home? My money is on the Broncos strictly based on the pass rush. When Mahomes loses in the playoffs, he isn't able to overcome his offensive line. They could overwhelm us. - @jaymaul4.bsky.social
Bo Nix aside, I think this logic for Denver absolutely holds water. The single area on the team that I am the most short- and long-term worried about is the offensive line, so we logically have to pick a team that has the ability to challenge that unit.
The question the Chiefs will need to see answered over the next month or so: Do the Bills and Bengals have enough defensive firepower to push through KC's questionable line? Maybe this is out of blind loyalty to Mahomes, maybe it's because he's been so good behind such an iffy group already this season , but I think that any team planning to beat the Chiefs in January will need to have a solid day rushing the passer and an offense that's better and more consistent than what Denver offers... which is also where the perpetually under-the-radar Jaguars come into play for their part of the conversation.
With how our offense looks, both with the elite running game from either K9 or E10 and our passing game looking WAY better now that Josh Downs is already making an impact for us, do you think we can come out of the gauntlet of games to end the season 5-2 or better? - @zandersahlia.bsky.social
For record-keeping, here's the gauntlet in question: at Buffalo, at Cincinnati, vs. New England, vs. San Francisco. Then, the Chiefs go to LA to face the Chargers and host the Raiders. You have to expect that Kansas City wins the final two AFC West showdowns of the year, leaving that brutal five-game stretch where you're asking about going 3-2.
The Rams are significantly depleated from their preseason hype, and the Patriots are expected to be without quarterback Drake Maye. The Bills, Bengals and 49ers are all legitimate Super Bowl contenders.
Going even 2-3 down that stretch would be plenty for a playoff spot, sending KC to a hypothetical 11-5 season if they do handle those final two divisional games after the gauntlet. Even if the Chiefs are underdogs at Buffalo, at Cincy and home to the Niners, I'd be a bit surprised if they lost all three of those games.
Now, if they beat the Bills and Bengals, we're back to talking about their chances at the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
Can this team win the Super Bowl with this offensive line? - @MarkKnopke
Yes! I'm quite concerned about the state of the O-line, but (yes, even after two Super Bowl losses enabled by completely overwhelmed offensive line play) if you give me Mahomes, a fully stocked array of weapons both through the air and on the ground, and a defense that might be hitting its stride, that team can absolutely win a few one-off games while trying to hide the line's deficiencies.
Would it be more likely with better performances across the trenches? Absolutely. But the AFC doesn't have a singularly dominant team, and the Chiefs are just as plausible of a Super Bowl representative as anyone else in the conference.

title: Making Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes’ Case as the 2026 NFL MVP
full_text:
Considering how well he's performed in 2026, it's almost easy to forget that Patrick Mahomes is coming off a torn ACL and LCL . Just nine months removed from suffering a potentially career-altering injury, Mahomes made his comeback in the season-opening win over the Broncos and has appeared in every game since.
While it took the future Hall of Fame quarterback some time to rediscover his rhythm, he has returned to his usual form in his 10th season in the NFL. Mahomes threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns without an interception in the Chiefs' dominant win against the Falcons last week, putting him ahead of Peyton Manning for the most combined touchdown passes in a player's first 10 seasons. Nobody could have expected Mahomes to re-establish himself this quickly, but that's exactly what's happened. After his stellar Week 10 showing, Mahomes now holds the fifth-best odds to be named NFL's Most Valuable Player, per FanDuel Sportsbook . Could he capture his third MVP award by season's end?
Since the Chiefs inked running back Kenneth Walker to a three-year deal in the offseason, Andy Reid's offense has become more balanced and less reliant on the aerial attack. Even so, Mahomes ranks inside the league's top 10 in passing yards, passing touchdowns, and is second among all quarterbacks in touchdown-to-interception ratio (19-to-4).
The last three weeks alone, Mahomes has averaged over 300 yards through the air per contest, tossing 10 touchdowns without an interception on 70.1% passing. Those are numbers that could earn him serious MVP consideration if they persist.
Currently listed above Mahomes on the MVP ladder are Joe Burrow (+100), Josh Allen (+350), Brock Purdy (+400), and Trevor Lawrence (+550). But aside from Purdy and the injury-riddled 49ers, the other three quarterbacks don't come close to sharing Mahomes' predicament at wide receiver. Tyquan Thornton suffered a likely season-ending ankle injury in Kansas City's win over the Raiders in Week 4, while Rashee Rice missed time with a hamstring ailment. Those developments have compounded an already unpredictable receiving corps entering the campaign, yet Mahomes' production hasn't wavered one bit.
Not to take anything away from Burrow's historic first half of the season, but Mahomes doesn't have the luxury of throwing to the best receiver tandem in football in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins every week. The Chiefs also have a more dependable defense that allows the offense to play with a lead, whereas Cincinnati's defensive struggles often force Burrow to throw 40+ times just to keep the Bengals competitive. There's far more to consider in the MVP discussion than yards and touchdowns.
Although Mahomes still has some ground to make up in the passing-yardage department, his efficiency has been difficult for the other MVP hopefuls to match. He has been able to limit turnovers in addition to showcasing his new-and-improved deep ball, something that has contributed to Kansas City's offensive resurgence.
With former Colts slot wideout Josh Downs now in the mix , Mahomes can finally maximize the weapons at his disposal. That was made evident in the Falcons game when five different pass-catchers recorded 40 or more receiving yards and Mahomes was distributing the rock to everyone. MVP voters put a lot of stock into a team's record when evaluating prospective award contenders. Burrow, Allen, Lawrence, and Mahomes are all battling to secure AFC's top playoff seed, which could go a long way in determining the eventual winner. A 13 or 14-win finish for the Chiefs may be enough to push Mahomes over the top if the other candidates lose ground in the playoff race.
It understandably took time for Mahomes to trust his surgically repaired knee and gradually learn what his body could withstand on the field. His comfort levels have steadily improved throughout the year, and he's now playing even better than he did in the past few seasons. There is no better time for Mahomes to start hitting his stride than now.
Burrow will remain the consensus favorite for the award until further notice, but if he experiences a second-half slump and Mahomes keeps playing at this level, don't be surprised if the three-time Super Bowl champ receives first-place MVP votes at the end of the year.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Expect Tre' Harris to Have Another Big Game
full_text:
The Chargers have an easier matchup this week…well, that's what fans hope it will be. The Bolts face the Jets on Sunday, following their first win of the season versus the Ravens .
Multiple players, especially Tre’ Harris, should have standout games , which in turn, could help fantasy managers this week
Here are six Chargers players you should start and sit this week.
Hampton is one of the Chargers players I feel best about this week.
He’s coming off an impressive performance against Baltimore, and his physical running style gives him a chance to control the game. What I like most is his ability to make plays even when the offense isn’t firing on all cylinders.
The Chargers should give him plenty of opportunities, and I expect him to be a major part of their game plan. He’s a strong starting option this week.
Harris is someone fantasy managers should seriously consider putting in their lineups. He’s beginning to show what he can bring to this offense, and his performance against Baltimore was encouraging. I like his ability to make contested catches and create opportunities downfield. The biggest question is how consistently the Chargers will get him involved, but I believe he’s earned more opportunities.
Herbert hasn’t been as productive as fantasy managers would like, but I’m not ready to give up on him.
He’s still capable of making difficult throws and creating plays when the pocket starts breaking down. His ability to contribute with his legs also gives him some additional fantasy value. I expect Los Angeles to look for ways to get its passing attack moving.
McConkey is one of the most talented receivers on this roster, but his back injury makes this a difficult week to trust him. Even if he suits up, there’s no guarantee he’ll be operating at full strength. Fantasy managers can’t afford to gamble on limited production when healthier options are available. I’d rather take a safer approach and leave him on the bench until there’s more confidence in his health.
Johnston has the physical tools to become a dangerous receiver, but his inconsistency is a problem for fantasy managers. He can make an impressive play, but that doesn’t always translate into dependable production.
With other receivers competing for opportunities, it’s difficult to predict when he’ll have a productive afternoon.
Mitchell has plenty of speed and can be dangerous when he gets room to operate. However, his role in this offense makes him difficult to trust right now.
Hampton appears to be the primary running back, which limits Mitchell’s opportunities to make a fantasy impact.
Unless the Chargers significantly increase his workload, I don’t see enough upside to justify starting him. Keep him on the bench this week.

title: Chargers D-Line Mauls Ravens: 2027 Draft Impact & Top Prospects
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers defense has been solid all season and the defensive front has significantly outplayed their record. The defensive front's efforts were finally rewarded on primetime as they manhandled the Baltimore Ravens offensive line en route to the Chargers' first victory of the 2026 season.
Defensive tackles Teair Tart and Dalvin Tomlinson were absolute game wreckers and were accompanied by Jamaree Caldwell and rookie Nick Barrett who both had their moments along the front. It takes a whole team effort to keep future Hall of Fame running back Derrick Henry at ten total yards on ten carries.
Defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary clearly had a plan to stop Henry and challenge the defensive line to own the trenches. Owning the trenches was an understatement. To go along with the 16 total yards given up on the ground to the Ravens, the Chargers were credited with 31 pressures by Pro Football Focus, 29 from the defensive line.
Tuli Tuipulotu led the way in pressures with nine total, including one on first-round rookie Vega Ioane where Tuipulotu blasted Ioane back into the legs of quarterback Jacoby Brissett. For the most part, at least to national audience, the Chargers defensive front is comprised of a group of solid defenders but are putting together performances with a lack of superstars.
Khalil Mack is the most well-known of the defenders on the Chargers front but as everyone knows, he is definitely closer to the end of his career despite still playing at a high level. Tuipulotu is a rising star but lacks the true quick win off the edge ability that some of the other top edge rushers in the NFL possess.
The defensive line's success is in large part due to playing together and playing as a unit under the tutelage of defensive line coach Mike Elston. Elston has been able to take veterans and Day 3 picks like Nick Barrett and Justin Eboigbe, who missed the Ravens game with injury, and turn them into the best version of themselves.
Looking to the future, the Chargers have all but Dalvin Tomlinson under contract in 2027. Given the success of the unit, should the Chargers add in a blue-chip rookie into the mix to make a strength stronger? Perhaps an early-day two addition? Most of the top defensive tackles in the NFL are draft in the top 50 picks in the draft. What could Mike Elston do with a top-tier talent alongside group of defensive linemen who fit the system and play together?
If the Chargers do want to consider adding a defensive tackle early in the draft, who might they be considering? Let's take a look forward at which prospects could fit the category.
Xavier Gilliam burst on the scene this season after transferring from Penn State. The 20-year-old defensive tackle puts fear into offensive linemen the same way fast wide receivers put fear into defensive backs. Gilliam is explosive off of the snap shows violence in his hands and brings intense energy to the defensive line.
Listed a5 6'2 305 pounds, Gilliam is on the smaller side for the Chargers preference but his elite burst and  well-rounded game is worth a look. He is only 20 years old and could easily add more size in an NFL weight room and maintain his elite traits. Now that the Chargers have won a game and are no longer holding the top spot in the draft, Gilliam may be in consideration depending on where the Chargers ultimately pick.
The Chargers typically deploy bigger defensive tackles, capable of taking on double teams. Xavier Gilliam can do that but he is a much better fast twitch penetrator. ✅️Elite burst ✅️Violent ✅️High energy ✅️A+ production ✅️Only 20 years old ✅️1st rounder pic.twitter.com/DsdCS7WfAr
Will Echoles from Ole Miss is big interior defensive lineman with a well-rounded skill set. He will eat double teams but also displays great awareness of where the ball is at in run defense. He also flashes a good array of pass-rush moves and will have instant wins on the line of scrimmage.
Echoles is another young, 20-year-old prospect with room to grow and a body to build in an NFL weight room.
Ole Miss defensive tackle Will Echoles is a big powerful IDL. His production has taken a dip this year but has a good blend of pass rush and run defense abilities. ✅️Has quick win pass rush moves ✅️Can anchor and eat double teams ✅️Gives strong effort pic.twitter.com/K2lZFxpgci
Senior defensive tackle A'Mauri Washington from Oregon is a prototypical Chargers-sized defensive tackle at 6'3 325lbs. Washington went back to school for his senior season, he will enter the NFL with significant experience. Chargers defensive tackle Jamaree Caldwell played with Washington back in 2024.
Washington has top of the food chain talent and shows off the talent with elite flashes. The only reason he is projected to be a second-round prospect is his inconsistencies.
Despite his inconsistencies on the field, there is a chance, as a member of Bruce Feldman's annual "Freaks List", Washington may boost his stock with a stellar combine performance. Given how Chargers defensive line coach Mike Elston has been able to get the most out of his defensive lineman, it begs the  question, what could he do with a talent like Washington?
Oregon's A'Mauri Washington has such fun and elite flashes. Going back to school probably didn't move his draft stock much as he lands in a similar range. But with his traits...can you imagine what Mike Elston could do with him? ✅️Powerful ✅️Elite burst ✅️Good pass rush pic.twitter.com/389ddfA1ec
David Stone is a Junior defensive tackle with elite explosion and violence at the line of scrimmage. He can be a bit wild and has not had the season equal to the lofty expectations entering the year.
Ahmad Moten is a fifth-year senior for the Miami Hurricanes. He played alongside Chargers 2025 first-round pick Akheem Mesidor and has elite burst for an interior defensive lineman.
Texas Tech's AJ Holmes may be the best interior pass rusher of the top prospects if not at least the most productive. He often lives in the backfield of opposing offenses.

title: Could Chargers Trigger Bidding War for NFL Draft's First Overall Pick?
full_text:
Holding the first overall pick in the NFL Draft is an opportunity that can change a franchise for years. In recent years that's definitely been the case.
If the Los Angeles Chargers find themselves in possession of the top selection. The front office could have an interesting situation on their hands , especially if multiple organizations become interested in moving up.
Adam Schefter predicts that an auction for the first overall pick would happen if the Chargers or Titans secure it. Also noting teams would trade up specifically for Drew Mestemaker.
The biggest factor would be how badly other organizations want the player expected to go first. Quarterbacks are often the driving force behind major draft-day trades obviously.
Particularly when a franchise believes it has finally identified its potential long term answer at the position.
If two or three teams become convinced that the same prospect is worth pursuing, the Chargers could find themselves in an excellent negotiating position. Instead of accepting the first reasonable proposal, it could encourage interested teams to compete against one another. That is exactly the kind of leverage a front office should take advantage of. That is why the Chargers would need to approach this opportunity with a clear plan. If their scouting department believes the player available at number one is a rare talent who could become a franchise cornerstone, keeping him might be the best decision.
Bottom line is, if the organization receives an overwhelming offer. Turning one selection into several opportunities could be difficult to resist.
In my opinion, the organization would be wise to explore every possible offer before making a final decision. A team should never assume that the first overall selection automatically makes one player more valuable than several opportunities to improve the roster. There is a strong argument for keeping the pick and selecting a player who could immediately become a major part of the team’s future. Finding an elite prospect is difficult, and passing on that opportunity is a decision that could come back to haunt an organization. At the same time, it would be difficult to ignore an offer that includes multiple valuable draft selections and potentially established players.
A potential bidding war could give the franchise an opportunity to reshape its future in a single afternoon. Whether it chooses to select a superstar prospect or trade the pick for a massive return, the priority should remain the same. Building a roster capable of competing at the highest level. Making the right decision could prove far more important than simply owning the first overall pick.
Discussing a world in which the Tennessee Titans land the No. 1 overall pick in April’s NFL Draft, as they currently have. Cc: @tyschmit 🎧 https://t.co/zy1jY5Gg8R pic.twitter.com/CHM6ke7LmP
