title: Vikings' Afterthought Could Get His Long-Awaited Opportunity Amid Isaiah Rodgers Injury Concerns
full_text:
Week 11 is a huge time for the Purple and Gold as the Vikings prepare for a pivotal Sunday Night Football matchup against the all-powerful 49ers . It's the kind of game that will validate the legitimacy of Minnesota's Super Bowl aspirations, making it clear that both sides of the ball must step up to beat San Francisco this weekend.
Players can only help if they're dressed to do so, though. Although certain Vikings have made themselves indispensable to the team's plans each week, others are struggling to even see a handful of snaps come their way.
That's the case for one rookie defender, who's clearly fallen out of defensive coordinator Brian Flores's plans now that the second half of the 2026 campaign is underway.
The Vikings' latest draft class has had varying levels of success this season. Guys like Caleb Banks, Domonique Orange, Jake Golday, and Max Bredeson have found weekly roles (big or small), while Caleb Tiernan and Demond Claiborne have had opportunities to prove themselves. Even Jakobe Thomas's outlook is on the rise after finally being activated in Week 10.
Taking the above into account, one has to wonder if first-year cornerback Charles "Chuck" Demmings will see legitimate defensive action this season.
Demmings's usage has been sparse, as he's barely played any defensive snaps. But things could change for the rookie after the latest injury news coming out of Minnesota.
On Friday, the Vikings' latest injury report revealed that CB Isaiah Rodgers (quad) is officially questionable for Week 11's clash with the 49ers. He was limited in Thursday and Friday's practices after missing Wednesday's session.
Final #Vikings injury report OUT: WR Jordan Addison and QB Kyler Murray QUESTIONABLE: CB Isaiah Rodgers and S Jay Ward pic.twitter.com/c0rANSvTNV
Rodgers has played 83% of defensive snaps (467) and owns the 14th-best coverage grade (73.7) among 105 cornerbacks on Pro Football Focus , so it's safe to say a potential absence would be felt.
At the same time, any missed time for Rodgers could be an opportunity for Demmings to prove himself.
Drafted 163rd overall in April, Demmings quickly became a Vikings fan favorite throughout the offseason . Between his personality-filled interviews and the fact that his coverage frustrated Justin Jefferson during practice, there was hope that the S.F. Austin product could be a legitimate contributor in Minnesota's secondary as early as his rookie season. He added to that optimism by finishing the preseason with a 64.5 coverage grade after allowing only 2-of-6 passes for 38 yards and a 56.3 passer rating while recording a break-up, per Pro Football Focus .
Instead, it's safe to say that Demmings has become an afterthought at best.
The 23-year-old CB has played two defensive snaps (compared to 29 on special teams) in his four appearances, both opportunities coming against the Buccaneers in Week 3. He's only played one game since then, and while a few absences were due to a hamstring injury, he's also been a healthy scratch multiple times.
As great as it'd be to see what Demmings can do in regular-season action, he'll likely remain a victim of circumstance for the rest of the season. The Vikings' cornerback room is too deep and talented to justify taking away someone else's playing time for him. As Sports Illustrated 's Trevor Ripley said earlier this week : "Who is going to pull Isaiah Rodgers, Byron Murphy, or James Pierre for Charles Demmings?"
The CB trio has exceeded expectations this season, and removing one from the equation would be a massive blow to Flores & Co.'s defense. Injuries in the secondary could also create opportunities to see the field, but nothing is guaranteed—especially when the Rodgers-Murphy-Pierre connection hasn't missed a game yet.
That said, Rodgers will become an unrestricted free agent in March, and while some fans want to re-sign him, a potential exit would open the door for Demmings to challenge for a bigger role next summer. Then it'll be up to him to put what he learned this season into action.
For now, Sunday Night Football could be a preview of what that future might look like if Rodgers isn't healthy enough to take on San Francisco.
If he gets a chance this weekend, it'll be interesting to see whether Demmings can erase any talk about him being an afterthought. He has the talent to develop into a solid contributor one day, but Rodgers's injury might speed up that process. The Vikings need players who can make an immediate impact and help with their championship dreams, and Demmings is now in a position to prove he can be that guy.

title: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers in Mexico City
full_text:
Even if you’re not a fan of the Vikings or 49ers, Sunday night’s primetime match in Mexico City is the definition of a “must-watch.” Two of the best teams in the NFL colliding on the international stage, with playoff seeding and bragging rights on the line, is everything the NFL dreamed of when it set the 2026 schedule last spring.
The stakes could not be much higher for a late-November game, and I expect both teams to put on a show. With a newfound Kirk Cousins-sized confidence boost in Minnesota , the Vikings should be set up well to meet the moment.
Here are three things I see happening Sunday night at Estadio Banorte.
The 49ers have been one of the most balanced offenses in the NFL, averaging a league-high 399.8 yards per game. They’re averaging the seventh-most passing yards per game at 255.8 and the third-most rushing yards per game at 144. San Francisco is also second in the league with 31.2 points per game.
Simply put, the 49ers' offense can move the ball any way it needs to.
The Minnesota Vikings defense ranks 1st in dropback success rate allowed, per @SumerSports The San Francisco 49ers offense ranks 1st in dropback success rate and has the highest dropback success rate of any team through 10 weeks since the 2018 Saints
The Vikings' defense, on the other hand, has allowed the fewest points (14) and the second-fewest yards (236.1) per game to opposing offenses. They’ve also held their own against some of the league's best offenses, holding Detroit, Buffalo, and Green Bay to 19, 23, and 10 points over the last few weeks. Now that they have a dependable QB to keep the offense on the field, they’ll be able to catch their breath in the high altitude of Mexico City. Minnesota's defense will need all hands on deck to slow down an elite offense, but Brian Flores will certainly have his unit ready.
Give me the Vikings defense to hold the 49ers under 330 total yards and 24 points.
The Vikings signed Jauan Jennings this past May for two main reasons: to open up the run game as a blocker and to be a reliable third wide receiver after Jalen Nailor’s departure in free agency. So far, neither has materialized the way head coach Kevin O’Connell and interim general manager Rob Brzezinski had hoped.
Jennings has also missed the Vikings’ past two games with a calf injury, after previously missing Week 2 to attend to a personal family matter. Now, with Jennings set to return against his former team and WR2 Jordan Addison missing time, the former 49er has his chance to shine .
Jennings’s struggles this season have largely been due to poor quarterbacking. The 29-year-old has certainly been open, and Cousins may be the perfect passer to actually get him the ball. I predict that Jennings finds new life and scores at least one touchdown against his former team on Sunday night.
This may already be the NFL’s game of the year. The well-balanced 49ers against the blitz-happy Vikings is a matchup made for the primetime stage. But who says this has to be their only meeting?
In fact, if both teams continue on their current paths, a late-round playoff matchup may be an inevitable sequel.
We simulated the rest of the season using PFN’s NFL Playoff Predictor. 🔮 Here’s the projected playoff bracket 👀 pic.twitter.com/QBo8zogNJ6
There’s a lot of football to be played, and neither team is in the easiest of divisions, but these are two squads built for postseason success. You may need to bookmark this one, but I predict that Sunday will not be the last time we see Minnesota and San Francisco battle this year.
Whoever takes round two may end up having Valentine’s Day plans at SoFi Stadium.

title: 3 Vikings Contract Extensions That Must Be Hammered Out in 2nd Half of Season
full_text:
We're nearing the end of November, and the Vikings are focused on what's left of the 2026 NFL season. With a 7-2 record and the rejuvenated energy of starting quarterback Kirk Cousins's return , expectations are high that the Purple and Gold will be contenders in the second half of the campaign.
However, it is never too soon to prepare for the future . Several Vikings contributors are scheduled to become free agents at the conclusion of this season. General manager Nolan Teasley and the Minnesota front office will want to work out extensions for key players as soon as possible.
The longer Teasley waits to offer an extension to these players, the more their price tag will likely rise. Locking down these three players first would go a long way toward preparing for the 2027 NFL season to be able to evaluate the salary cap situation moving forward.
Vikings edge rusher Andrew Van Ginkel is tied for second in the NFL in sacks this season with 8.5. The combination of him and Dallas Turner has been a recipe for success this year in defensive coordinator Brian Flores's defense.
Van Ginkel's 66.8 Pro Football Focus grade might not look special , but his 32 quarterback pressures, two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, and one interception go a bit further in showing what he means to Minnesota's defense.
Andrew Van Ginkel just took it right from him! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qROgreyURh
The 31-year-old defender is currently playing on a one-year, $23 million contract, but is playing 81% of the Vikings' defensive snaps and is important in Flores's squad and should be a top priority to bring back.
Like Van Ginkel, Blake Cashman has been a cornerstone of the Vikings' defense this season. He has played 94.3% of possible defensive snaps this season. Although he missed last week's game against the Packers while recovering from a concussion , he should return to the lineup soon.
Cashman has an 86.8 PFF grade this season, ranking him second among qualifying linebackers. He has excelled in coverage, earning an 82.6 PFF grade, but has also thrived as a pass rusher, generating 16 pressures and four sacks while blitzing.
Blake Cashman steps up for the sack 😤 INDvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MSl2dfO6k7
The 30-year-old defender is in the final year of his three-year, $22.5 million contract with Minnesota and is in line for a raise for his play over the last few seasons. The Vikings' front office should prioritize keeping him on a multi-year extension.
The secret about Jalen Redmond is o ut . Although he is scheduled to become a restricted free agent after this season, getting an extension done now would save Minnesota from having to match any offer sheet another team offers him.
Redmond ranks fourth among defensive linemen with an 83.7 PFF grade. generating 25 quarterback pressures, resulting in 19 hurries, three hits, and three sacks. His 90.0 PFF run-defense grade ranks him first among all defensive linemen this year, underscoring his effectiveness.
Jalen Redmond was incredible against the Bills. 5 pressures, half a sack, and his usual great run defense. He's playing at an All-Pro level this season. pic.twitter.com/7bEsuRnyDV
It is shocking that Redmond is on a one-year, $1.075 million deal this year. The Vikings will need to give the 27-year-old defender a generous offer to reward him for playing on this relatively small contract and keep him around on Minnesota's defensive line.

title: Elijah Williams’s Potential Is Too Promising for the Vikings to Keep Ignoring
full_text:
Defense has been the Minnesota Vikings' hallmark this season. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores' unit is allowing only 14.0 points per game and leading the league with 37 quarterback sacks this season.
The Vikings' defensive line has played excellently. Some of the players getting the bulk of the work on the line are playing great football. Jalen Redmond has played 464 defensive snaps with an 83.7 Pro Football Focus grade. Levi Drake Rodriguez has played 336 defensive snaps with a 74 PFF grade. Also, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins has played 294 defensive snaps with a 56.4 PFF grade.
Since those individuals are playing well and taking the majority of Minnesota's 563 total defensive snaps, there hasn't been a great reason to play Elijah Williams. With Ingram-Dawkins missing time due to an injury and other ailments keeping players out of the lineup, Williams made his first appearance of the season in Week 9 against the Bills.
In just two games, Williams has played 53 defensive snaps and 16 special teams snaps for the Vikings. In that limited time, he has accumulated 11 tackles, including two for a loss and one sack of Packers quarterback Jordan Love.
Williams is a 24-year-old second-year defensive lineman who was an undrafted free agent out of Morgan State in 2025. The six-foot-three, 298-pound defender has put together good back-to-back showings against the Bills and Packers, which could force the team to keep him active on game day.
He was inactive through Minnesota's first seven games of the season, but currently has a 70.3 PFF score with a run defense grade of 68.6. The Vikings have struggled against some of the league's top running backs , so getting Williams more time on the field on Sunday Night Football against the San Francisco 49ers would be wise.
Minnesota allows 111.9 rushing yards per game but is giving up 140 per game over the last three weeks. This week, the Purple and Gold will take on Christian McCaffrey in a massive test of their ability to stop the run and contain a dynamic running back.
The Vikings should not rush Ingram-Dawkins back into the lineup. If he needs more time to recover from his ankle injury, head coach Kevin O'Connell should feel comfortable having Williams fill in for Sunday night's game and beyond.

title: The Vikings' Best, Worst and Most Likely Outcomes vs. the 49ers in Week 11
full_text:
It's the game circled on everyone's calendar, as two of the league's top teams clash in Mexico City. The Vikings and 49ers are each hoping to establish themselves as the top threat in the NFC, and this game could very well be an NFC Championship preview.
It's the Vikings and Niners on Sunday Night Football, so here's the best, worst and most likely outcomes for Minnesota in Week 11.
Fresh off a massive 30-10 win over the Packers, the Vikings are hoping to carry that momentum across the border in a matchup with the 49ers. Kirk Cousins has another week in this system, and key players like T.J. Hockenson and a revenge-fueled Jauan Jennings are getting healthy. It's a great opportunity for the Vikings to show the world that this is the most complete team in football, but the 8-1 Niners may have something to say about it first.
The win over Green Bay proved that the Vikings are capable of becoming the most dangerous team in the league. I mean, even other NFC contenders are already fuming that the Vikings were able to add Cousins for a middling draft pick at the deadline. The defense is already regarded as generational, but now the three phases are all starting to ascend for Minnesota, and an offensive masterclass against the top team in the conference would open up every door in front of the Vikings.
Still, let's not forget that all that separated Cousins from throwing two interceptions against Green Bay were a few blades of grass grazing his knee, and that his promising game was nearly a regrettable one. He'll hopefully improve every week with the Vikings, but Cousins must be treated like a smart, vocal elevator —and not a magic fix to every offensive issue.
Speaking of offensive issues, the Vikings opted to stand pat at the deadline when it came to the possibility of adding a running back, and the hope is that Aaron Jones Sr. stays healthy and Jordan Mason...does better. The Vikings rank 29th in EPA per rush, and the 49ers defense sits at third in the same metric for defending it. That might be a problem.
For all the good that Cousins brings to the Minnesota offense, his mobility is not one of them. If the run-game isn't productive, and play-action loses effectiveness, well, you can see how things can start spiraling.
The duo of Jones and Mason are averaging only 4.1 yards per carry and have just two rushes over 20 yards total on the year. That won't scare many teams, and with Jones nursing a nagging knee issue while Mason continues to be bottled up, it's fair to wonder if this is what ends up holding the team back against San Francisco and beyond.
Purdy is in the NFL MVP conversation despite throwing to mostly guys picked up off the couch for most of the season. Now, with Deebo Samuel back, and Mike Evans possibly returning as early as this week, the Niner offense is about to enter nightmare territory for opposing defenses.
Brian Flores has a bit of a scary reputation himself, though, and even the NFL's most elite quarterbacks have struggled against his defense. Jordan Love was brought down eight times last week, and Josh Allen, Jared Goff and Caleb Williams all tossed interceptions in their respective games. Malik Willis and Tyler Shough couldn't even eclipse 100 yards in losing efforts. Purdy will get his licks in, but don't expect an MVP-type performance out of Mr. Irrelevant this week.
For the Vikings, the motto on offense is once again to just do enough. Cousins did exactly that at Green Bay with 207 yards and two scores, and as long as the chains are moving and the oxygen is flowing , the defense will ensure this thing doesn't turn into a shootout.

title: Vikings Shouldn’t Ignore the Jakobe Thomas-Shaped Elephant in the Room in Week 11
full_text:
Last Sunday, rookie safety Jakobe Thomas played the first game of his NFL career against the Green Bay Packers. Until Week 10, the 23-year-old defensive back had been inactive on game day, waiting on the sideline for his opportunity to play.
Against the Packers, Thomas didn't play a single defensive snap but received 17 special teams reps. He made the most of his chances, registering two tackles and forcing a fumble on a kickoff return in the fourth quarter to seal the victory for Minnesota.
It took one game for Thomas to make an impact, but now the question of how to get the third-round draft pick more involved must be asked. He appears ready to be a contributor. Relegating him to being inactive seems like a waste of talent.
The Vikings have been taking a patient approach to developing their rookies this season, and making Thomas inactive for the first eight games of the season likely felt like torture for the six-foot-one, 211-pound defensive back.
Getting him involved on special teams was a great start. Now, Minnesota knows they have a player that the team needs to see more from. However, the Vikings' current safety plan doesn't leave many available defensive snaps for the young defender.
Josh Metellus is playing 99.11 percent of defensive snaps, while veteran safety Harrison Smith is in on 55.06 percent of defensive plays. Theo Jackson is essentially the player Brian Flores trusts to fill in, playing 52.04 percent of defensive snaps.
The problem is that Metellus and Smith aren't having great seasons for Minnesota, according to Pro Football Focus .
Metellus has a 35.7 PFF grade this season, ranking him dead last among qualifying safeties. Smith isn't faring much better, with a 44.6 PFF grade, ranking 95th out of 110 safeties.
Minnesota needs to prepare for a future without Smith, who is likely in his final NFL season. Getting Thomas more reps now could help get him ready to potentially take his role next season or provide support as a rotational defensive back, as Jackson is being used this year.
Taking a few snaps from Smith and Metellus to give to Thomas could pay huge dividends for the future and add more depth at the position this season. Having an asset like him watching from the sidelines instead of being on the field would be a mistake for head coach Kevin O'Connell.

title: 3 Vikings Coaching Decisions I'd Make If I Were Kevin O'Connell Ahead of the 49ers Game in Week 11
full_text:
The Vikings are back in the win column after dismantling the Packers in Green Bay. Head coach Kevin O'Connell finally had his squad playing complementary football, and that absolutely has to continue into Sunday Night Football too.
So with the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers on the horizon, here's everything I would do if I were in Kevin O'Connell's shoes for Week 11.
Price got his first significant offensive action against Green Bay and rewarded the Vikings with four catches for 49 yards and a touchdown, plus a 12-yard run. With Jordan Addison out for at least a few weeks, the Vikings need to get their star returner more involved .
The former undrafted free agent has carved out a nice role on special teams, but maybe the Vikings have been underutilizing Price. Teams often try to get these shifty guys into gadget-type roles on offense, but after an impressive showing against the Packers, Price may be a solid receiver. The Vikings will still prioritize Jauan Jennings for his blocking and historical production, but it shouldn't be out of the question to see Price's routes take a sharp uptick.
Clearly, keeping guys fresh at elevation is a no-brainer, but this advice should probably continue past Week 11 too. Reserves Elijah Williams, Caleb Banks, and Domonique Orange have all shown that they deserve their snaps . And while taking Jalen Redmond or Levi Drake Rodriguez off the field isn't making the defense better, the Vikings will need those guys in the playoffs.
Redmond has played the fourth-most snaps among all defensive interior linemen this season, but the guys behind him are starting to make sitting 'Big Red' less nerve-wracking. Williams notched a sack against Green Bay, while Banks had his best game of the season, earning an 82.2 Pro Football Focus grade.
Minnesota had concerns about its defensive line depth leading up to the trade deadline, but the reserves are coming on strong down the stretch. The Vikings will still need to lean on their starters heavily, but maybe seeing Redmond jog off the field won't spike so many fans' blood pressure.
Cousins was as advertised in his first start for Minnesota this year, and the temptation may be to start stretching out the playbook against San Francisco. My question would be: Why? Sure, add a few extra installs for the new week, but let's not forget this is still a guy who has been in purple for just eight days at this point.
Cousins did remarkably well last Sunday despite being out of the system for three years, but let's not press things. The last thing the Vikings need is for O'Connell to get greedy and start to call the game for 2023 Cousins. Thankfully, it appears that the player and coach are very aware of their shortcomings, but we've also seen the stubborn side of things too when O'Connell resisted scaling things back for a struggling J.J. McCarthy.
Ultimately, Cousins and the Vikings will be fine by being just good enough. Let's keep things Camry and not Ferrari here.

I took to X to get your questions and takes before one of the biggest NFL matchups of the year.
To submit your questions, reach out to Jason Harmon on X .
If Kirk Cousins continues to play at this level , I’m not even sure that hearing his name in MVP conversations would be that surprising, especially if he does it while playing for two different teams. Cousins’ 2,547 passing yards rank fifth in the league, while his 22 passing touchdowns rank second. If he continues this success now that he’s back with the Vikings, it’ll be hard to find any other QB in NFL history who has put up that kind of performance with two different teams in one season.
I mean, what an absurd Kirk Cousins throw. Both to put the air underneath, and to keep it on the back shoulder. pic.twitter.com/RCwMnJLihQ
This has been a fascinating talking point around the Vikings’ upcoming matchup with the 49ers in Mexico City. The Vikings plan to hold a normal week of practice before heading south one day before the game on Saturday. Meanwhile, the 49ers are spending the week practicing in Colorado Springs to acclimate to the higher altitude before arriving in Mexico on the same day.
Different approaches to altitude preparation ahead of the 49ers vs. Vikings game in Mexico City: • 49ers: Arrived in Colorado Springs yesterday (6,621 ft). • Vikings: Staying in Minnesota (860 ft) until Saturday. • Mexico City game elevation: 7,280 ft.
While most football fans are used to seeing altitude affect games played in Denver, Mexico City’s altitude is about 2,100 feet higher. Oxygen intake will certainly be a factor. I’m no health expert, and medical professionals even seem to disagree on which approach may be best, but with San Francisco making their third trip across the border, they may have a leg up from experience alone.
If Kevin O’Connell’s statements this week are any indication, he’s expecting a big performance from Jauan Jennings on Sunday. With Jordan Addison recovering from thumb surgery, the Vikings will be reliant on Jennings to return from a calf injury that held him out against the Bills and Packers.
#Vikings HC Kevin O’Connell on Jauan Jennings’ revenge game vs the #49ers : “With us being down Jordan Addison, we’re gonna need him to make some plays in the pass game.” (Via @KFAN1003 ) pic.twitter.com/BOjGi3HeuY
It’s no secret Jennings has had a rough season so far, but more opportunities and better quarterback play may be exactly what he needs. Familiarity with his former team certainly doesn’t hurt either.  Sunday is just the start of what could be a highly productive month for Jennings, as Addison may not return until the Dec. 20 game against the Lions.  The back half of this season could be an entirely different story than his frustrating start.
Make no mistake, a win on Sunday against a great 49ers team could prove to be a season-defining moment for the 2026 Vikings. For all the offensive turmoil that plagued the team over their first eight games, Cousins’ return has brought optimism that this may be a truly special year after all.
Sunday night could easily be the biggest game of the 2026 NFL season. Shoutout to the fans in Mexico City who get to witness an all-timer. pic.twitter.com/37oFawfBs6
The Vikings defense is currently on pace for almost 70 sacks, a total not reached since the Eagles did it in 2022. They just so happened to make it to the Super Bowl that season. All Cousins and the offense need to do is hold on to the ball and score points on occasion. The stellar Minnesota defense and kicker Will Reichard will handle the rest.

title: Patriots Must Shut A.J. Brown Down for the Remainder of 2026
full_text:
I've been very positive when it came to the A.J. Brown situation with the New England Patriots this year. I thought the trade was the right move to make back in June. I had high expectations after watching him shine in training camp. I kept up a positive outlook when he returned off of injured reserve.
But with the wide receiver now reportedly set to miss several weeks with a hamstring injury, it's time to call a spade a spade. Based on early returns, the Patriots, 10 games in, have lost the Brown trade and it's time to shut the receiver down for the rest of the season.
It's been a mess, and it's only going to get worse if the team doesn't pull the plug.
With Drake Maye out with a fractured fibula and likely set to miss the rest of the season, the year is a lost cause — regardless of what happens at quarterback. Keep Tommy DeVito under center, promote Behren Morton, sign Daniel Jones. Doesn't matter. The 5-5 Patriots are still alive for the postseason, but the beeps on that vital signs machine are slowing down.
It's time to just have Brown finish the season on IR. There's no reason to trot him out there on Sundays.
The Patriots knew he had injury issues in his past, and executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf felt confident in the team's assessment of him when they sent two draft picks to the Philadelphia Eagles back in June . He looked great in the summer and the Maye-to-Brown connection was going to take this offense to new heights.
Then comes a high-ankle sprain suffered in the opener. He's out for four games and that chemistry with his quarterback, out the window.
Then when it's time to get him back after missing four games, his performances against the Jets and Bears were dismal. Six receptions, 85 yards and multiple drops.
Then the knee issue — something he's dealt with when he was with Tennessee and Philadelphia — flared up. It forced him to miss two more games. Brown was clearly fighting through injury and the team, strapped for healthy players amid their injury-riddled campaign, probably forced him back too soon.
Then a hamstring injury comes up after making his second catch against the Lions in Germany. He walked off the field, headed into the blue medical tent and then promptly into the Patriots locker room. The Patriots lost 35-10, their second-straight loss.
At this point, the Patriots need to look at Brown, all bruised and battered, and not make this any worse. He's played in four games, caught 11 passes and is dealing with three times the lower-body injuries than he has touchdowns.
Operating under the assumption that the Patriots won't make the playoffs, they have just three IR return designations — and two of them are likely going to wide receiver Romeo Doubs and offensive guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, who are both eligible to be activated next week. Brown is able to be placed on IR again, but would have to miss another four weeks.
Is it even worth using up a potential return on a receiver who's spent more time on the injury report than the end zone this year?
The Patriots are facing a gauntlet of a schedule after their bye and with whoever is throwing passes, it's not going to be a good outlook for the oft-injured Brown.
I've been very positive about Brown, the lifelong Patriots fan, making an impact in New England in 2026.
But right now, the best move that the team can make is just to rip the cord from the power socket on the year and get him ( and his quarterback/next-door locker mate ) healthy for 2027.

title: Patriots Have No Excuse Not to Pursue Daniel Jones After Colts Release
full_text:
After a disaster of a performance on Thursday Night Football, the Indianapolis Colts officially released quarterback Daniel Jones.
They've now promoted Anthony Richardson to the starting spot and now Jones, who was in the second year of his two-year, $88 million contract with the Colts, is subject to waivers (and free agency, if he doesn't get claimed).
Do the New England Patriots, still reeling from the ankle injury of Drake Maye, try to get Jones under center and try and right the ship? They should.
First off, the Colts totally botched Jones' situation. Clearly struggling and needing to try and rebuild for the future, the team passed on trading both Jones (who had reported interest from the Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens) and running back Jonathan Taylor. One week after the deadline, and Jones is no longer a Colt.
With that being said, the Patriots have just Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton in the building at quarterback sans Maye . DeVito has started games in the NFL before (replacing Jones on the New York Giants back in 2023), but didn't look all that inspiring against the Detroit Lions last week in Germany.
The Patriots are 5-5 and yes, still very much in the thick of the AFC postseason picture. Jones offers a style of quarterback play that, if used correctly, could correlate with a Josh McDaniels-style of offense. He's had experience with Brian Daboll, a disciple of McDaniels, and could slot in under center in New England.
But this year isn't a good assessment of Jones' play. Through 11 games, the 29-year-old is 205-for-351 (58.4%) with 1,974 passing yards, seven touchdowns and 13 interceptions — the most in the NFL. Last night against the Houston Texans in primetime, he went 12-for-27 with 144 yards and a pick.
Not all that great. When you consider the defenses the Patriots are going to facing heading into the stretch run (Minnesota Vikings, Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos), it might not get that much better.
The Patriots can't afford to miss out, though. DeVito didn't play well in his elevated opportunity and rookie Morton hasn't taken a snap in a regular season game. Sure, they might have the playbook down pat heading into Week 12, but Jones' ceiling, albeit low, is still higher.
Jones is subject to waivers now, and any team that puts in a claim for him would take on about $2 million in 2026 salary, plus more than $10 million in injury guarantees in 2027. If he goes unclaimed, the chances that a team throws a dart at him on their quarterback dartboard increases.
The Patriots have the 16th waiver claim and the Ravens — who traded for Jacoby Brissett at the deadline — have the 14th. The Vikings also swung a deal for Kirk Cousins, so both of those teams feel like longshots to add him. There really isn't any other major suitor in play right now.
The Colts haven't been good and Jones is a big reason why. But with the Patriots teetering on a midseason collapse and needing to find a quarterback capable of playing (and fast), it's worth kicking the tires on the veteran.

title: Patriots HC Mike Vrabel Describes Leadership Plan Heading Out of Bye Week
full_text:
For Mike Vrabel, he's focused on fixing the problem. The problem for the New England Patriots through 10 weeks? It's a myriad of things, which includes tackling, injuries, offensive firepower, covering and a whole lot of miscues that cause a team to be 5-5.
But the Patriots head coach isn't going to try and patch things up with his voice. This week, when asked about what his message was to the fans after a second-straight bad loss to an NFC North team, Vrabel said he's more worried about improving.
"I think the biggest thing is that I believe in trying to say less and try to do more," Vrabel said Monday. "So, to sit here and try to sell some message, I think that our fans in the year and a half that we've been here recognize when we have our chance to win the football game, put ourselves in position, don't stall out drives, don't make mistakes, don't give up big plays, get stops on third down, all those things that we know that leads to winning, especially against good teams."
But as the Patriots sit quietly on their bye week, and their quarterback Drake Maye potentially done for the season, the fanbase could use a jolt of energy. 45 points allowed to the Packers, then 35 to the Lions. Nothing seems to be going right for the Patriots ... and these next few weeks are going to be major chances for Vrabel to show that the team's culture and identity remains in tact.
Even in their wins, they haven't been totally consistent. Showing they can start to be a consistent team without Maye and try to scrape together some wins is a step in the right direction.
"We haven't had consistent performances. So, a lot of things lead to the performance, and that's the turnovers, the split-second decisions, the critical mistakes, the missed tackles, the drops," Vrabel said. "There's a bunch of stuff, and it all leads to being inconsistent. So, we need to have consistent actions.
"Again, we've talked about preparation. How we prepare is great. I thought that we had a good week, but the only thing that matters is how we perform and how we play on Sunday. So, we'll still have to continue to prepare, and we'll just have to find ways to play better and play more consistent."
As of now, it's safe to assume backup quarterback Tommy DeVito — who has starting experience — will take the reigns under center. He's capable, though it didn't come across against Detroit in Munich. If the defense can right the ship and start to look like a Vrabel-led team oozing with culture and confidence, this season doesn't have to be over for the Patriots.
But based on how they've looked, that might be a tall task for even Vrabel to fix.

title: Patriots' Robert Kraft, Bill Belichick Inch Closer to Pro Football Hall of Fame
full_text:
The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced Thursday that two of the biggest names in New England Patriots history — Robert Kraft and Bill Belichick — have moved one step closer to football immortality.
Both the Patriots chairman/owner and longtime head coach were named the finalist in their respective categories ahead of this winter's final selection meeting. Kraft, the contributor candidate, has been on the ballot for quite some time. Belichick, the coaching candidate , is in his second year as a possible inductee.
Kraft and Belichick will be two of 15 possible candidates that will be voted on by the Pro Football Hall of Fame selection meeting ahead of Super Bowl LXI. Per newly-installed bylaws, a candidate must receive 80% or more of the vote to be inducted. The 15-group ballot will be trimmed down to seven, and voters must select six of the seven for induction.
Here's a quick look at the qualifications of both Patriots legends, and how they've (somehow) been left out of the halls of Canton, Ohio, to this point in time.
Belichick's nine Super Bowl appearances and six Super Bowl wins as a head coach are NFL records, and yet somehow he was left out of induction last year in his first year of eligibility . His 302 regular season wins are third-most in league history and his 31 playoff wins are the most ever. There isn't a coach more qualified to earn a bust in Canton than Belichick.
And yet, he was snubbed a year ago and drew a lot of cricitism. Since then, the Pro Football Hall of Fame has changed a lot of how the voting process happens, including shrinking the voting pool, removing the senior category for players. Now, candidates like Belichick and Kraft are on the same ballot as the players.
The legendary head coach, who's now leading the University of North Carolina, was hired in 2000 to replace Pete Carroll on the sideline. Since then, he was able to build the league's greatest two-decade dynasty and help orchestrate the growth of the greatest player of all time (Tom Brady).
Belichick left the Patriots following a 2023 season in which the team went 4-13 and ended up with the third overall pick. The 74-year-old beat out Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan for the final spot.
Kraft has been a name in Hall of Fame conversations for more than a decade, and for good reason. Since purchasing the Patriots in 1994, the team has played in 11 Super Bowls — more than any other NFL owner — and won a league-high six.
Last year was the first time that Kraft , who grew up as a Patriots fan, made it past the contributor subcommittee. His absence from the Hall of Fame continued to make headlines each year, as Kraft's contributions to the league (including several TV deals and helping to end the 2011 lockout) have positively pushed the NFL forward.
Kraft advanced in the contributor category, beating out Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten. He'd become the Patriots' first non-player/coach to be inducted into the Hall of Fame if selected.
"I think the ability to continue to grow this area, to grow what is Patriots, the Patriot Place and everything that surrounds this place. The success speaks for itself," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said about Kraft on Nov. 4. "I think he's always continuing to grow the game. I think having these conversations as a coach now with Robert about the media deals, the ability to grow the game, trying to strengthen our relationship with the players and what's best for the game of football.
"I mean, he admittedly started out as a fan of the team and then obviously was able to buy them. I started out as a fan of the Browns. I didn't end up buying the Browns, but I played in the NFL, so I guess we all have a dream. He's certainly done a lot."
They could both be enshrined alongside former Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski, who's eligible for the first time this year. He was the most recent inductee into the Patriots Hall of Fame this year .

title: 9 Former Patriots Selected in 2027 UFL Draft, Including Fan-Favorite QB
full_text:
Even with the NFL in full swing, there is always more football to be played. The United Football League, back for another season, just finished its 15-round draft for the 2027 season — and there are plenty of familiar faces that were selected.
Over the course of two days, nine former New England Patriots players — spanning from draft picks to futures signings — heard their names called by one of eight UFL teams. This year, New England got their own UFL team, with the Rhode Island Breakers set to debut in Pawtucket.
Here's a look at every former Patriot who'll now be suiting up this spring.
Once the apple of New England's eye, the 2023 undrafted free agent was a name to watch that season . An electric player at Louisville, Cunningham came to the Patriots as their third-string quarterback. He was given a few chances to also make the team at wide receiver, but only suited up in one game. Cunningham bounced around between the active roster and practice squad before being signed by the Baltimore Ravens.
The final draft pick of Jerod Mayo's first and only draft class with the Patriots, Bell was a project tight end who was more of a developmental player. He made the 53-man roster out of training camp and played in 15 games, but the Florida State alum caught two passes for 20 yards before being cut the following summer.
Carvin had a very short stint in New England, only being a member of their practice squad in 2024. After a ton of shifting up front, the Patriots signed Carvin on Aug. 24 and he remained with the team until Oct. 8. He'd later sign with the Jacksonville Jaguars (two seperate times) and the Houston Texans.
The first former Patriot to play for Rhode Island, Crossley was a part of the roster in some capacity for the last two years. An undrafted rookie out of SMU, the cornerback signed with the Patriots shortly after the 2025 draft and was a part of their practice squad. He would sign a futures contract to remain with the team in 2026 and after a pretty solid training camp/preseason, was cut this summer.
Like Carvin, Herring was nothing more than a practice squad player. The former Delware defensive back — who spent the start of his rookie season with the Green Bay Packers — signed with New England in September of last year after a workout. He'd be released roughly three weeks later.
Butler was a member of the Patriots training camp roster this year after sticking around on the practice squad last year as a rookie. Initially, the offensive guard parlayed a successful rookie minicamp invite into a spot on the roster — and he was a potential practice squad candidate this year after roster cuts in August.
Out of anyone on this list, Battle has the most playing time. Over a two-year stretch from 2024 to 2025, Battle played in six games with the Patriots, recording five tackles and three pass breakups (all of which came in Week 18 of 2024). He was on New England's practice squad for their trip to Super Bowl LX last February, but signed a futures deal with the Miami Dolphins after the game.
The son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Jerry Rice , Brenden had a week-long stint in New England in 2025. The 24-year-old wideout signed with the Patriots' practice squad on Nov. 4 and was prompty released on Nov. 11. He'd later sign with the Seattle Seahawks, Las Vegas Raiders and Green Bay Packers.
The Patriots had two Butlers on their preseason roster this summer, and now both of them are heading to the Orlando Storm. The Patriots signed Butler, a rookie out of San Diego State, in early August and he was mainly a depth safety/special teamer during his time in New England. He'd be released with an injury designation — pushing him to injured reserve — before the Patriots reached a settlement.

title: Patriots GTA Rewind: New England's Record During Each Release Year
full_text:
The New England Patriots , if they're interested in video games, got a perfect time for their bye week. The highly-anticipated released of Grand Theft Auto VI, the newest installment of Rockstar Games' action video game that's taken more than a decade to officially drop.
It's the eighth GTA game to be released, and the first one in 13 years. A lot has changed in that time, especially with the Patriots — who have seen a legendary head coach and quarterback come and go from the last time someone booted up a new GTA.
Here's a trip down memory lane and a look at the Patriots ' records every year that GTA dropped.
Patriots Record: 10-6, AFC East Champions
The first year after Bill Parcells departed as head coach, the Patriots were once again on top of the division — with Pete Carroll leading the way. They opened up the season on a four-game winning streak before coming back down to Earth. The Patriots would beat the Miami Dolphins in the Wild Card before dropping a defensive slugfest to the Pittsburgh Steelers one round later, 7-6.
Patriots Record: 8-8, 5th in AFC East
Carroll got two GTA games in his Patriots tenure before seeing the door. The Patriots got off to a fast 6-2 start, looking like they'd get back to the postseason. But a string of losses in November and December sent them spiraling down to .500. Drew Bledsoe, in his seventh year as the starter, threw 19 touchdowns and 21 interceptions.
Patriots Record: 11-5, Super Bowl Champions
GTA turned to roman numerals, just like how Bill Belichick turned to Tom Brady under center. They started 5-5 and an injury to Bledsoe forced Brady to step into the game, but they got hot at the right time to win the division. Then came iconic playoff wins against the Oakland Raiders, Steelers and St. Louis Rams en route to their first championship title . Brady was named MVP for his performance in Super Bowl XXXVI.
Patriots Record: 9-7, 2nd in AFC East
The Patriots took a step back in 2002 after their championship win. This year is the one lost year in what was the stretch run of three Super Bowls in four seasons. Brady, in his first full campaign as the starting quarterback, threw for a league-high 28 touchdowns, but a four-game losing streak early on put them behind the 8-ball.
Patriots Record: 14-2, Super Bowl Champions
One of the greatest Patriots teams of all time. They rattled off a six-game winning streak to start the season, and then won six in a row after their Week 8 loss to Pittsburgh. Both sides of the ball were elite, with the Patriots offense ranking second in points and seventh in yards. Defensively, led by the core of Tedy Bruschi, Rodney Harrison, Mike Vrabel, Richard Seymour, Willie McGinest, Vince Wilfork and others, was the second-best scoring unit in the NFL. A Harrison interception in Super Bowl XXXIX sealed their dynastic run.
Patriots Record: 11-5, 2nd in AFC East
Brady tore his ACL in the opening game, and it forced Matt Cassel under the spotlight . The Patriots, coming off the heartbreaking Super Bowl XLII loss from a year prior, had the roster to compete for another title. But Brady's season-ending injury really limited things offensively and the Patriots missed their shot at the postseason by a single game.
Patriots Record: 12-4, 1st in AFC East
The Patriots looked really good in 2010-2012, and again from 2014-2019. The one year in between those runs was a bit of an outlier. Don't get me wrong, they won 12 games and won the division. But that was a Patriots team that really didn't look like they were the same for a bit. They had lost some key guys in the offseason (Wes Welker, Patrick Chung, Danny Woodhead), but patched it together and played their way to a conference championship appearance.
Patriots Record: 5-5 (so far), 2nd in AFC East
It's been a long time since 2013. The Patriots have had two new head coaches and a lot more quarterbacks. Now in 2026, the defending AFC champs have Vrabel and Drake Maye leading the charge . They've been up-and-down to start this season and after Maye fractured his ankle in Week 10, it's starting look a lot more down in the coming weeks.

title: Grading Patriots Offensive Position Groups 10 Weeks In
full_text:
With the New England Patriots on their bye week and sitting at 5-5, it's a good time to evaluate how New England's offense has performed through the first 10 weeks. Here's a look at each offensive position group's performance and a subjective grade.
It feels like an unfortunate time to grade the QB position, given the recent news about Drake Maye's injury. Nevertheless, a grade must be assigned. Maye has had a roller-coaster season, with exceptionally high highs and very low lows. Early in the season, his performances were a noticeable departure from the level of play that earned him MVP runner-up honors the year prior. His fortunes changed during New England's Week 4 trip to Buffalo, kicking off a six-game stretch in which he accounted for at least three touchdowns in every game. His efforts earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Month honors for October. After Maye went down with a reported fractured ankle, backup Tommy DeVito left much to be desired. Against the Lions, DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for just 81 yards, with one touchdown and an interception. Given DeVito's limited opportunities, it's difficult to assign him a meaningful season-long grade. As a result, this evaluation primarily reflects Maye's performance.
Even with his early-season struggles, it's difficult to overstate how important he has been to New England's success. He's been the primary reason the Patriots have remained competitive, especially as injuries have depleted the talent around him. However, it's equally difficult to overlook his 11 interceptions, which lead the NFL and have cost the Patriots at several points this season. The supporting cast hasn't exactly made his job easier, but Maye still deserves his share of the responsibility. Maye's ability to elevate the offense has been impressive, but turnovers and early-season inconsistencies have kept him from earning a higher mark.
The Patriots made significant investments in their receiving corps this offseason, hoping to give  Maye a more dynamic group of weapons to work with. That started with acquiring A.J. Brown in exchange for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder , followed by signing Romeo Doubs to a four-year, $70 million contract in free agency. Unfortunately, injuries derailed those plans almost immediately. Brown has appeared in just four games through 10 weeks after suffering a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and dealing with a prolonged degenerative knee condition. Doubs, meanwhile, recorded 14 catches for 261 yards and three touchdowns before landing on injured reserve with a shoulder injury. The result? Maye has played just 16 offensive snaps with both receivers on the field at the same time, leaving New England's anticipated upgrade at wide receiver largely unrealized.
Drake Maye played 16 total snaps this season with A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs on the field at the same time.
Efton Chism III, Demario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Mack Hollins have had their moments, but the unit as a whole has been underwhelming given the significant capital invested in the group.
As a unit, the Patriots rank 16th in the NFL in rushing yards per game. While there have been stretches of effective production, the group has also been shut down at times, struggling to find week-to-week consistency. Rhamondre Stevenson has continued to be a reliable presence in New England's backfield, contributing as a runner, pass catcher and pass blocker. He's been their do-it-all guy. Corey Kiner has also been a solid addition since the Patriots acquired him in exchange for a 2028 seventh-round pick , providing an effective downhill running presence (averaging 4.5 yards per carry on 60 attempts). Lan Larison has had limited opportunities to make an impact in meaningful playing time. He did record his first NFL touchdown against Detroit, hauling in a 10-yard reception, but the score came with the outcome of the game already largely decided. The Patriots were, however, blindsided by the unexpected absence of TreVeyon Henderson. He had been having a difficult start to the season before revealing that he was dealing with an unusual medical emergency that ultimately landed him on injured reserve.
🙏🏽 pic.twitter.com/l52XuixPOc
Some of the unit's issues can be attributed to the significant injuries New England has sustained along its offensive line, but the bottom line is that the running game has been relatively average to below average.
One position group that has delivered for New England this season has been the tight ends. Hunter Henry has been a model of consistency throughout his Patriots career, leading the team in receptions (34) while ranking second in receiving yards (383). While Henry has struggled as a run blocker, his role as Maye's safety blanket shouldn't be forgotten. Rookie Eli Raridon has also shown plenty of promise as a pass catcher. His 71.8 PFF receiving grade ranks third among rookie tight ends, and he's already found the end zone twice. New England also hasn't been able to utilize fullback Reggie Gilliam as much as they likely hoped. After suffering ankle and knee injuries following the Patriots' win over Buffalo, Gilliam landed on injured reserve, limiting him to just five games and 71 total snaps this season. Tanner Arkin and Cameron Latu have primarily served as blocking tight ends in his place. Their roles became increasingly important after Julian Hill, whom New England signed to a three-year, $15 million contract in free agency, suffered an injury during OTAs. Arkin and Latu have been serviceable replacements, helping maintain some stability in the blocking game.
The Patriots' offensive line has been dealt a difficult hand this season, particularly at guard, where injuries have forced considerable turnover. New England lost Mike Onwenu to an ankle injury in Week 2, Alijah Vera-Tucker to a hamstring injury after Week 6, and Ben Brown on two separate occasions due to knee injuries. Despite the constant shuffling, several players have performed well individually. Brown, Vera-Tucker, Matt Pryor and Jared Wilson have all posted pass-block win rates above 90%, according to ESPN Insights. At tackle, Will Campbell has been solid for most of his sophomore season, allowing just three sacks through 10 weeks. Morgan Moses has been slowed down by foot and knee injuries. He's only allowed one sack, but that doesn't tell the full story. Both tackles have accounted for six penalties this season, tied for most on the team. First-round rookie Caleb Lomu has shown plenty of promise filling in at both tackle spots, making two starts without allowing a sack across 103 pass-blocking snaps. However, the individual performances haven't translated into consistent success up front. The Patriots are allowing pressure on 43.8% of dropbacks, the third-highest rate in the NFL. They're also allowing the fifth-highest pressure rate when opponents don't blitz (39.8%). While New England leads the league in time to throw (3.3 seconds), that may speak more to Maye's ability to extend plays and evade pressure than the protection in front of him. Ultimately, injuries and constant lineup changes have taken their toll. There have been some encouraging individual performances, but the offensive line has struggled to provide consistent protection and establish itself as a reliable unit.

title: Patriots WR A.J. Brown Likely Missing More Time After Sustaining Third Lower Body Injury
full_text:
New England Patriots A.J. Brown could be heading back to the sidelines due to an injury, missing his seventh game of the season.
After sustaining a hamstring injury in the second half of the Patriots' Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany, Brown was seen heading into the locker room. Brown, who had previously missed extended time with a high ankle sprain , made his return against the Lions after missing two weeks with a knee injury.
The veteran receiver, who the Patriots acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles in the offseason , rejoins a plethora of players who are unable to take the field for the Pats.
On Wednesday, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the following :
"In the short term, where the offense turns next is fascinating. Brown has a hamstring injury, which most likely puts him out for a little while. Romeo Doubs is eligible to return from injured reserve after his shoulder injury. One of their most explosive players, TreVeyon Henderson, is on IR for at least three more games. Rhamondre Stevenson is banged up. The trade deadline has passed, so it's not like the team can identify instant improvements. So, scoring points must be a collective effort, starting with the running game."
Brown's most recent injury enters in the shadows of star quarterback Drake Maye's ankle fracture, which is reported to potentially keep the third-year quarterback out for the remainder of the season.
AJ Brown expected to miss more time with a hamstring injury. Per: @JFowlerESPN pic.twitter.com/FwZWFH93EU
New England's receiving core is at its most typical without Brown on the lineup . In Week 12, the Patriots will have Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III available at receiver.
Wide receiver Romeo Doubs will also be eligible to be activated off the injured reserve, if he's ready to play after sustaining a shoulder injury in Week 6.
Tommy DeVito is expected to start for the Patriots after they come off the bye in Week 12 against the Chargers. After DeVito's rough performance on Sunday , the fourth-year backup quarterback will need all the help he can get.
Although, Brown's production this season indicates he might not be of much help to the Patriots or their second-string QB. Three of the Pats five losses have come when Brown's on the field, and his 11 receptions rank second to worst among non-running backs, while his 128 receiving yards are the lowest of all pass catchers on the Patriots roster.
After paying a heavy price for the Super Bowl-winning receiver, the Patriots will have to wait even longer for his production to show.

title: Should We Give Up On the 2026 Patriots?
full_text:
What is there to look forward to for the rest of this season for New England Patriots fans? Truthfully, not much. But there are places where the Patriots can find success, and maybe even a playoff birth this season.
After what many are describing as a "Super Bowl hangover," the New England Patriots sit at 5-5 entering their bye week.
Losing half the amount of games in the first 10 weeks of play isn't what fans drew up for a team that lost just three regular season games and ran through the AFC playoffs. But there have been flashes of brightness, and despite a major setback, not all hope is lost for the Patriots.
Quarterback Drake Maye's injury during Week 10's game against the Lions is what has most people in New England ready to call it quits on the 2026 season.
Maye, whose ankle was fractured while being sacked on the final play of the drive , was ruled out indefinitely and reports say that he could miss extended time and potentially, the rest of the season.
Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito's performance on Sunday didn't give Patriots fans much to believe in either, as the fourth-year player completed 50% of his passes for 81 yards, as well as a touchdown and an interception.
While speculation remains about whether the Patriots stick with DeVito, switch to seventh-round pick Behren Morton, or look elsewhere for their starting quarterback , fans should pump the breaks at calling this team 'broken.'
There's no reason to have faith in DeVito as a backup quarterback yet. But if he can collect a few wins while Maye is recovering , then the Patriots stand a chance at earning a Wild Card spot.
Yes, you heard that correctly: while Maye is recovering. There is a very real chance that Maye plays football again this season. Though reports indicated Maye could be out for the rest of the season, the same insiders making these claims said that both Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson would miss extended time with separate injuries that caused neither of the two to miss game action.
The skepticism behind the reports that Maye's injury is season-ending should be discussed more when evaluating the near future of this Patriots team.
Currently, the Patriots are sitting one game back from the seventh seed in the AFC playoffs. New England has seven games to play in the 2026 season, with a majority of those games against teams with a winning record.
The biggest competitors for the Patriots spot in the playoffs are the Clevleand Browns (6-4) and the Las Vegas Raiders (4-6).
Cleveland has proven to be a challenging team to get through, but each of their wins this season has come in a one-score game. This should indicate that their legitimacy to contend for a playoff spot is overvalued. They could drop more than half of their remaining schedule, which includes to games against the Bengals and a trip to New Jersey to face the Giants.
🏈AFC Playoff Picture through Week 10!🏈 Is your team gonna make the playoffs? pic.twitter.com/3thecJox41
The Raiders, aren't as much of a concern for the Patriots, after New England dominated Las Vegas in Week 5 . This head-to-head victory for the Pats helps break a tie if the two teams find themselves in one. Las Vegas and New England will both play one of the best divisions in football in the reamining weeks of the season, but Vegas has to face the AFC West one additional time, compared to the three matches slated for the Patriots.
Realistically, New England should hope to win four of the last seven games to squeak into the playoffs. Finishing with a 9-8 record would allow the Patriots to secure a Wild Card spot and their second straight trip to the postseason. This record is commonly seen with seven seeded teams in the AFC.
Houston will also pose a threat to the final Wild Card spot, despite winning just three games this season. Last year, the Texans went on a large win streak to secure a playoff spot after a poor start to the season.
The familiarity of rooting for a tank is all too recent in the memory of Patriots fans, who watched back-to-back seasons where New England earned top-four picks in the NFL Draft.
Unfortunately, five wins is most likely too many for a pick that high, but New England could still end up close to the top 10 if they continue playing like they have over the past two weeks.
In the trade for A.J. Brown, the Patriots gave up a 2028 first-round pick instead of their first-round pick from this upcoming draft.
Mike Vrabel isn't the type of coach to tank for a draft pick. He build his idenitity on believing in the players that show up to the Patriots facility on day one of training camp.
The vibes in the Patriots building are “not good” Per: @DanGrazianoESPN He describes it as a “total Meltdown”. - ESPN insider @JFowlerESPN notes “Mike Vrabel is known for culture-building and tough-minded defense, and cracks in the foundation are showing on both fronts.” pic.twitter.com/CkzMiJhUqV
For this reason, it's unlikely that the Patriots will intentionally lose games, or put themselves in position to lose games, in favor of a better draft position.
However, if the Patriots don't make the playoffs, they'll likely miss it by a small margin (unless they completely collapse for the remainder of the season), which would put them in a difficult position, drafting in the late teens (where the not good enough, but not bad enough teams end up).
After the buy-in the front-office exercised this offseason, it's playoffs or bust for the Pats, whether or not Maye is their quarterback.

title: Is Drake Maye Coming Back This Year? Patriots Teammate Doesn't Think So
full_text:
The outlook for Drake Maye doesn't look great, and a fellow New England Patriots captain certainly didn't help.
Kevin Byard, who was voted a captain alongside Maye in his first season with the Patriots, was speaking on WEEI's Rich & Ken Tuesday and was asked about players stepping up in the wake of several major injuries across the board.
He mentioned how that's the reality of the situation the Patriots are in, and also offered some information about Maye's potential timeline.
"Like at the end of the day, our quarterback's out. He's probably going to be out for the rest of the season. And the reality of the situation is, is that we're going to have to get behind Tommy Two Chains (Tommy DeVito) at the end of the day," Byard said. "And you know, we're all going to have to do more, myself included. Everybody has to play better around our quarterback.
"I mean, this is honestly before Drake was injured as well. But we got to play better around our quarterback. We got two choices: we can rally behind this guy or we can pack it up. I mean, that's just where we're at right now in the season."
The Patriots haven't offered any additional comments about Maye's ankle, which was injured in the first quarter of Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions. Maye was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson — who tore his ACL celebrating the play — and would head to the locker room after a short time on the sideline.
DeVito came in to replace Maye, who is feared to have fractured his ankle.
"I'm not going to make any comments about his status until he gets back here," Mike Vrabel said Monday. "He's en route back here. He stayed with a few of our people, and they're en route back here. So, once he gets back here, and our people are able to visit with him again and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer. But I wouldn't imagine him being available when we come out of the bye."
The Patriots are 5-5 and now on their bye week , so they'll have some time to figure out their plans under center if Maye can't go for the remainder of 2026. If he isn't able to return in any capacity, it's a major blow for a team that was looking to get back to the Super Bowl after a season of great forture injury-wise.
This year? Not so much. Maye has been the latest player to suffer an injury that's put the team behind the 8-ball. Whether it's DeVito, rookie Behren Morton or an external signing , there will likely be a new quarterback leading the way.

title: Saints vs. Bears: Scouting Chicago's Dangerous Defense and 4 Key Playmakers
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints (3-6) face another difficult challenge Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears (7-2), whose defense has played a key role in the team's success this season.
While head coach Ben Johnson's offense has attracted considerable attention, Chicago's defense presents its own challenges for a New Orleans team that continues to struggle with offensive consistency under Kellen Moore .
Chicago's defense has been a driving force behind the Bears' impressive 7-2 start in Johnson’s second season at the helm, establishing itself as one of the NFL's toughest units to move the football against.
The Bears rank eighth in scoring defense (20.4 points allowed per game) and seventh in total defense (310.9 yards per game), with their greatest strength coming against the run. Chicago is surrendering just 91.1 rushing yards per game, the seventh-fewest in the league, while ranking 15th against the pass (219.8 yards per game).
However, what makes this defense particularly dangerous is its ability to get off the field. The Bears lead the NFL in third-down defense, allowing opponents to convert just 22.8% of their opportunities, and rank 12th in red-zone touchdown percentage allowed (53.8%). Chicago has also pressured opposing quarterbacks consistently, recording 26 sacks (ninth) while collecting seven interceptions (tied for 11th).
With injuries along the offensive line and an inconsistent rushing attack, the Saints must find ways to protect quarterback Tyler Shough, establish offensive balance and avoid costly turnovers.
Here's a statistical breakdown of Chicago's defense and three players the Saints must account for Sunday.
Through Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season; NFL rankings in parentheses.
Booker has emerged as one of Chicago's most productive pass rushers this season, leading the Bears with five sacks while recording 27 tackles and two forced fumbles.
Containing Booker is crucial for New Orleans given its offensive line injuries.

title: Saints vs. Bears: Scouting Caleb Williams and Chicago's Dangerous Offense
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints (3-6) face one of their toughest defensive tests of the season Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears (7-2).
In his second season as Chicago's head coach, Ben Johnson has established one of the NFL's most productive and balanced offenses, ranking seventh in scoring and total offense and fourth in rushing offense.
Between quarterback Caleb Williams ' playmaking ability, a talented backfield tandem featuring D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai , and an emerging star in wide receiver Luther Burden III, the Bears have no shortage of offensive weapons.
Considering New Orleans' offensive struggles, Brandon Staley 's defense will have little margin for error if the Saints hope to pull off an upset.
Here is a statistical breakdown of Chicago's offense and three players the Saints must account for Sunday.
Through Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season; NFL rankings in parentheses.
QB Caleb Williams (1,546 passing yards, eight touchdowns, five interceptions)
RB D'Andre Swift (576 rushing yards, 10 touchdowns)
RB Kyle Monanagai: 60 carries for 324 yards (5.4 yards per carry) and three touchdowns
WR Luther Burden III: 644 receiving yards, four touchdowns
WR Rome Odunze: 32 catches for 328 yards and a touchdown
TE Colston Loveland: 37 catches for 363 yards and two touchdowns
Despite missing three games earlier in the season with a hamstring injury, Williams has completed 68.7% of his passes for 1,546 yards, eight touchdowns and five interceptions in six games. He has also rushed for 145 yards and two touchdowns.
The former No. 1 overall pick's arm talent, mobility and ability to extend plays outside the pocket present a significant challenge for New Orleans.
While Chase Young, Carl Granderson and the Saints' defensive front must consistently generate pressure, maintaining disciplined rush lanes to contain Williams will be just as important to keep Williams from escaping the pocket and creating explosive plays downfield.
Swift serves as one of Chicago's primary offensive engines, driving both the ground attack and contributing significantly through the air.
Through Week 10, Swift has rushed for 576 yards and 10 touchdowns on 155 carries, alongside 24 receptions for 162 yards. Despite averaging 3.7 yards per carry, his high-volume scoring efficiency makes him critical to Chicago's offensive consistency.
Paired with Kyle Monangai, Swift forms a versatile backfield rotation designed to control game tempo and keep down-and-distance manageable.
To stay competitive, the Saints defense must disrupt this backfield early and prevent Chicago from establishing a sustained rushing rhythm.
In his second NFL season, the former Missouri standout has established himself as Chicago's top receiving threat, securing 49 catches for 644 yards (13.1 yards per reception) and four touchdowns.
Clearing concussion protocol on Tuesday, Burden delivers a major boost to the Bears' receiving group ahead of Sunday's game. His downfield separation, run-after-catch dynamic, and adaptability in Johnson's offensive system present a tough defensive assignment.
With cornerback Martin Emerson Jr . dealing with a concussion and the Saints releasing safety Justin Reid this week , New Orleans' secondary will face a considerable test against Burden and Chicago's talented receiving corps.

title: Saints Stock Down Report: Moore Running Out of Excuses Ahead of Bears Matchup
full_text:
Coming off their bye week with a chance to win consecutive games for the first time this season, the New Orleans Saints got the same old, same old .
While a handful of individual performances were encouraging during their loss to the Carolina Panthers last Sunday, the defeat exposed recurring issues that have plagued New Orleans all season, from questionable coaching and poor offensive execution to costly mistakes in critical moments.
With a challenging three-game stretch looming, it's becoming increasingly difficult to overlook the Saints' lack of progress in Year 2 under Kellen Moore .
Here are three whose stock has fallen after Sunday's loss to Carolina.
At what point does the rebuilding excuse run out?
The Saints have scored nine first-quarter points through nine games and have been held scoreless in the opening quarter seven times. Coming off a bye week, New Orleans failed to score in the entire first half against Carolina.
After the Carolina loss, it is the 25th time that the Saints have trailed in a game … out of the 26 games Moore has coached in. That’s worst in the NFL since the start of the 2025 season.
Recurring offensive struggles and an inability to win winnable games have made it increasingly difficult to identify tangible progress under Moore .
Even worse, New Orleans has to play the Chicago Bears (7-2), Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) and the Green Bay Packers (6-4) over its next three games, and the chances of winning at least one of those games are low considering not only are they better personnel-wise, but they have better coaching staffs.
Playing without Erik McCoy and Taliese Fuaga certainly didn't help, but Sunday's performance exposed the Saints ' lack of quality offensive line depth.
New Orleans rushed for 49 yards on 25 carries, averaging 2.1 yards per carry, but without Tyler Shough ’s 25 yards off of scrambling out of the pocket, the Saints averaged 1.4 yards per carry. On top of the poor run blocking, the unit could not protect Shough, surrendering three sacks. Pro Football Focus gave starting right guard Jeremiah Wright an abysmal 25 overall grade.
The offensive line remains one of the franchise's biggest roster construction failures.
McKinstry 's costly pass interference penalty in the closing seconds helped Carolina move into field-goal range, setting up Ryan Fitzgerald 's game-winning kick.
Although one play doesn't define an entire performance, the former second-round pick must show more consistency as the Saints evaluate their long-term future in the secondary, especially after releasing safety Justin Reid on Thursday.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly: Can the Saints Do Anything Right?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints had an opportunity to take control of the NFC South on Sunday, but instead delivered another frustrating performance that raised more questions about the direction of the franchise.
New Orleans (3-6) suffered a heartbreaking 20-17 loss to the Carolina Panthers at the Caesars Superdome, surrendering a game-winning 54-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald as time expired.
Despite Carolina committing 17 penalties for 152 yards, the Saints couldn't capitalize, finishing with just 49 rushing yards, two turnovers and another disappointing offensive performance under head coach Kellen Moore .
The loss dropped New Orleans to 1-4 at home and 0-2 against NFC South opponents, leaving the Saints searching for answers as their season continues to unravel.
Here is the good, bad and ugly from Sunday's loss.
Rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson led the Saints with 11 receptions, the most since Pierre Thomas caught 12 passes against the Chicago Bears in December 2007.
After missing the first seven games of the season, the rookie wideout has wasted little time demonstrating why New Orleans selected him eighth overall in April's NFL Draft.
His separation, contested catches, and reliability complement Chris Olave and should make this passing attack even deadlier.
However, the offense has become too predictable.
After a strong performance last week, the Saints' rushing attack went back to its old ways, gaining just 49 yards on 23 carries (2.1 yards per carry) against Carolina.
Quarterback Shough led New Orleans with 25 rushing yards, while Travis Etienne Jr. (14 yards), Audric Estime (6 yards), and Alvin Kamara (4 yards, 3-yard touchdown) combined for minimal output.
Although the absence of right tackle Taliese Fuaga and center Erik McCoy provides important context, the struggles within the ground attack were already present prior to their injuries.
Moore was hired because of his success as the offensive coordinator of the Philadelphia Eagles , one that had the NFL’s top rushing offense in 2024 and propelled them to a Super Bowl victory. He must fix the run game for New Orleans to sustain drives and score consistently.
Through nine games this season, the answer has been a firm no.
Carolina repeatedly handed the Saints chances by committing 17 penalties and struggling offensively, but New Orleans failed to capitalize.
The Saints were shut out in the first half, committed two turnovers, and generated insufficient offense against a sub-.500 Panthers squad. Even after Charlie Smyth tied the game with a 55-yard field goal with 41 seconds remaining, a pass interference penalty on Kool-Aid McKinstry set up Fitzgerald's game-winning kick.
More concerning is the lack of progress under head coach Kellen Moore.
Over nine games, the Saints have struggled with offensive inconsistency, poor execution and an inability to close games. Their 3-6 record inspires little confidence, and individual flashes from Tyson, Shough, and the defense cannot mask overall failure. To make matters worse, the Saints have trailed in all but one of the 26 games that Moore has coached in as the head coach of the Saints.
With upcoming road trips to Chicago and Cincinnati followed by a home game against the Green Bay Packers , the schedule provides no relief. Instead of making a statement in the NFC South, New Orleans showed just how far it remains from contention.
