title: DeVonta Smith Will Play vs. Steelers, Heating Up Eagles' Race for Leader in Receiving Yards
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – The race is on between DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon to see who will lead the Eagles in receiving.
Smith will return to the lineup on Sunday when the Pittsburgh Steelers visit for a 1 p.m. kickoff after missing five of nine games this season with a hamstring and three of the previous games before the bye. He has 310 receiving yards in limited action. Lemon has overtaken him and has a two-yard head start with eight games to play. Lemon also has more catches, with 37 to Smith’s 26.
“I feel great,” said Smith earlier in the week, “just continue to go out here this week, get these reps with Joe (Milton), and we just go from there.”
Milton will make his second start at quarterback. He took over the job in Week 9, so Smith has not played with him.
“Joe's a great quarterback,” said Smith. “He's still learning the offense. We're trying to get him up to speed. Being out for a while, I haven't got those reps with him, haven't kind of really been in the huddle with him. So, it’s me trying to learn how he is, how he calls the plays, and things like that. What his thought process is as well.”
Lemon has one game under his belt with Milton. That could be an advantage for the rookie in his quest to lead the team in receiving. Another advantage Lemon could have is that Dontayvion Wicks will miss his fourth straight game with an ankle/foot injury.
With A.J. Brown traded in the offseason, the expectation was that Smith would make it two straight years leading the team in receiving. Last year, he had 1,008 yards, edging Brown, who had 1,003.
In addition to Wicks, linebacker Zack Baun was ruled out for Sunday. Baun suffered a back injury in the Eagles’ pre-bye loss to the Giants.
Jihaad Campbell, who missed the previous two games with a hamstring/quad injury, will line up with Jeremiah Trotter Jr. as the starting linebackers, but depth could be an issue with Smael Mondon listed as doubtful for Sunday with an ankle injury suffered after stepping in for Baun against the Giants and making five tackles in 26 defensive snaps.
Running back Will Shipley, who had his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the week, is still on IR but is listed as questionable. If he plays, the Eagles will have to make a roster move to add him.
The Steelers listed six players as questionable: linebackers Patrick Queen and Nick Herbig, receivers Michael Pitman and Roman Wilson, safety DeShon Elliott, and rookie guard Gennings Dunker.

title: 3 Things Eagles Need From Joe Milton in Week 11 vs. Steelers
full_text:
Eagles quarterback Joe Milton will get his second consecutive start , and the second start of his career, against the Steelers on Sunday.
Milton completed 18 passes for 169 yards against the Giants in Week 9, and he'll look to build on that performance coming out of the bye week against the Steelers. That said, here are three things the Eagles will want to see from Milton in his second start.
With one start already under his belt and an extra week to learn the offense afforded by the bye week, Milton is feeling increased confidence ahead of the game against Pittsburgh.
“What's different for me now? My confidence. Just confidence in knowing this offense and what these coaches and my teammates around me are instilling in me and talking to me about," Milton said.
This increased confidence should translate to increased accuracy for Milton, who completed just 52% of his passes (18 of 34) in his first start. In fairness to Milton, he was consistently under pressure, but he still had his fair share of errant throws he'd like to have back. It would be nice to see improvement in that area. The fact that he'll likely have top receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks back should help.
Milton has garnered nicknames for his arm strength . He recently revealed (h/t Zach Berman) that he prefers "Mr. Rocket" to "Bazooka Joe."
Joe Milton doesn’t like “Bazooka Joe.” He prefers “Mr. Rocket.” “Bazookas only travel so far,” he said. pic.twitter.com/tur5oWbaJU
However, we didn't really get to see too much of that rocket arm in Milton's first start against New York. He averaged just five yards per attempt on his 34 passes during the game, and his longest completion went for just 20 yards. It would be nice to see the Eagles open things up a little bit more in that regard.
That would look like offensive coordinator Sean Mannion dialing up more deep balls to threats like Smith and Makai Lemon. At this point, there's nothing to be gained for the Eagles by remaining conservative. They might as well open things up and let Milton show off that nickname-worthy arm.
The thing that Milton did best in his start against New York was picking up yards with his legs. He actually led the Eagles in rushing in the game with 64 yards on nine carries—an average of 7.1 yards per carry. His ability to take off makes Milton an inherently dangerous quarterback, and he should continue to lean into that skill when the opportunity presents itself.
The goal for Milton moving forward should be to find a nice mix between showing off his arm and using his legs to move the ball downfield.

title: Potential Daniel Jones Flyer Leaves Eagles' Offense With Nothing to Lose (And Everything to Gain)
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles’ offensive shift this season has been a disaster .
Through nine games, the Eagles' perennial postseason berth is in hospice at 2-7 and in the midst of a seven-game losing streak, averaging just 16.4 points and 260 total yards per game—numbers that rank near or at the bottom of the league in points, yards, yards per play, and efficiency metrics.
The unit under first-time offensive coordinator Sean Mannion had looked lifeless from a structure standpoint, even when Jalen Hurts was under center , never mind novices like Tanner McKee and current starter Joe Milton.
Hurts is on injured reserve and likely out for the remainder of the season with blood clots in his lungs. The replacements—McKee (three starts, all losses) and Milton (one start: 18-of-34 for 169 yards)—have not provided a meaningful evaluation of Mannion's scheme, the rebuilding offensive line, or the skill-position talent.
Milton gets another start against the Steelers this weekend, but his development isn't going to reveal much about the actual scheme, as his late arrival from the practice squad in Dallas demands scaling things back.
Enter Daniel Jones, whom the Colts waived on Friday after an 11-game stretch that produced a league-worst 13 interceptions, a 65.4 passer rating, and a 3-8 record as a starter.
Per Shane Steichen, we have released QB Daniel Jones. pic.twitter.com/jdGAZqj9ZI
Jones is subject to waivers and would carry only a modest remaining salary this season if claimed, but a somewhat significant injury guarantee for 2027 virtually assures the veteran with 93 career starts will get to the open market and choose his next destination at something near the veteran minimum.
Jones would offer the kind of professional experience the Eagles’ current backups simply do not have and the opportunity to get maybe four to six games of clean evaluation for Mannion’s system.
This is not a call for Jones to be the long-term answer. He has been turnover-prone and inefficient in 2026, still working back from last year’s Achilles injury. But that is precisely why he is useful right now.
The Eagles have not yet seen what this offense looks like with a veteran starter who has navigated full seasons, protections, and complex defenses.
McKee and Milton have been asked to play with almost no runway. Signing Jones would give Mannion, head coach Nick Siriann, and general manager Howie Roseman a better read: Is the scheme fundamentally flawed? Is the offensive line too porous? Are the receivers unable to win at the required rate? Or has the problem been, at least in part, the lack of a quarterback who has actually done this at a high level for an extended stretch?
The Eagles are already out of realistic playoff contention. The second half of the season is an evaluation window, whether they want it to be or not. Using that period with a 29-year-old signal caller who has started nearly 100 games would be far more informative than continuing to cycle through developmental options who have combined for a handful of starts.
If Jones looks competent, it isolates issues elsewhere. If he looks as bad as he did in Indianapolis, the organization learns that the supporting cast and scheme may need even more overhaul than already planned.
From Jones’s perspective, Philadelphia can offer the kind of playing time that could convince another organization to take a flyer on him for the 2027 season. Another fringe benefit is that Jones remains very close to Eagles star running back Saquon Barkley from their days together with the Giants.
The cost would be low to sign Jones, and the information value could be high if the goal is still to figure out what has gone so wrong with the system.
However, if the Eagles have already made that decision and Mannion is essentially coaching out the string, Milton should remain the starter to see if he can develop into a capable backup for future seasons.

title: 3 Positions the Eagles Can't Afford to Use Their First-Round 2027 Draft Picks On
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season hasn't gone according to plan for the Eagles. Instead of being in position to compete for a playoff berth down the stretch, they are in position to compete for a top-five overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.
Philadelphia sits at the bottom of the NFC East with a 2-7 record and would be selecting fifth overall if the draft started today, according to Tankathon .  The Eagles also own the Jaguars' first-round pick (No. 26) in 2027. That gives general manager Howie Roseman a chance to address multiple positional needs before the second round even begins.
Roseman has thrived in this spot before. The last two Eagles to be drafted with a top-five pick were offensive tackle Lane Johnson (2013) and quarterback Carson Wentz (2016). Both players became Pro Bowlers and helped lead Philadelphia to its first Super Bowl title.
But whether it's No. 5 or No. 26, time will tell which positions Roseman will prioritize with his first-round picks. As tempting as it might be to draft various players, the Eagles have some positional needs bigger than others. Here are three first-round positions Philadelphia must avoid in the 2027 NFL Draft.
The quarterback position will always be discussed when a team has a high first-round pick. In Philly's case, taking a quarterback in the first round would signal a rebuilding mindset rather than a retooling one. That's a button Roseman does not need to push with quarterback Jalen Hurts still on the roster.
Hurts was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 6 after a calf injury caused blood clots to form in his body. While it's undoubtedly a scary injury, it's one that he can make a full recovery from. Hurts is only 28 years old and has led Philadelphia to the playoffs in each of the previous five seasons.
With that said, the Eagles have not gotten much from Tanner McKee or Joe Milton in Hurts's absence. Both pros will enter free agency next offseason. Snagging a quarterback on Day 2 of the draft would give Philly a prospect to develop as Hurts plays through the remaining two years of his contract.
There's a hole at safety in the Eagles' secondary. Veterans Marcus Epps, Michael Carter II and Kenny Moore have split the snaps alongside Andrew Mukuba this season. All three pros will become free agents after 2026. That doesn't mean that a safety needs to be selected in the first round, though.
Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio's system is built around eliminating explosive plays with a two-high safety shell. As a result, Philly doesn't rely on safeties to step up in run defense as much as other franchises do. This allows them to thrive with budget veterans or late-round steals at the position.
The NFL Draft dates all the way back to 1936. The Eagles have been part of every single one and have never selected a safety in the first round. Roseman has prioritized building the roster through the trenches during the past decade. There's no reason to deviate from that strategy in 2027.
Rookie Eli Stowers is the only tight end under contract for the Eagles in 2027. Dallas Goedert, Zach Ertz, Johnny Mundt and Grant Calcaterra are currently playing on one-year deals. Injuries and a lack of playing time haven't helped Stowers prove he can be the No. 1 option at the position, either.
Roseman will have to add to the tight end room before next September arrives. It's a must, but not a must that has to be handled in the first round. Only three of the nine tight ends to make the Pro Bowl over the last two years were first-round picks. Late-rounders have broken out across the league.
Passing on a dynamic edge rusher or a strong offensive lineman in favor of a first-round tight end would be overdramatic. Philly's poor offensive scheme is a bigger worry than the players who are running it. Tight end depth can be found in the later rounds, or through free agency and trades.

title: How the Eagles’ Week 14 Colts Matchup Changes After Daniel Jones’s Release
full_text:
With the playoffs looking more like a long shot by the day, most Eagles fans are already looking ahead to the future . They might lose more often than win down the stretch, but each remaining game gives Eagles fans a better idea of what needs to be done this offseason, both in terms of what needs to be added and subtracted.
Although fans are focused on what this weekend's clash with the Steelers might reveal , it might not be too early to start thinking about Week 14. After all, the NFL's latest breaking news will certainly impact it.
On Friday afternoon, the Colts announced that quarterback Daniel Jones has been released one season into his two-year, $88 million extension. Indianapolis clearly felt that the former NFC East QB was doing more harm than good under center after going 3-8 with a 58.4% completion rate, NFL-leading 13 interceptions, and a career-worst 65.4 passer rating in 11 starts.
Per Shane Steichen, we have released QB Daniel Jones. pic.twitter.com/jdGAZqj9ZI
With a date against the Colts scheduled for Sunday, Dec. 13, at Lincoln Financial Field, here's how Jones's release could impact the Eagles' plans.
Now that Jones was unceremoniously dumped, Anthony Richardson Sr. will be the Colts' starting quarterback for the rest of the season. Riley Leonard is the only other QB on their 53-man roster and practice squad.
It would've been nice to see defensive coordinator Vic Fangio's unit terrorize Jones, who is 2-4 in six all-time matchups against the Eagles. Instead, Philadelphia will likely be facing Richardson, who hasn't started a game since Week 16 of the 2024 season. He's completed 3-of-6 passes for 17 passing yards since then, underscoring the fact that Fangio & Co. won't have much recent tape to go over.
One thing that Eagles fans can likely expect from Richardson is worse accuracy than Jones. Even though the ex-Giant has only completed 58.4% of his passes this season, Richardson has been much worse, with an uninspiring 50.6% completion rate on 354 career attempts. That includes a 47.7% rate in 2024, which is also when he had as many games with two-plus interceptions as without them (4). He also threw five INTs in his last three starts before the Colts decided to pull the plug.
Jones is a mobile QB, but it's safe to say that Richardson will likely be running the ball a lot more than he does, especially when comparing their career numbers:
Richardson will be more likely to run with the ball, so it'll be important for defensive linemen like Jalen Carter, Moro Ojomo, and Byron Young to be ready. That's especially true when the Colts' athletic QB is known to have ball security issues, having fumbled 12 times on 111 carries between the 2023 and 2024 seasons. In other words, he lost the ball on about one out of every 10 rushing attempts, giving the Eagles even more reason to pressure him early and often.
Still, it's never wise to underestimate any opponent—no matter how promising the matchup might be. Richardson was a fifth-overall pick for a reason, and playing low-stakes football down the stretch might provide the pressure-free environment he needs to thrive. He also has proven to be clutch at times, boasting three career game-winning drives as a starter—one fewer than Jones has had since the start of 2025.
The Colts already lost to the Texans on Thursday night and will face the Giants in Week 12 before going on bye, giving the Eagles at least one recent Richardson game to scout before the Week 14 clash. The eventual outcome already looks promising for Philadelphia, and hopefully that becomes truer depending on what the early tape on Richardson shows.
Wins might not matter much at this stage of the season, but it'd be nice for Eagles fans to have something to cheer about down the stretch.

title: Eagles vs. Steelers Week 11: Who Wins & Why in Upcoming Battle Of Pennsylvania
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Eight games remain, but in the watered-down NFC East, the Eagles are clinging to the hope that a winning run over that stretch could land them atop the division for a third straight year.
It’s a slim chance, but a chance nonetheless. To make it happen, it has to start with a win on Sunday against the 6-3 Steelers , who visit the 2-7 Eagles.
That said, here are some matchups to be mindful as the Eagles look to beat the Steelers, along with a final score prediction.
Pros don’t like losing on purpose in a violent sport where a career can end at any time, but Philly would complain about a top-five draft pick if they lose out. That doesn’t mean the players will necessarily mail it in.
As left guard Landon Dickerson so aptly put it: “You don't make it to this highest level being a quitter when things get tough. That's not a professional athlete mindset. So, no matter what the circumstance is, we're gonna come in here every day and work and try and get better.”
With the NFC East as bad as it is, you never know what might happen if the Eagles find a way to keep the competitive fires burning and start winning.
“As we see that there's still hope, there are still things that are happening in our division that still provide hope that you can get this thing turned around,” said head coach Nick Sirianni.
The Eagles rookie has struggled the past two games, particularly in pass protection. That’s not a good sign with T.J. Watt coming to town. Watt is tied for seventh in the league with 7.5 sacks and has 122.5 in his Hall of Fame career. He lines up primarily as the left-side outside linebacker, but he also moves to the right side in subpackages.
Losing Jordan Davis in a trade opened a hole in the middle of the Eagles’ defense, specifically at nose tackle. It would help if the Eagles knew who their nose tackle would be. Davis was really their only one. Whoever it is—Ty Robinson and Byron Young will likely be the main players here—will have their hands full against Frazier, one of the best centers in the game.
Frazier is ranked first among 35 qualified centers in Pro Football Focus 's overall grade (79.5), third in run blocking, and fourth in pass blocking. He hasn’t allowed a sack, with just seven pressures and three penalties on 532 offensive snaps.
The Steelers’ QB is going to be in the Hall of Fame one day, but he is 4-3 against the Eagles in the regular season. All those games came with the Packers. It will be up to the Eagles' defense to put pressure on Rodgers. The defense is coming off a six-sack performance against the Giants, though linebacker Zack Baun, who had two of those, may not play due to a back injury.
Britain Covey should return from a knee injury that cost him the previous two games. His 12.6 yards per return are second-best in the NFL, while the Steelers' punt return coverage is ranked No. 8 in punt return yardage.
On kickoffs, the Steelers are ranked 30th in covering kicks but have a very good returner in Iowa rookie Kaden Wetjen.

title: Joe Milton’s Quiet Confidence Shines As Opportunity Knocks With the Eagles
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - A month ago, Joe Milton was on the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. On Wednesday, he stood in front of reporters at the Jefferson Health Training Complex.
The QB1 of the moment in South Philly was discussing his thoughts about the legendary Aaron Rodgers as the 2-7 Eagles try to steady the ship against a 6-3 Pittsburgh team that hasn’t won in Philadelphia since 1965.
When asked by Eagles On SI how closely he has followed Rodgers, Milton smiled and admitted he was watching film of the current Steelers starting QB the night before, realizing he is about to headline against one of the best to ever do it.
“Damn, I’m 26 going against A-Rod,” Milton said. “That’s A-Rod we’re talking about.”
A few minutes earlier, another NFL legend, Eagles’ defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, was describing Rodgers as one of the best QBs in history.
“Obviously I've seen a lot of him over the years,” Fangio said of Rodgers. “I mean, I don't think anybody can make a top five list of quarterbacks all time without him on it. Just a very pretty passer, great release, super knowledgeable, great anticipation. Just a guy I have a total lot of respect for.”
It’s a big moment and “a blessing” to square off with Rodgers, according to Milton, before the grounded part of the equation mixed in for the young QB.
That mix for Milton—wide-eyed enough to feel the moment, steady enough not to get lost in it—is the story of the signal caller’s sudden opportunity with the Eagles.
Milton has the next eight games to make a case and show whether he belongs.
When asked what’s different from Milton’s first thrown-together start before the bye against the New York Giants, the Florida native didn’t talk about his arm talent or scheme fit. He settled on confidence and how it's burgeoning.
“My confidence in knowing this offense and what these coaches and my teammates around me are instilling in me,” Milton said. “And just my reason to asking questions. I’m great at asking questions… I don’t think I can ask no lesser questions than I already do.”
Milton used the extra time the bye week provides to echo what the coaches wanted fixed—protections, blitz pickups, the verbiage.
“It was very helpful… being able to pick up the blitzes whenever they show up, and just really just understanding the verbiage that we’re pronouncing and saying here,” he said.
Milton’s opportunity with the Eagles arrived sans a training camp with the organization after having spent the first month of the season in a different city.
On Wednesday, he sounded like someone who stopped treating the playbook as a foreign language.
“I know what I need to know far as this offense… It’s not rocket science. Football is football no matter where you go,” said Milton. “Coverage is not gonna change… A play gonna be a play. And if it’s a run game, just hand it off to a running back.”
Milton doesn’t care for “Bazooka Joe,” a nickname developed as a nod to his prodigious arm strength. “I don’t like it,” he said flatly before offering up an alternative. “Rocket. Mr. Rocket.”
Why? “’Cause bazooka’s only travel so far.”
The smile came out again when he was asked about throwing to DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks for the first time at practice. Both starting receivers are expected to return on Sunday after missing multiple games.
The most revealing comments came when Milton was asked about the opportunity in front of him and the conversations he’s been having with those close to him.
Adversity has taught him to stay exactly where his feet are.
“I’ve been through a lot of adversity in my life, to where if you would’ve put me in this situation six years ago, I probably would’ve been too happy for the moment,” Milton admitted. “… But being able to go through so much adversity… I’m able to just be exactly where my feet are, and just take a deep breath.”
Milton pointed to his college career, which started at Michigan and finished at Tennessee. He got hurt with the Vols and watched his roommate, Hendon Hooker, ball out and win SEC Player of the Year.
Milton mulled transferring again and decided there was no point—just learn the offense and get better.
It’s the same approach he’s using now: ask the same question twice if he has to, take the notes, let the coaches repeat the teaching point until they stick.
Pittsburgh’s defense will come with its own problems. T.J. Watt and company can get home with the best in the league.
“They are allowed to do whatever. All I know what I have to do is just move the ball. Get the ball out and just move the ball,” said Milton.
His relationship with Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has evolved quickly, something Milton attributed to Mannion’s own experience of playing the position at a high level in college at Oregon State and for many years as an NFL backup.
Eight games to prove your worth is not the longest runway, but it’s significant enough for a quarterback to make a dent in the NFL’s psyche.
Milton believes he belongs in the moment he’s been given.

title: Eagles' DeVonta Smith Gets Honest About Injury, His Return and Losses Piling Up
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – There were some changes inside the Eagles’ locker room when they returned from their bye on Wednesday.
Practice squad defensive tackle was in Jordan Davis's old locker, and along the row of offensive linemen starters, Drew Kendall had moved into Cam Jurgens’ locker and Markel Bell took up residence in Lane Johnson’s locker.
Oh, and DeVonta Smith was back at his usual locker. The receiver was holding court for reporters, too. Usually a Friday talker, Smith was available two days earlier than he usually takes questions.
He is on track to return to the field on Sunday, when the Eagles host the Pittsburgh Steelers, after missing three straight games leading up to the bye. He has been out for five of the Eagles’ nine games this season with an injured hamstring.
He took aim at reports that he could miss the rest of the season after returning from a two-game absence to play against the Carolina Panthers, then being shut down for the next three games after that.
“I was 100 percent (against Carolina),” he said. “I know someone asked Nick about shutting me down during the season. I didn't rest my (butt) this whole summer. I didn't continue to get up at 4:30 in the morning every day to not play. My focus had been getting to where I was supposed to be. I felt 100 percent for that game. I feel 100 percent now. Some things happen out of my control because I know I do everything I can do for my body to make sure I’m in tip-top shape.”
Smith was a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice but that didn’t stop Joe Milton from enjoying his return. Same with Dontayvion Wicks, who was limited but should be available on Sunday.
“Those two guys coming back, obviously helps out the team, and for me to throw to those guys today was amazing,” said the third-year quarterback who will make his second straight start. “I mean, shoot, I couldn't stop smiling for real if you ask me. It was great because those guys, they, they boost the offense more, but they also give the guys that are younger in the room some more juice.”
Smith didn’t get too much into what happened against Carolina to sideline him again. He said he was on a snap count.
“We were right at the number, it just happened to happen,” he said.
It was likely reaggravated in a game that saw him targeted 14 times by Taner McKee. Smith made seven catches for 75 yards, including a 19-yard touchdown.
That he is ready to return is all that matters now, along with his ability to stay healthy and play the final eight games. He was asked if it’s been one of the most frustrating seasons from an injury standpoint and the losses that continue to pile up.
It’s something he certainly isn’t used to having spent his career mostly healthy and without absorbing many defeats. It’s a career that has seen him become just the fifth player to ever win a national title, a Heisman Trophy, and a Super Bowl, joining Tony Dorsett, Marcus Allen, Charles Woodson, and Reggie Bush.
“The injury, it is what it is,” he said in response to the frustration question. “Nothing I can do about it. I kind of got away from frustrating myself with that. I'm doing everything I can. But from a team aspect, I mean, it is frustrating.
“At the end of the day, you know, it's not over, especially in this division. I feel like there's still a chance in our division right now. But you can only take it one week at a time, so focusing on this week. Getting the win would be the biggest thing right now; just get back on track.”

title: Eagles Add Jaydon Blue to 53-Man Roster: How the Signing Impacts the RB Room in Week 11
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles had to do something .
Coming out of their Week 10 bye , Saquon Barkley was the only active running back on Philadelphia's 53-man roster, and Barkley is banged up, as he's been playing through hamstring and back injuries in recent weeks. So, the Eagles made a move by signing back Jaydon Blue to the active roster ahead of their Week 11 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Blue previously appeared in Philadelphia's two most recent games against the Washington Commanders and New York Giants, but he didn't receive any carries in either game. That will likely change this week.
With Blue as the only active back on the roster behind Barkley, he's almost guaranteed to get his first carries of the season, as the Birds have been cautious about Barkley's workload given the injury issues that he's dealing with. The last couple of weeks it was Elijah Mitchell in the role of the other back behind Barkley, but the team clearly wants to go in a different direction with Blue this week. Meanwhile, Mitchell is back down on the practice squad.
In five games for the Dallas Cowboys last season, Blue tallied 38 carries for 129 yards and one touchdown while averaging 3.4 yards per carry. It makes sense that the Eagles would want to see if they could potentially get some similar production out of the Texas product.
Barkley may be a bit healthier than he was before the bye thanks to an extra week of rest, so it remains to be seen how many carries he'll receive against Pittsburgh. It's possible that he'll be able to handle an increased workload, but the team will still certainly want to mix things up by sending Blue in for some plays at least.
The Eagles also opened the practice window for running back Will Shipley, who has been sidelined for the past month due to a partial tear of his plantar fascia in his foot. That means that Shipley is trending towards a return to on-field action, but it's unlikely that he'll be ready by the weekend. So, Blue should have an opportunity to show his stuff.
Blue is currently on a one-year contract, which means that he'll be a free agent over the offseason. Perhaps he'll be able to use his upcoming on-field opportunity to showcase his skills in order to help himself out at the negotiating table in a few months.
If he performs well in his role, it could encourage the Eagles to consider bringing him back next season as a depth piece. He could also be auditioning for other teams, but the Eagles will have first dibs, as Blue will be an exclusive rights free agent, meaning that the Eagles will be able to dictate whether they want to bring him back, or not. How he plays in the coming week(s) could have a major impact on his football future.

title: Eagles Sticking With Sean Mannion Looks Even Bolder After Cowboys' Christian Parker Decision
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA—The struggling Dallas Cowboys stripped Christian Parker of defensive play-calling duties after 10 games. The Eagles, staring at arguably an even worse offensive situation, are sticking with Sean Mannion despite a 2-7 start and seven consecutive losses.
Both are first-time coordinators and play-callers. Dallas’s defense is last in the NFL in yards allowed (393.8 per game) and rushing yards allowed (154.1), and 30th in points allowed (28.2).
After surrendering a franchise home-record 584 yards and three long touchdowns in a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer handed the headset to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine while keeping the 34-year-old Parker, the former Eagles secondary coach and defensive pass game coordinator, as the DC.
Parker will still run meetings and lead walkthroughs. He just no longer will call the games. Schottenheimer framed it as a win-now decision with Pettine’s experience, not a full demotion, and reiterated that Parker has a bright future.
Parker's former boss in Philadelphia, Vic Fangio, agreed with that sentiment after watching the young coach aid in the development of Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean en route to a Super Bowl LIX championship with the Eagles.
“Patience is not in overabundance in today’s society, especially in the sports world, but Christian will recover from that,” Fangio insisted. “It happened to [Broncos Head Coach] Sean Payton many years ago in New York and I think he’s recovered nicely. Joe Brady, who’s the head coach at Buffalo, he got fired during the season, didn’t even get kept on. I think he’s recovered nicely, as has [Cardinals Head Coach] Mike LaFleur in Arizona. The Jets fired him during the season a couple years ago. He’s recovered nicely. Christian will do the same thing. He’ll be fine.”
The Eagles are in their own mess on the offensive side of the ball, of course. They are  last in total yards and near the bottom in scoring under Mannion .
Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots, the offensive line and skill-position groups have been thinned by attrition, and the offense has struggled to generate consistent drives or an identity.
After a bye-week evaluation, however, Nick Sirianni confirmed Mannion remains the play-caller.
“Yeah,” Sirianni said when asked if Mannion is still calling the plays. “I think we had a really good bye-week process, got to evaluate a lot of things within that. You go through that — I think I put into pretty good detail how we go through things and the things that present themselves as you go through it.
“I think we have a good plan of action moving forward of the things that we want to do to move forward and to get better. Obviously, we haven’t been good enough on offense, but I like our plan of attack and our process that we went through last week.”
Pressed on what he sees beyond work ethic, Sirianni pointed to Mannion’s process: “I think he’s really smart. I think he has a great football mind. He thinks through everything. I think one thing I always value about him is [that] anybody can come and give a play and say, ‘Hey, I want to do this, or I want to do that.’ I think he just has a really good monotonous approach to figuring out everything that could potentially happen in that situation, what the downfalls are, what the upside is and whether we move forward with some of those things. I think that just speaks to the detail that he has.”
Sirianni admitted “it hasn’t gone well enough for any of us this year offensively.”
“That’s coaches, that’s players,” the Eagles coach said. “We all have things that we need to do better, but I do love that approach that he has with that. As we looked at some of our schemes that he’s brought in, some of those have been really, really good. It has to be better as a whole without getting too much into the specifics of what those are. We just need to build on that.”
The contrast here is stark.
Dallas treated 10 games of historically poor defensive performance as enough to strip a first-time play-caller of the job’s most visible duty. The Eagles are showing that patience Fangio noted is in short supply and giving Mannion more runway after an even longer stretch of bottom-of-the-league offensive production.
The dichotomy between two organizations reveals different risk tolerances – patience vs. pragmatism.
The Cowboys are prioritizing experienced in-game management while the division race still theoretically exists. Philadelphia is betting on the process, the detail, and the schemes, even as the demonstrated performance to date remains among the worst in the league.

title: Steelers Cannot Ignore This Opportunity
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are getting healthier, but the one position they may actually be getting more beat up at is safety.
DeShon Elliott suffered a knee injury before the team's Week 10 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals, ending his night before it ever started. He returned to practice in a limited capacity this week, but it's unknown what will happen in Week 11, or if his injury is something more concerning - or related to his prior knee injury.
He missed most of the season while on Injured Reserve after being declared not ready come Week 1 from an injury that ended his 2025 season.
So, the team's two reliable safeties are Jaquan Brisker and seventh-round rookie Robert Spears-Jennings.
And they clearly need help.
That help may have just emerged. The New Orleans Saints released safety Justin Reid, who requested to be let go by the franchise to try and join a contender before the playoffs. The 29-year-old is already a two-time Super Bowl champion with the Kansas City Chiefs, and is now looking for a new home to finish his 2026 campaign.
Thank you New Orleans ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/FNHDVM6l1A
That is the perfect scenario for the Steelers. This team needs help at the safety position and was looking for defensive back help at the trade deadline . After not finding any, they got embarrassed by the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10, which put a spotlight on all of their issues - and how desperately they need to fix some of them.
Reid has 126 starts (of 130 games) under his belt and a true free safety with centerfield ability. He carries 11 interceptions with him to his next team and could step into a starting role immediately.
Maybe the Steelers don't want to replace Spears-Jennings as a starter, but they can certainly use help with another free safety. Reid allows Brisker to play more in the box, and Elliott not to have to worry about being out of position when he comes off the bench. And if everyone eventually meshes and gets healthy, this is a group of four that has two players who thrive playing much more natural to their skill set.
It's a must for the Steelers. If they haven't already, they should be putting in a waiver claim for Reid immediately and hope they land him. If they haven't and don't plan to wait it out, they should be all over trying to sign him the second he hits the open market.
This is an opportunity that could be a significant difference-maker for Pittsburgh and their playoff aspirations. This team needs help and can't avoid it any longer . And the solution to one of their problems is now available.

title: Steelers Must Eventually Take Action With DK Metcalf
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have a real DK Metcalf problem on their hands.
Metcalf, simply put, has fallen completely short of expectations as the Steelers' No. 1 wide receiver. Drops have become a major issue for the 28-year-old (six on the season, second-most among WRs according to Pro Football Focus ) and he's failed to win his routes consistently, resulting in a general lack of separation when compared to what he's previously shown on tape throughout his career.
With three years left on a four-year, $132 million extension that he signed with Pittsburgh upon arriving via trade from the Seattle Seahawks in March 2025, the organization needs Metcalf to turn his season around in order to get anything remotely resembling a positive return on investment.
At this point, however, the Steelers also have to seriously consider cutting into his playing time and perhaps give him a bit of a reset given his overall struggles in 2026.
After a rough Week 1 performance against the Atlanta Falcons in which Metcalf was called for offensive pass interference on two occasions while also dropping a pair of passes, Aaron Rodgers told reporters that he was going to keep looking his way despite a slow start to the season.
"I'm not worried about DK at all, man," Rodgers said on September 16. "I love DK. He's one of my closest friends on the team, and I'm going to keep feeding him."
Rodgers has made good on that promise. Metcalf has 71 targets through nine games, which is the most on the Steelers and 26 ahead of Germie Bernard (45) in second place while also being tied for the 18th-most across the NFL.
Unfortunately, though, Metcalf's large share of the work in Pittsburgh's passing game hasn't come with positive results. Sure, he's had a few bright moments, such as his 115-yard outing in Week 4 against the Cleveland Browns and a 93-yard contest vs. the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6.
Metcalf's 50 percent catch rate is the worst in the league (per Sharp Football Analysis' Warren Sharp ), however, and he's on pace for a career-low 816 yards over 17 games.
He cannot be relied upon as Rodgers' clear-cut No. 1 option for much longer. Metcalf doesn't get open and make plays down the field nearly as often as the Steelers need him to, and his drops are a major issue.
Pittsburgh likely won't outright bench Metcalf unless things really spiral out of control. At the same time, reducing his snap count and putting less on his plate, even if it's just temporary, could help both him and the offense readjust.
Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) have missed five and four games, respectively, while residing on the reserve/injured list. That has put the Steelers' offense in a bit of a pickle due to a lack of receiver depth beyond Metcalf and Bernard.
Both Pittman Jr. and Wilson had their 21-day practice windows opened this week , however, meaning that their returns could be imminent.
Pittsburgh hasn't had a fully healthy receiver room in right around a month-and-a-half, though it is closing in on that being the case with Pittman Jr. and Wilson back on the practice field.
Once both players return, it should open up more possibilities for the Steelers' offense while also taking some of the pressure and heat off of Metcalf by letting Rodgers spread the ball around more, which would be a positive for all parties involved during the final stretch of the regular season.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Former Steelers OL Makes Surprising Troy Fautanu Suggestion
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — Troy Fautanu has become an important part of the Pittsburgh Steelers' offensive line, and could remain so for the foreseeable future.
Former Steelers offensive lineman Willie Colon, who played seven seasons with the team from 2006 to 2012, winning Super Bowl XLIII, sees Fautanu as a crucial player for the Steelers' offensive line, arguing for a contract extension on the " In The Locker Room " podcast.
“Troy, yeah, you pay Troy," Colon said. "I mean, it makes sense from the standpoint of, at this point, he's starting to be the anchor of your offensive line.
"He's still a very young, good left tackle that has a lot of upside, and the ceiling's high for him. And then, you understand, him going into next year, he's going to be more comfortable at the position. He's not going to have to worry about the switch around and all that.
'He's going to be your left tackle moving forward. And now you can start to groom him and shape him up to be what he needs to be for the line. So if I was Omar Khan and company, I would start thinking about extension and getting him together ASAP.”
The Steelers made Fautanu their first-round selection in 2024 out of Washington, as they have spent the past few seasons building up their offensive line.
Fautanu played in just one game as a rookie, as he dislocated his kneecap, ending his season early on, but came back in 2025.
He spent all last season as the starting right tackle, not missing a game, and helping the Steelers win the AFC North Division.
Fautanu has started at left tackle in 2026, with Steelers head Mike McCarthy putting 2026 first-round draft pick Max Iheanachor at right tackle.
The move was not foreign to Fautanu, who played most of his time on the left side at Washington, but he's not been as good as people expected.
Fautanu has given up 22 total pressures, including five sacks and six hits, according to Pro Football Focus .
He gave up two sacks to New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young in the 16-10 win in Paris, France, in Week 7, the first time in his career he's done so.
Fautanu is still adjusting to a new position in the NFL, especially after playing on the right side his first full season as a professional.
The Steelers offensive line has some strong young talent, including center Zach Frazier, right guard Brock Hoffman and left guard Mason McCormick .
Keeping this unit strong will play a big role in the future of the Steelers' offense, especially after quarterback Aaron Rodgers retires after this season.
The Steelers will monitor Fautanu and his progress, and if he improves the way they think he will, they should consider the contract extension.
Dominic writes for Pittsburgh Pirates On SI, Pittsburgh Panthers Pn SI and also, Pittsburgh Steelers On SI. A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

title: Steelers' Injury Report Highlighted by Nick Herbig's Status vs. Eagles
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers enter their Week 11 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles with several major injury questions.
Most of those questions are positive ones for the Steelers - like will wide receivers Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. both return against the Eagles or just one? Will they activate rookie offensive lineman Gennings Dunker from the IR?
But as the positive news mounts, the Steelers are never too far from a setback. With the team's latest injury report ahead of their Week 11 matchup, another player is now the biggest concern. Outside linebacker Nick Herbig did not participate in two previous practices due to a rib and hip injury, and after being designated as not participating in a third straight team session, he has been listed as questionable against the Eagles.
Additionally, the Steelers listed Dunker, Pittman, Wilson, inside linebacker Patrick Queen, and safety DeShon Elliott as questionable. Queen is dealing with a fractured thumb he sustained in Week 10, but is expected to play, while Elliott missed Week 10 due to a knee injury he suffered pregame.
Nick Herbig, DeShon Elliott, Michael Pittman Jr, Roman Wilson, Gennings Dunker All questionable for Steelers pic.twitter.com/pwDcNWK1Wx
There was a brief moment during the team's Week 10 loss where Herbig was in serious discomfort and exited towards the sidelines. After a few moments, however, he was back on the field. He finished Week 10 playing 28 defensive and 12 special teams snaps. It was just a slight decrease in share of the snap count compared to previous weeks.
More concerning is how much this will hamper Herbig moving forward. It's already been a difficult 2026 campaign for the fourth-year EDGE rusher. He is fourth on the team in sacks, with 3.0 in nine games, but he's currently being outproduced by T.J. Watt (7.5 sacks) and Alex Highsmith (3.5 sacks), as well as inside linebacker Patrick Queen (3.5 sacks).
Even if Herbig plays in Week 11, there's no telling how close to 100% healthy he truly is.
As far as the other players on the report, part of that feels far easier to decipher. Both Pittman Jr. and Wilson have been full participants in practice this week. That's the strongest indication that both could return to the lineup. Add in the fact that the Steelers waived receiver Brandon Smith, and it feels like a foregone conclusion that both pass-catchers are in the lineup against the Eagles.
Dunker is not so clear-cut, in my opinion. The Steelers need the third-round pick to be able to suit up, simply due to the lack of available offensive lineman. After Mason McCormick was placed on Injured Reserve due to a dislocated ankle, the Steelers have just seven healthy offensive linemen on the active roster.
If Dunker cannot go, the team will likely have to elevate one of two offensive linemen from their practice squad, Steven Jones and Doug Nester. If either is added to the active roster, it would mark their NFL debuts.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Seven Former Steelers Players Selected in 2027 UFL Draft
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Multiple former Pittsburgh Steelers were selected in the recent 2027 UFL Draft, giving them their next chance to make it in professional football.
While their opportunities with the Steelers didn't pan out, seven players who recently spent time in Pittsburgh are set to make their way to the spring league, which kicks off their upcoming season in March of 2027.
A few of these names will be very familiar to the Steelers and their fanbase, but the rest are names that spent brief moments here during preseason or training camp.
Beanie Bishop was the definition of a flash in the pan with the Steelers. Originally undrafted out of West Virginia University, Bishop signed with the franchise as a free agent ahead of the 2024 training camp and preseason.
Despite little fanfare upon his arrival, Bishop earned a spot on the active roster and exceeded expectations. He appeared in 17 games as a rookie, making 45 total tackles and 0.5 sacks.
What was most impressive, however, was his playmaking ability as a first-year player. Bishop defended seven passes and recorded four interceptions, two of which came off of current Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
After that breakout rookie year, Bishop's NFL career quieted. He failed to make the Steelers' roster the following season, and he bounced around the league looking for a home.
Now, he gets his next chance with the St. Louis Battlehawks, who made him the 29th overall pick in the recent draft.
Another round down 💪 #UFLDraft pic.twitter.com/qmHqVVlHTS
At this most recent training camp, a pair of defensive backs stood out. Those players were Devan Boykin and Jack Henderson, and it seems the UFL agreed, as both were taken in the recent draft.
Boykin was a member of the Indiana Hoosiers' 2025 NCAA National Championship team before signing with the Steelers as an undrafted free agent. He appeared in all three games of the preseason, playing mostly as a nickel corner.
Henderson is a long and rangy safety who displayed an impressive level of athleticism during this past preseason. He spent two preseasons with the Steelers after finishing his collegiate career at the University of Florida. He couldn't quite displace rookie seventh-rounder Robert Spears-Jennings, however, and that cost him a spot in the organization.
For all of the seven players drafted by UFL organizations, it's a golden opportunity. It provides the chance to show that they are the type of players many NFL franchises wish they could be, and it might land one or several of them another chance in the top professional league in the world.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Aaron Rodgers' Roster Comments Should Send Message to Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have a few issues on their team, but wide receiver sits right at the top.
DK Metcalf has underperformed and the team is hoping that the r eturn of Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson will be enough to help this group reach the level it needs to. If not, they'll keep looking at their internal options, with Max Hurleman being the name that keeps coming up.
Hurleman was mentioned by both head coach Mike McCarthy, quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Metcalf himself as an option to help the receiver core. The second-year player out of Notre Dame is on their practice squad and just returned from the practice squad IR.
And once again, Rodgers is making a pitch for him.
"I'd love to see Max [Hurleman] get some opportunities on special teams," Rodgers said during his weekly press conference. "Again, that's above my pay grade, though."
Hurleman is an explosive athlete who was the Fighting Irish's punt returner during his final college season. While also a reliable pass-catcher and someone who has experience playing running back and cornerback as well, he could be a contributor for Pittsburgh in multiple ways.
But Rodgers pointing out special teams is interesting. The Steelers have one of the worst kick and punt return units in the National Football League, and rookie fourth-round pick Kaden Wetjen has been a pretty big disappointment in his first season.
Hurleman may be the answer they're looking for, or at least another direction the team can look to help improve the group.
On a weekly basis, McCarthy seems to discuss the poor performance of the special teams unit, and special teams coordinator Danny Crossman doesn't have much of an answer for Wetjen other than continuing to get more comfortable.
The second-year UDFA has shone in two preseasons and training camps, and may be worthy of a shot on the 53-man roster. Even McCarthy admitted that.
If it also helps the Steelers get into better field position before the offense takes the field, why not test out the move? It almost makes too much sense for Pittsburgh to give it a shot.
Wetjen may be the future of the return position, but he's not making the plays a fourth-round returner needs to make. Right now, he's one of the big problems this team needs to solve before the postseason.
And their answer may have just came back from injury and is waiting on the p-squad.

title: Steelers Offense Must Lean on Two Names Against Eagles
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers' rushing attack disappeared in Week 10. The Cincinnati Bengals decimated the Steelers in their AFC North showdown, defeating them by a final score of 38-18.
The Steelers were outplayed in every facet of the game, but the most disappointing part was Pittsburgh's inability to move the ball on the ground. The Steelers finished Week 10 with 102 rushing yards, but that doesn't tell the full story.
It was a forgettable performance all-around, but in order to find any success on offense, they must reignite the running game. Thankfully, their Week 11 opponent, the Philadelphia Eagles, presents a favorable opportunity for the Steelers to get back on track.
Needing a win, the Steelers have to rely on their top duo of Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren, no matter what.
The lack of a run game in Week 10 can be attributed to the fact that the Steelers were down early. After the Bengals jumped out to a 24-3 lead at halftime, the offense had little choice but to abandon the run game in a comeback effort.
Still, whenever the Steelers went back to the rushing game, it proved unproductive. Lew Nichols led the team with 43 rushing yards, but that was all gained in garbage time. The top two running backs, Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren, combined for 41 total rushing yards on just 12 carries and 34 receiving yards on seven receptions.
But I would argue the Steelers abandoned the run game too early against the Bengals. Even facing a three-touchdown deficit, the Steelers' only productive piece of their offense during the season is their run game. Their best players all season long have been Jaylen Warren and the offensive line. So, when the team went down, it made no sense to me that their comeback efforts were so reliant on passing the ball.
Sure, the running game wasn't bearing any fruit, but it produced just 43 fewer yards than the passing game did.
Thankfully for the Steelers, the Eagles are a far inferior team compared to the red-hot Bengals. It's been a season of disarray in Philadelphia, with starting quarterback Jalen Hurts out for the season, plus the trading away of multiple starters on both sides of the ball.
That's led to a 2-7 record and one of the NFL's worst defenses. The Eagles are allowing an average of 353.4 total yards per game and 126.1 rushing yards. Both figures rank 25th in the NFL. They are also allowing 24.6 points per game, ranking 19th in the league so far.
The Eagles' defense is especially vulnerable against the Steelers' rushing attack after they moved defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a pair of draft picks ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline.
Down one of their most impactful defensive players, Dowdle and Warren must be the focal point of Pittsburgh's offense in Week 11. The pair combined for just 12 carries in Week 10, and that number has to be doubled against the Eagles.
The Steelers have to get their top duo more involved on offense. No matter what happens or how the game plays out, the Steelers absolutely cannot abandon the running game again.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Antonio Brown Shares Advice for Steelers' DK Metcalf
full_text:
Antonio Brown offered some advice to Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf as he continues to run into issues with drops.
During an appearance on "The Matchup" podcast with former Steelers teammate Emmanuel Sanders and Chris Harris Jr., Brown stated that Metcalf needs to start going back to the ball while improving his concentration.
"I see DK Metcalf trying to box a guy out. Yo bro, you gotta go back to the ball. Take your nose to the ball," Brown said . "I feel like guys gotta be more confident taking their nose to the ball. You gotta take your nose to the ball first, and your eyes gotta catch it. It's eyes, nose hands.
"Most of these guys, they just use hands, no eyes. You gotta have the concentration. You gotta be focused to be a good pass catcher."
"I see D.K. Metcalf trying to box a guy out. Yo bro, you gotta go back to ball. Take your nose to the ball." @AB84 on WR drops in @NFL With @ChrisHarrisJr & @ESanders_10 on 'The Matchup' https://t.co/wK4t72rMEb pic.twitter.com/48O6vrYwlr
The Steelers can't afford for their No. 1 wide receiver, who also has three seasons left on a four-year deal worth $132 million, to keep dropping passes.
The reality of the situation, though, is that Metcalf's hands have always been inconsistent. He posted a combined 20 drops during his first two seasons in the NFL (2019 & 2020) with the Seattle Seahawks, per Pro Football Focus , before settling in and having 18 over his final four campaigns with the team.
Metcalf then finished with six drops in his first season with Pittsburgh in 2025 after arriving in a trade from Seattle.
Now, however, he has six drops through nine games, which is the second-most among wide receivers, behind only Matthew Golden of the Green Bay Packers with 11 ( per PFF ). That means Metcalf is on pace for 11 drops in 2026, which would tie his career-high from 2020.
If he were producing at a star level, Pittsburgh could at least put up with a drop here and there. That's not the case, though, nor is it close to it.
Despite being tied for the 18th-most targets in the league with 71, which is also the most for any Steeler this season, Metcalf has just 432 yards and has an incredibly poor catch rate of 49.29 percent to go with it.
To Brown's point, Metcalf has some work to do in terms of refining his technique and building on his concentration.
There are times when he lets the ball travel too deep instead of extending his arms, which leads to drops such as the one he had down the field in Week 8 against the Cleveland Browns.
On the flip side, there are also instances where Metcalf doesn't track the ball into his hands and starts turning upfield before he has it secured.
At this point, Metcalf might just need a reset. Whether that's having his role simplified or playing less snaps once Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are officially back from the reserve/injured list, he can't continue to go about his business like usual until he fixes his woes.
Metcalf isn't unsalvageable, nor is his 2026 campaign, but there's a lot of work to do over the final eight games of the regular season.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Waive WR After Wilson, Pittman Return to Practice
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are parting ways with a veteran wide receiver.
Ahead of their Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles, the Steelers announced that they have waived Brandon Smith from the 53-man roster.
With Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) both having their 21-day practice windows opened this week while on the reserve/injured list, a bit of a roster crunch is coming at receiver for Pittsburgh. As a result, Smith is now on his way out.
The 27-year-old signed to the 53-man roster just before the Steelers took on the Cleveland Browns in Week 8 after the team exhausted all three of his elevations from the practice squad this season.
Smith's first time on the game day roster, which came by way of a practice squad elevation, was back in Week 5 vs. the Indianapolis Colts after Pittman Jr. landed on IR.
He was then elevated again in Week 6 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after Wilson was placed on IR, and his third elevation was in Paris vs. the New Orleans Saints during Week 7.
Smith, who was a standout during training camp, has played in a total of five games for Pittsburgh this season. Over that span, he recorded four catches for 39 catches over 154 offensive snaps.
Smith will likely return to the practice squad when and if he clears waivers, though he can no longer be elevated and thus would have to re-sign to the 53-man roster somewhere down the line in order to play for Pittsburgh again during the regular season.
After placing Mason McCormick (ankle) on IR earlier this week in addition to waiving Smith, the Steelers now have two open 53-man roster spots.
As a result, Wilson and/or Pittman Jr. could theoretically be back on the roster in time to play against the Eagles. The same goes for Gennings Dunker (knee), whose own 21-day practice window was opened this week as well.
It's a safe bet that at least one of Wilson or Pittman Jr. will suit up vs. Philadelphia and take Smith's spot. Dunker would appear to have a good shot of making his return this weekend too and serve as the top backup guard behind starters Spencer Anderson and Brock Hoffman, though Pittsburgh could also elevate Doug Nester and/or Steven Jones from the practice squad and have them fill a depth role.
Because the Steelers will ultimately need to free up three spots in order to accommodate the returns of Wilson, Pittman Jr. and Dunker, another 53-man roster move will be required.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers’ Nick Herbig Becoming Growing Concern Before Eagles Game
full_text:
There's some concern for the availability of Pittsburgh Steelers EDGE rusher Nick Herbig for the team's Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
On the Steelers ' second injury report of the week following practice on November 19, Herbig was listed as a non-participant with a hip/ribs injury.
The 24-year-old has now missed each of Pittsburgh's first two practice sessions this week, and with game designations set to come out on November 20, Herbig's status bears watching as the team gets ready to head over to Philadelphia.
Though he finished out the remainder of the contest and thus was not ruled out, Herbig did go down with an apparent injury during the first half of the Steelers ' 38-18 blowout loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10.
Herbig got banged up as he was attempting to tackle Bengals running back Samaje Perine from behind while Patrick Queen hit him high.
From there, Herbig headed to Pittsburgh's sideline and was checked out by the team's trainers before reentering the game shortly after.
He logged 40 total snaps vs. Cincinnati, with 33 coming on defense and seven on special teams (per Pro Football Focus ) while posting a single tackle and a pressure.
Herbig, despite a fruitless outing against the Bengals, had really started to kick things into gear as a pass rusher ahead of the Steelers' Week 9 bye.
He logged five pressures ( per PFF ) and a sack in the team's Week 8 victory over the Cleveland Browns after having finished with five pressures and a pair of sacks in a Week 6 comeback win on the road against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
If Herbig isn't active against the Eagles, T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Jack Sawyer would all be in line to play more snaps for Pittsburgh.
None of the Steelers' EDGE rushers have missed any games up to this point in the season, making it tough to pinpoint what the workload would look like in the event that Herbig doesn't suit up this week.
Herbig has logged an average of 34 defensive snaps per game this season, with 29 of those coming along the defensive line according to PFF's data.
Watt and Highsmith would likely see a larger increase in their snap count over Sawyer, but the latter has been on the field for 32 percent of Pittsburgh's defensive reps this season (up from 25 percent in 2025, per Pro Football Reference ) and thus should also earn a few more opportunities if Herbig isn't out there against the Eagles.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: The Biggest Threats to Seahawks Returning to Playoffs
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are on the outside looking in for the NFC playoff picture during their Week 11 bye, but they still have a strong chance of making it to the postseason.
NFL.com gives the Seahawks a 49 percent chance of making it to the playoffs, largely due to the fact that several teams are fighting for playoff positioning in the NFC. Even though they are in eighth place in a seven-team playoff picture, they have better odds than the Green Bay Packers, who currently sit at a 39 percent chance.
Here's a look at the biggest threats to the Seahawks making it back to the postseason.
The Packers hold the final spot in the playoffs, but they are also in last place in the NFC North, where all four teams are above .500 through the first 10 weeks of the season. The Packers are also on their bye week, but they will face off against the Los Angeles Rams the day before Thanksgiving.
That is their first of four games down the stretch against teams that are currently in the playoff picture. The Packers are in direct competition with the Seahawks for this final spot, which makes them the biggest direct threat to Seattle.
Naturally, the Rams are going to find themselves here because they play two games against the Seahawks in the final three weeks of the season.
Both teams have the same record through 10 games, and their positioning as division rivals makes them an obstacle and hurdle for the Seahawks' playoff hopes.
Ultimately, the biggest threat to the Seahawks making the playoffs is themselves. Seattle is in control of its own destiny, and they have often found themselves in places where they have lost the game on their own, through unforced errors compared to the other team.
The Seahawks have lost three of their four games this season by less than three points, and in all of those games, they could have won if they did not make their own mistakes. The Seahawks hold the No. 1 defense in the NFL, which puts them in position to win any game. The offense has been what's inconsistent about this season, and that unit needs to clean things up in the second half if they want a chance to get back to the playoffs.

title: 4 Reasons Why The Seahawks Restructured Sam Darnold, Julian Love, and Ernest Jones
full_text:
Yesterday, it was announced that the Seattle Seahawks had freed up $9.88 million in 2026 cap space by converting base salary into bonus money on three veterans. Sam Darnold , Julian Love and Ernest Jones all had some of their short term cap hits pushed out into the future. What we don’t yet know is why they did it, so let’s run through a few different options.
This seems to be the most likely reason why the team would feel an immediate need for nearly $10 million in 2026 cap. Remember, the trade deadline has passed, so there will be no major player acquisitions right now. It’s possible that the team is thinking about handing out a new contract that will come with a significant additional 2026 hit.
The Seahawks entered yesterday with less than $4 million in space, so any additional cost would probably require these moves. The candidates for such an extension would be Quenton Nelson, Zach Charbonnet , Uchenna Nwosu, Josh Jones, and Anthony Bradford. My guess would be Charbonnet, since he’s on his rookie deal, so it lines up.
To make a long story short, what the Seahawks did with the contracts of these three veterans is push 2026 cap hits into future seasons, while also increasing the hypothetical dead cap if the team moves off of them before their contracts are up. This indicates the team isn’t planning on parting ways with them this offseason, and are comfortable with the guarantees.
It’s not a sure thing. In 2024, the Seahawks restructured D.K. Metcalf’s contract, and then traded him the following offseason. Plans can change, and none of these restructures are extreme enough to be committing. But it seems like Darnold, Love, and Jones are part of the long-term here in Seattle. It’s up to each individual to decide if they approve of that .
This one is a bit of a sleeper. Remember, unused cap space gets rolled over into future seasons, so if the Seahawks don’t use the $9.88 million, it opens up for use in 2027. Obviously, that doesn’t matter if the money got sent to 2027 in the first place, but not all of it was. We know for a fact that some of Darnold’s money was kicked into 2028 and 2029 with void years.
I haven’t yet seen confirmation of the same with Love and Jones, but assuming void years are in play here, you could look at this as borrowing from 2028 to open up space in 2027. Byron Murphy and AJ Barner might be the targets here. It’s a bit of a stretch, but with the trade deadline passed, I think we need to be a little creative to solve this one.
I’m pretty dubious of this one, but it’ll obviously be considered. Brandon Aiyuk is about to come available, and there could be a bidding war for him. Tyreek Hill is still waiting for his chance to return to the field. Joey Bosa, Cam Robinson, Will Dissly, and many more are hoping for another shot in the NFL. There are interesting talents you could go pick up.
I just don’t think any of them are looking at much more than the veteran minimum at this point. Maybe Aiyuk, but I suspect the $3.5 million the team had before the restructures would be sufficient for any of this business. There has to be something bigger going on. I’m thinking Charbonnet gets extended over the next few days, but only time will tell.

title: 3 Seahawks Players Who Have Been Pleasant Surprises Entering Bye Week
full_text:
Entering their Week 11 bye , the Seattle Seahawks are just 6-4. That's a disappointing record considering they were 14-3 last season. It also has them chasing the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers, who are currently the No. 1 seed in the NFC.
While Seattle would love to have a better record, they know they have been able to overcome some obstacles this season. Injuries have left them short at some key positions, but head coach Mike Macdonald and his staff have found a way to keep them in playoff contention .
With that being the case, let's take a look at three players who have been able to help the Seahawks more than expected this year stand out as pleasant surprises.
No one expected Emanuel Wilson to carry the load at running back, but that's what he's had to do throughout the first 10 games of the season. Seattle knew Zach Charbonnet would miss the start of the year, but they expected rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price to be the centerpiece of their rushing attack.
Injuries limited Price, who has just 208 yards and one touchdown in six games played this season. His absence forced Wilson into the spotlight and while his yards per carry aren't exciting (just 3.6 yards), Wilson has 403 yards and three touchdowns in eight games.
He had his best game in the win over the Kansas City Chiefs, going for 100 yards on 24 attempts, but has not seen a carry since that game due to the return of Price and Charbonnet . Still, his efforts, especially in that win, were a pleasant surprise.
Following their win in Week 1, Seahawks On SI's Brendon Nelson named Nehemiah Pritchett the Seahawks next breakout star . He was completely accurate as Pritchett went from a developmental piece to a trusted defender. Pritchett has five pass breakups and two interceptions this season, showing major growth both in coverage as well as in run defense. His arrow continues to point up and he's been a huge part of their defensive success this season.
Sam Darnold was injured on the first drive of the season and Drew Lock stepped in to deliver the win over the New England Patriots. Since then, Darnold has continued to struggle with health, which means Seattle has turned to Lock to start three games this season.
Lock has done his job during those starts, completing 73.1 percent of his attempts for 837 yards with seven touchdowns and no interceptions. More importantly, Seattle is 3-0 during his starts.
The Seahawks' season could have been undone by Darnold's injuries this year, but instead, Lock has played well enough that there are calls for him to keep the starting spot .

title: 3 Seahawks Who Won't Be in Seattle in 2027
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have seven games left after their bye , but it could be the last stretch of games for some people in Seattle.
With over 20 free agents seeing their contracts expire this offseason, some players won't be around for 2027. Here's a look at three players who are likely finishing out their tenures in Seattle.
Drew Lock is on this list because he is likely going to receive a raise from some team this offseason. Lock is currently under contract for $2.5 million, but he has won three games this season as a starter. He came in as a relief for Sam Darnold in Week 1 against the New England Patriots after just the first drive.
Some could say he's responsible for most of the wins the Seahawks have had this season up until the bye. Given that he is a free agent coming up, other teams may look at him as a potential bridge quarterback option that could start at points next season.
Some of those teams may include the Arizona Cardinals, who he's beaten twice already this year, as well as the Minnesota Vikings, who have former Seattle general manager Nolan Teesley, who's quite familiar with Lock from their days with the Seahawks.
Rodney Thomas II is having a great first season with the Seahawks, but there is potential for it to be his last. He received a starting job early in the year, but has not seen the starting lineup since Week 4. He played nearly every defensive snap in the first four games, but has only seen seven since Week 5.
The Seahawks have utilized Thomas mostly on special teams since his demotion from the starting lineup. With Bud Clark expected to come back next year after a horrific injury in the preseason, there might not be room for him on the depth chart. Other teams could look at him as a potential one-year option guy that would offer more money than the Seahawks.
Zach Charbonnet is in the final year of his deal, and he is about to set his value on the market based on how he performs in the last seven games of the season. In his first three appearances in 2026, after returning from his torn ACL, he has proven that he can lead a backfield. Charbonnet is averaging a career-high 4.6 yards per carry and is at 64.7 yards per game, which is also a career high.
It's one thing to do this over a three-game stretch, but if he can do it over 10 games, that could add a lot of value for him on the open market. The Seahawks should be interested in another contract with Charbonnet if it doesn't break the bank, but given the fact that they selected Jadarian Price in the first round of last year's draft, the team might opt to choose his replacement as opposed to signing him for another deal.
