title: 3 Reasons Why The Seahawks Should Extend Zach Charbonnet
full_text:
A month ago, I wouldn’t have even entertained this conversation. It seemed like the playbook for Zach Charbonnet this season was obvious. He’d get back on the field, help the team by being competent in pass protection and not fumbling, look like a shell of his former self, and (maybe) start rounding into shape by January. Useful, but not worth keeping around.
After the last few games, my perspective has completely flipped. Now, I wonder if the Seattle Seahawks should sew this one up before the end of their bye week. Zach Charbonnet’s time as a Seahawk can not end after this season is over, and they should extend his contract. The sooner the better. Let’s go over a few reasons why I believe this is the case.
I don’t want to make any sweeping and final judgements after three games, but the way Charbonnet looks right now to me is beyond anything I’ve seen from him previously. He was a good player, of course, but for the last couple games he’s looked both faster and more violent to me. And that goes beyond the poor caliber of defense he’s played in those games.
Charbonnet’s yard per carry averages his first three seasons were 4.3, 4.2, and 4.0. So far this year, it’s 4.6. We need more data, but keep in mind he’s playing behind a makeshift, unstable offensive line. If this is the Charbonnet we’re getting going forward, then I want it to be part of this team. Get him running behind Quenton Nelson and you might have something special.
Unlike with Ken Walker III, any Zach Charbonnet extension should not be something that alters the financial state of the franchise. Spotrac estimates his future contract value at 3 years and about $19 million, which is less than half what Walker got. That kind of money has an impact, but it’s rather unlikely that it costs you a quality player or ruins your future plans.
If you extended him now, it might not even be that much. For the moment, Charbonnet is still a running back who is fresh off an ACL tear and has never had a thousand yard season in his career. It could end up being a 3 year deal at $15 million, or even 2 years at $10 million. Some long-term security now might be worth more to Zach than rolling the dice later.
As of this moment, the Seattle Seahawks are approximately a coin flip to make the playoffs this year. A big reason why is them trying to play games without NFL-caliber running backs in an offense that is designed to be run-first. A single Jadarian Price injury derailed their offense until he and Charbonnet returned. We can’t let that happen again in 2027.
I like Price, but he may not be much more than a change-of-pace back in the NFL (remember this is what he was in college). I like this upcoming running back class in the draft, but putting that much pressure on rookies is dubious. The Seahawks need a proven veteran in the backfield, and Charbonnet is better than any free agent you could sign next year.

title: Seahawks Draft Picks Heading into Bye Week
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have 11 draft picks at their disposal going into the 2027 NFL Draft.
With the team currently enjoying their bye week , here's a look at what those 11 picks look like throughout the three-day event in the spring.
The Seahawks have their own first-round pick this year, and it could be within the top 20 if they were to miss the playoffs. However, Seattle is hoping to pick as close to number 32 as possible, just like they did in 2026 after they won the Super Bowl.
The Seahawks also own their second-round pick, which they are hoping will be as close to No. 64 as soon as possible because that would mean Seattle wins the Super Bowl for the second straight season.
The Seahawks traded their third-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for Quenton Nelson just before the trade deadline. Part of the reason they were willing to part ways with the pick is that they have a pair of compensatory picks coming their way in 2027.
The Minnesota Vikings hiring former Seattle assistant general manager Nolan Teasley and Boye Mafe leaving free agency for the Cincinnati Bengals would give the Seahawks potentially another third-round pick. If not a third, it would likely move into a fourth-rounder.
The Seahawks traded their own fourth-round pick to the Cleveland Browns in the 2026 draft so that they could select Beau Stephens from Iowa in the fifth round. However, they own another compensatory pick from losing Kenneth Walker III in free agency to the Kansas City Chiefs.
In the fifth round, the Seahawks have three picks to work with, including their own and a pair of compensatory picks from Riq Woolen and Coby Bryant, who left in free agency to sign with the Philadelphia Eagles and Chicago Bears, respectively.
The Seahawks traded their own sixth-round pick to the Los Angeles Chargers for Avery Smith just before the start of the season, but they are expected to have a compensatory pick to replace that one.
The Seahawks have their own seventh-round pick , on top of another from the Atlanta Falcons, which they acquired in exchange for offensive tackle Michael Jerrell.

title: Why Seahawks OC Brian Fleury is Fighting for His Job
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury is in his first season with the team , and it hasn't gone exactly as planned.
After spending seven seasons on the coaching staff for the San Francisco 49ers, Fleury was given a promotion to become the Seahawks' offensive coordinator , but the numbers have shown that he hasn't quite been ready for the job. Here are the reasons why the Seahawks could keep Fleury and fire him as well.
The Seahawks have had four offensive coordinators in the last four years, and it could become five if they choose to fire Fleury. He isn't likely going to be a head coach in 2027, so the only reason he wouldn't be back with the Seahawks is if they fired him.
As a team, the Seahawks are averaging 333.2 yards per game, which ranks 15th in the league, right in the middle of the pack. They're also scoring 22.3 points per game, which ranks 17th in the league. The numbers aren't at the standard of a Super Bowl contender, but they also aren't completely awful either.
One could also make the argument that the Seahawks' offensive troubles have not been linked to the play calling, but rather to the personnel. The team has not been fully healthy in the backfield until the past few weeks, and the quarterback situation has been a work in progress with Drew Lock and Sam Darnold splitting time under center.
If the Seahawks fail to reach their goals this season, they are going to have to make some kind of change or pivot in the offseason. While Fleury may deserve a second chance to correct some of his mistakes, the Seahawks might not have the time to give him that opportunity.
They may look for a different voice in the league that could elicit the results they got when Klint Kubiak was the offensive coordinator in 2025.
If they feel there is someone better suited for the role other than Fleury, the team might take those actions this offseason, as opposed to waiting another year or two for things to get better. Time is of the essence in Seattle's Super Bowl window, and they can't waste it.

title: 3 Most Disappointing Seahawks Players Entering the Bye Week
full_text:
At 6-4 , the Seattle Seahawks are still in good shape to make a run at the playoffs, but it's still not an ideal record for them. The defending champs have already lost more games this year than they did in 2025 when they went 14-3 and secured the No. 1 seed in the NFC.
Of course, expecting the same record might have been foolish. As Super Bowl winners , the Seahawks entered 2026 with a target on their backs. They also have a more difficult schedule as the reigning NFC West champions.
Still, they have the talent to win every week, making their current record somewhat disappointing. On that note, here's a look at three individuals who have contributed to the up-and-down season and are considered the biggest disappointments entering the bye week.
Looking for a spark at the 2025 deadline, the Seahawks made a trade with the New Orleans Saints to bring over receiver and return man Rashid Shaheed. He had just 188 yards on 15 receptions in nine games with Seattle, but scored two touchdowns on special teams.
He flashed enough to give the Seahawks hope that he could be a key piece of the puzzle going forward, leading to a three-year, $51 million extension . Through 10 games, he has 17 receptions for 171 yards with no touchdowns. Making matters worse, he hasn't been explosive on returns, averaging 10.3 yards per punt return and 27.0 on kickoffs, both down from 2025. Seattle bet big in Shaheed, and so far, that gamble hasn't paid off.
Seattle made the bold move to let Kenneth Walker leave in free agency, and they replaced him with rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price. Injuries have slowed him down as Price has missed four games. He has yet to break out this season, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry and has just 208 yards. He did score his first career touchdown in the win over the Las Vegas Raiders, which hopefully will give him a boost in the second half, but as of now, he hasn't delivered as expected.
As we enter the bye week, there's no player who has been more of a disappointment for Seattle than quarterback Sam Darnold. After a strong 2025 campaign, Darnold has struggled with accuracy and ball protection. His completion percentage dropped from 67.7 to 60.2 and he has 10 touchdowns against nine interceptions.
Darnold has missed three games due to injury, and is just 3-4 as the starter. Seattle is 3-0 with Drew Lock playing in place of him, which has led to questions about Darnold's job security. He proved in 2025 that he can play at an incredibly high level, and needs to show he can bounce back once the bye week ends.

title: 3 Seahawks Fighting for Next Contract
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are at the bye week , looking ahead to their final seven games of the season.
The team has over 20 players expected to hit free agency at the end of the season , some of whom Seattle will want to keep to continue their winning trends. Here's a look at three players who are likely on the team's radar to try and return for next season.
Quenton Nelson is the new kid on the block after being acquired in a trade ahead of the deadline with the Indianapolis Colts. It remains to be seen if Nelson would agree to a long-term extension with the Seahawks, but Seattle would certainly entertain the idea if it was possible. Nelson is 30 years old and still has a lot of high-level football ahead of him as one of the top interior linemen in the league.
The Seahawks would consider signing him to a new deal if the price was right, but the value of his new deal will likely be determined by how he performs coming off this injury in the final seven games of the year.
Myers has been the Seahawks' kicker for every game since 2019, but his contract is up at the end of the year. So far this season, Myers has only missed three field goals, one of which came against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10.
Myers can be one of the top kickers in the league when he's performing at his best, so the team will likely want to renegotiate a new deal with him, depending on how he performs in the last half of the season. Myers could sign a deal that keeps him in Seattle for the remainder of his career, so there should be interest on both sides to get something done.
Sundell is in a different boat than the others as an exclusive rights free agent. This means Seattle will be the only team that can negotiate with him, and they will likely keep him, considering he has played every snap this season as the team's starting center.
Sundell could earn up to $5 million on his next contract, so it is in his best interest to put his best football in front of him so that he can be rewarded with a handsome payday in the offseason.

title: Positions the Seahawks Can Upgrade in the 2027 or 2028 NFL Draft
full_text:
There are plenty of games left for the Seattle Seahawks (6-4), who are just on the outside of the NFC playoffs. The Seahawks have been dealing along the roster since the season started , but it’s been developing as the season progressed. Seattle is still competing for a playoff spot, but the front office is creating scenarios for building their roster.
​The 2027 NFL Draft will give the Seahawks several opportunities to build their roster. The biggest focus will be on the front office to address the biggest weaknesses on the roster or problems that will be coming after next season. This 2027 Draft possesses a lot of talented players that the Seahawks will address with their biggest position needs. The 2028 NFL Draft also has a lot of potential.
​The Seahawks didn’t acquire an edge rusher in the 2026 NFL Draft or the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline. After this season, Derick Hall is the only rusher returning to the team for the 2027 season. This might be an indication that the Seahawks might wait until the draft to make a move for a franchise edge rusher.
While the pass rush pressure is high, the Dark Side Defense doesn’t possess high sack numbers . If there is a position for general manager John Schneifer to select in the first round of the 2027 Draft, it would be for an edge rusher.
​The Seahawks possess the league’s best wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba , but they are limited outside of him. Cooper Kupp is running out of steam, Rashid Shahed is an explosive gadget receiver, and second-year receiver Tory Horton hasn’t stepped up. Quarterback Sam Darnold or Drew Lock needs another young receiver to be open when they are escaping the pocket. The wide receiver position would be an area that the Seahawks could address within the first three rounds.
​This season raised a lot of key concerns about the interior defensive line moving forward. Veteran defensive tackles Leonard Williams and Brandon Pili have gone through injuries . There is still a lot of information and concern over Williams’ stinger injury.
Their other veteran in Jarran Reed, might have been on the trade block, but has one year left on his deal. Finally, Rylie Mills has been good, but not great in his first full season. A day-two pick in the 2027 or 2028 Draft might have to be accessed on a reliable, young defensive tackle opposite Byron Murphy II.
​Here is the wildcard position. The Seahawks might trust Darnold or Lock moving forward after this season with a new contract. If the Seahawks take this route, then a day three pick should be accessed.
If, however, Seattle’s front office is ready for a new franchise quarterback in 2027 or beyond, then a day one or early day two pick would have to be made for a young quarterback in the 2027 draft. If the Seahawks bring back Darnold next season without an extension, then they should be at the front of the quarterback-needy teams for the 2028 NFL Draft.

title: Why the 49ers will Lose to the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City
full_text:
The 49ers will lose to the Vikings Sunday Night in Mexico City, but not for the reason you might think.
Most people picking the Vikings to win expect the 49ers' defensse to struggle, considering it gave up 40 points to the Cowboys last week and 29 points to the Falcons a few weeks ago.
I don't expect the 49ers' defense to struggle. They get to face Kirk Cousins, a decidedly mediocre quarterback whom they just intercepted three times two weeks ago when he was on the Raiders. The 49ers also don't have to face the Vikings' No. 2 wide receiver, Jordan Addison, because he's out.
The only player the 49ers' defense really has to worry about is Justin Jefferson, who's great, but I doubt he'll score three touchdowns by himself without Addison on the field.
The reason the 49ers will lose this game is their offense. It's the best offense in the league, but it's going to struggle on Sunday.
That's because the Vikings have the best defense in the league, and their defensive coordinator, Brian Flores, has ownage over Shanahan. A Shanahan-coached team never has scored more than 17 points in a game against a Flores-coached team.
Chris Simms, Shanahan's best friend, thinks Shanahan will struggle on Sunday.
"I don't think Shanahan is going to be able to get in his bag," Simms said on NBC Sports . "I don't. One of the things I know with Kyle and what he has said about Brian Flores in the past is, 'I've come to terms with the fact that half the game is going to be sh---y, and I'm hoping the other half of the game we can make some big plays.
"I think you'll see some inconsistencies from the 49ers. You might see one drive where they go three plays, 70 yards and score a touchdown, then they go three-and-out four drives in a row. I think that's the game you'll see."
This game will come down to the chess match between Shanahan and Flores, and Shanahan hasn't shown that he can win that contest. He likes to use condensed formations -- wide receivers lined up extremely close to the tight end and offensive linemen -- which invite defensive players to line up close to the quarterback and blitz.
Brock Purdy is elite at beating blitzes with quick passes if he knows where the blitzes are coming from. Unfortunately for Purdy, he and Shanahan don't do a good job of anticipating Flores' blitzes -- the condensed formations make it difficult to decipher pre-snap who is and isn't blitzing -- and Shanahan doesn't give Purdy the power to reset protections at the line of scrimmage, which is a big reason Purdy got sacked six times when the 49ers faced the Vikings in 2024. It's also why the 49ers gave up 9 unblocked rushers to the Chiefs in the Super Bowl.
The proper adjustment would be to spread out the Vikings' defense in one-by-three formations that provide the threat of quick screen passes to Deebo Samuel on the perimeter, but I don't expect Shanahan to make this adjustment. He won't abandon his scheme even when it's the reason the 49ers will lose.

title: Why the 49ers Have a Massive Advantage Over the Vikings
full_text:
Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy have never beaten the Minnesota Vikings together. They're like their NFC Kansas City Chiefs.
They have struggled against the Vikings, and defensive coordinator Brian Flores is the reason for that. He has the San Francisco 49ers' number.
To make matters worse, his defense this season is better than the previous two times he's faced the 49ers. It could be a long night in Mexico City for the 49ers.
However, they have a better chance of having the last laugh this time, and it's thanks to their massive advantage that they have over the Vikings.
That massive advantage is the acclimation to elevation. The 49ers have been practicing in Colorado Springs all week. It sits 6,035 feet above sea level, which is roughly 1,300 feet lower than Mexico City.
While it's not a perfect match, the fact that the 49ers have closely replicated the conditions in Mexico City for their war with the Vikings gives them the advantage.
They won't gas out as much or as early in the game as the Vikings will, which will help the 49ers get off to a fast start. They're already feeling the difference after being there since Monday.
"I know everyone makes a big deal about it and sometimes it is, but I'm less out of breath right now walking here than I was on Wednesday I think when I talked to you guys," Kyle Shanahan said. "Then I couldn't read the whole injury report, so everybody gets better each day but you can definitely still feel it. We'll be better after today, a little bit better tomorrow, but still when you get to Mexico City and it's 2,000 feet higher, we'll still feel it then too but it definitely won't be as bad."
Shanahan is underselling how crucial it was to acclimate to the elevation this week. It's just like when they went to Australia a week before playing the Los Angeles Rams in the season opener.
It turns all of the disadvantages that would typically derail a team into a massive advantage. It helped them in Week 1, and it will certainly help them in Week 11 against the Vikings.
In a way, playing the Vikings in Mexico City was an awesome setup as opposed to Santa Clara. The 49ers need all the help they can get to defeat the Vikings with playoff seeding on the line.

title: 3 Key 49ers Who Will Be Crucial to Beating the Vikings
full_text:
The Mexico City showdown with the Minnesota Vikings is a critical one for the San Francisco 49ers with playoff seeding on the line.
It won't be easy beating the Vikings, but it can be if three key 49ers are at their best. That said, here are the three 49ers players who will be crucial to beating the Vikings on Sunday night.
Minnesota's defensive front is scary, especially because defensive coordinator Brian Flores calls blitzes to assist them. The physicality and overwhelming numbers have been an issue for every offensive line they've faced this year.
The 49ers' offensive line will be key in this matchup, but Connor Colby needs to be the one who steps up. He's by far the weakest link on the offensive line. Colby has the fourth-highest pressure rate allowed (12.5%) among left guards.
He can easily get overwhelmed and confused should Flores unleash a flurry of blitzes to his side. The 49ers should expect that and provide support, but they can't do it for the entire game. Colby will need to hold his own at some points.
If he can't and struggles throughout the game, it will be extremely difficult for the 49ers to find a rhythm on offense. And if Colby struggles, it might be indicative of the rest of the offensive line's performance.
It's time for Brock Purdy to get some payback against the Vikings. He's 0-2 in his career against them, which is thanks to Flores. Purdy has more giveaways (4) than touchdowns (2) in those two games.
Defeating the Vikings will only be possible if he continues his high level of play. He will need to be sharp when Flores inevitably dials up a million blitzes. Thankfully, Purdy is sharp against the blitz.
He leads the NFL with 12.1 yards per attempt when blitzed this season, the first qualified quarterback since at least 2016 with more than 11 yards per attempt against the blitz.
His 12 touchdowns against the blitz are the most in the league, per Next Gen Stats. If Purdy can continue to play well against the blitz, he will have neutralized a major strength of the Vikings' defense.
No other 49ers player leading up to this game has been talked about more than Nick Bosa . He's yet to collect a sack this year and isn't making a significant impact that a player of his elite caliber should be.
Bosa has generated pressure on 12.5% of pass rushes this season, the lowest mark of his career, and has gone five games without a sack, his longest career drought.
If he can quiet all of that talk with a big-time performance against the Vikings. All eyes are on the 49ers' offense against the Vikings' defense, but Bosa and the 49ers' defense can steal the show and be the driving force in winning the game.

title: 49ers Give Encouraging Mike Evans Update Ahead of Vikings Matchup
full_text:
So you're saying there's a chance?
Mike Evans was listed as one of the nine questionable players ahead of the 49ers' Mexico City matchup with the Vikings. That's a good sign that he will be active.
Evans has missed the last three games with Achilles tendinitis. He made his return to practice on Thursday in a limited capacity. However, the 49ers want to see how he fares on Saturday.
Usually, a player listed as questionable will be good to go for the upcoming game. But the 49ers need to be careful with Evans. They probably shouldn't play him against the Vikings.
The last thing they need is for Evans to undo all of the positive gains he's made with his Achilles. As much as they need him against Minnesota, they need him more for the long haul.
If one more week off will help him, even if it's just a bit, they should do that. I'd lean towards Evans not playing against the Vikings, but it's a toss-up at this point.
The 49ers know how important defeating the Vikings is. It will have major implications for attaining the No. 1 playoff seed in the NFC.
That might be enough to convince the 49ers to let Evans suit up. You can expect the 49ers to wait as long as possible to make an official ruling before game time.
"Having Mike out there, everyone knows how good Mike is," Kyle Shanahan said. "I think the guys have done a good job holding it down with him not out there, but Mike's our guy and a very unique player and been doing it at a high level for a very long time. Played really unbelievable for the games he played in this year and it'd be great to get him back.”
Along with Evans, Dre Greenlaw is the other toss-up, questionable player ahead of the Vikings matchup. He's nursing a neck injury, which is scary and tricky.
The 49ers will need to take it up until game time to fully know if he can go. As of now, they are hopeful he can go, but I'd imagine Greenlaw will play through the pain, if anything.
As for the other questionable 49ers: Upton Stout, C.J. West, Nate Hobbs, Khalil Kareem, Mac Jones, Jordan James, and Luke Gifford.

title: How the 49ers Decide When the Play Kaelon Black
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers appear to have finally found a competent backup running back to complement All-Pro rusher Christian McCaffrey. While 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak noted that they do not go into the game with a set amount of carries for each, they do hope to get both of them into a rhythm.
Still, the determination of who leads the team in carries, or who is better in specific scenarios, is more game-dependent.
“I think a lot of it's game-dependent,” said Kubiak when discussing the running back split. “You go into every game hoping to get both guys in a rhythm, hoping to get both guys some carries. I think it's game-dependent.”
The team typically has been reserving the tough , inside runs that require physicality for the rookie from Indiana. Then, McCaffrey, the aging superstar, is saved for the rushes that can be big plays. Black helps block more in the passing game; McCaffrey catches more passes. While Kubiak did not straight up admit that was the split, he did note the difference.
“(Black's) got a good feel, he's been— he's running physical, running hard, and then Christian goes in there and gets his drive, where he had a 17-yarder and an 18-yarder, and that was awesome,” Kubiak said, describing a sequence in the second half of the Cowboys game.
Kubiak noted that Black started with power and McCaffrey came after that with a big play. This is what the 49ers coordinator said is the ideal scenario.
“That's kind of what you want, that's the perfect scenario,” stated Kubiak. “Both guys getting a rhythm, both guys get their carries, but you got to kind of feel how the game's going, you got to kind of feel what your team needs, kind of who has the hotter hand. Who you're kind of feeling more, and I think that just kind of changes drive to drive, and you let it play out, but you go in hoping to get both guys involved and to affect— because I think both guys have a different effect on the defense, and you want to get them both involved.”
Getting Black involved in this way is keeping McCaffrey fresh. More than that, Black is not being used to the point where he will hit a rookie wall. Rather, he will be starting to hit his stride around now. The 49ers' usage at running back could be the difference from past years that can put the team over the edge.

title: 49ers Coach Reveals What Makes Vikings Defense So Dangerous
full_text:
When the San Francisco 49ers take on the Minnesota Vikings in Week 11, it will feature one of the best offenses in the NFL against one of the best defenses in the NFL. 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak opened up on the challenges that the Vikings defense presents, making them one of the best in the NFL.
Kubiak noted that everything starts with the experience and comfort level the players have in the defense.
“They're going to throw a lot at you,” stated Kubiak on Thursday. “To me, the thing that jumps out the most is: this is a unit that's been playing together for, I think, 3 or 4 years now, and so the comfort level and the familiarity that this group of players has is kind of unmatched in this league.”
Jalen Redmond and Levi Drake Rodriguez have been on the team since 2024. Dallas Turner was a 2024 draft pick, and Andrew Van Ginkel was signed that same offseason, along with Blake Cashman. Byron Murphy has been with the team since 2023, while Josh Metellus and Harrison Smith were in Minnesota before Brian Flores.
Kubiak noted that the experience the core has could not be replicated easily.
“I mean, these guys— they're playing in this scheme where they're throwing different blitzes at you, different coverages, but the way they're tied together and the way that they can all play so fast and decisively— that's what makes this an elite defense to me,” stated Kubiak. “I think if you tried to go and install this defense in a new place, it would take a while to get a group of guys to play the way they play.”
Due to that ability, Kubiak noted that this makes it easier for Flores to call up different pass rushes and blitzes that other teams cannot.
“They know how to kind of back each other up. It's just a unit that is so tied together that it's so impressive,” added Kubiak. “Then you add the challenges of the scheme on top of it. It's probably the most unique scheme you're going to go against in the league in terms of the amount of blitzes they're going to run. The different ways they're going to try to affect the quarterback. Ut's a huge challenge, and they're going to do that to stop the run. They're going to do that to affect you in the drop-back passing game to get to the quarterback. So we got to work cut out for us.”
The 49ers offense ranks first in both EPA/play and success rate. The Vikings defense is also first in EPA/play and success rate.

title: Kyle Juszczyk Reveals His Proudest Moment in a 49ers Jersey
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers and Kyle Juszczyk have worked in tandem for over a decade.
In fact, he's technically the longest-serving player for the 49ers in the Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch era. He's been there since the initial rebuild after joining in free agency and has since played a role in both of the franchise's trips to the Super Bowl.
2026 marks his tenth year representing the City by the Bay, and Juszczyk was asked by NBC Sports Bay Area for his career highlight with the franchise so far, he stated: "It's a big question because I'm proud of so many moments here. It's really hard to pinpoint one because I've been part of so much.
"My favourite game as a 49er has to be the 2023 NFC Championship Game, when we beat Detroit here to reach the Super Bowl.
"Being down 17 points at halftime and making that comeback was special. It was a special season, too. George and Deebo were doing the Netflix series Receiver, so every once in a while, my wife and I go back and watch that episode.
"It feels like there's no chance we're going to win that game, and then it turns into this magical comeback. I felt like I played a big part in it, too. I had some really big plays that I'm proud of.
"Going back and watching that game is such an emotional rollercoaster, and it's incredibly fulfilling."
The game in question featured what could only be described as one of the most memorable comebacks in recent NFL history. However, one intriguing detail is that Juszczyk admits he still watches the documentary focused on his own teammates, revisiting those memories of that remarkable occasion.
In the same interview, he shared words that would undoubtedly resonate with the Faithful, reflecting exactly what they would want to hear from a player.
"Just a sense of pride [of representing the 49ers]. You walk in every day and see those faces and plaques up on the wall," he said.
"When you first join the program, you envision yourself one day maybe being up there. For it to finally be real and to have my face and George's face right there is pretty cool."
Of course, Kittle joined just a month later in the 2017 NFL Draft. Having two players who have been around since then is invaluable, as both have helped set the tone for the culture Shanahan and Lynch wanted to instil when they arrived.

title: 49ers GM John Lynch Predicts Nick Bosa's Return to Form In Coming Weeks
full_text:
A lot of eyes are on San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa as he hasn't produced at his previous peak levels so far this season.
In his defense, he's had very limited playing time over the past two seasons due to injuries. However, there is a growing argument that his best days may be behind him because of those injuries . He's had three ACL tears.
Despite this growing concern, general manager John Lynch ( like head coach Kyle Shanahan ) is defending Bosa's subpar performances this season.
"When you're a tremendous player, like Nick is, you create a standard," Lynch said on his usual weekly interview with Bay Area radio station KNBR . "And there's somewhat of a—I don't want to call it a burden because that has a negative context—but there is a responsibility that you feel as a player. Nick impacts every game that he plays, and he does at such a high level.
"I think when he doesn't [live] up to his standard, he's going to call himself things like 'weak link.' ... Nick did have five pressures the other day, which is a high number, but he expects more out of himself.
"He didn't have training camp," Lynch added. "We're in a new defensive scheme, which asks some different things of him. And so, I think that's what Nick's alluding to. There's some adjustment, but he's stacked some good weeks of practice.
"And I just have so much confidence in him that I have the same standard that he has for himself. Nick's standard for himself is probably higher than anybody, but we have such a high standard.
"I know that we have a motivated Nick Bosa. He's an incredibly diligent worker, and I think he'll be impacting games starting this week in a big way."
Bosa has yet to pick up a sack in four games so far. It's a significant drop-off, and the 49ers are paying him a huge amount of money to make as many sacks as possible.
It makes sense to defend him because the reasons Lynch made are completely valid, but Bosa will need to improve drastically with each passing week or the front office might have to make some incredibly tough decisions.
His future has been uncertain, largely due to speculation and financial considerations, but Bosa knows better than anyone that he needs to deliver on the field. His decline since 2021 and 2022 has been significant.

title: 49ers Have Clear Blueprint to Beat Vikings' Defense
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are 7-2 and have the best defense in the NFL. However, there is a key to beating them. The way to beat the Vikings is to lean on the run and continue to push the ground game.
The Vikings have played five above-average rushing attacks, according to rbsdm.com . They are 4-0 when facing below-average rushing groups and 3-2 when facing teams who have had success running the ball.
They beat the Chicago Bears in Week 2, but the game was played in a storm, and Caleb Williams got hurt. Despite that, the Bears threw the ball more than they ran it in a game that ended 9-3.
They beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before Tampa Bay realized that their ground attack was the way to win games. Baker Mayfield had 34 pass attempts in the game and also got hurt. Bucky Irving had 15 rushing attempts.
They beat the Indianapolis Colts, but Indianapolis showed a blueprint for success. They hung tight in a 16-10 win despite four sacks and one intercepion by Daniel Jones. That is because Jonathan Taylor had 18 rushes for 95 yards, and Seth McGowan added 11 rushes for 46 yards.
Since then, the Vikings have gone 1-2, beating the Green Bay Packers, who have one of the worst rushing attacks in the NFL. Jordan Love was sacked eight times as the Vikings' defense knew exactly what was coming.
The Lions beat them with 39 rushing attempts to 25 passing attempts. That is despite trailing 7-6 most of the game and trailing 15-12 late. The Lions' seven-play, fourth-quarter, game-winning scoring drive to take the lead featured five rushes for 57 yards and two pass attempts for 12 yards.
Buffalo controlled the game in their win, but they had 44 rushing attempts to 31 pass attempts for Josh Allen attempts. You could argue the Bills leaned on their MVP candidate too much in the win. Allen was sacked four times and threw an interception.
The 49ers have Christan McCaffrey. This is what you drafted Kaelon Black for. The 49ers' rushing attack is just as strong as Detroit's and Buffalo's. Throwing the ball will lead to trouble. Running the ball can be a slog at times, but it will keep the team in the game and allow them to wear down the Vikings late. Look for San Francisco to get very run heavy in Week 11.

title: Five Major Questions the 49ers Must Answer Against the Vikings
full_text:
When the San Francisco 49ers take on the Minnesota Vikings in Week 11 it will be one of the more anticipated matchups of the season. What are some of the biggest questions that are likely to be answered this week?
With Keenan Allen in the mix, Deebo Samuel healthy, and Jordan Watkins taking strides, the need for the depth receivers to play is dwindling. Robinson went from 37 snaps in return to the field to 21 snaps with Allen added to the team.
Cowing played 26 snaps in Week 7, then 18 snaps with Robinson back. He was down to 12 snaps with Allen added. Do either of them need more snaps, or do we see them start to get phased out?
The 49ers drafted Black to take on the tough carries between the tackles and to grind out yards. The way to beat the Vikings is to avoid third down and obvious passing by all means. So, Black being able to grind out a few yards at a time is beneficial in this scenario. Do they lean on Black for a career-high in attempts?
The last time that Brock Purdy had an MVP case, it was derailed by Mike MacDonald and the Baltimore Ravens in a prime-time scenario. It was later in the 2023 season, but the game and the stakes have a similar feel, with Purdy going up against the top defense at the time. This game will go a long way in his candidacy.
It has only been two weeks into the safety rotation , but it is starting to get clear that Mustapha is one of the three safeties that cannot leave the field anymore. He has played 82% and 77% of the 49ers' defensive snaps in the past two weeks. Is it time to get back to 100% for the third-year safety?
Bosa tore his ACL last season. He came back for two games this year and injured his calf. Now, he is back from that injury for two games. It is fair to highlight how long it has been since Bosa has had a sack, but the slump can be explained. However, production has to come soon.

title: Buccaneers-Lions Game Features Massive Swing for Playoff Chances
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are sitting at a paltry 3-6 record after their Week 10 bye. In most NFL divisions, that would be the end of the road for any playoff-hopeful team. Thankfully for the Bucs, they don't play in most NFL divisions.
The Bucs play in the NFC South, where the Carolina Panthers lead the division with a 4-5 record. The Bucs are very much in the race, and a division win would mean making the playoffs and hosting a playoff game.
The Bucs are going to have to win quite a few games outside of their four remaining division games to make that happen, though, and that includes their Week 11 game this Sunday against the Detroit Lions. The Lions are 7-2 and present a tough challenge, so it would be an upset if the Bucs could pull it off.
If they do, though? Their playoff chances will increase dramatically.
Per The Athletic's Playoff Simulator , the Bucs have a 47% chance of making the playoffs. They're second in the division behind the Panthers, but despite that, they still have the highest playoff odds in the NFC South.
A win over the Lions would put that percentage much higher, though. Beating Detroit shoots Tampa Bay's number up 11 percentage points to 58%, as they'd go into their crucial Week 12 game against the Panthers either one game behind or tied for the lead. A loss would plummet them down seven percentage points to 40%.
The Lions have some significant stake in this game too, however. They currently have a 74% chance to make the playoffs in a division with all four teams winning six or more games — if they beat the Bucs, that number shoots up eight percentage points to 82%, while a loss brings it down 12 percentage points to 62%.
Even if the Bucs lose, though, hope is not lost. They'll play the division-leading Panthers in Week 12 on Monday Night Football, and even with a loss against the Lions, they'd still have a 53% chance to make the playoffs. Win two in a row, though? Tampa Bay would be looking at a 73% chance.
The Bucs will do their best to get that win on Sunday in Detroit at 1 p.m., but it won't be easy.

title: Buccaneers' Todd Bowles Gets Put on the Spot About Bruce Arians
full_text:
Bruce Arians handed the keys to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' head coaching position over to Todd Bowles after he retired in 2022, and the two have maintained their close friendship ever since.
Arians had a short stint in a front office role with the Bucs since his retirement, but in a recent interview with NFL insider Jordan Schultz, he relayed that he is itching to get back into coaching in 2027.
Arians expressed that he doesn't want to join a team in any capacity other than as the head coach, so it will be interesting to see if he garners any interest once the coaching carousel begins.
When speaking with the media following practice, Bowles gave his thoughts on whether his predecessor could still coach despite being 74 years old.
"I talk to Bruce [Arians], but we don't talk about coaching," Bowles exclaimed . "Tom Moore made Bruce look like a college student. So, you can still coach at that age, and Tom's probably a younger heart more than anybody. And so, it doesn't surprise me. Bruce can do whatever he wants to do."
It was a funny little quip from Bowles comparing the former Bucs' offensive assistant Tom Moore to Arians.
Moore coached in some capacity until the age of 88 years old, which means that Arians has some 14 years to catch him.
With all that said, it's hard to imagine that Bowles isn't right in stating that Arians can do whatever he puts his mind to.
Arians had retired before unretiring and joining the Bucs in 2019 to try and win his first Super Bowl.
If he does in fact return to coaching, he likely will only accept an offer where he can foresee himself having ultimate control while also having high thoughts on how the roster is stacked up to potentially go out and contend for his second Lombardi Trophy.
But will Arians return to coach the Bucs if Bowles is relieved of his duties at the end of the season? It's highly doubtful.
Arians handed the keys to Bowles after winning a Super Bowl, so taking over following him could likely create a rift between the two, especially if there were to be behind-the-scenes talks.
On top of that, this Bucs' roster probably doesn't move Arians enough to come back and coach.

title: Buccaneers Announce Likely Starting Quarterback vs. Lions
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers face a must-win game on Sunday (they all are, from here on out) when they play the Detroit Lions in Week 11.
The Bucs would like to have their starting quarterback, Baker Mayfield, available for that contest. His status was in doubt this week, though, as he's been dealing with a foot injury in conjunction with his dislocated thumb that he suffered in Week 3.
There were initial reports that Mayfield would be a "long shot" to play against the Lions, but that all changed when he practiced on Thursday and then spoke to the media afterward.
The Bucs held their final practice of the week on Friday, and Mayfield once again practiced — so head coach Todd Bowles' announcement on who would start against Detroit should come as no surprise.
Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters on Friday that Mayfield is "trending in the right direction" to play Sunday — as a result, he should be good to go and is expected to start the game against the Lions.
Todd Bowles says Baker Mayfield is “trending in the right direction” to play Sunday: pic.twitter.com/1Rw7DdD4vo
Bowles told the media on Wednesday that he was waiting to see how Mayfield responded in practice for the rest of the week before making a decision. Mayfield has clearly been able to practice without too much limitation, and because of that, he'll get the nod under center against Detroit.
If Mayfield were unable to go, the Bucs would turn to undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. Daniels has started three games this season and is 1-2 in those games, and although he told the media Thursday that he was prepared to start if needed, Mayfield is healthy enough to get the start.
"Continue to do what I've been doing since Chicago – doing everything I can to get all the treatment and rehab possible and prepare like a professional," Mayfield said Thursday. "For me, it's continuing that. If I continue that, I imagine being able to play. Obviously, like I told you guys before, when it came to the Steelers game, didn't think I was going to be able to. If I feel like ‘J.D.’ (Jalon Daniels) gives us a better option to win, [I have] no shame in admitting that. We'll see how it goes, but [I’m] progressing well and [we'll] see how tomorrow shapes up."
Mayfield has thrown just three touchdowns to four interceptions at the head of a league-worst passing offense in yards per game. He'll work with offensive coordinator Zac Robinson and the rest of the offense to try to turn things around, but he'll have to do it while battling injury — something Mayfield is no stranger to.
The Bucs will play the Lions at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Ford Field. When they do, it seems Mayfield will get the nod.

title: Buccaneers and NFC South Could Be Reason for New NFL Rule
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have won the NFC South four out of the last five seasons, but it has never come in dominant fashion.
The Bucs have won the NFC South with a double-digit record just once since 2022, and they won the South with a losing 8-9 record once in the same timespan as well. They've only ever won the NFC South by more than a game a single time, since then, too, in 2024.
The NFC South has been the worst division in football for some time now, and that isn't changing this year — the division doesn't have a team with more than four wins in it after Week 10. The division may be so bad, in fact, that the NFL could look to change the rules about how the playoffs work.
As it stands, every division winner gets a top-four seed in the playoffs and hosts at least one playoff game. That includes the NFC South, meaning that a divisional winner can — and in the NFC South's case, often has — host a playoff game against a much better team with a better record simply because they won a weaker division and the visiting Wild Card team did not.
That may be changing soon, and partially because of the NFC South's ineptitude. Per NFL insider Dan Graziano, the NFL may revive a discussion from last year about potentially changing the format where poor teams who won their division can host a playoff game and get a No. 4 seed.
Graziano: There are rumblings from league office about reviving discussion from 2025 offseason about whether teams that win their divisions with sub-.500 records should be guaranteed home playoff games and top-four seeds in their conference.
The Bucs and the NFC South have been the biggest culprits here, but it was the Detroit Lions, who have been on the other side of this dilemma, who proposed this rule change in 2025. The Lions finished last in the NFC North in 2025 despite finishing 9-8, while the 8-9 Panthers won the NFC South and were a No. 4 seed in the NFC.
As it stands right now, the Bucs are just one game out of the NFC South lead with a 3-6 record. Meanwhile, the Lions lead the NFC North — but they're in a three-way tie at 7-2, and the last-place Green Bay Packers are 6-4.
The Buccaneers likely wouldn't have made the playoffs in seasons like 2022, 2023 and 2024 had they been in a more difficult division. That advantage they have could go away soon if the NFL were to change this playoff rule.
Divisions are cyclical, however, so the NFC South could become very good in the next few years and the NFC North could potentially falter. There have been plenty of bad divisions over the past few years, but the Buccaneers and the NFC South are major reason why this conversation has been happening lately.
The Bucs and Lions play each other at 1 p.m. in Detroit on Sunday.

title: Buccaneers Thursday Practice Update: Did Baker Mayfield Participate?

title: Buccaneers Know They Must Stop This Lions Star
full_text:
Alex Anzalone knows a thing or two about the Detroit Lions.
Before joining the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the 2026 off-season, Anzalone played with the Lions from 2021-25 and achieved a good amount of success there while also being a team captain for multiple seasons.
He is also not the only transplant from Detroit, as fellow Buccaneer Al-Quadin Muhammad also joined the Bucs this offseason and was with the Lions from 2024 to 2025.
Both of these players know what the Lions are capable of, especially on the offensive side of the ball as they faced the Lions' stars every day for multiple years. One major player they are going to have to keep an eye on in this upcoming game is Jahmyr Gibbs.
Gibbs has already had a fantastic season for the Lions, reaching 1,000 rushing yards through only nine games and also posting 11 rushing touchdowns, 384 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns as well. He may very well be the best running back in the entire NFL and is a surefire candidate for Offensive Player of the Year
Anzalone has a simple answer when asked to describe Gibbs and players like him.
"In the league, when you play against players like this, I call them Aliens," Anzalone said. "They're from a different planet, and you have to play them differently... Gibbs is obviously one of them, and he's proven that."
Thankfully for the Bucs, the defense has been playing very well as of late in terms of getting turnovers and has been especially good at stopping the run this season.
Right now, the Bucs have the No. 1 rushing defense in the NFL in terms of yards allowed and are also first in the NFL in rushing touchdowns allowed. However, it is important to note that teams have not tried to run against the Bucs much this season, as they are second-to-last in rushing attempts against their defense.
The biggest concern that could be Gibbs' receiving ability. Both Anzalone and Trotter have struggled in moments with coverage this year, but have been doing much better in recent weeks.
If the Buccaneers are able to slow down Gibbs and really take control of the game as they were able to do in games against the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons with good defense, they could get their biggest win of the season to date.

title: Buccaneers Get Good News and Bad News After Bye Week
full_text:
Despite the fact that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are a disappointing 3-6 on the season, in addition to being one full game outside of first place in the NFC South, there are still positives to be found regarding the team's outlook for the remainder of the regular season.
Most notable among those positives is the Buccaneers' remaining strength of schedule, which is widely considered to be the easiest in the NFL after what was a difficult first half of the year. The other is that, despite their struggles, the Bucs remain undefeated in division games (2-0) on the season with four NFC South games still remaining.
Despite the potential that somehow still exists for the Buccaneers to go on a run and make the postseason, a few things will need to go right. And right now, one of the main things is the injury front.
As it stands right now, the Buccaneers have several key players dealing with injuries, which could threaten their availability for this Sunday's matchup against the Lions in Detroit.
Despite exiting last week's game vs. the Bears due to a knee injury, OLB Yaya Diaby appears to be trending in the right direction to play on Sunday.
First practice back from the bye — Antoine Winfield Jr. and Baker Mayfield didn’t practice, but Yaya Diaby IS practicing.
After practice, Bowles confirmed that Diaby is "trending in the right direction", which is a big boost to a defense that has played like one of the best in the league over the past month or so. The Bucs will need all of the defensive reinforcements they can get in order to slow down the Lions' explosive offense.
Another piece of good news coming out of Tampa today is that All-Pro LT Tristan Wirfs was also at practice. Although Wirfs didn't necessarily sustain a significant injury, as far as we know, he was seen limping off the field after the team's tough loss in Chicago.
Not only was star safety Antoine Winfield Jr. not seen at practice on Wednesday, but Bowles cast some serious doubt on Winfield's availability for this game in Detroit when he spoke to the media after practice.
Todd Bowles says that Yaya Diaby is “trending in the right direction.” Antoine Winfield Jr. is “very sore right now” and Bowles didn’t seem as optimistic about his chances this Sunday
Winfield left the game vs. Chicago when he injured his ankle trying to make a tackle and he did not return. Although the Bucs' defense looked excellent as the game went on even without Winfield in the lineup, his presence is still essential for Bowles' defense to function at full capacity.
Trying to limit the impact of players like Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta, Jahmyr Gibbs and Jameson Williams will be that much more challenging without Winfield on the field than it would be if he were to suit up for this game.
When the Bucs promoted QB Easton Stick to the 53-man roster and signed Cooper Rush to the practice squad, it was an obvious sign that Baker Mayfield's status was in serious doubt for this contest. Mayfield took a number of big hits last Sunday night in Chicago, and he was hobbling around most of the night with a foot injury.
Although we haven't got much specific info about the nature of the injury, those moves did not inspire much confidence in the belief that Mayfield would be healthy enough to start this weekend.
That being said, Bowles was not ready to not rule Mayfield out for this game after Wednesday's practice.
"He's made a lot of progress," Bowles said. "We want to see him do some things later on today and tomorrow and kind of make that determination on Friday, but he's a lot better than he was a week ago. I don't know if that's ready or not, I want to see it myself, and we'll see what he can do tomorrow."
Any time a starting quarterback is hurt, it can't be good news for the team. That being said, the fact that a glimmer of hope still exists for Mayfield to play this weekend is worth taking note of.
Regardless of whether Mayfield suits up on Sunday in Detroit or not, the Buccaneers will need to have as many healthy players on the field as possible in order to upset a very talented Lions team.

title: What We Saw From Baker Mayfield at Buccaneers Practice and What it Means
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 3-6 and still treading water as they look to make the playoffs. They're a game out of the division lead, but every game is crucial from here on out — and they have what may be their toughest game of the year on Sunday.
The Bucs are set to play the Detroit Lions on the road in Week 11. The Lions are 7-2 and boast one of the best offenses in football, and the Bucs will have to keep up on both sides of the ball to pull off the upset and get the win.
Their best shot at doing that would be with their starting quarterback, Baker Mayfield. But Mayfield is dealing with an ankle injury he picked up against the Chicago Bears, and his status for Week 11 heading into this week has been up in the air.
Here's the latest report on Mayfield's status, combined with what we saw from him at One Buccaneer Place on Wednesday:
ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday morning that Mayfield is a "long shot" to play against the Lions, but that he's more likely than not to play against the Carolina Panthers in Week 12's divisional game.
"From my understanding, the Bucs know Mayfield is probably a long shot for this week but also know Mayfield will push to get ready and play, so they aren't ruling out the possibility," Fowler wrote . "There's more optimism about next week's matchup with Carolina, a crucial divisional game."

First practice back from the bye — Antoine Winfield Jr. and Baker Mayfield didn’t practice, but Yaya Diaby IS practicing.

Should Mayfield be unable to play, the Bucs would turn to Jalon Daniels, who has already started three games for the team. In his three starts, Daniels is 1-2 with three touchdowns and five interceptions. Mayfield himself is 2-4 as a starter in Tampa Bay this year, throwing three touchdowns and four interceptions.

title: The Craziest Buccaneers Stats Through the First Half of the Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have had a season of ups and downs (mostly downs). They're 3-6 and have the worst passing offense in football, but they're just a game out of the NFC South, have an elite defense and boast an impressive running game.
The Bucs are, in many ways, a statistical enigma — it's hard to tell whether they are much better than their record or right where they're supposed to be. We've collected a few stats that make the Bucs a bizarre football team throughout their first nine games of the season.
The Buccaneers have the best rushing offense in the NFL (163.9 rushing yards per game) and the very worst passing offense in the NFL (141.9 net passing yards per game). They also have more rushing yards than passing yards at this stage of the year — not great.
The Bucs have to find ways to throw the football if they want to win games. They can really lean on the run game (and have in all of their wins), but the passing game has failed them in more ways than one.
Bucs kicker Chase McLaughlin has yet to miss a kick in any capacity. He's a pristine 22-for-22 on field goal attempts and he's 18-for-18 on extra point attempts. He's also Tampa Bay's leading scorer, currently accounting for 84 points.
We don't mean to jinx him, but McLaughlin could be on his way to a historic season. Three NFL kickers in history — Gary Anderson, Jeff Wilkins and Mike Vanderjagt — have had a perfect kicking season during the regular season.
Only Vanderjagt has had a perfect season through the regular season and the playoffs. The Bucs would have to make it to the playoffs for McLaughlin to test out that record, too.
The Buccaneers are 3-6 and one of the worst teams in the NFL by record (and most of the others are also in the NFC South). Despite that record, though, the team has a positive point differential of +24 points. That's the 11th-best number in the NFL.
Every team ahead of Tampa Bay has won six or more games. The Bucs have lost every single one of their games by one score, and two of those losses were by three points.
Tampa Bay has had a blowout against the Panthers to help increase that number, and holding the Atlanta Falcons to zero points the week after helped their differential, too. But two things seem to be for certain — the Buccaneers find themselves in close games a lot, and they have a lot of trouble actually winning them.
The Bucs have been doing this for the past few years now, but they seem to play better on the road than they do at home.
The Bucs are 2-2 on the road this year, but they're just 1-4 when playing at Raymond James Stadium. Their average points scored across those splits is also fairly interesting — they average 16.8 points per game on the road and 29.5 on the road.
The team's win over the Panthers is a bit of an outlier, by either way, the Bucs seem more comfortable on the road. Thankfully, they'll be heading to Detroit to play the Lions next Sunday at 1 p.m.

title: Chris Godwin is Costing the Buccaneers $85,000 Per Yard Right Now
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers passing attack has been their weakness this season.
The Bucs currently own the NFL's worst passing game in the league, having not even thrown for over 1,500 yards at the midway point of the season and not a single wide receiver eclipsing the 300-yard mark.
It hasn't been pretty, and for one wideout in particular, it's starting to look even worse thanks to how much money he is making.
Former Pro Bowl wide receiver Chris Godwin signed a contract extension with the Bucs before the start of the 2025 season for three years, worth $66 million. The $22 million per year was enough to keep him in Tampa Bay rather than seeing him walk to a team like the New England Patriots.
But now, just a year and a half into that deal, it's looking like a massive overpay.
Godwin has never looked quite right after dislocating his ankle in 2024, and his stats mirror that sentiment.
Last season, Godwin had the lowest receiving yardage total of his career with just 360 yards. He also only saw action in nine games as he dealt with rehab and injuries, and he only found the end zone twice.
Now, Godwin, who has already seen as much action as he did all of 2025, is set to have yet another down season. Godwin has only mustered 29 catches for 259 yards and no touchdowns.
That means that he is currently earning nearly $85,000 per yard in annual cash compensation. That is not a great return on your value or investment. If you account for his actual salary cap hit, that number gets higher at $130,050 per yard.
It's highly unlikely that a magic wand is waved and the Bucs' passing game improves enough for Godwin's contract to be worth it. That means the Bucs' front office should be looking at alternatives this offseason.
Godwin's team option, $20.7 million, is in 2027. However, the Bucs do have a potential out once the 2026 season concludes if they decide to cut bait with the aging wideout.
If Tampa Bay decides to cut Godwin outright before June 1, they would not only save the $22 million he is owed in salary, but they would also save approximately $13.7 million in cap space with his dead money coming way down.
There are always options on the table, however. Godwin and the Bucs could decide to meet for him to take a massive pay cut to stay with the team until his contract runs out — see Jamel Dean just last year — before he hits free agency.
They also could come together on a trade that could net them draft capital this offseason, but this scenario seems highly unlikely as they should have traded him beforehand if they were to go that route.

title: Best — and Worst — Case Scenario for Titans' Week 11 Matchup With Cowboys
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans enter their Week 11 faceoff with the Dallas Cowboys with some relative optimism. If the Titans win, it's a road victory just two weeks after the bye. If they lose, the top pick they currently hold looks all the more likely.
Win-win, even in a loss. But regardless of the draft outlook, Titans fans don't have to pretend that success right now is completely irrelevant. It's important to see present strides, and moral victories mean little on the heels of three straight losing seasons.
Before tomorrow's shot at redemption, here are what I see as the best (and worst) outcomes for the team's Week 11 matchup in the Lone Star State.
It's not a hot take to say that the Titans' defense has been their biggest issue over the past two weeks. However, that unit's struggles look much worse when shown alongside an offense that's getting better and better.
Tennessee has allowed 40 or more points in back-to-back weeks. The Titans' secondary is by far and away the defense's weakest limb. This downward spiral has effectively buried what have been Cam Ward's two best games of the year.
In the case of a Titans win, not only do Ward and the offense continue their hot streak, but Robert Saleh's defense finally keep pace a little and form a more complete product for Tennessee. The 4-6 Cowboys scored 40 in their latest defeat, so it's no slight challenge.
All the same, something has to give eventually. Either Saleh makes some major changes, or things start to come together. In the case of the latter, the Titans get a semi-comfortable win tomorrow.
But what if the Titans' offense starts to falter? That's what happens in our worst-case scenario this week.
After scoring 36 and 23 in Weeks 8 and 11, Ward slowly returning to his previous form would be disastrous for the Titans. It wouldn't be shocking for Ward to be outdone by QB Dak Prescott and his cast of veteran weapons (CeeDee Lamb, Jake Ferguson, etc.); he's been beaten by two elite, more experienced QBs in Joe Burrow and Trevor Lawrence already.
That's the poor outlook here. Ward failing to overcome the Cowboys' league-worst defense, regardless of what Tennessee's defense is up to, would erase much of the newfound excitement that has been ground in the second-year passer.
It's essentially youth vs. experience every week for the Titans, but this week looks more like a trap than ever. If Ward beats Prescott - who is in his 11th season - on the merits of his own playmaking, Week 11 could be a real turning point for the Titans' future.
Of course, this worst-case scenario imagines the opposite.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Staff Predictions for Titans vs. Cowboys: A Close Game Across the Board, But Split 2 Ways on the Result
full_text:
Last week, the Titans On SI staff predicted an unfortunate defeat at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars. That came to pass, but not without enough positive momentum for a few of us to change our tune this week.
The Titans enter Dallas with just one win in nine tries, and as of now, the top pick in the 2027 draft. Every discussion around this team is double-edged; the future takes hold on the now for a team in the Titans' position.
For Sunday's Week 11 matchup with the Cowboys, the staff are evenly divided. Here are our individual cases for the outcome:
In recent weeks, the Tennessee Titans have produced positive trends that have me cautiously optimistic heading into Jerry’s World, especially with QB Cam Ward seeming to find his stride. However, the Titans’ defense has fallen apart.
Across their last three matchups, Tennessee has allowed an average of 36 points per game, including back-to-back games of at least 40 points given up.Although the Cowboys’ defense hasn’t lived up to expectations, QB Dak Prescott has led Dallas to a top-five scoring offense with an average of nearly 29 points per game.
Dallas has the offensive weapons to dominate an underwhelming Tennessee secondary. I anticipate even a herculean effort from ex-Cowboys RB Tony Pollard can’t undo the Titans’ defensive errors from another loss.
The Titans are 1-8 coming off a 17-point loss, but I feel good about the team's chances this week.
It helps that Dallas has one of the worst defenses in the league and just swapped their defensive play-callers right before this matchup. It also helps that Cam Ward is on a tear and will return his best pass-catcher on the road this week.
Like the rest of the staff, I think it'll come down to the wire. Ultimately, if Tennessee is going to pull away, it will be because Robert Saleh's defense finally finds a way to reward the offense for improving on a weekly basis. Give me the Titans in their second victory of the season in Week 11.
This just feels like the type of game where the Cowboys end up laying an egg and all of the national sports shows spend the week making fun of them because of it.I expect the Titans’ talented young tandem of QB Cam Ward and WR Carnell Tate to make their presence felt throughout the contest as they play together for the first time in nearly a month.
It also wouldn’t shock me if RB Tony Pollard ends up having a big day against his former team.But with the Titans’ defensive struggles being just as bad, if not worse than Dallas’, I think the Titans end up falling just short in a game that produces a lot of points by both teams.
Tennessee’s offense is finally gaining momentum, while Dallas’s defense is going in the opposite direction. If Brian Daboll’s unit can play efficient, mistake-free football, and Robert Saleh’s defense holds Dak Prescott and the dynamic Cowboys’ offense in check, the Titans should pick up their second win of the year.
The Titans have all the ingredients for an upset here. We'll see if the team can finally put together a complete game and pull off the win.

title: The Titans Could Upset the Cowboys in Week 11... But a Loss Isn't the End of the World for 1 Reason
full_text:
Unfortunately for Tennessee Titans fans, we're at the time of the season where the offseason is becoming more interesting than the regular season with a playoff spot nowhere in sight.
After the Los Angeles Chargers defeated the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on Monday, the Titans moved from No. 2 in the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft to the top pick. The Chargers were the last standing winless team up to that point; now they share a league-low 1-8 record with Tennessee and Miami.
Currently, the Titans possess the top pick in the draft due to their strength in schedule.
As of Friday, Tennessee currently has a 48% chance of clinching the No. 1 pick and a 94% chance of having a top-five pick, according to the A to Z Sports Playoff Predictor . The technology approximates teams' chances of making the playoffs and the probability of clinching the top draft pick.
For example, if the Titans miraculously win out the remainder of the season, the site approximates they would have a 41% chance of making the playoffs. On the contrary, if the Titans lose out, their chances for the No. 1 pick rise to 99% odds, especially with the Colts and Texans on their schedule also sitting at the bottom of the AFC standings.
On Sunday, the Titans travel to Dallas to face off against the Cowboys, who stand at 4-6, which is second in the NFC East behind the 5-3-1 New York Giants. Although the Cowboys currently have a losing record, they're still in the race for a division title.
If Tennessee loses to the Cowboys and Dallas goes on to win their division, it will benefit their strength of schedule when settling tiebreakers with the other teams with the same record at the end of the season. Interestingly enough, the Titans have already lost to the Giants, because they play all NFC East opponents this season.
So far this year, Tennessee has lost to three division leaders: the Bengals, Jaguars and Giants. If the season ended today, all three teams would make the playoffs. According to the 2026 Playoff Picture on NFL.com, the Browns, another team the Titans lost to, would have the Wild Card spot.
Although a loss to Dallas would be another defeat added to the tally, it certainly wouldn't be the worst outcome for the Titans with the playoffs falling out of reach this late into the season. Later this season, Tennessee has to play the AFC South-leading Jaguars again, and the Steelers, who currently have the sixth seed in the AFC. Pittsburgh is still trailing Cincinnati for the AFC North title spot.
There's a legitimate chance the Bengals, Steelers, Browns and Jaguars make the playoffs in the AFC. Currently, the Giants are most likely to win the NFC East and earn a playoff berth. The upcoming Cowboys and Commanders still have an outside shot at making the postseason.
The Titans have lost to a litany of solid teams, and in a roundabout way, continuing that trend could secure them a generational talent at the top spot.

title: The Tony Pollard Debate: Titans Have a Huge Offseason Decision to Make, For Multiple Reasons
full_text:
Once the Titans' 2026 season comes to a merciful end, all eyes will turn toward draft season. Tennessee's moves prior to the trade deadline allowed the franchise to stack up on assets in an effort to speed up the progress of their multi-year rebuild.
Although, certain moves regarding their thinner-than-ever veteran presence loom overhead. Perhaps the most important among those is what to do with RB Tony Pollard, who has had his best season as a Titan, and one of the best seasons of his career, in the final year of his contract.
Not only is Pollard on pace for his fifth straight 1,000-yard season, but his six touchdowns are already just three short of the career-high nine he set with the Dallas Cowboys, back in 2022. He faces Dallas for the first time as a Titan this coming Sunday - the matchup is extremely favorable, to boot.
Pollard is the least of the Titans' worries currently; he's been the team's most consistent player on the offensive side of the ball for weeks now. But when his contract is up, does Tennessee pay a soon-to-be 30-year old back?
Not only that, but do they outbid the other inevitable suitors that had interest in him at the deadline?
Coming into this year, long-time backup Tyjae Spears was Pollard's clear successor. But Spears is also a free agent next year, and between consistent injury issues and poor production when he's on the field (22 carries for 94 yards on the year), that route looks less viable now than ever.
Tennessee could also sign a different free agent, but that list is dominated by veterans who don't look near as polished as Pollard right now; names like Alvin Kamara and Aaron Jones headline an underwhelming pool of possibilities.
Realistically, the Titans either sign Pollard to a new deal, draft his replacement, or both. RBs Jadan Baugh and Kewan Lacy would both pose as promising developmental pieces for the Titans, if one or both fall to Tennessee at the right spot.
30 is typically the cutoff for backs' efficiency. We can't forget that Pollard has performed way above the bar of expectation this season; this sort of production can't be expected of him for long, even if he shows no signs of slowing down right now.
The debate really comes down to how soon general manager Mike Borgonzi is willing commit to a full-youth roster. When do veterans from past coaching regimes phase out in favor of a completed rebuild? We'll find out where the GM stands by next spring.
