title: How Titans' Abysmal Coverage Stats Create a 2027 Draft Need Tennessee Can't Afford to Ignore
full_text:
Draft season starts early for 1-8 football teams. That's an unfortunate reflection of a squad's progress, but for the Tennessee Titans, the sheer amount of draft capital they hold over the next two years makes this phase more exciting than usual.
We've already dreamed up a draft where Tennessee ends up with absurd offensive firepower; Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith finds himself at the center of those dreams, and in one instance alongside Florida RB Jadan Baugh. But are those necessarily needs?
You could argue that to some extent, but a recent stat from Fantasy Points Data charts the 30 defenders in the league who have allowed the most Expected Points Added (EPA) when targted this season.
Alontae Taylor came in fourth, with +28.0 EPA, while fellow CB Marcus Harris placed eighth, with 24.1. Tennessee has allowed 40+ points and 350+ passing yards in back-to-back games. The Titans won't get far in the long run with coverage that poor.
Tennessee could always try and scrounge up a fix in free agency, but that's what they tried to do last offseason. You could say it was a matter of poor decision-making that could be rectified, but even then, the draft promises more future-forward potential.
The Titans will benefit from two first-round and two second-round selections in 2027. That's what trading your two best defenders and longest-tenured veterans gets you, in addition to the heartache.
That turns us to the candidates, which NFL Draft On SI just conveniently grouped into an early rankings system for us to pull from.
The obvious one is Notre Dame CB Leonard Moore, whose speed and length have consistently led to him topping pre-draft charts. He's been the undisuputed best CB in this class all year, and is currently a finalist for the 2026 Nagurski Trophy given the best defender in the nation.
Kelley Jones, out of Mississippi State, could be another intriguing option a little further down draft boards if Tennessee becomes attached to Jeremiah Smith first. He's got the speed and size to blanket receivers downfield, at 6'4", 205 lbs, and poses as another promising option.
The Titans will have the picks to take their pick at a bit of emergency help in a secondary. Ultimately, this debate will be decided by general manager Mike Borgonzi, who will have to choose between more offensive weapons to strengthen an already surging unit, and defensive help in a position group that is actively losing the Titans games.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Could Titans Have the Best of Both Worlds by Trading Top Pick, But Still Landing Jeremiah Smith?
full_text:
With the Tennessee Titans ’ season all but over, a lot of the talk surrounding the team revolves around what they’re going to do with their plethora of draft picks that currently includes the top pick in next year’s draft.
The undisputed prize of the 2027 class is undoubtedly Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith. He’s the type of prospect who could immediately jump in and give the Titans one of the most formidable receiver tandems in the league on day one alongside WR Carnell Tate — his former college teammate. Smith is only 20 years old and is legitimately one of the true can’t-miss non-QB prospects this century.
Another possible scenario ESPN’s Adam Schefter mentioned this week is the possibility of the Titans having a bidding war between QB-desperate teams should they secure that top pick. That's also an appealing possibility... but what if the Titans somehow manage both?
It’s unlikely, but let’s look at how it could happen.
I’ll just be honest from the start, this is not gonna be a normal trade. If I’m giving up the right to have Smith inside the building for the next decade, I’m gonna be asking for a lot.
If nobody wants to reach that price, then the Titans should have absolutely no problem staying put with their current haul of five picks in the top 70, especially when that class is headlined by arguably the safest slam dunk prospect regardless of position since DE Myles Garrett.
In most cases, the conversation wouldn’t even start without three first-round picks. Ideally, the Jets would be the trade partner since they currently have three first-rounders at their disposal. Even if they miss out on Smith in that scenario, a package that could potentially give them five first-round picks come April would be the type of move that could get this team back on track sooner rather than later.
But for the Titans to land a package of Smith plus picks, they’ll likely need to trade with a QB-desperate team that hopefully sits towards the top of the draft.
The ultimate dream scenario is a team like the Dolphins or Jets ending up with the second pick and they end up falling in love with Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker to the point where they end up doing whatever it takes to make sure they get him.
That would put the Titans in a perfect scenario where they could take the best offer from the team with the second pick and still select Smith. It definitely sounds like a fever dream, but crazier things have happened.
Only time will tell how all of this will play out, but one thing is for certain, the Titans have a massive offseason ahead of them and they absolutely cannot let it go to waste. If Tennessee does end up with that first pick, the options are limitless — and it's possible a historic trade is the cherry on top.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that. He also writes scripts for EA Sports' Madden games, where fans may have heard his work.

title: Titans Starting Cedric Gray Should Force Robert Saleh to Bench a Long Overdue LB
full_text:
Cedric Gray, after missing the Titans' Week 1 loss as a result of a concussion, spent the entirety of this season's first half trying to work his way back into Robert Saleh's rotation. His lack of snaps was confusing after Gray's great 2025 season, but that noise is in the rearview mirror now.
Without Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton in Week 10, Gray was essentially left as Tennessee's lone reliable LB against the Jacksonville Jaguars. He left no doubt in that contest that it was time to make a change in the unit. Gray hauled in his first career INT and had a team-high nine tackles.
Fittingly (and finally), Gray seems to be trending toward a promotion. Today, DC Gus Bradley said Gray is getting the majority of first-team reps in practice. Gray proved he deserves to start at WILL, and all signs point to him getting that opportunity vs. the Dallas Cowboys next Sunday.
Who, then, starts next to Gray. Where one question is answered, another is raised for Tennessee. The answer should be obvious: Hill, in his first season, has been arguably the Titans' best defender. Now is the time for Saleh and the Titans to bench Barton... but will they?
Hill leads the Titans with 82 tackles in eight games - and that's by a comfortable margin. Second to Hill is S Kevin Winston Jr., with 56. Gray comes in an fourth, with 46, in eight games also.
Where does Barton slide into the picture? All the way down in ninth, with 34 tackles. With both Hill and Barton practicing again ( to varying degrees ) after missing last week, the question is naturally begged as to which one will join Gray more often than not.
Coach Saleh has made it clear that he and this Titans regime value veteran talent. Calvin Ridley should've been traded at the deadline, but he was kept around. John Franklin-Myers (30) and Jermaine Johnson (27) were two of his biggest offseason pickups.
Barton is 29, and definitely fits that bill with eight seasons in the league. But with underwhelming tackling metrics and nothing else about his game that specifically stands out, there should be nothing stopping Tennessee from committing to the youth in their LB room.
The vet can play complimentary minutes, and fill in where needed. But at this point, both Hill and Gray have proven to be superior playmakers in a defense that desperately needs help. If you're willing to play the young guys on offense with Cam Ward (Ayomanor, Dike, Restrepo), why not here as well?
This is more of a preventative warning than anything else, but after Barton played over Gray for unclear reasons up to now, it wouldn't be a shock to see him get the nod again. We just have to hope Saleh sits the veteran and trusts the future of his own unit.

title: Analyzing a Realistic Path for Titans to End up With the Best WR and RB in 2027 Draft
full_text:
The 2027 NFL Draft is shaping up to be the Tennessee Titans' most important in years. We said that last spring, too, but both things can be true. The rebuild got more dire this season, but due to a handful of trades, we could be looking at an outlook-changing haul.
In our own draft speculation, we've vied for Tennessee to select top WR Jeremiah Smith. That is assuming the Titans hold on to the first pick. The natural follow-up to that would be a defensive piece, but ESPN's Jordan Reid just threw out an offense-heavy mock that's hard to refuse.
Therein, Tennessee takes RB Jadan Baugh at 26th overall (via the Chicago Bears), which would equip Cam Ward with the top receiver and back in the draft. This seems outlandish, but the cards are falling into place to make this a real possibility.
The Titans currently have the first pick, and while Baugh is undeniably talented, he's not as highly-rated a prospect as Jeremiyah Love was last season. As things stand right now, Tennessee is in position to steal Smith off the board, and then take the top back right where he's projected.
Worries about the defense - which is currently Tennessee's biggest problem - would be fair to assert here. The Titans already took Carnell Tate last season; why triple down on the offensive side of the ball?
The answer is a three-parter: Tennessee has two second-round picks in 2027, there are multiple strong candidates in free agency, and investing in Cam Ward is simply that important.
The first point is the simplest. Two second-rounders offers plenty of promise to build young defensive depth after the proposed first round. LB Anthony Hill Jr. was a second-round selection, and he has a case as the best player on the Titans' defense post-deadline.
Turning to free agency, guys like S Brian Branch, EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu, and CBs Ja'Quan McMillian and Isaiah Rodgers are all likely to be available. Per Spotrac, the Titans' in-season cap ($39.1 million) is still the highest in the NFL. That's a good sign for potential offseason additions.
The last one almost doesn't have to be said. Ward is Tennessee's most important player; his development as the team's franchise QB is critical to this draft not being all about taking a signal caller and resetting the system once again.
If Ward continues to get better, drafting to maximize his potentially and build around him should be the top priority. Why stop with Tate? Add a record-setting WR and an RB with 15 touchdowns in the SEC. That's taking the next step.

title: 1 Chimere Dike Stat Makes the Entire Argument for Titans to Start Him at WR
full_text:
Perhaps the Tennessee Titans' greatest story heading into Week 11 is the shakeup coming in the WR room. With Carnell Tate returning at WR and Wan'Dale Robinson being sent to IR, Cam Ward's arsenal of weapons is shifting in multiple ways.
This could come as a worry for Titans fans, as Ward has played his best football in the past two games prior to this movement. But, if anything, it should bode well for Tennessee's matchup with the Dallas Cowboys.
However, we're here today to hone in on one specific player that the Titans should be pushing as a result of this movement. Second-year WR Chimere Dike deserves to be catching passes right behind Carnell Tate.
Check out this all-purpose yards statistic from Ian Hartitz, which went viral on X :
Most all-purpose yards this season: 1. Jahmyr Gibbs (1,384) 2. Chimere Dike (1,267) 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (1,236) 4. Bijan Robinson (1,207) pic.twitter.com/D48PstGaZd
Gibbs, Smith-Njigba, and Robinson are three of the league's premier playmakers. These are team-defining guys that are typically the beginning and end of lists like these. Then you have Dike.
It's true that the bulk of those yards are on returns, but it should say something about Dike (a Pro-Bowl special-teamer) that he found his way on this list as someone who is typically limited to kickoffs. The extended impact Dike has had in his short run as a WR demands more clock at the position.
Prior to Carnell Tate sitting in Week 8 with a shoulder injury, Dike had six total receptions on the season, and 53 yards. In the two games without Tate since, Dike has seven receptions, 87 yards, and scored his first touchdown of the year against the Cincinnati Bengals.
What's more, Dike seemed to play a major part in Ward's recent rise under center. The two caught fire at the same time; just because Tate is returning doesn't mean that Dike should again be relegated to the scraps of receiving opportunities for other pass-catchers.
Dike is either the second or third best WR on this team, with fellow sophomore Elic Ayomanor having a horse in the race as well. Either way, that makes him a starter, especially with Robinson out. Nothing about Dike's game has suggested that this will be a temporary move, either.
Tennessee drafting Jeremiah Smith next year would obviously change the rotation, but if things stay as they are at WR, Titans fans can look out for Dike to play a more permanent role going forward. He just got a real, extended shot, and the aforementioned statistic is the proof in the pudding that it's only up from here.

title: Why All Signs Point to Tony Pollard’s Revenge Game vs. Cowboys Leading to a Titans Win
full_text:
On Sept. 8, 2019, a 22-year-old rookie from Memphis, Tennessee made his NFL dreams come true, debuting in his first career game under the bright lights of the iconic AT&T Stadium. A Week 1 rivalry battle between the New York Giants and Dallas Cowboys finished with a dominant 35-17 home win, and the rookie recorded 13 carries for 24 yards.
Now, more than seven years later as a member of the Tennessee Titans, RB Tony Pollard returns to Arlington, where his NFL career began.
Prior to returning to his home state in 2023, Pollard played his first five NFL seasons as a Dallas Cowboy. In the navy and silver, he blossomed from RB Ezekiel Elliott's backup to taking over the starting position and earning a Pro Bowl nod in 2022.
In Pollard's half-decade tenure with the Cowboys, he had three 1,000-yard rushing seasons and led Dallas in rushing twice.
Dallas with Pollard made the playoffs three consecutive years from 2021 to 2023, including a monstrous 31-17 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road in the Wild Card, which was the final game of QB Tom Brady's unprecedented career. Since his departure, the Cowboys haven't won a playoff game again.
On Sunday, Pollard will face his former team, who are desperate for a win, for the first time as a Titan.
Over the previous few weeks, the former Cowboy has had an unbelievable resurgence for a running back in his age 29 season.
Since Week 7, Pollard leads all running backs with five rushing touchdowns and is tied for the most 20-plus yard rushes. Furthermore, he ranks in the top-10 for running backs in rushing and receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, according to Fantasy Pros .
It's important to note that Pollard didn't play Week 9 due to Tennessee's bye, and his stats are being compared to running backs who have played one more game than him in that stretch.
Across his last three games against Cleveland, Cincinnati and Jacksonville, Pollard is averaging 130 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns per game. Pollard became the first Titan to record at least 390 yards from scrimmage and six touchdowns in a three-game stretch since future Hall of Famer RB Derrick Henry in December 2018 .
Pollard has been the backbone of an improving Tennessee offense . The Titans were averaging a league-low 11.6 points per game, which has improved to a ninth-best 25.5 since Week 6.
The Cowboys' defense has been heavily scrutinized, especially after a falling out with future Hall of Fame talent EDGE Micah Parsons that led to a franchise-altering trade with the Green Bay Packers. Dallas hoped to make a strong push for the playoffs after spending big in the offseason to improve their weak defense.
However, they're is in second place in the NFC East with a middling 4-6 record, trailing the New York Giants, who have a 5-3-1 record despite losing their starting quarterback for the season in Week 2. A loss to Tennessee would be devastating for their playoff hopes, especially if the Giants defeat Jacksonville on Sunday.
The Cowboys have scored the second-most points this season with 286 while allowing 282 points, which is the third-most in the NFL. Dallas has a near one-to-one scoring-to-points allowed ratio.
Pollard will be the focal point of the Titans' offensive attack on a Cowboys defense that allows 154.1 rushing yards per game and 5.2 yards per carry, which are both league worsts, according to Team Rankings.
Over the last three weeks, Pollard has averaged more than 4.8 yards per carry and 93 rushing per game. Tennessee has been giving the starting back a workhorse role all season, preparing him for a perfect matchup like this one against Dallas.
When facing a fellow bottom-10 run defense in yards per rush and yards per game, Pollard dominated with 117 yards on the ground and two rushing touchdowns on 5.6 yards per carry against the Bengals.
On Wednesday, news broke that the Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker has been removed from play-calling duties in favor of senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine.
The Cowboys' defensive struggles this season could lead to a high-scoring dogfight with an improving Tennessee offense led by a charging Pollard. Tennessee has a legit chance of upsetting the Cowboys, who are 1-4 at home this year, and it all ties back to the latter's former RB.
Isaiah is an award-winning journalist and photojournalist. A graduate from the University of Kentucky, he has previously been published by BloodHorse, KY Insider, and the Kentucky Kernel for multimedia sports coverage. Isaiah is a Tennessee Volunteer at heart bringing his local expertise to Titans coverage.

title: Commanders’ Week 11 Rooting Guide: What a Perfect Sunday Would Mean for Washington
full_text:
The Washington Commanders are excused from playing this Sunday for a second straight week after beating the New York Giants 24-21 on November 12. With a potential third win in four weeks awaiting Washington on Monday night, Burgundy and Gold fans can spend Sunday watching the rest of the NFC East before the Commanders get their chance to move up.
As unenviable as the 7-2 Cincinnati Bengals are as a matchup opponent for a 3-5-1 Commanders team that's only recently learned to combine talent with discipline, Washington's NFC East neighbors are burdened by their own pressure to perform. Here’s what Washington needs from the rest of the NFC East on Sunday: Dallas–Tennessee and Philadelphia–Pittsburgh kick off at 1 p.m. ET. Jacksonville–New York follows at 4:25 p.m. ET.
If any matchup is likely to threaten the Commanders' chances of seeing a slate in which everything goes their way, it's their arch-nemesis getting handed as easy an opponent as they could ask for. With just one win to their name, the Tennessee Titans read like exactly the kind of easy-out to help involuntarily right Dallas' ship from the safety of its own state-of-the-art stadium.
But the Cowboys, much like the Commanders, have failed to impress the masses from coaching or execution standpoints. As talented a scoring offense as they are, the Boys in Blue have never been able to take control of their season, tripping over their own spurs in a seemingly endless sequence. Their 4-6 record isn't impressing anyone, even after scoring 40 in a Week 10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
The Titans, to their credit, have scored at least 23 points in four straight games, with quarterback Cam Ward having quietly strung together a few productive outings to start November. He won't be challenged any more than usual by the porous Dallas defense, opening a window for the Commanders' first fortuitous domino to fall. A Dallas win would make the Cowboys 5–6 (.455). Even if Washington beats Cincinnati on Monday, the Commanders would be 4–5–1 (.450) and remain behind Dallas in winning percentage. That makes Tennessee’s upset more than a bonus for Washington.
Unlike just about every one of their hopeful division mates, the Eagles have very little worth playing for over halfway through the season. They've lost seven straight games, sliding to the depths of the NFL's standings, borderline unthinkable territory for them to encounter so quickly after eight playoff appearances over their last nine years.
Without so many of their most recognizable faces taking the field, they seem to have waved the white flag early, rather than trying to hobble on at the pace of the Wild Card race. They can't score, let alone string together a lengthy series of plays on their drives, and it's resulted in a -73 point differential through nine performances.
The #Eagles are the only team in the NFL that go 3 & out more often than they score (TD or FG), and it's hard to describe the degree to which this fact is true so please kindly have a look at this graph: pic.twitter.com/guLv7jo8GZ
This is a situation the Commanders know well , with the Eagles' rollover helping to put Washington on course for a much-needed Week 8 win , and the competitive Pittsburgh Steelers stand a good chance of taking advantage of the opportunity at mounting success of their own. Even if they, too, don't exactly make for the most viewer-friendly product, count this game as the one least worth Commanders fans' attention.
Then, later that afternoon, those familiar 5-3-1 Giants will have to follow their crunch-time loss to the Commanders with a home game against the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars. It's a duel the Commanders ought to watch closely, not just because they'll have to prepare for the same AFC power later this season.
“The #Jaguars ’ defense has posted a 2.10-second average time to pressure when blitzing this season, the quickest since at least 2019.” - @NextGenStats pic.twitter.com/Nu16NDPz2z
They're capable on both sides of the ball, certainly one of the tougher opponents the teetering Giants could have asked for at this point in their strange season.
As pleasantly surprising as their 3-1 start has been, considering franchise quarterback Jaxson Dart's inability to make it through two games before suffering a season-ending knee injury, the Giants have been playing .500 football since tying the Commanders in Week 5 . With New York's offense slowing down, Jacksonville looks to make J.J. McCarthy uncomfortable under center after holding two of their last three opponents to 10 or fewer points.
A Dallas loss would move Washington into second place before Monday night. If the Giants also lose, the Commanders would enter their game against Cincinnati 1½ games behind the Giants. If Washington then beats Cincinnati on Monday, the Commanders will finish Week 11 in second place at 4–5–1, one game behind the 5–4–1 Giants. Dallas would fall to 4–7. Sunday can open the door; beating the 7–2 Bengals is how Washington walks through it. READ : Why Cincinnati’s Run Defense Gives Washington an Opening

title: Commanders News: Jayden Daniels Could Lose Two More Weapons Before Bengals Game | Burgundy Roundup
full_text:
- Treylon Burks' nagging foot injury reared its ugly head again Friday as the Washington Commanders receiver missed practice after being a full participant on Thursday. The receiver position is thin with Terry McLaurin, Dyami Brown and Jaylin Lane on injured reserve, so this could be huge heading into Monday night's matchup with Cincinnati and Joe Burrow. - Seeing Rachaad White's name pop up on the injury report Friday as limited with a heel injury was certainly concerning. Now Washington has to make decisions on two running backs this weekend. The other backfield concern, Jacory “Bill” Croskey-Merritt, practiced fully for a second straight day as he ramps up in his return from injured reserve . Bill simply wants to play, and said Friday that the groin trouble had affected his ability to run downhill at full speed: "It's a day-by-day thing. We'll see how this week goes." The team still needs to activate him if they plan on using him against the Bengals.
Bill. On his groin injury and sitting out four games. Sounds like he's still tracking for MNF. pic.twitter.com/XNoEzsKx8J
- At Friday's presser, Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough said the offense is built around zone schemes. He stressed getting blockers to that second level, past the defensive linemen, more effectively. Blough praised Sam Cosmi's physicality and said Washington tries to run behind him. "So, we'll do whatever it takes to win and at the end of the day, we just have to continue to stick with it and get these guys up on the second level a little better," Blough said. - Cincinnati’s starting guards have yet to practice fully this week. Right guard Dalton Risner missed a second straight day Friday with knee issues, while left guard Dylan Fairchild remained limited with an oblique injury. Saturday’s final report should give us a better idea of who will be protecting Burrow inside. - Cornerback Dax Hill missed another practice with an illness, while safety Kyle Dugger improved to full participation with his quad injury. Burrow (illness) and Tee Higgins (knee) practiced fully again, with Burrow saying Friday he was feeling better. Linebacker Oren Burks remained out with a groin injury. Jonathan Allen and B.J. Hill received rest days. - “Pick up the blitzes. Have to be ready for Cover Zero,” Burrow said Friday, emphasizing the need to know where his quick answers are against Washington’s pressure . Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones wants him taking an extra hitch before the ball comes out. “You wanna try to change up the looks for him as much as possible,” Jones said. He also credited Cincinnati’s backs and tight ends for their protection, pointing to Drew Sample’s ability to help block before slipping out as an outlet for Burrow. - Daronte Jones compared Ja’Marr Chase to a running back once he has the ball in his hands. “Once that ball is off, then what?” he said. He stressed taking good pursuit angles and getting multiple defenders to the ball to limit one-on-one tackles. Chase Brown was part of that discussion, too, with Jones pointing to the running back’s ability to make one cut and take the ball the distance.
The Washington Commanders have had a sticky start to their 2026 season, but as the dust settles, several candidates for contract extensions are emerging. Three players who have made a case for an extension are K’Lavon Chaisson, Tyler Owens, and Treylon Burks.
For the first time this season, the Commanders will wear their all-black Hail Raisers as part of a blackout game against one of the AFC's top teams. The uniform features the classic burgundy and gold stripes as well as the franchise's new alternate logo: a Spear "W" logo helmet decal on both sides meant to symbolize the top fighters, the front lines, those leading a mission who are unafraid to step into the fire. "All black is fire, so it's gonna look good," Charles Omenihu said. "Monday night, you can't ride up any better."
Jayden Daniels kept it simple when he talked Thursday about what Washington has to do against Cincinnati. “We gotta put up points,” he said. The Bengals are averaging 30.9 points per game, and the Commanders are at 21.8. A six-minute drive that ends in a field goal still puts a lot on Washington’s defense the next time Joe Burrow gets the ball.
It's been three games since we last updated the Washington Commanders Rookie Power Rankings , and the class is starting to separate itself. Washington is 2-1 since the bye, with several rookies continuing to take on significant roles while others are still trying to establish themselves. We've also got some movement in the rankings this time around, so here's where everyone stands after nine games.
Woefully underrecruited out of high school in Waterloo, Iowa, Sinnott had the opportunity to play FCS-level football on scholarship. But the future Commanders’ Day 2 draft pick believed he had more talent than FBS teams were giving him credit for. So, with that confidence and a one-year offer from his father on his side, he walked on at Kansas State with no promises, no security, and no future other than the one he earned himself.
Commanders LB Leo Chenal back at practice after having neck surgery pic.twitter.com/pgK62WMt1p
The running game has to produce more consistently . Washington averaged 3.2 yards on 33 carries against the Giants. Offensive coordinator David Blough wants the offense to stay ahead of the sticks and create more third-and-short situations. That would help Washington sustain possessions and give Daniels more opportunities to work from scoring range. “We have to just be more efficient everywhere in between as an offense,” Blough said. “And that starts with the running game and it's all the backs, it's all the o-line together, it's quarterbacks, all of it.”
“But one thing I can always say is I always give that city my all, gave that team my all, and when fans come out to watch us play, they knew that 93 was gonna show up and give everything he had. “At the end of the day, the things that I did wrong, I apologize and move on.” “I'm just trying to make it as normal as possible,” Allen said. “I'm gonna be excited to see some of the guys out there that I haven't seen in a while, but at the end of the day, I'm focused on what we gotta do.”

title: Commanders’ Red Zone Problem Starts Before They Reach the 20
full_text:
In Washington's last game against the New York Giants, the Commanders reached the red zone once and scored on a one-yard catch by Ben Sinnott. Antonio Williams and Stefon Diggs scored touchdowns from 31 and 32 yards, respectively. The Commanders have 22 red zone possessions in nine games and have converted 12 into touchdowns (54.5%), which ranks 20th in the league through Week 10. According to Sharp Football Analysis , just 29.1% of Washington’s drives reach the red zone or produce a touchdown before getting there, a stat that ranks them 27th in the league. On the flip side, the Bengals have allowed touchdowns on 12 of 30 red zone possessions (40%), the third-lowest rate in the NFL. The remaining possessions produced 11 field goals and seven scoreless trips. Pittsburgh came away without a touchdown on either of its two red zone trips Sunday. On one possession, the Steelers reached Cincinnati's 20, gained two yards on their next two plays, then lost nine on a Jonathan Allen sack. They settled for a 45-yard field goal. Pittsburgh’s other red zone trip ended as time expired with the game already out of reach.
EZ view of play Mason McCormick injured his right ankle on. #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/jSSHuVOOUX
That's how a drive gets away from you. A negative play can take away some of the offense's options, especially when there's already less room for receivers to work. Washington's possession before halftime against New York offered something to build on. Rachaad White gained seven yards on consecutive carries to move the ball from the 15 to the 1. Jayden Daniels was stopped on first down. His next pass to Diggs fell incomplete. Washington needed its third chance to get in, with five seconds remaining when Sinnott scored. The running game has to produce more consistently . Washington averaged 3.2 yards on 33 carries against the Giants. Offensive coordinator David Blough wants the offense to stay ahead of the sticks and create more third-and-short situations. That would help Washington sustain possessions and give Daniels more opportunities to work from scoring range. “We have to just be more efficient everywhere in between as an offense,” Blough said. “And that starts with the running game and it's all the backs, it's all the o-line together, it's quarterbacks, all of it.” Washington converted seven of 14 third downs against New York. There is an opening to keep drives going against Cincinnati , too. Taking advantage would let Washington put together longer possessions and keep Joe Burrow waiting on the sideline. Blough took responsibility for getting more points out of the offense: "And that starts with me. We gotta get more points on the board to help our group out." title: Commanders Rookie Power Rankings: Who Has Earned Washington's Trust After Nine Games?
full_text:
It's been three games since we last updated the Washington Commanders Rookie Power Rankings , and the class is starting to separate itself. Washington is 2-1 since the bye, with several rookies continuing to take on significant roles while others are still trying to establish themselves. We've also got some movement in the rankings this time around, so here's where everyone stands after nine games.
Sonny Styles continues to make it difficult for anyone to take the top spot away from him. The rookie linebacker has 80 tackles through nine games, including 13 in each of Washington's last two contests against the Rams and Giants. He's now reached 13 tackles in four of his last five games, with 34 coming in the three games since our previous rankings. Styles has also recorded five tackles for loss, a sack, an interception, a forced fumble, and four passes defensed this season. The Pro Football Focus grades haven't necessarily followed that production. Styles' overall grade has dropped from 68.9 in our last edition to 66.2, ranking 33rd among 82 qualifying linebackers. But there's more to his game than simply collecting tackles, and we saw a perfect example against New York. With the Giants facing third-and-three late in the fourth quarter, Styles recognized the formation, adjusted to what he believed was coming, and dropped J.J. McCarthy for a two-yard loss . That stop helped give Jayden Daniels one more opportunity, which he turned into the game-winning touchdown. For a rookie who has already played 567 defensive snaps, those are the kinds of plays that keep him at No. 1.
Sonny Styles vs The Backfield. The Commanders rookie LB is now the 3rd favorite (10%) to win DROY on Kalshi 😳🔥 pic.twitter.com/qRNqeFos0s
Antonio Williams continues to push Styles for the top spot, although his situation has become a little more complicated. Through nine games, Williams has 28 receptions for 326 yards (11.6 per catch) and two touchdowns, including the 31-yarder against the Giants that gave Washington a 17-14 lead in the third quarter. Since the bye, Williams has caught 10 passes for 121 yards and a touchdown, but his playing time tells us more about how Washington views him. He played 50 of 60 offensive snaps against Philadelphia (83%), followed by 52 of 62 against the Rams (84%) and 59 of 69 against the Giants (86%). That's 161 snaps over three games, more than any other Washington receiver during that stretch. His PFF overall grade has slipped from 74.0 to 70.3, but the opportunities are clearly there. What hasn't followed is a comparable increase in targets. Williams was targeted just twice against New York despite leading the receivers in playing time, something Dan Quinn addressed this week . With Terry McLaurin out for the season, Washington needs Williams involved more often, particularly on early downs. The next step isn't getting him onto the field; it's getting him the football.
Antonio Williams was sensational Sunday night. Unguardable pic.twitter.com/uh06r9UegT
Remember when Drew Stevens was struggling to make extra points early in the season? That hasn't been much of an issue lately. Since the bye, Stevens has made seven of eight field-goal attempts and all five extra points, bringing his season totals to 17-of-20 on field goals (85%) and 15-of-18 on extra points (83.3%). Stevens connected on four field goals against Philadelphia, becoming the first Washington rookie to do so since James Tuthill in 2002. He followed that performance by making both attempts against the Rams and his only attempt against the Giants. PFF still has him at a 59.0 field-goal grade, but his improvement since the first two games is difficult to ignore. The rookie who set two franchise kicking records earlier this season is becoming a much more dependable option for Washington.
Welcome to the Drew Stevens era. 🏈 16/19 on the season 🏈 12/12 inside of 50 yards 🏈 13/14 since Week 2 pic.twitter.com/fyzQEfhaTF
Joshua Josephs moves up one spot, but not because he's suddenly become the pass rusher we saw during the preseason. His playing time remains limited, with 14 defensive snaps against Philadelphia, 18 against the Rams, and just 10 against the Giants. Through nine games, he's played 128 defensive snaps and has yet to record a sack. PFF has Josephs at 51.9 overall, an improvement from his 44.6 grade in our last edition. The pass-rush production still hasn't materialized, but he's at least maintaining a role in Washington's defensive rotation. With Matt Gulbin's latest opportunity not going particularly well, that's enough to move Josephs ahead of him.
Matt Gulbin got another opportunity against the Rams when Lucas Patrick suffered a concussion, but things didn't go as Washington hoped. Gulbin played 35 offensive snaps at center, allowing a sack, a quarterback hit, and a hurry on 28 pass-blocking snaps, according to PFF . His season grade has dropped from 63.2 to 45.3, including a 27.2 pass-blocking grade. What happened four days later against New York is just as important. With Patrick still unavailable, Washington turned to Nick Allegretti rather than Gulbin. Allegretti played all 69 offensive snaps at center, and the offensive line allowed just one sack in the win. I've already made the case for keeping Allegretti involved at center , and with Patrick now cleared from concussion protocol, Gulbin could find himself further down the pecking order. That's enough to drop him one spot.
There isn't much new to report on Athan Kaliakmanis, who hasn't played an offensive snap since replacing Marcus Mariota against Indianapolis in Week 4. His 15-of-33 performance for 186 yards, a touchdown, and an interception remains his only regular-season action. With Jayden Daniels starting and Mariota back as the primary backup, Kaliakmanis has returned to his developmental role.
Tanoa Togiai remains on Washington's active roster but has yet to play an offensive snap this season. He was inactive again against Philadelphia and New York, leaving him in the same position he's occupied since making the team as an undrafted rookie. Until he gets an opportunity, there's nothing new to evaluate.
The Commanders will play host to the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night, giving the rookies another chance to build on what they've done so far. With eight games remaining, there's still plenty of time for these rankings to change. title: 3 Commanders Playing Their Way to a Contract Extension
full_text:
The Washington Commanders have had a sticky start to their 2026 season, but as the dust settles, several candidates for contract extensions are emerging. Three players who have made a case for an extension are K’Lavon Chaisson, Tyler Owens, and Treylon Burks.
Through nine starts this season, Chaisson has recorded 24 tackles, 3.5 sacks, and three forced fumbles (already a career high). What he means to the defense was on full display against the Eagles, with a sack and three quarterback hits, but his ability to create turnovers has been his best asset on a team that stressed that exact thing all offseason and in training camp. Chaisson, 27, played 48 of Washington’s 65 defensive snaps (74%) against the Giants . During free agency this past offseason, he signed a one-year deal worth $11 million with $10.3 million guaranteed and will be an unrestricted free agent in 2027. What Chaisson brings to the Commanders' defensive edge rotation is more than worth a reasonable two- to three-year extension.
K'Lavon Chaisson 🤝 Nick Cross 📺 #LARvsWAS FOX pic.twitter.com/n168zBSITh
The backbones of great teams come from all positions on the football field. It just so happens that Tyler Owens has found his niche on special teams. One of the team's best athletes, Owens has had some issues in coverage as a safety. But when it's time to lace 'em up on special teams, this guy is a demon. In eight games this season, he's recorded eight special teams tackles, including the tackle that went viral in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Owens' contract differs from Chaisson's in that he'll be coming off an undrafted contract and will be a restricted free agent in 2027. They can likely bring him back on a short, modest contract to keep developing.
Now THIS is the proper way to use AI. They turned Tyler Owens into the Hulk 😂 pic.twitter.com/yDziA4uv9S
Treylon Burks is a player who has grown on me since the team signed him to the practice squad last season. Originally drafted to be the replacement for A.J. Brown in Tennessee, injuries have derailed his career. That said, he's found new life in Washington, and through seven games this season, he has 14 catches for 260 yards (18.6 yards per reception) and two touchdowns. He's already doubled his receiving yardage and touchdowns from last season, when he finished with 10 catches for 130 yards and one touchdown in eight games. Most recently, Burks played 42 snaps (61%) against the Giants and, with Terry McLaurin out for the year, has become one of the team's top long-ball receivers . According to Over the Cap , his current one-year deal is for $2.35 million, with a maximum value of $4 million. I think he gives the team another option for Jayden Daniels, whom he's developed chemistry with over the last year. A short extension with a slight pay increase seems about right for Burks as the team continues to see how high his ceiling can go. With a history of injuries, the deal should be structured to protect the team and reward him with bonuses based on how much time he actually sees the field.

He made the most highlight plays on the team during training camp, and he's the only Commander who gets more productive the further downfield he is Here are his targets this year #RaiseHail https://t.co/qkjxGkcHYM pic.twitter.com/WshLqDmldC

One study, published Thursday by researchers at Boston University and Banner Health, was based on a small sample of former American football players who donated blood while alive. full_text:

I can’t even lie i need a 10 reception game from Antonio Williams vs the Bengals pic.twitter.com/tw0AfzSwvz

Against the Eagles, he had seven targets, five catches for 54 yards and a second-and-10 conversion . David Blough has made room for him on the field. Now the staff has to decide where his touches fit in the call sheet. Against the Bengals, I want to see Williams involved in the first half and on early downs, before Washington needs him to rescue a drive. title: Commanders Mailbag: The Jayden Daniels Throw Washington Can’t Repeat Against the Bengals
full_text:
We want to hear from you! Each week, we invite you, the Burgundy and Gold faithful, to send in your Washington Commanders questions about everything going on in Ashburn/Landover. We want to make sure everyone gets a chance to have their take heard in the HTTR4LIFE Mailbag, so we'll answer questions on either Monday or Friday, depending on the volume of responses each week. You can send your Washington Commanders questions for the HTTR4LIFE Mailbag to hailbng+si@gmail.com . Jayden Daniels delivered the finish Washington needed against the Giants, but his first two interceptions of the season nearly changed the outcome. This week’s mailbag looks at those throws and whether Nick Allegretti should stay at center if Lucas Patrick is cleared for the Bengals game.
Question from Yannick B. via email The first interception came with 5:28 left in the 4th quarter on a pass that Jayden Daniels put on Chig Okonkwo's inside shoulder. The ball should have gone to the other shoulder on the outside, where only Okonkwo could get it. Jevon Holland made a great play, but the truth is it was bad ball placement in the heat of the moment. Those are the types of plays you want to see your quarterback take chances on, though; he did what you want, just not the outcome the team needed.
Jevon Holland Picks Off Jayden Daniels In A Huge Moment. He Read It The Whole Way And Jumped Right In Front Of It. This Was A Great Defensive Play. Definitely Not A Great Ball From Daniels, Though. He Can't Throw That One In A Spot Like This. Giants Defense Comes Up Big. pic.twitter.com/mAfEYGLKm4
The second interception came on a pass that should never have been thrown, with Daniels trying to force it to Okonkwo after Okonkwo appeared to cut his route a bit short. Giants safety Ar'Darius Washington jumped the route altogether and grabbed New York's second interception in little over three minutes. The play appeared to be partly Okonkwo's fault for not cutting back across the middle on a double move, but mainly on Daniels for throwing it with the defender playing back. Maybe he missed the defender purposely playing off. I don’t see two interceptions as a trend, but that second throw is the one he can’t repeat against Cincinnati.
Ar’Darius Washington picks off Jayden Daniels. The Giants get another massive takeaway. pic.twitter.com/khx25ncZOE
Question from Greg M. on Facebook Greg, you sir have the million-dollar question. I believe the staff would wholeheartedly love to live in a world where Nick Allegretti is the starter for the rest of the year. That was their plan coming out of the offseason . Patrick’s arrival gave them another option that didn't include throwing rookie Matt Gulbin to the wolves before he was ready. That said, I think you stick with what works, and the offensive line did well with Allegretti in the lineup last weekend . There is always a chance the staff will view Allegretti as being more valuable as a plug-in if needed, but Patrick has experience at both guard positions and can work that role as well.
